examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司啱啱起步，需要啲開荒牛嚟做最辛苦嘅工作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 aam1 aam1 hei2 bou6, seoi1 jiu3 di1 hoi1 wong4 ngau4 lai4 zou6 zeoi3 san1 fu2 ge3 gung1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司剛起步，需要一些願意吃苦、做最辛苦工作的「開荒牛」。
examples.english_sentence: The company is just starting up; it needs some hard‑working pioneers (literally '開荒牛') to do the toughest jobs.

mandarin_meaning: 開蒙 / 啟蒙（開始教育、啟發）
english_meaning: to enlighten; to initiate someone into learning; to open someone's mind or understanding
explanation_mandarin: 表示開始教育或啟發某人，使其獲得初步知識或有所領悟；也可指被啟發、開竅。
explanation_english: Refers to beginning to educate or to enlighten someone so they gain initial knowledge or insight; can also mean someone becoming enlightened or having their eyes opened.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次講座幫我開蒙，令我明白投資嘅基本概念。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 gong2 zo6 bong1 ngo5 hoi1 mung4, ling6 ngo5 ming4 baak6 tau4 zi1 ge3 gei1 bun2 goi3 nim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次講座幫我開蒙，讓我明白投資的基本概念。
examples.english_sentence: This lecture opened my eyes and helped me understand the basic concepts of investing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細個嗰陣係由老師開蒙，識到好多基礎知識。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 go3 go2 zan6 hai6 jau4 lou5 si1 hoi1 mung4, sik1 dou3 hou2 do1 gei1 co2 zi1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他小時候是由老師開蒙，學到了很多基礎知識。
examples.english_sentence: When he was young, his teacher initiated him into learning and he acquired a lot of basic knowledge.

mandarin_meaning: 敞篷车
english_meaning: convertible (open-top car)
explanation_mandarin: 指車頂可以打開或收起的汽車，即敞篷車，通常用來描述有開放式車頂的車款。
explanation_english: A car whose roof can be folded down or removed; a convertible or open-top automobile.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗部開蓬車，成日夏天周末去海邊兜風。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 bou6 hoi1 pung4 ce1, sing4 jat6 haa6 tin1 zau1 mut6 heoi3 hoi2 bin1 dau1 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他买了一辆敞篷车，夏天的周末常常去海边兜风。
examples.english_sentence: He bought a convertible; in summer he often goes for drives to the beach on weekends.

mandarin_meaning: 开药（为病人开处方/配药）
english_meaning: to prescribe medicine; to write a prescription; to dispense medicine
explanation_mandarin: 指醫生或醫護人員為病人開出藥方或處方，給予或指示服用藥物。為香港粵語常用說法。
explanation_english: Refers to a doctor or healthcare professional prescribing medication for a patient—writing a prescription or authorizing medicine. A common expression in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生幫我開藥，叫我每日食三次。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 bong1 ngo5 hoi1 joek6, giu3 ngo5 mui5 jat6 sik6 saam1 ci3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 医生帮我开药，叫我每日吃三次。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor prescribed medicine for me and told me to take it three times a day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我去藥房攞藥，係醫生開嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 heoi3 joek6 fong4 lo2 joek6, hai6 ji1 sang1 hoi1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我去药房取药，是医生开的。
examples.english_sentence: I went to the pharmacy to collect the medicine that the doctor prescribed.

mandarin_meaning: （衣服的）开衩，指裙子或衣服上为了行动或美观而开的开口；也可作动词，表示在衣服上开这种口
english_meaning: a slit or vent in a garment (e.g. skirt or qipao); can also be used as a verb meaning to put a slit in clothing
partOfSpeech_english: noun (can also be used as a verb)
explanation_mandarin: 常用於描述裙子、旗袍等衣物在側面或前後裁出的開口，讓行動更方便或增加造型效果；作動詞時表示為衣物裁出這樣的開口。
explanation_english: Refers to the slit cut into garments (such as skirts or qipaos), usually at the side or front/back to allow easier movement or for styling; used as a verb it means to cut such a slit into clothing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條長裙有開衩，行路方便啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 coeng4 kwan4 jau5 hoi1 caat3, haang4 lou6 fong1 bin6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条长裙有开衩，走路方便一些。
examples.english_sentence: This long skirt has a slit, making it easier to walk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 件旗袍側邊開衩，好性感。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin6 kei4 pou4 zak1 bin1 hoi1 caat3, hou2 sing3 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件旗袍侧边开衩，很性感。
examples.english_sentence: The qipao has a slit on the side — very sexy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 設計師喺條裙度開咗衩，方便行動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sit3 gai3 si1 hai2 tiu4 kwan4 dou6 hoi1 zo2 caat3, fong1 bin6 haang4 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 设计师在裙子上开了衩，方便行动。
examples.english_sentence: The designer put a slit in the skirt to make movement easier.

mandarin_meaning: 开裆裤 (kāidāngkù)：裆部有开口的裤子，传统上供婴幼儿方便排便或换尿布。
english_meaning: open-crotch pants; crotchless pants — trousers with an opening at the crotch, traditionally used for toddlers to make toileting easier.
explanation_mandarin: 指裤子裆部有开口或不封裆的设计，传统上用于婴幼儿，便于排便或换尿布；在现代也可作为复古或特定用途的服饰。
explanation_english: Refers to pants with an opening at the crotch area, traditionally used for infants and toddlers to facilitate toileting and diaper changes; nowadays may be seen as an old-fashioned or niche garment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路著開襠褲，爸媽換尿片方便啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 zoek3 hoi1 dong1 fu3, baa4 maa1 wun6 niu6 pin3 fong1 bin6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子穿开裆裤，父母换尿布比较方便。
examples.english_sentence: Children wearing open-crotch pants make it easier for parents to change diapers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢種開襠褲係舊式，依家較少見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zung2 hoi1 dong1 fu3 hai6 gau6 sik1, ji1 gaa1 gaau3 siu2 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这种开裆裤是旧式的，现在较少见。
examples.english_sentence: This type of open-crotch pants is old-fashioned and is less commonly seen nowadays.

mandarin_meaning: 開設 / 開辦 / 設立（建立、設置某項服務、機構或課程）
english_meaning: to establish; to set up; to open (e.g., an account, service, office, or course)
explanation_mandarin: 表示建立或設置某項機構、服務、課程或帳戶等，強調開始提供或成立該項目。
explanation_english: To establish or set up an organization, service, course, account, etc.; emphasizes starting or making available that item.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大學開設咗一個新嘅課程。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 hok6 hoi1 cit3 zo2 jat1 go3 san1 ge3 fo3 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大學開設了一個新的課程。
examples.english_sentence: The university has started a new course.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 銀行開設咗網上服務，方便客戶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngan4 hong4 hoi1 cit3 zo2 mong5 soeng6 fuk6 mou6, fong1 bin6 haak3 wu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 銀行開設了網上服務，方便客戶。
examples.english_sentence: The bank has launched online services to make things more convenient for customers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司打算喺九月開設一個新嘅研發部門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 daa2 syun3 hai2 gau2 jyut6 hoi1 cit3 jat1 go3 san1 ge3 jin4 faat3 bou6 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司打算在九月開設一個新的研發部門。
examples.english_sentence: The company plans to set up a new R&D department in September.

mandarin_meaning: 有話就說 / 直接說出來
english_meaning: Speak up; say what you have to say
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語表達，用來催促或要求對方把心裡想說的話說出來，類似「有話就說」或「說吧」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese imperative used to urge someone to speak up or state their point; similar to "say it" or "if you have something to say, say it."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開講有話，唔好拐彎抹角，直接講啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 gong2 jau5 waa6, m4 hou2 gwaai2 waan1 mut6 gok3, zik6 zip3 gong2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 有話就說，別拐彎抹角，直接說吧。
examples.english_sentence: If you have something to say, say it — don't beat around the bush, say it directly.

mandarin_meaning: 開始賭博 / 開設賭局
english_meaning: to start gambling; to hold or run a gambling session
explanation_mandarin: 指開始進行賭博或開設賭局，常用於私下或非法的賭博活動描述。
explanation_english: Refers to beginning to gamble or setting up a gambling session; often used for private or illegal gambling activities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上星期有人喺村入面開賭，最後被警察捉咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 sing1 kei4 jau5 jan4 hai2 cyun1 jap6 min6 hoi1 dou2, zeoi6 hau6 bei6 ging2 caat3 zuk1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上個星期有人在村裡開賭，最後被警察抓了。
examples.english_sentence: Last week someone held a gambling session in the village and was eventually arrested by the police.

mandarin_meaning: 开赛；比赛开始
english_meaning: to start a match / the start of a competition; kick off
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞 / 名詞（視語境而定）
explanation_mandarin: 「開賽」指比賽或賽事開始的時間或動作，可用作動詞（開始比賽）或名詞（比賽的開始）。在香港粵語中常用於體育賽事或活動的場合。
explanation_english: “開賽” refers to the start of a match or competition. It can be used as a verb (to start a match) or as a noun (the kick-off/start). Commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese for sports events and similar occasions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽今晚七點開賽，唔好遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 gam1 maan5 cat1 dim2 hoi1 coi3, m4 hou2 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比赛今晚七点开赛，别迟到。
examples.english_sentence: The match starts at 7pm tonight; don't be late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 賽事準時開賽，所以要早啲到場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: coi3 si6 zeon2 si4 hoi1 coi3, so2 ji5 jiu3 zou2 di1 dou3 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 赛事准时开赛，所以要早点到场。
examples.english_sentence: The event will start on time, so arrive a bit early.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 一陣間比賽就開賽，準備好裝備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat1 zan6 gaan1 bei2 coi3 zau6 hoi1 coi3, zeon2 bei6 hou2 zong1 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一会儿比赛就要开始了，准备好装备。
examples.english_sentence: The match will start soon; get your gear ready.

mandarin_meaning: 离开；走开；（开车）驶走
english_meaning: to leave; to go away; (of a vehicle) to drive off
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示離開某處或（車輛）啟動後駛走。可用於人離開或車輛起步離去。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to leave a place or (for a vehicle) to start off and drive away. Used for people departing or vehicles pulling away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋而家開走啦，等陣見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 zau2 laa1, dang2 zan6 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们现在走了，待会儿见。
examples.english_sentence: We're leaving now, see you later.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到有人嚟，就開走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 jau5 jan4 lai4, zau6 hoi1 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一听到有人来，就离开了。
examples.english_sentence: He left as soon as he heard someone coming.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度阻住，開走啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 zo2 zyu6, hoi1 zau2 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别在这里挡着，走开吧！
examples.english_sentence: Don't block here, move/leave!

mandarin_meaning: 開始跑 / 出發 / 開走
english_meaning: to start running; to set off; to take off (e.g., a vehicle); to make a run for it
explanation_mandarin: 口語常用詞，表示開始跑或開始出發（可用於人、車等），在口語中亦可指突然跑掉或逃走。
explanation_english: A colloquial expression meaning to start running or to set off (applies to people, vehicles, etc.). Informally it can also mean to bolt or run away abruptly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽一響哨，佢哋就開跑喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 jat1 hoeng2 siu3, keoi5 dei6 zau6 hoi1 paau2 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比賽一響哨，他們就開始跑了。
examples.english_sentence: When the race whistle blew, they started running.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 架的士啟動之後就開跑，開去機場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaa3 dik1 si2 kai2 dung6 zi1 hau6 zau6 hoi1 paau2, hoi1 heoi3 gei1 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 計程車發動後就開走了，開往機場。
examples.english_sentence: After the taxi started, it set off toward the airport.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 發現差佬嚟，佢見到就即時開跑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 jin6 caa1 lou2 lai4, keoi5 gin3 dou2 zau6 jik1 si4 hoi1 paau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 發現警察來，他一看到就立刻跑掉了。
examples.english_sentence: When he saw the cops coming, he ran off immediately.

mandarin_meaning: 开路
english_meaning: to clear the way; to pave the way; to lead the way
explanation_mandarin: 表示清除道路以便通行；也可比喻為某事創造條件或帶頭開創新局面。
explanation_english: To clear a physical path for passage; figuratively, to pave the way or pioneer something, creating conditions for others to follow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你去前面開路，我哋跟住過嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 heoi3 cin4 min6 hoi1 lou6, ngo5 dei6 gan1 zyu6 gwo3 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你去前面开路，我们随后过去。
examples.english_sentence: Go ahead and clear the way, we'll follow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺呢個行業開路，創造咗好多新機會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ni1 go3 hong4 jip6 hoi1 lou6, cong3 zou6 zo2 hou2 do1 san1 gei1 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在这个行业开路，创造了很多新机会。
examples.english_sentence: He paved the way in this industry, creating many new opportunities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等我落車，你幫我開路先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 ngo5 lok6 ce1, nei5 bong1 ngo5 hoi1 lou6 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等我下车，你先帮我开路。
examples.english_sentence: Let me get off the car, please make a way for me first.

mandarin_meaning: 转身离开；愤怒或不满地走开
english_meaning: to storm off; to walk away angrily or in displeasure
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，表示因不滿、惱怒或尷尬而迅速轉身離去或走開。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to leave abruptly or storm off because of anger, displeasure, or embarrassment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢同我吵完就開踭走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tung4 ngo5 caau3 jyun4 zau6 hoi1 zaang1 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他跟我吵完就轉身走了。
examples.english_sentence: After arguing with me, he stormed off.

mandarin_meaning: 脫身 / 有空
english_meaning: to be free (to have spare time) / to get out of an obligation
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示結束工作或事務後有空，或從某種職責、約束中脫身、抽身。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to be free (have time) after finishing duties, or to get out of an obligation/commitment.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我做完今日嘅報告，終於開身喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zou6 jyun4 gam1 jat6 ge3 bou3 gou3, zung1 jyu1 hoi1 san1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我做完今天的報告，終於有空了。
examples.english_sentence: I finished today's report, finally I'm free.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今晚得唔得閒？我可能未能開身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 maan5 dak1 m4 dak1 haan4? ngo5 ho2 nang4 mei6 nang4 hoi1 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今晚有沒有空？我可能沒辦法脫身。
examples.english_sentence: Are you free tonight? I might not be able to get free.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上個星期老細安排咗個會議，我唔容易開身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 go3 sing1 kei4 lou5 sai3 ngon1 paai4 zo2 go3 wui6 ji5, ngo5 m4 jung4 ji6 hoi1 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上個星期老闆安排了一個會議，我不容易抽身。
examples.english_sentence: Last week the boss scheduled a meeting; I can't easily get away.

mandarin_meaning: 开车（驾驶汽车）；网络/口语俚语：发表或讲述带有色情、性暗示的内容
english_meaning: to drive (a car); slang: to make sexual innuendo or post erotic/sexually explicit content
explanation_mandarin: 1) 直接含义为驾驶汽车。2) 在网络或口语中，用作俚语，指发表或讲述带有色情或性暗示的言论（相当于“开黄腔”“发黄色内容”）。
explanation_english: 1) Literally means to drive a car. 2) As internet/colloquial slang, it refers to making sexual jokes, innuendo, or posting erotic content.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日要開車去上班。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1jat6 jiu3 hoi1 ce1 heoi3 soeng5 baan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天要开车去上班。
examples.english_sentence: I'm going to drive to work today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱考到牌，終於可以自己開車啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 haau2 dou3 paai4, zung1 jyu1 ho2 ji5 zi6 gei2 hoi1 ce1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他刚刚考到驾照，终于可以自己开车了。
examples.english_sentence: He just got his driver's license; he can finally drive by himself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋喺聊天室入面成日開車，講啲黃色嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 hai2 liu4 tin1 sat1 jap6 min6 seng4 jat6 hoi1 ce1, gong2 di1 wong4 sik1 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们在聊天室里老是在“开车”，说黄色的内容。
examples.english_sentence: They're always 'driving' in the chatroom—making sexual jokes.

mandarin_meaning: 开办；设立、开始举办（机构、活动、课程等）
english_meaning: to establish/launch; to start or set up (an organization, event, course, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 表示設立或開始舉辦某些機構、單位、活動或課程，例如開辦公司、學校或公開課程。
explanation_english: Means to establish or begin running something (an organization, unit, event, or course), e.g., to open a company, start a school, or offer a program.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋公司下個月會開辦一個新分部。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gung1 si1 haa6 go3 jyut6 wui5 hoi1 baan6 jat1 go3 san1 fan1 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们公司下个月会开办一个新分部。
examples.english_sentence: Our company will open a new branch next month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學校打算下學期開辦多個成人進修課程。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 haau6 daa2 syun3 haa6 hok6 kei4 hoi1 baan6 do1 go3 sing4 jan4 zeon3 sau1 fo3 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 学校打算下学期开办多个成人进修课程。
examples.english_sentence: The school plans to offer several adult continuing-education courses next semester.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府計劃喺市中心開辦免費健康檢查。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 gai3 waak6 hai2 si5 zung1 sam1 hoi1 baan6 min5 fai3 gin6 hong1 gim2 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府计划在市中心开办免费健康检查。
examples.english_sentence: The government plans to run free health checks in the city center.

mandarin_meaning: 开通；开启或使畅通（如开通服务、开通道路、开通思想）
english_meaning: to open/activate; to make smooth or accessible (e.g. activate a service, open a road, open someone's mind)
explanation_mandarin: 表示把某個通道、服務或概念打開、啟用或使暢通；也可指心態上打開、接受新的想法。
explanation_english: Indicates opening or activating a channel, service, or making something passable; can also mean opening one's mind to accept new ideas.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我已經幫你開通咗漫遊服務。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 bong1 nei5 hoi1 tung1 zo2 maan6 jau4 fuk6 mou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我已经帮你开通了漫游服务。
examples.english_sentence: I've already activated the roaming service for you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條新路開通咗之後，交通情況改善咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 san1 lou6 hoi1 tung1 zo2 zi1 hau6, gaau1 tung1 cing4 fong3 goi2 sin6 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条新路开通之后，交通情况改善了。
examples.english_sentence: After the new road opened, the traffic situation improved.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁頑固，試下開通下腦筋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 wun4 gu3, si3 haa5 hoi1 tung1 haa5 nou5 gan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那么固执，试着开通一下脑筋。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so stubborn; try to open your mind a little.

mandarin_meaning: 把心裡話說出來；暢所欲言、把不滿或秘密講清楚
english_meaning: to open up; to speak one's mind or vent; to come clean
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用語，指把心裡的不滿、煩惱或心事說出來，讓對方知道或釋放情緒。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to open up and say what's on one's mind—venting, speaking frankly, or making something clear to others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有咩唔開心就開通頂講，我哋聽緊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 me1 m4 hoi1 sam1 zau6 hoi1 tung1 ding2 gong2, ngo5 dei6 teng1 gan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有甚麼不開心就把心裡話說出來，我們在聽。
examples.english_sentence: If you're unhappy about something, just open up and say it — we're listening.

mandarin_meaning: 偏袒、站隊或為某人辯護（在爭論中選擇一方）
english_meaning: to take sides; to side with or defend someone in an argument
explanation_mandarin: 口語、廣東話用語，指在爭論或衝突中支持或偏袒某一方，替對方說話或辯護。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to support or favor one side in an argument or dispute, to back someone up or defend them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日出錯，你就唔好成日幫佢開邊啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ceot1 co3, nei5 zau6 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 bong1 keoi5 hoi1 bin1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是出錯，你就不要總是替他偏袒/說話。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps making mistakes; don't always take his side.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媒體唔應該喺新聞報道中開邊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mui4 tai2 m4 jing1 goi1 hai2 san1 man4 bou3 dou6 zung1 hoi1 bin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媒體不應該在新聞報導中偏袒一方。
examples.english_sentence: The media shouldn't take sides in news reports.

mandarin_meaning: 挑起爭端；挑釁、找碴
english_meaning: to pick a fight; to provoke or stir up trouble/controversy
explanation_mandarin: 香港口語，指有人故意挑釁、找碴或引發爭論、衝突，屬於俗語／俚語用法。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong colloquial/slang expression meaning to deliberately provoke, pick a fight, or stir up controversy or disputes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日開邊瓣，大家傾返正經嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 seng4 jat6 hoi1 bin1 baan6, daai6 gaa1 king1 faan1 zing3 ging1 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別老是挑釁，大家談點正事吧。
examples.english_sentence: Stop constantly picking fights — let's talk about something serious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺討論區成日開邊瓣，就係想搏人注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 tou2 leon6 keoi1 seng4 jat6 hoi1 bin1 baan6, zau6 hai6 soeng2 bok3 jan4 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在討論區老是挑起爭端，就是想博取關注。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps stirring up trouble on the forum just to attract attention.

mandarin_meaning: 開口說話；先發言
english_meaning: to speak first; to break the silence; to be the first to say something
explanation_mandarin: 字面為「開金口」，引申為先開口說話或打破沉默，常用於請某人先發言、先報價或首次開口表態。有時帶請人先說話或做開場的意思。
explanation_english: Literally 'open the golden mouth'. Idiomatically it means to speak first or break the silence—used when asking someone to start speaking, give the first opinion, or make the first offer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢終於開金口講嘢，講咗之後大家先知道發生咩事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zung1 jyu1 hoi1 gam1 hau2 gong2 je5, gong2 zo2 zi1 hau6 daai6 gaa1 sin1 zi1 dou3 faat3 sang1 me1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他終於開口說話，說完之後大家才知道發生了什麼事。
examples.english_sentence: He finally spoke up; after he said it everyone finally knew what had happened.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆叫我哋先開金口講價，睇下對方點回應。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 giu3 ngo5 dei6 sin1 hoi1 gam1 hau2 gong2 gaa3, tai2 haa5 deoi3 fong1 dim2 wui4 jing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老闆叫我們先開口報價，看看對方的反應。
examples.english_sentence: The boss told us to speak first and state a price to see how the other side would react.

mandarin_meaning: 字面上是解開鈕扣；口語上可比喻揭露、挑起事端或說出令人尷尬的事
english_meaning: literally 'open the button door' — literally to unbutton; colloquially used to mean to expose something, bring up sensitive matters, or stir up trouble
explanation_mandarin: 原本可理解為解開衣物鈕扣，但在廣東話口語中常用作比喻，指揭露隱私、挑起爭端或說出令場合尷尬、不愉快的事。屬於較隨意的用語，常見於香港口語或非正式場合。
explanation_english: While it can be interpreted literally as unbuttoning clothing, in Cantonese colloquial use it is often a metaphor for exposing someone's private matters, provoking trouble, or saying something that makes the situation awkward or unpleasant. It is informal/slang and mainly used in casual Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好亂開鈕門。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lyun6 hoi1 nau2 mun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要隨便揭人短。
examples.english_sentence: Don't randomly 'open the button' (don't expose people's faults).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺聚會上突然開鈕門，搞到大家唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 zeoi6 wui5 soeng6 dak6 syun4 hoi1 nau2 mun4, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在聚會上突然揭開舊事，讓大家不開心。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly 'opened the button' at the gathering and brought up old matters, making everyone unhappy.

mandarin_meaning: 开销（支出、费用）
english_meaning: expense(s); expenditure; cost
explanation_mandarin: 指日常生活或特定用途的支出、費用，常用來表示某段時間內需支付的開支總額。
explanation_english: Refers to expenses or expenditures for daily life or specific purposes; commonly used to indicate the total costs incurred over a period.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你最近嘅開銷比以前大咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zeoi3 gan6 ge3 hoi1 siu1 bei2 ji5 cin4 daai6 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你最近的开销比以前大了。
examples.english_sentence: Your recent expenses are larger than before.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 每個月我都要計算啲開銷，免得唔夠錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mui5 go3 jyut6 ngo5 dou1 jiu3 gai3 syun3 di1 hoi1 siu1, min5 dak1 m4 gau3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 每個月我都要算一下開銷，免得不夠錢。
examples.english_sentence: Every month I calculate my expenses so I don't run out of money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢筆開銷係必要嘅投資。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bat1 hoi1 siu1 hai6 bit1 jiu3 ge3 tau4 zi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這筆開銷是必要的投資。
examples.english_sentence: This expense is a necessary investment.

mandarin_meaning: 挑起爭端；挑釁、挑事
english_meaning: to pick a fight; to provoke or start an argument/confrontation
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示故意挑起衝突、發難或向人挑釁，常用於非正式語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to deliberately provoke, pick a fight, or take the offensive; typically used in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再喺度開鋒啦，大家講下好唔好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 hai2 dou6 hoi1 fung1 laa1, daai6 gaa1 gong2 haa5 hou2 m4 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再在這裡挑事了，我們大家講一下可以嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Don't start picking fights here again; can we all just talk it out?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到唔鐘意嘅說話就會開鋒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 m4 zung1 ji3 ge3 syut3 waa6 zau6 wui5 hoi1 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一聽到不喜歡的話就會挑釁。
examples.english_sentence: Whenever he hears something he doesn't like, he starts provoking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上次喺酒吧嗰陣，兩個人突然開鋒，差啲打交。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 ci3 hai2 zau2 baa1 go2 zan6, loeng5 go3 jan4 dat6 jin4 hoi1 fung1, caa1 di1 daa2 gaau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上次在酒吧的時候，兩個人突然挑起衝突，差點打起來。
examples.english_sentence: Last time at the bar, two people suddenly started fighting and almost came to blows.

mandarin_meaning: 說錯話；失言；不小心洩露（秘密）
english_meaning: to say the wrong thing; to blurt out; to let slip (a secret)
explanation_mandarin: 口語粵語短語，指不小心說了不該說的話或說錯話，可能造成麻煩或洩露秘密。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning to say something one shouldn't have said or to misspeak, often causing trouble or revealing a secret.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一時唔小心開錯口，講咗朋友嘅秘密。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 si4 m4 siu2 sam1 hoi1 co3 hau2, gong2 zo2 pang4 jau5 ge3 bei3 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一時不小心說錯話，洩露了朋友的秘密。
examples.english_sentence: He accidentally said the wrong thing and revealed his friend's secret.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好開錯口，否則件事會變得麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hoi1 co3 hau2, fau2 zak1 gin6 si6 wui5 bin3 dak1 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別說錯話，否則事情會變得麻煩。
examples.english_sentence: Don't say the wrong thing, otherwise it will make things troublesome.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢開錯口之後收唔到口，越講越多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 co3 hau2 zi1 hau6 sau1 m4 dou2 hau2, jyut6 gong2 jyut6 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說錯話之後收不住，越說越多。
examples.english_sentence: After he said the wrong thing he couldn't stop and kept saying more.

mandarin_meaning: 开锁
english_meaning: to open/unlock a lock; locksmithing (can be legal service or illegal lock‑picking)
explanation_mandarin: 指打开锁或解除锁定，可以指合法的开锁服务（如找开锁师傅）或非法的撬锁行为。
explanation_english: To open or unlock a lock. It can refer to legitimate locksmith services (hiring someone to open a lock) or illegal lock‑picking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔小心鎖咗門，要搵人開鎖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 so2 zo2 mun4, jiu3 wan2 jan4 hoi1 so2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不小心把门锁上了，要找人开锁。
examples.english_sentence: I accidentally locked the door; I need to find someone to unlock it.

mandarin_meaning: （電影/電視）開機、開拍；開始拍攝
english_meaning: to start filming / to begin principal photography
explanation_mandarin: 粵語片語，屬於影視行業用語，指電影或電視劇正式開始拍攝（開機、開拍）。有時也可引申指重大工程或項目開始。
explanation_english: A Cantonese film/TV production term meaning to begin shooting (start principal photography). It can also be used figuratively to mean the start of a major project.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 導演話星期一會開鏡，大家要準時到位。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dou6 jin2 waa6 sing1 kei4 jat1 wui5 hoi1 geng3, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 zeon2 si4 dou3 wai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 导演说星期一会开机（开拍），大家要准时到位。
examples.english_sentence: The director said shooting will start on Monday, everyone must be on set on time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 部戲下個月正式開鏡，製作團隊已經緊張籌備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou6 hei3 haa6 go3 jyut6 zing3 si6 hoi1 geng3, zai3 zok3 tyun4 deoi2 ji5 ging1 gan2 zoeng1 cau4 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那部片下个月正式开机（开拍），制作团队已经紧张筹备。
examples.english_sentence: The film will officially begin shooting next month; the production team is already busy preparing.

mandarin_meaning: 惹麻煩 / 惹事 / 闖禍
english_meaning: to cause trouble; to get into trouble; to stir up a mess
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面為「開鍋/開鑊」，引申為招惹麻煩、惹事或把事情搞得一團糟。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning "open the wok." Figuratively it means to cause trouble, stir up a mess, or get into hot water.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再開鑊啦，已經夠亂。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi6 hoi1 wok6 laa1, ji5 ging1 gau3 lyun6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要再惹事了，已經夠亂。
examples.english_sentence: Don't cause any more trouble; it's already messy enough.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一講呢啲嘢就會開鑊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 gong2 ni1 di1 je5 zau6 wui5 hoi1 wok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一說這些話就會惹麻煩。
examples.english_sentence: Whenever he talks about that, trouble will start.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次真係開大鑊，件事可能會好麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 zan1 hai6 hoi1 daai6 wok6, gin6 si6 ho2 nang4 wui5 hou2 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次真的是惹上大麻煩，事情可能會很麻煩。
examples.english_sentence: This time it's really a big mess; the issue could become very troublesome.

mandarin_meaning: 開始；開場（活動、演出或討論的開始）
english_meaning: to start; to kick off; to begin (an event, performance, meeting, or discussion)
explanation_mandarin: 「開鑼」是廣東話俗語，原指敲鑼作為演出或活動開始的信號，現泛指活動、會議、演出或討論等的開始或開場。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '開鑼' originally referred to striking a gong as a signal that a performance was starting. Colloquially it now means to start or kick off an event, meeting, performance, or discussion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚嘅演唱會八點開鑼，記得早啲入場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ge3 jin2 coeng3 wui2 baat3 dim2 hoi1 lo4, gei3 dak1 zou2 di1 jap6 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚的演唱會八點開始，記得早點入場。
examples.english_sentence: The concert starts at 8 tonight; remember to get in early.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 會議一開鑼，大家就開始討論議題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wui6 ji5 jat1 hoi1 lo4, daai6 gaa1 zau6 hoi1 ci2 tou2 leon6 ji5 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 會議一開始，大家就開始討論議題。
examples.english_sentence: Once the meeting starts, everyone begins discussing the agenda items.

mandarin_meaning: 不停地長時間說話或反覆懇求（常帶有哀求、嘮叨或拉攏之意）
english_meaning: to talk at length or persistently (often to plead, nag, or make a long pitch); to badger or whine repeatedly
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，形容人在別人面前長時間說話、反覆請求或嘮叨，目的通常是想說服、乞求或施壓。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who talks for a long time or repeatedly pleads/nags in front of others, typically to persuade, beg, or pressure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺人面前開長喉，想人幫佢借錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai6 jan4 min6 cin4 hoi1 coeng4 hau4, soeng2 jan4 bong1 keoi5 ze3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常在別人面前不停地央求，想讓別人幫他借錢。
examples.english_sentence: He often begs persistently in front of others, trying to get someone to lend him money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 記者喺記者會上開長喉，不停追問個官員嘅責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gei3 ze2 hai6 gei3 ze2 wui2 soeng6 hoi1 coeng4 hau4, bat1 ting4 zeoi1 man6 go3 gun1 jyun4 ge3 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 記者在記者會上不停追問官員的責任。
examples.english_sentence: The reporter kept pressing the official with questions at the press conference.

mandarin_meaning: 开门 (kāimén)
english_meaning: open the door; open (a shop); to admit/let in
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是把門打開。也可用於商店或機構表示“開始營業/開門營業”，或比喻地表示開始接待、開始做事或接受新事物。
explanation_english: Literally means to open a door. It can also mean to open a shop (open for business), or be used figuratively to indicate beginning to receive people, starting an activity, or being open to something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可唔可以幫我開門？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 hoi1 mun4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以帮我开门吗？
examples.english_sentence: Can you help me open the door?

mandarin_meaning: 开门见山（形容说话或做事直截了当，直接切入主题）
english_meaning: to get straight to the point; to be direct and straightforward
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語 / 副詞（或形容詞用法）
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容說話或行事非常直接，不拐彎抹角，馬上切入重點。
explanation_english: Describes speaking or acting in a direct, straightforward way—immediately getting to the main point without beating around the bush.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘢一向開門見山，唔鍾意繞圈子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 je5 jat1 hoeng3 hoi1 mun4 gin3 saan1, m4 zung1 ji3 jiu4 hyun1 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說話一向開門見山，不喜歡繞圈子。
examples.english_sentence: He always gets straight to the point; he doesn't like beating around the bush.

mandarin_meaning: 开阔
english_meaning: spacious; wide; open; broad-minded
explanation_mandarin: 表示空间或视野宽广、开阔，也可比喻胸襟或思想宽广、不拘小节。
explanation_english: Describes a space or view that is wide and open; can also be used metaphorically to describe someone who is broad-minded or open-hearted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上到山頂，景色好開闊，可以望到成個城市。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng5 dou3 saan1 deng2, ging2 sik1 hou2 hoi1 fut3, ho2 ji5 mong6 dou3 seng4 go3 sing4 si5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上到山顶，景色很开阔，可以望到整个城市。
examples.english_sentence: When we reached the mountain top, the view was very expansive; we could see the whole city.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅心胸好開闊，唔會計較細故。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 sam1 hung1 hou2 hoi1 fut3, m4 wui5 gai3 gaau3 sai3 gu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的胸襟很开阔，不会计较小事。
examples.english_sentence: He is broad-minded and doesn't fuss over small matters.

mandarin_meaning: 开关 (kāiguān)
english_meaning: switch; (to) turn on/off
explanation_mandarin: 指用來控制電器或機械通斷的裝置（開或關）；也可作動詞，表示打開或關上（電源、裝置等）。
explanation_english: A device that controls the flow of electricity or operation of a machine (a switch); also used as a verb meaning to turn something on or off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 客廳嘅電燈開關喺邊度？
examples.jyutping_sentence: haak3 teng1 ge3 din6 dang1 hoi1 gwaan1 hai2 bin1 dou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 客厅的电灯开关在哪里？
examples.english_sentence: Where is the light switch in the living room?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出門前記得關埋所有開關。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 mun4 cin4 gei3 dak1 gwaan1 maai4 so2 jau5 hoi1 gwaan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出门前记得把所有开关都关上。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to turn off all the switches before you leave.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部機有兩個開關，一個係緊急用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 gei1 jau5 loeng5 go3 hoi1 gwaan1, jat1 go3 hai6 gan2 gap1 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部机器有两个开关，一个是紧急用的。
examples.english_sentence: This machine has two switches; one is for emergency use.

mandarin_meaning: 開關（按鈕）
english_meaning: switch (on/off); power switch
explanation_mandarin: 指用來開啟或關閉電器的按鈕或開關裝置，為廣東話常用稱呼。
explanation_english: Refers to the button or switch used to turn electrical appliances on or off; a common Cantonese term.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 部風扇個開關掣壞咗，開唔到風。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou6 fung1 sin3 go3 hoi1 gwaan1 zai3 waai6 zo2, hoi1 m4 dou3 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 風扇的開關壞了，開不了。
examples.english_sentence: The fan's switch is broken; it won't turn on.

mandarin_meaning: 开辟；开拓、开设（道路、领域、市场等）
english_meaning: to open up; to found, to develop, to pioneer (e.g., a road, field, market, or opportunity)
explanation_mandarin: 表示开拓或设立新的事物、空间或领域，常用于开辟道路、市场、园区等正式或书面语场合。
explanation_english: A formal verb meaning to open up or establish something new — used for developing roads, parks, markets, industrial zones, or figuratively creating new opportunities or fields.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條新路係由政府開闢嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 san1 lou6 hai6 jau4 zing3 fu2 hoi1 bik1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条新路是由政府开辟的。
examples.english_sentence: This new road was opened/constructed by the government.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司打算喺郊區開闢一個工業園區。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 daa2 syun3 hai2 gaau1 keoi1 hoi1 bik1 jat1 go3 gung1 jip6 jyun4 keoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司打算在郊区开辟一个工业园区。
examples.english_sentence: The company plans to develop an industrial park in the suburbs.

mandarin_meaning: 开除
english_meaning: to dismiss; to fire; to expel
explanation_mandarin: 表示解除某人的職務或將某人除名（例如公司解雇員工或學校開除學生）。
explanation_english: Means to remove someone from a position or membership (e.g., firing an employee or expelling a student).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司話佢犯咗大錯，要將佢開除。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 waa6 keoi5 faan6 zo2 daai6 co3, jiu3 zoeng1 keoi5 hoi1 ceoi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司說他犯了大錯，要把他開除。
examples.english_sentence: The company said he made a big mistake and is going to fire him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺校內發表唔適當嘅言論，畀學校開除咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 haau6 noi6 faat3 biu2 m4 sik1 dong3 ge3 jin4 leon6, bei2 hok6 haau6 hoi1 ceoi4 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在校內發表不當的言論，被學校開除了。
examples.english_sentence: He made inappropriate remarks at school and was expelled by the school.

mandarin_meaning: （1）亮牌、開牌（麻將或紙牌中把手牌攤出來或碰、吃等，稱為「開面」）；（2）出面、親自到場處理（與「出面」近義）；（3）（口語）臉部被劃破或裂開
english_meaning: (1) to open one's hand / reveal melds (in mahjong or card games); (2) to show up / step forward in person to deal with something (similar to “come forward”); (3) (colloquial) to cut/split one's face
explanation_mandarin: 「開面」在粵語作動詞使用，主要用法有：一是在麻將或打牌時把手牌亮出、開牌或碰、吃等，稱為「開面」；二是指親自出面、到場處理事情（和「出面」意義相近）；少數情況下也可口語化指臉部被劃破或裂開需要縫合。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '開面' is a verb. Main usages: (1) in mahjong or card games, to open your hand by revealing melds or showing cards/tiles; (2) to appear in person or step forward to handle an issue (similar to 'come forward'/'show up'); (3) colloquially, to cut/split one's face (injury).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好淨係暗聽，開面先有機會贏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 am3 ting1, hoi1 min6 sin1 jau5 gei1 wui6 joeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要只暗聽，要亮牌才有機會贏。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just wait with a concealed hand; open your melds if you want a chance to win.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆叫你開面處理客人嘅投訴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 giu3 nei5 hoi1 min6 cyu2 lei5 haak3 jan4 ge3 tau4 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老闆叫你出面處理客人的投訴。
examples.english_sentence: The boss asked you to step forward and handle the customer's complaint.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢打波跌低，唔小心開面，要縫針。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daa2 bo1 dit3 dai1, m4 siu2 sam1 hoi1 min6, jiu3 fung4 zam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他打球跌倒，不小心割破臉，需要縫針。
examples.english_sentence: He fell while playing and accidentally cut his face; he needs stitches.

mandarin_meaning: 开头
english_meaning: beginning; to start
explanation_mandarin: 表示事情、時間或過程的開始，也可作動詞表示開始做某事。
explanation_english: Refers to the beginning of something; can also be used as a verb meaning to start or initiate an action.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開頭嗰陣我唔識佢哋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 tau4 go2 zan6 ngo5 m4 sik1 keoi5 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一开始我不认识他们。
examples.english_sentence: At first, I didn't know them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋開頭講咗啲規矩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hoi1 tau4 gong2 zo2 di1 gwai1 geoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们一开始讲了一些规矩。
examples.english_sentence: At the start, we talked about some rules.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可唔可以幫我開頭寫第一段？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 hoi1 tau4 se2 dai6 jat1 dyun6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你能不能帮我开头写第一段？
examples.english_sentence: Could you help me start by writing the first paragraph?

mandarin_meaning: （1）吃飯、開始吃（2）謀生、維持生計
english_meaning: (1) to start eating / have a meal (2) colloquially: to make a living
explanation_mandarin: 「開飯」是廣東話常用口語，主要用來表示開始吃飯或用餐時間，也可引申指以某種方式謀生、賺取生活費。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '開飯' commonly means to start a meal or that mealtime has begun. Colloquially it can also mean to earn a living or support oneself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開飯喇，大家一齊食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 faan6 laa3, daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 開飯了，大家一起吃吧。
examples.english_sentence: Meal's ready — let's all eat together.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢靠補習開飯，收入都幾穩定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kaau3 bou2 zaap6 hoi1 faan6, sau1 jap6 dou1 gei2 wan2 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他靠補習維持生計，收入還算穩定。
examples.english_sentence: He makes a living by tutoring; his income is fairly stable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐廳今晚七點開飯，記得訂枱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 teng1 gam1 maan5 cat1 dim2 hoi1 faan6, gei3 dak1 ding6 toi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餐廳今晚七點開飯，記得訂位。
examples.english_sentence: The restaurant starts serving at 7pm tonight — remember to book a table.

mandarin_meaning: 開飯；開始吃飯
english_meaning: to start a meal; to begin eating
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用語，表示開始吃飯或開始用餐；亦可指開始供應或上菜。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to begin a meal or start eating; can also mean to start serving food.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋而家開餐啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 hoi1 caan1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們現在開飯吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's start eating now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廚房準備好未？可以開餐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceoi4 fong4 zeon2 bei6 hou2 mei6? ho2 ji5 hoi1 caan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 廚房準備好了嗎？可以開飯了。
examples.english_sentence: Is the kitchen ready? We can start the meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開餐前記得洗手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 caan1 cin4 gei3 dak1 sai2 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 開飯前記得洗手。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to wash your hands before eating.

mandarin_meaning: 開館 / 开馆 (kāiguǎn)：（館）向公眾開放；（展覽、館所等）開始營運或對外接待。
english_meaning: to open (a venue such as a museum, library, or exhibition); to open the doors to the public.
explanation_mandarin: 指博物館、圖書館、展覽等場所開始營業或對公眾開放，亦可用於宣佈展覽等正式啟動。
explanation_english: Refers to the start of operation or opening to the public of places like museums, libraries, or exhibitions; can also announce the official opening of an exhibition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新展覽下星期一正式開館。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 zin2 laam5 haa6 sing1 kei4 jat1 zing3 sik1 hoi1 gun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新展览下星期一正式开馆。
examples.english_sentence: The new exhibition will officially open next Monday.

mandarin_meaning: （一）開始；起初；開頭
english_meaning: at the beginning; at first; the start
explanation_mandarin: 表示某個事情或時間段的開始，常用作副詞或名詞，相當於「一開始」「開頭」。
explanation_english: Indicates the beginning of an event or time period. Used as an adverb or noun, equivalent to 'at the beginning' or 'at first'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開首我以為佢唔會嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 sau2 ngo5 ji5wai6 keoi5 m4 wui5 lei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一開始我以為他不會來。
examples.english_sentence: At first, I thought he wouldn't come.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開首嗰陣天氣好唔穩定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 sau2 go2 zan6 tin1 hei3 hou2 m4 wan2 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一開始那陣子天氣很不穩定。
examples.english_sentence: At the beginning the weather was very unstable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做報告嘅時候，開首要講下背景。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 bou3 gou3 ge3 si4 hau6, hoi1 sau2 jiu3 gong2 haa5 bui3 ging2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做報告的時候，開頭要說一下背景。
examples.english_sentence: When giving the presentation, at the start you should mention the background.

mandarin_meaning: 舉行祭祀/上香儀式（通常在祖堂或為亡者舉行）
english_meaning: to hold an incense-offering/ancestor-worship ceremony (often at an ancestral hall or for the deceased)
explanation_mandarin: 「開香堂」是廣東話用語，指在祖堂或家中舉行上香、祭祖或為亡者舉行法事、開壇等儀式。常見於葬禮、祭祀或落成、修葺祖堂時的宗教/民俗活動。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "開香堂" refers to holding an incense-offering or ancestor-worship ceremony — performing incense, memorial rites, or ritual services (often at an ancestral hall or for the deceased). It commonly appears in funeral, memorial, or ancestral-hall ceremonies.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚要喺祖屋開香堂，叫晒親戚嚟上香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jiu3 hai2 zou2 uk1 hoi1 hoeng1 tong4, giu3 saai3 can1 cik1 lei4 soeng5 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚要在祖屋開香堂，叫親戚來上香。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight we'll hold an incense-offering ceremony at the ancestral house and ask relatives to come pay incense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 下個月佢哋會為阿爺開香堂，請咗道士來做法事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 go3 jyut6 keoi5 dei6 wui5 wai6 aa3 je4 hoi1 hoeng1 tong4, ceng2 zo2 dou6 si6 lei4 zou6 faat3 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 下個月他們會為祖父開香堂，請了道士來做法事。
examples.english_sentence: Next month they will hold an incense-offering ceremony for their grandfather and have a Taoist priest perform the rites.

mandarin_meaning: 開演出；舉辦表演、演唱會；（口語）做出鋪張、招搖的行為
english_meaning: to put on a show / hold a performance or concert; (colloquial) to show off, make a spectacle
explanation_mandarin: 「開騷」在粵語中常用來表示舉辦演出或演唱會，例如歌手或樂隊上台表演。口語中也可指在場合中故意表現、招搖或吸引注意。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "開騷" commonly means to hold a performance or concert (e.g., a singer or band performing). Colloquially it can also mean to act showy or put on a spectacle to attract attention.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今晚喺紅館開騷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 maan5 hai2 hung4 gun2 hoi1 sou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今晚在紅館開演唱會。
examples.english_sentence: He's having a concert at the Coliseum tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個樂隊下個月會喺酒吧開騷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ngok6 deoi6 haa6 go3 jyut6 wui5 hai2 zau2 baa1 hoi1 sou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個樂隊下個月會在酒吧演出。
examples.english_sentence: This band will be playing at the bar next month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日喺社交場合度開騷，淨係想吸引注意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 se5 gaau1 coeng4 hap6 dou6 hoi1 sou1, zing6 hai6 soeng2 sik1 jan5 zyu3 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常在社交場合炫耀，只是想吸引注意。
examples.english_sentence: He always puts on a show at social events just to attract attention.

mandarin_meaning: 开斋；打破斋戒/结束禁食；（俗）结束霉运或久旱之后首次得手、获胜
english_meaning: to break a fast; (colloquial) to end a dry spell — to get a first success/win after a period without one
explanation_mandarin: 「開齋」原意為結束斋戒、吃第一頓飯。粵語口語化後也可用作比喻，表示在一段時間沒有勝利或收穫之後，第一次取得成功或贏利。
explanation_english: Literally 'to break the fast' (end a period of fasting). In Cantonese colloquial use it can also mean to break a losing streak — to achieve a first success, win, or profit after a dry spell.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 齋戒做到日落，我哋而家可以開齋喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zaai1 gaai3 zou6 dou3 jat6 lok6, ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 ho2 ji5 hoi1 zaai1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 斋戒到日落，我们现在可以开斋了。
examples.english_sentence: The fast lasts until sunset; we can break the fast now.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢排投資一直虧損，今日終於開齋，賺返啲錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 paai4 tau4 zi1 jat1 zik6 fai1 syun2, gam1 jat6 zung1 jyu1 hoi1 zaai1, zaan6 faan1 di1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这段时间投资一直亏损，今天终于开斋，赚回了一些钱。
examples.english_sentence: I've been losing money on investments lately; today I finally 'opened the fast' — I made back some money.

mandarin_meaning: 褲襠開了；露出內褲／褲子拉鍊沒拉好（常用於尷尬場面）
english_meaning: to have one's fly open / to have pants unzipped (often causing embarrassment); to be caught with one's pants down
explanation_mandarin: 口語／俚語表達，指褲子的襠部或拉鍊沒有扣好／拉好，導致露出內褲或尷尬暴露；也可引申為被當場揭穿或出醜。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression meaning someone's fly or crotch area is open (pants unzipped), exposing underwear and causing embarrassment; can also be used figuratively for being exposed or caught off guard.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你條褲開𧟘褲喇，快啲拉返拉鍊啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tiu4 fu3 hoi1 dong1 fu3 laa3, faai3 di1 laai1 faan1 laai1 lin6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你的褲襠開了，快把拉鍊拉好。
examples.english_sentence: Your fly is open — zip up your pants quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 閏（rùn）：在曆法中插入的額外日子或月份，見於閏年、閏月；亦可作動詞，表示插入。
english_meaning: Intercalary; to intercalate — an extra day or month inserted in a calendar (as in a leap year or leap month).
explanation_mandarin: 用於描述曆法中額外插入的日子或月份（如閏年、閏月）；作動詞時表示把日子或月份插入曆法。
explanation_english: Refers to an extra day or month inserted into a calendar (e.g., leap year, leap month). As a verb, it means to insert such an extra day or month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年係閏年，二月有二十九日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 hai6 jeon6 nin4, ji6 jyut6 jau5 ji6 sap6 gau2 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年是閏年，二月有二十九天。
examples.english_sentence: This year is a leap year; February has 29 days.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 農曆有時會有閏月，要隔幾年先插入一個月。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nung4 lik6 jau5 si4 wui5 jau5 jeon6 jyut6, jiu3 gaak3 gei2 nin4 sin1 caap3 jap6 jat1 go3 jyut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 農曆有時會有閏月，要隔幾年才插入一個月。
examples.english_sentence: The lunar calendar sometimes has a leap month; an extra month is inserted every few years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你問日期，記得分清閏年同平年。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 man6 jat6 kei4, gei3 dak1 fan1 cing1 jeon6 nin4 tung4 ping4 nin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你問日期，記得分清閏年和平年。
examples.english_sentence: If someone asks about the date, remember to distinguish a leap year from a common year.

mandarin_meaning: 闰年 (rùnnián)
english_meaning: leap year
explanation_mandarin: 曆法中的一種年份，為了使曆法與太陽年或農曆循環對齊而加入的額外時間（如陽曆中加入閏日、農曆中可能加入閏月）。在公曆中，閏年指二月份有29天的年份。
explanation_english: A year that contains an extra day (or an extra month in lunisolar calendars) added to keep the calendar synchronized with the solar year. In the Gregorian calendar a leap year means February has 29 days.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年係閏年，二月有29日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 hai6 jeon6 nin4, ji6 jyut6 jau5 ji6 sap6 gau2 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年是闰年，二月份有29天。
examples.english_sentence: This year is a leap year; February has 29 days.

mandarin_meaning: 闰日 (rùn rì)
english_meaning: leap day (an extra day inserted into the calendar, usually February 29)
explanation_mandarin: 閏日是指為了調整曆法與太陽年或季節的對應而額外加入的一天，通常出現在閏年的二月（二月二十九日）。
explanation_english: A leap day is an extra day inserted into the calendar to keep it aligned with the solar year or seasons, commonly February 29 in leap years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年有個閏日，二月就有二十九日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 jau5 go3 jeon6 jat6, ji6 jyut6 zau6 jau5 ji6 sap6 gau2 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年有閏日，所以二月有二十九天。
examples.english_sentence: This year has a leap day, so February has 29 days.

mandarin_meaning: 闰月（农历中为调整阴阳历而插入的额外月份）
english_meaning: leap month; intercalary month (an extra month inserted into a lunar calendar)
explanation_mandarin: 农历（阴历）中为使月相周期与太阳年对齐而在某些年份插入的额外月份，称为闰月。
explanation_english: An extra month inserted into the lunar calendar in certain years to align the lunar months with the solar year; also called an intercalary or leap month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今年農曆有閏月，啲節日會點排要留意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 nin4 nung4 lik6 jau5 jeon6 jyut6, di1 zit3 jat6 wui5 dim2 paai4 jiu3 lau4 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今年农历有闰月，节日的安排要注意。
examples.english_sentence: There is a leap month in the lunar calendar this year, so be mindful of how the festivals are scheduled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你喺閏月出生，你嘅農曆生日通常要點慶祝？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 hai2 jeon6 jyut6 ceot1 saang1, nei5 ge3 nung4 lik6 saang1 jat6 tung1 soeng4 jiu3 dim2 hing3 zuk1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你在闰月出生，你的农历生日通常要怎么庆祝？
examples.english_sentence: If you were born in a leap month, how do you usually celebrate your lunar birthday?

mandarin_meaning: 闲（xián）：空闲、闲暇、没事做
english_meaning: idle; free; at leisure
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容词（也可作名词，表示闲暇）
partOfSpeech_english: adjective (can also function as a noun 'leisure')
explanation_mandarin: 表示没有事情做、时间空闲或不忙。
explanation_english: Indicates having free time, not busy, being at leisure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日好閑，可以幫你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 hou2 haan4, ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天很闲，可以帮你。
examples.english_sentence: I'm free today, I can help you.

mandarin_meaning: 閒情逸致 (xián qíng yì zhì)
english_meaning: leisurely mood and refined tastes; a relaxed, elegant enjoyment of life
explanation_mandarin: 表示閒適悠閒的心情和雅致的情趣，常用來形容有閒暇並享受生活中優雅、恬淡的情調。
explanation_english: Denotes a relaxed, leisurely mood and refined tastes; used to describe enjoying elegant, tranquil pastimes and a leisurely lifestyle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢退休後，過住閑情逸致嘅生活，日日種花同寫字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teoi3 jau1 hau6, gwo3 zyu6 haan4 cing4 jat6 zi3 ge3 sang1 wut6, jat6 jat6 zung3 faa1 tung4 se2 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他退休後，過著閒情逸致的生活，天天種花和寫字。
examples.english_sentence: After he retired, he lives a life of leisure and refined pastimes, planting flowers and practicing calligraphy every day.

mandarin_meaning: 闲 (xián)；有空、空闲；闲散
english_meaning: free; idle; leisure; not busy
explanation_mandarin: 表示有空閒、不忙或閒散，也可指消遣時光或閒談。視語境可為中性（有空、清閒）或帶負面（閒散、不務正業）。常見於詞組如「有閒」「清閒」「閒話」。
explanation_english: Indicates having free time or being idle; can mean leisure or idleness. Depending on context it can be neutral (having spare time) or negative (idle, not industrious). Common in compounds like "有閒" (have free time), "清閒" (leisurely), "閒話" (idle talk).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今晚有冇閒？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 maan5 jau5 mou5 haan4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今晚有空吗？
examples.english_sentence: Do you have free time tonight?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近好閒，成日唔做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 hou2 haan4, sing4 jat6 m4 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近很闲，整天不工作。
examples.english_sentence: He's been very idle recently; he doesn't work all day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日有啲閒時間，可以幫你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jau5 di1 haan4 si4 gaan3, ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天有一些空闲时间，可以帮你。
examples.english_sentence: I have some free time today; I can help you.

mandarin_meaning: 閒事 / 与自己無關或不重要的事情
english_meaning: idle matters; trivial matters; other people's business
explanation_mandarin: 指與自己無關、瑣碎或不值得插手的事情；也常用來說不應干預別人的事。
explanation_english: Refers to matters that are trivial or not one's concern; often used to indicate things one should not meddle in.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好理閒事，專注做好你自己份內嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lei5 haan4 si6, zyun1 zuk6 zou6 hou2 nei5 zi6 gei2 fan6 noi6 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要管閒事，專心做好你自己的本分。
examples.english_sentence: Don't meddle in other people's business; focus on your own responsibilities.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲閒事唔值得你浪費時間理佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 haan4 si6 m4 zik1 dak1 nei5 long6 fai3 si4 gaan3 lei5 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些閒事不值得你浪費時間管它。
examples.english_sentence: These trivial matters aren't worth your time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日插手人哋嘅閒事，搞到大家都唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 caap3 sau2 jan4 dei6 ge3 haan4 si6, gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是插手別人的閒事，弄得大家都不開心。
examples.english_sentence: He always meddles in others' business, making everyone unhappy.

jyutping: haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 deoi1 mok6 kei5
mandarin_meaning: 別管閒事，別湊熱鬧
english_meaning: Mind your own business; don't join the crowd / don't get involved
explanation_mandarin: 一句粵語俗語，用來勸告別人不要多管閒事，也不要湊熱鬧或圍觀別人的爭執或事務。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying used to advise someone to mind their own business and not to join the crowd or get involved in other people's disputes or affairs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 街市度有人吵交，我同你講：閒事莫理，眾埞莫企，唔好插手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaai1 si5 dou6 jau5 jan4 caau2 gaau3, ngo5 tung4 nei5 gong2: haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 deoi1 mok6 kei5, m4 hou2 caap3 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 市場上有人吵架，我跟你說：別管閒事，別湊熱鬧，不要插手。
examples.english_sentence: There was a fight in the market. I told you: mind your own business; don't join the crowd; don't get involved.

jyutping: haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 deng6 mok6 kei5
mandarin_meaning: 別管閒事，也別湊熱鬧。
english_meaning: Mind your own business and don't crowd around (don't meddle or join the commotion).
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來勸人不要干涉別人的事情，也不要去湊熱鬧或站在一旁圍觀以致惹事。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese saying advising people not to interfere in others' affairs and not to join or crowd around a commotion; essentially 'mind your own business and don't be a bystander who causes trouble.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 發生嗰啲事唔關我事，閒事莫理，眾碇莫企啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 sang1 go2 di1 si6 m4 gwaan1 ngo5 si6, haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 deng6 mok6 kei5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 發生那些事跟我沒關係，別管閒事，也別湊熱鬧了。
examples.english_sentence: Those incidents aren't my business — mind your own business and don't crowd around.

jyutping: haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 dei6 mok6 kei5
mandarin_meaning: 別多管閒事，也別圍觀或湊熱鬧（不要干涉別人的事情，也不要站在旁邊圍觀）
english_meaning: Don't meddle in others' business, and don't stand around gawking or crowding the scene.
explanation_mandarin: 一句俗語，用來勸阻別人不要插手或干涉與自己無關的事情，也不要在一旁圍觀或湊熱鬧。
explanation_english: A colloquial admonition telling people not to interfere in matters that don't concern them and not to crowd around or gawk at the situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到隔籬嗌交，唔好湊熱鬧，閒事莫理，眾哋莫企。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 gaak3 lai4 aai3 gaau1, m4 hou2 cau3 jit6 naau6, haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 dei6 mok6 kei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到隔壁吵架，別湊熱鬧，不要多管閒事，也別圍觀。
examples.english_sentence: When you hear the neighbors arguing, don't join the commotion—don't meddle in others' business and don't stand around gawking.

jyutping: haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 ding6 mok6 kei5
mandarin_meaning: 別管閒事，也別圍觀（不要湊熱鬧）
english_meaning: Mind your own business; don't gawk or gather around (don't join the crowd to watch)
explanation_mandarin: 用來提醒別人不要插手他人的事情，也不要圍觀或去湊熱鬧。
explanation_english: A colloquial admonition telling people not to meddle in others' affairs and not to stand around gawking or join the crowd.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 遇到人吵交，閒事莫理，衆碇莫企，唔好去湊熱鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu6 dou3 jan4 caau1 gaau1, haan4 si6 mok6 lei5, zung3 ding6 mok6 kei5, m4 hou2 heoi3 cau3 jit6 naau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 遇到有人吵架，別管閒事，也別圍觀，不要去湊熱鬧。
examples.english_sentence: When you see people arguing, mind your own business and don't stand around gawking; don't join the crowd.

mandarin_meaning: 闲人；局外人；无事可做的人
english_meaning: idle person; outsider/unauthorized person; someone not involved
explanation_mandarin: “閒人”在廣東話中常有兩層含義：一是指沒事可做、閒散的人；二是指與某事無關、非相關人員或未獲授權的人（如告示“閒人勿入”）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, “閒人” has two common senses: (1) an idle or leisure person who has nothing to do; (2) an outsider or unauthorized person not involved in a particular matter (as in signs like “閒人勿入” — no unauthorized persons).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢度係私人地方，閒人勿入。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 hai6 si1 jan4 dei6 fong1, haan4 jan4 mat6 jap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这里是私人地方，闲人勿入。
examples.english_sentence: This is private property; unauthorized persons keep out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係個閒人，成日冇嘢做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 go3 haan4 jan4, seng4 jat6 mou5 je5 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是个闲人，总是没事做。
examples.english_sentence: He's an idle person who always has nothing to do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 開會嘅時候，閒人唔好留低。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoi1 wui6 ge3 si4 hau6, haan4 jan4 m4 hou2 lau4 dai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 开会的时候，闲人不要留下。
examples.english_sentence: During the meeting, non-participants should not stay behind.

mandarin_meaning: 闲聊；聊闲天
english_meaning: chit‑chat; idle talk; small talk
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指沒有重要內容的閒聊或打發時間的聊天。可作名詞或動詞，常說「講閒偈」。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese term for casual, idle talk or chit‑chat. Can be used as a noun or verb; commonly appears in the phrase "gong3 haan4 gai3" (講閒偈) meaning "to chat/idly talk".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋唔好講啲閒偈，快啲做工啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 m4 hou2 gong2 di1 haan4 gai3, faai3 di1 zou6 gung1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们别说闲话了，赶快工作吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's not chit‑chat — get back to work quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等人嘅時候我成日會同朋友講啲閒偈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 jan4 ge3 si4 hau6 ngo5 seng4 jat6 wui5 tung4 pang4 jau5 gong2 di1 haan4 gai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等人的时候我经常和朋友闲聊。
examples.english_sentence: When I'm waiting for someone I often chat idly with friends.

mandarin_meaning: 闲聊；说闲话、议论他人
english_meaning: idle talk; chit-chat; gossip
explanation_mandarin: 「閒口」是廣東話的口語，指無事閒聊或說別人的閒言閒語、八卦、議論他人。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term meaning idle talk or gossip — chatting about trivial matters or talking about others behind their backs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日閒口人，講實事啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 haan4 hau2 jan4, gong2 sat6 si6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要总是说别人的闲话，说实事吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always gossip about people; talk about the facts.

mandarin_meaning: 閒事；無聊的事或話；瑣碎、不重要的事情（口語）
english_meaning: idle stuff; trivial matters; nonsense; small talk (informal)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用詞，通常指無關緊要的瑣事、閒聊的話題或廢話，有時帶輕視或不耐煩的語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term for trivial matters, idle chit-chat, or nonsense. Often used informally and can carry a dismissive or annoyed tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好理閒嘢，專心做你份工啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lei5 haan4 je5, zyun1 sam1 zou6 nei5 fan6 gung1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別管閒事，專心做你的工作。
examples.english_sentence: Don't mind idle stuff; focus on your work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日講啲閒嘢，講到我都煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 gong2 di1 haan4 je5, gong2 dou3 ngo5 dou1 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是說些無聊的話，說得我都煩。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks nonsense; it gets on my nerves.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚冇嘢做，出去行下街，傾下閒嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 mou5 je5 zou6, heoi3 gaai1 haang4 haa5 gaai1, king1 haa5 haan4 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚沒事做，出去逛逛，聊聊天吧。
examples.english_sentence: Nothing to do tonight — let's go out and have a bit of small talk.

mandarin_meaning: （自稱）在下；我（帶有自謙或戲謔語氣的第一人稱）
english_meaning: I / me (a self-deprecating or joking first-person pronoun)
explanation_mandarin: 「閒家」是廣東話口語或戲曲語境中用作自稱的詞，帶有自謙、戲謔或幽默的語氣。
explanation_english: “閒家” is a Cantonese self-reference used as a first-person pronoun, often with a self-deprecating, humorous, or theatrical tone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 閒家今日唔方便出席。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haan4 gaa1 gam1 jat6 m4 fong1 bin6 ceot1 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天不方便出席。
examples.english_sentence: I'm not able to attend today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 閒家講句笑啫，唔好太認真。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haan4 gaa1 gong2 geoi3 siu3 ze1, m4 hou2 taai3 jing6 zan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我只是在開玩笑，別太認真。
examples.english_sentence: I'm just joking, don't take it too seriously.

mandarin_meaning: 閒暇的情致；悠閒的心情
english_meaning: leisurely mood; idle mood; a taste for leisure
explanation_mandarin: 指閒暇時的情緒或興致，常用於描寫有閒適、悠閒心情的狀態（如「閒情逸致」）。
explanation_english: Refers to a mood or disposition for leisure—an inclination toward relaxation or leisurely pursuits (often seen in compounds like "閒情逸致").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家有啲閒情，想同你去茶樓飲下午茶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 jau5 di1 haan4 cing4, soeng2 tung4 nei5 heoi3 caa4 lau4 jam2 haa6 ng5 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在有點閒情，想和你去茶樓喝下午茶。
examples.english_sentence: I have a bit of leisure right now and want to go to a teahouse for afternoon tea with you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 週末終於有啲閒情逸致，可以畫畫同寫字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zau1 mut6 zung1 jyu4 jau5 di1 haan4 cing4 jat6 zi3, ho2 ji5 waak6 waak6 tung4 se2 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 週末終於有些閒情逸致，可以畫畫和寫字。
examples.english_sentence: Finally this weekend I have some leisure and can paint and write.

mandarin_meaning: 閒情逸致（xián qíng yì zhì）：閒適的情趣與雅致的情懷，指悠閒賞玩的心境和雅興。
english_meaning: A leisurely and refined mood; the tasteful enjoyment of leisure and elegant pastimes.
explanation_mandarin: 形容人因閒適而產生的雅致興趣或閒適情懷，常用以描述悠閒自在、追求雅趣的生活態度。
explanation_english: Describes a relaxed, refined mood or taste for elegant leisure activities; used to depict a leisurely, cultivated attitude toward life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 周末我想去郊外，享受一下閒情逸致。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zau1 mut6 ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 gaau1 ngoi6, hoeng2 sau6 jat1 haa5 haan4 cing4 jat6 zi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 週末我想去郊外，享受一下閒情逸致。
examples.english_sentence: This weekend I want to go to the countryside to enjoy a bit of leisurely refinement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 讀詩、飲茶，真係有閒情逸致。
examples.jyutping_sentence: duk6 si1 jam2 caa4, zan1 hai6 jau5 haan4 cing4 jat6 zi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 讀詩、喝茶，真有閒情逸致。
examples.english_sentence: Reading poetry and drinking tea really has a leisurely, refined charm.

mandarin_meaning: 平日；平常的日子（非假期或非特別節日）
english_meaning: ordinary day; on a normal day (non-holiday / weekdays)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，表示平常的日子，通常指非假期或非特別節日的日子，相當於普通話的「平日／平常日」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning ordinary days, usually referring to non-holidays or non-special occasions — roughly equivalent to 'on weekdays' or 'on a normal day.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 閒日我通常朝早九點返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haan4 jat6 ngo5 tung1 soeng4 ziu1 zou2 gau2 dim2 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 平日我通常早上九点上班。
examples.english_sentence: On normal days I usually go to work at 9 AM.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳閒日人流較少，週末就好多人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 haan4 jat6 jan4 lau4 gaau3 siu2, zau1 mut6 zau6 hou2 do1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间餐厅平日人流较少，周末就很多人。
examples.english_sentence: This restaurant has fewer people on ordinary days; it's very crowded on weekends.

mandarin_meaning: 闲暇时；有空的时候
english_meaning: in one's spare time; when free; occasionally
explanation_mandarin: 表示在有空闲的时候或业余时间做某事，可作时间状语使用。
explanation_english: Indicates doing something during one's free time or spare moments; used as an adverbial time expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 閒時我會去跑步。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haan4 si4 ngo5 wui5 heoi3 paau2 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 闲暇时我会去跑步。
examples.english_sentence: I go running in my spare time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果閒時有時間，記得打電話俾我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 haan4 si4 jau5 si4 gaan3, gei3 dak1 daa2 din6 waa2 bei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果有空的话，记得打电话给我。
examples.english_sentence: If you're free sometime, remember to call me.

cantonese: 閒時無燒香，急時抱佛腳
jyutping: haan4 si4 mou4 siu1 hoeng1, gap1 si4 bou2 fat6 goek3
mandarin_meaning: 平時不做準備，到了緊要時刻才匆忙應付（臨時抱佛腳）
english_meaning: Only take action at the last minute; scramble or seek help when in trouble instead of preparing in advance (to cram or do a last-minute fix)
explanation_mandarin: 形容平常不注意準備或不採取行動，到了緊要關頭才匆忙應付或求助，帶有責備拖延和臨時抱佛腳的含義。
explanation_english: Describes someone who doesn't prepare when there's time but scrambles to act or seek help at the last minute; conveys procrastination and last-minute cramming.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢平時唔溫書，成日閒時無燒香，考試嚟到先急時抱佛腳，成績當然唔好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ping4 si4 m4 wan1 syu1, sing4 jat6 haan4 si4 mou4 siu1 hoeng1, haau2 si3 lai4 dou3 sin1 gap1 si4 bou2 fat6 goek3, sing4 zik1 dong1 jin4 m4 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他平時不複習，總是到考試才臨時抱佛腳，成績當然不好。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't study regularly; he always waits until exams to cram at the last minute, so his grades are obviously poor.

mandarin_meaning: 閒暇（xiánxiá）：空閒的時間，休息或從事閒適活動的時間。
english_meaning: leisure; spare time; free time
explanation_mandarin: 指可以自由支配、不受工作或事務牽制的時間，常用於書面或較正式語境。
explanation_english: Refers to time that is free from work or obligations, available for rest or leisure activities; often used in formal or written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 閒暇嘅時候，我鍾意睇書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haan4 haa6 ge3 si4 hau6, ngo5 zung1 ji3 tai2 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 閒暇的時候，我喜歡看書。
examples.english_sentence: In my spare time, I like to read books.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你有閒暇，記得打電話畀我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 jau5 haan4 haa6, gei3 dak1 daa2 din6 waa2 bei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你有閒暇，記得打電話給我。
examples.english_sentence: If you have free time, remember to call me.

mandarin_meaning: 有空；閒暇
english_meaning: to be free; to have spare time; idle
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞 / 名詞（口語俚語）
explanation_mandarin: 「閒科」是香港粵語口語或俚語，用來表示有空、沒事可做或閒暇的狀態。常出現在日常對話中，語氣偏口語化。
explanation_english: “閒科” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang used to indicate being free or having spare time — an idle or unoccupied state. It appears in casual spoken contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我呢排幾閒科，有時間可以幫你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ni1 paai4 gei2 haan4 fo1, jau5 si4 gaan3 ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我最近比較閒，有時間可以幫你。
examples.english_sentence: I'm quite free lately; I can help you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司今期新project多到，大家都唔閒科。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gam1 kei4 san1 project do1 dou3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 haan4 fo1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司這期新項目很多，大家都沒空。
examples.english_sentence: The company has so many new projects this term that nobody is free.

mandarin_meaning: 闲置 (xiánzhì)
english_meaning: to leave unused; to be idle; unused/idle
explanation_mandarin: 表示把物品、設備或資源放著不用或處於閒置、未被利用的狀態。
explanation_english: To leave an item, equipment, or resource unused; to be in an idle or unutilized state.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部舊電話已經閒置咗好耐，唔知點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 gau6 din6 waa2 ji5 ging1 haan4 zi6 zo2 hou2 noi6, m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这部旧手机已经闲置了很久，不知道怎么办好。
examples.english_sentence: This old phone has been left unused for a long time; I don't know what to do with it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司啲設備閒置咗，浪費咗資源。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 di1 se3 bei6 haan4 zi6 zo2, long6 fai3 zo2 zi1 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司的设备闲置了，浪费了资源。
examples.english_sentence: The company's equipment is idle, wasting resources.

mandarin_meaning: 闲聊 / 聊天
english_meaning: to chat casually; small talk; idle chat
explanation_mandarin: 指随意、轻松地谈话，通常是不涉及重要或严肃话题的闲谈。
explanation_english: To converse casually about light or unimportant topics; informal chatting or small talk.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋成日見面都係閒聊啫，唔會講啲正經事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 seng4 jat6 gin3 min6 dou1 hai6 haan4 liu4 ze1, m4 wui5 gong2 di1 zing3 ging1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们常常见面只是闲聊，不会谈正经事。
examples.english_sentence: We often meet just to chat; we don't talk about anything serious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 等佢閒聊完先啦，我要返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dang2 keoi5 haan4 liu4 jyun4 sin1 laa1, ngo5 jiu3 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等他们聊完先吧，我要去上班。
examples.english_sentence: Wait until they finish chatting — I have to go to work.

mandarin_meaning: 闲言闲语 / 流言蜚语（指无根据的闲聊、传闻或议论）
english_meaning: idle talk; gossip; rumors
explanation_mandarin: 指沒有實際根據、無關緊要或帶有誹謗性的閒聊與傳聞，常用來形容流言或小道消息。
explanation_english: Refers to idle talk, gossip, or rumors—often baseless or trivial remarks that can harm reputations or create misunderstandings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好理會閒言閒語，專心做好你份工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lei5 wui6 haan4 jin4 haan4 jyu5, zyun1 sam1 zou6 hou2 nei5 fan6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要理会闲言闲语，专心做好你的工作。
examples.english_sentence: Don't pay attention to gossip; focus on doing your job well.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司入面滿街閒言閒語，影響咗團隊士氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jap6 min6 mun5 gaai1 haan4 jin4 haan4 jyu5, jing2 hoeng2 zo2 tyun4 deoi2 si6 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司里面到处都是闲言闲语，影响了团队士气。
examples.english_sentence: The company is full of gossip, which has affected team morale.

mandarin_meaning: 闲聊；聊天；打发时间
english_meaning: to chat idly; to chit-chat; (sometimes) to gossip
explanation_mandarin: 在粤语中，“閒計”表示随意聊天、闲聊或打发时间，有时含有八卦或谈论别人私事的意味。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '閒計' means to chat idly or chit-chat to pass the time; it can sometimes imply gossiping about others' private matters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚出嚟飲茶，閒計下啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ceot1 lai4 jam2 caa4, haan4 gai3 haa5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚出來喝茶，閒聊一下吧。
examples.english_sentence: Come out for yum cha tonight — let's chat for a bit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日同人閒計，講啲無謂嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 tung4 jan4 haan4 gai3, gong2 di1 mou4 wai6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是跟人閒聊，說些無關緊要的事。
examples.english_sentence: He always chats with people, talking about trivial things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺度閒計人哋嘅私隱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 haan4 gai3 jan4 dei6 ge3 si1 jan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要在這裡閒聊別人的私事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't gossip about other people's private affairs here.

mandarin_meaning: 閒聊；閒言碎語；（有時指閒職或閒言閒語而引起的流言、批評）
english_meaning: idle talk; chit-chat; gossip
explanation_mandarin: 表示閒暇時言談的內容，通常指無關緊要的聊天或流言閒話，有時帶有負面含義（例如誤傳或批評）。
explanation_english: Refers to casual or idle talk—light conversation, chit-chat, or gossip. Can also imply rumor or petty criticism in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日講閒話，會傷害人架。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 gong2 haan4 waa6, wui5 soeng1 hoi6 jan4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要老是說閒話，會傷害到別人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't gossip all the time; it can hurt people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚一齊出嚟飲嘢，傾下閒話放鬆吓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jat1 cai4 ceot1 lai4 jam2 je5, king1 haa5 haan4 waa6 fong3 sung1 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚一起出來喝一杯，聊聊天放鬆一下。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go out for a drink tonight and chat to relax.

mandarin_meaning: 閒聊、聊家常
english_meaning: to chat casually about everyday/family matters; small talk
explanation_mandarin: 指與親友或熟人閒談日常瑣事、家長里短，通常沒有重要目的，主要是聯絡感情或消磨時間。
explanation_english: Refers to casually chatting with friends or family about everyday matters or family affairs—small talk used to keep in touch or pass the time, not for serious purposes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去你屋企坐吓，閒話家常啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 nei5 uk1 kei5 co5 haa5, haan4 waa6 gaa1 soeng4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去你家坐坐，聊聊家常吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to your place tonight and have a casual chat about everyday matters.

mandarin_meaning: 閒談；閒聊 (xián tán / xián liáo)
english_meaning: chat; casual talk; idle conversation
explanation_mandarin: 表示輕鬆、非正式的談話，通常是閒暇時的聊天，內容多為日常瑣事或閒聊，不涉及重要或正式議題。
explanation_english: Refers to relaxed, informal conversation—casual chatting or idle talk, usually about everyday matters and not important or formal topics.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋啱啱喺街市閒談咗幾句，冇講乜嘢重要嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ngaam1 ngaam1 hai2 gaai1 si5 haan4 taam4 zo2 gei2 geoi3, mou5 gong2 mat1 je5 zung6 jiu3 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們剛剛在菜市場閒談了幾句，沒講什麼重要的事。
examples.english_sentence: We just had a few casual words at the market and didn't talk about anything important.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好鍾意同長者閒談，聽佢哋講以前嘅故事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 zung1 ji3 tung4 coeng4 ze2 haan4 taam4, teng1 keoi5 dei6 gong2 ji5 cin4 ge3 gu3 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很喜歡和長者閒談，聽他們講以前的故事。
examples.english_sentence: He likes chatting with the elderly and listening to them tell stories from the past.

mandarin_meaning: 比立秋還要閒；形容非常閒、沒事可做（常用於形容人或生意非常清閒）
english_meaning: Extremely idle; having nothing to do; very slack (often used to describe a person or business being dead quiet)
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，字面意為比二十四節氣的「立秋」還閒，表示非常清閒或無事可做，也可用來形容生意冷清、沒人光顧。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally meaning "more idle than the start of autumn." It describes being extremely free or having nothing to do, and can also describe very slow or quiet business.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢排生意咁差，閒過立秋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 paai4 saang1 ji3 gam2 caa1, haan4 gwo3 lap6 cau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近生意這麼差，閒得像立秋一樣（非常冷清）。
examples.english_sentence: Business has been terrible lately — it's dead (completely quiet).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日都閒過立秋，唔好咁浪費時間啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sing4 jat6 dou1 haan4 gwo3 lap6 cau1, m4 hou2 long6 fai3 si4 gaan3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你整天都閒得像立秋一樣，別這麼浪費時間了。
examples.english_sentence: You're idle all the time; don't waste your time like that.

mandarin_meaning: 閒適（悠閒、舒適）
english_meaning: leisurely; relaxed; comfortable; at ease
explanation_mandarin: 表示一種悠閒、舒適、不急不忙、身心放鬆的狀態或感覺。
explanation_english: Indicates a leisurely, comfortable, unhurried state or feeling — being relaxed and at ease.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日天氣咁好，喺公園散步感覺好閒適。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 tin1 hei3 gam2 hou2, hai2 gung1 jyun2 saan3 bou6 gam2 gok3 hou2 haan4 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天天气这么好，在公园散步感觉很悠闲、很舒适。
examples.english_sentence: The weather is so nice today; walking in the park feels very relaxed and comfortable.

mandarin_meaning: 閒錢（xiánqián）－可自由支配的零用或多餘的錢
english_meaning: spare money; extra cash; disposable income (small-scale)
explanation_mandarin: 指暫時不用、可自由支配的錢，通常用來消費、休閒或作小額開支，而非用於必要生活費或長期投資。
explanation_english: Refers to money that is temporarily unused and available for discretionary spending—small extra cash used for treats, leisure, or minor expenses, not essential bills or long-term investments.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家冇乜閒錢，要等下個人工先得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 mou5 mat1 haan4 cin2, jiu3 dang2 haa6 go3 jan4 gung1 sin1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在沒什麼閒錢，要等下次發薪才行。
examples.english_sentence: I don't have much spare money right now; I have to wait until the next paycheck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果有閒錢，我想去旅行幾日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 jau5 haan4 cin2, ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 leoi5 hang4 gei2 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果有閒錢，我想去旅行幾天。
examples.english_sentence: If I have spare cash, I'd like to travel for a few days.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家有冇閒錢，可唔可以借我一千蚊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 jau5 mou5 haan4 cin2, ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 ze3 ngo5 jat1 cin1 man1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你現在有沒有閒錢，可以借我一千塊嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Do you have any spare money now? Can you lend me a thousand dollars?

mandarin_meaning: 悠閒地；輕鬆地；閒散地
english_meaning: leisurely; idly; casually; in a relaxed manner
explanation_mandarin: 「閒閒哋」是粵語口語用法，表示做事或狀態很悠閒、不著緊或隨意地進行。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese adverb meaning to do something in a relaxed, leisurely, or casual way; indicating idleness or lack of urgency.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日閒閒哋，唔使做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 haan4 haan4 dei6, m4 sai2 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天很悠閒，不用做事。
examples.english_sentence: I'm free today; I don't need to work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢閒閒哋行過嚟同我傾偈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haan4 haan4 dei6 haang4 gwo3 lei4 tung4 ngo5 king1 gai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他悠閒地走過來跟我聊天。
examples.english_sentence: He came over leisurely to chat with me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你閒閒哋有冇時間幫我？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 haan4 haan4 dei6 jau5 mou5 si4 gaan3 bong1 ngo5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有空的時候有沒有時間幫我？
examples.english_sentence: Could you help me when you have some free time?

mandarin_meaning: 悠閒地；不忙地；（口語）輕易地
english_meaning: leisurely; idly; casually; (colloquial) easily
explanation_mandarin: 閒閒地是廣東話口語的副詞，表示悠閒、不忙或輕鬆地；有時也用來表示輕而易舉、隨意地。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial adverb meaning to do something leisurely, idly, or at ease; sometimes used to mean doing something easily or without effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁急，閒閒地做啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 gap1, haan4 haan4 dei6 zou6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要那麼急，慢慢做吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so hurried; take your time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日閒閒地，想去行街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 haan4 haan4 dei6, soeng2 heoi3 hang4 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天有空，想去逛街。
examples.english_sentence: I'm free today and want to go shopping.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢閒閒地就拎到第一名。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haan4 haan4 dei6 zau6 ling1 dou3 dai6 jat1 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他輕鬆地就拿到第一名。
examples.english_sentence: He easily got first place.

mandarin_meaning: 闲杂（的）：闲散、无关或杂乱的；常用于“闲杂人等”，指无关或不相干的人员/访客。
english_meaning: idle/miscellaneous; unrelated or unauthorized (people) — often used in phrases like '閒雜人等' to mean miscellaneous or unauthorized persons/visitors.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞（常見於名詞短語，如「閒雜人等」）
partOfSpeech_english: adjective (often used in noun phrases, e.g. '閒雜人等')
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容閒散、無關或雜亂的人或事，常見用法為「閒雜人等」，表示無關或不該出入的人員。
