explanation_english: The glide or medial element that occurs between an initial consonant and the main vowel of a syllable (e.g. /j/, /w/). In Cantonese phonology, '韻頭' describes the medial component or the head of the rime.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學音韻學嘅時候，我哋要分辨每個音節嘅韻頭同韻母。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 jam1wan6 hok6 ge3 si4hou6, ngo5dei6 jiu3 fan1bin6 mui5 go3 jam1zit3 ge3 wan6tau4 tung4 wan6mou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 学音韵学的时候，我们要分辨每个音节的韵头和韵母。
examples.english_sentence: When studying phonology, we need to distinguish the medial (rhyme head) and the rime (final) of each syllable.

mandarin_meaning: 响；（表示发出声音）/ 在；对……来说（方言用法）
english_meaning: to ring / to make a sound; at/in; as for (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: “響”在粤语中有多种用法：常作动词表示发出声音（如電話響），也可作介词表示地点或用于表述观点（相当于普通话的“在/就……而言”）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '響' has multiple uses: commonly a verb meaning 'to ring' or 'to make a sound', and also a colloquial preposition meaning 'at/in' or a discourse marker 'as for'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 電話響咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: din6 waa2 hoeng2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 电话响了。
examples.english_sentence: The phone rang.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我響屋企等你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hoeng2 uk1 kei2 dang2 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在家等你。
examples.english_sentence: I'll wait for you at home.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 響我嚟講，呢個選擇最好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng2 ngo5 lai4 gong2, ni1 go3 syun2 zaak6 zeoi3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 就我而言，这个选择最好。
examples.english_sentence: As for me, this option is the best.

mandarin_meaning: 响亮
english_meaning: loud and clear; resonant; sonorous
explanation_mandarin: 形容聲音大而清晰、有穿透力；也可引申為名聲顯著、有氣勢。
explanation_english: Describes a sound that is loud, clear, and resonant; can also be used figuratively to mean prominent or impressive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個聲音好響亮，成個戲院都聽到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 seng1 jam1 hou2 hoeng2 loeng6, seng4 go3 hei3 jyun2 dou1 teng1 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的声音很响亮，整个戏院都能听到。
examples.english_sentence: His voice is very loud and clear; the whole theater could hear it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢首歌嘅合唱部分好響亮，好有氣勢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 sau2 go1 ge3 hap6 coeng3 bou6 fan6 hou2 hoeng2 loeng6, hou2 jau5 hei3 si3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这首歌的合唱部分很响亮，很有气势。
examples.english_sentence: The chorus of this song is loud and resonant and very powerful.

mandarin_meaning: 愛頂嘴/健談（口語）
english_meaning: mouthy; glib; quick to talk back (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「響口」是廣東話口語，形容一個人愛回嘴、好說話或愛誇張吹噓，有時帶負面（愛頂嘴、愛爭辯），有時可指能言善道（健談）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term describing someone who is mouthy or glib — quick to talk back, boast, or argue. It can be negative (talks back a lot) or neutral/positive (eloquent, good with words) depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日響口，成日頂嘴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 hoeng2 hau2, sing4 jat6 ding2 zeoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天愛頂嘴，總是回嘴。
examples.english_sentence: He's always mouthy and always talks back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好響口講大話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hoeng2 hau2 gong2 daai6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要隨便說大話。
examples.english_sentence: Don't brag / Don't boast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好響口，做銷售好啱佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 hoeng2 hau2, zou6 siu1 sau6 hou2 aam1 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很會說話，做銷售很適合他。
examples.english_sentence: He's very glib; good for sales.

mandarin_meaning: 不明（可能是罕見字、古字或打字錯誤）
english_meaning: Unknown (possibly a rare/archaic term or a typo)
explanation_mandarin: 「響咹」並非現代粵語常見詞彙，常見粵語詞典中沒有收錄。很可能是印刷或輸入時的錯別字，或是舊書、方言、個別俗寫的遺存。可能意指與「響」有關的表達（例如「響咧／響吖」）的變體，但未能確認具體讀音與用法。
explanation_english: “響咹” is not attested in common modern Cantonese dictionaries. It may be a typo, a rare/archaic character, or a nonstandard variant (for example of expressions like “響咧”/“響吖”). The precise pronunciation and usage are not verifiable from standard sources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺舊書上見到「響咹」，但唔確定係咪打錯字或舊寫法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 gau6 syu1 soeng6 gin3 dou2 「響咹」, daan6 m4 kok3 ding6 hai6 mai6 daa2 co3 zi6 wok6 gau6 se2 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在舊書上看到「響咹」，但不確定是不是打錯字或舊寫法。
examples.english_sentence: I saw “響咹” in an old book, but I'm not sure if it's a typo or an archaic spelling.

synonyms: 可能為「響咧/響吖」的變體

mandarin_meaning: 响当当 (xiǎng dāng dāng)，指有名氣、有分量、令人印象深刻或權威的重要人物/事物
english_meaning: impressive; prestigious; well-known and weighty; having high reputation or authority
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，形容某人或某事有分量、很出名或顯得非常重要、令人敬重或引人注目。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing a person or thing that is prominent, prestigious, or carries a lot of weight and reputation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係一個響噹噹嘅律師，案件多、口碑好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jat1 go3 hoeng2 dang1 dang1 ge3 leot6 si1, on3 gin6 do1, hau2 bei1 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是一個響當當的律師，案子多，口碑好。
examples.english_sentence: He is a prominent lawyer — he has many cases and a strong reputation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋公司啱啱攞咗個響噹噹嘅獎項，媒體都報導晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 gung1 si1 ngaam1 ngaam1 lo2 zo2 go3 hoeng2 dang1 dang1 ge3 zoeng2 hong6, mui4 tai2 dou1 bou3 dou6 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們公司剛剛拿到了一個響當當的獎項，媒體都報導了。
examples.english_sentence: Their company just won a prestigious award and the media covered it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係學界好響噹噹嘅教授，學生爭相報讀佢嘅課程。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 hok6 gaai3 hou2 hoeng2 dang1 dang1 ge3 gaau3 sau6, hok6 saang1 zang1 soeng1 bou3 duk6 keoi5 ge3 fo3 cing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是學界很響當當的教授，學生爭相報讀他的課程。
examples.english_sentence: He's a highly respected professor in academia; students rush to enroll in his courses.

mandarin_meaning: （罕用）字面可解為“響（聲音/在）+ 安（安寧/安全）”，並無固定常用詞義，偶爾可能作地名或人名出現。
english_meaning: (rare/nonstandard) Literally '響 (sound/at) + 安 (peace/safe)'. No established common usage; may appear as a place-name or personal/name transliteration.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 短語（罕用／可能作專有名詞）
explanation_mandarin: 「響安」並非日常口語中常見的固定詞語。單字「響」在粵語可作動詞（發聲）或介詞（響 = 在），「安」常作形容詞或名詞表示平安、安穩。組合起來沒有廣泛固定的語義，更多時候見於地名或人名的音譯，或是個別文本的特殊用法。
explanation_english: "響安" is not a commonly used set phrase in Cantonese. The character "響" can mean 'to sound' or function as a locative preposition ('at'), and "安" means 'peace/safety'. The combination has no widely established meaning and is most likely encountered as a toponym or a name transliteration, or in isolated/rare uses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講山上有個地方叫響安。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 saan1 soeng6 jau5 go3 dei6 fong1 giu3 hoeng2 on1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽說山上有個地方叫「響安」。
examples.english_sentence: I heard there's a place called '響安' on the mountain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個詞好罕見，平時唔會用響安嚟表達意思。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 ci4 hou2 hon2 gin3, ping4 si4 m4 wui5 jung6 hoeng2 on1 lai4 biu2 daat6 ji3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個詞很罕見，平時不會用「響安」來表達意思。
examples.english_sentence: This term is rare; '響安' is not normally used to convey meaning.

mandarin_meaning: 响尾蛇 (一种有尾铃的毒蛇，常指响尾属的蛇)
english_meaning: rattlesnake (a venomous snake with a rattle on its tail)
explanation_mandarin: 響尾蛇指的是有尾鈴的毒蛇，屬於響尾屬（如響尾蝮屬或環尾蝮等）的蛇類。除字面意思外，有時也會被比喻用來形容平時沉默、在關鍵時刻發動或具威脅性的人或事。
explanation_english: A rattlesnake is a venomous snake characterized by a rattle at the tip of its tail (genus Crotalus and related). Besides the literal meaning, it is sometimes used metaphorically to describe someone or something that is normally quiet but strikes suddenly or is threatening.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺山度見到一條響尾蛇，嚇親我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 saan1 dou6 gin3 dou3 jat1 tiu4 hoeng2 mei5 se4, haak3 can1 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在山上看到一條响尾蛇，把我嚇到了。
examples.english_sentence: I saw a rattlesnake on the mountain and it scared me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做事好似響尾蛇，平時冇聲，到要出手時就好猛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 si6 hou2 ci5 hoeng2 mei5 se4, ping4 si4 mou5 seng1, dou3 jiu3 ceot1 sau2 si4 zau6 hou2 mang5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事像響尾蛇，平時沒聲，到要出手時卻很猛。
examples.english_sentence: He works like a rattlesnake — usually quiet, but when he strikes he's fierce.

mandarin_meaning: 在那里；响度（声音的大小/响亮程度）
english_meaning: there; loudness (perceived sound level)
explanation_mandarin: 「響度」在香港粵語中有兩個常見用法：一是口語副詞，表示「在那裡／那邊」（例：我響度），二是技術或日常用語中的名詞，指聲音的響度或音量（例：響度太高）。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, "響度" has two common uses: as a colloquial adverb meaning "there/over there" (e.g., 我響度), and as a noun referring to loudness or volume (the perceived level of sound).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家響度做咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 hoeng2 dou6 zou6 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你现在在那里做什么？
examples.english_sentence: What are you doing over there now?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢首歌嘅響度太高，整到耳仔痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 sau2 go1 ge3 hoeng2 dou6 taai3 gou1, zing2 dou3 ji5 zai2 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这首歌的响度太高，把耳朵弄痛了。
examples.english_sentence: The loudness of this song is too high; it's making my ears hurt.

mandarin_meaning: 响彻云霄 (xiǎngchè yúnxiāo)：声音极为响亮、传得很远；引申指名声或影响极大、遍及各处。
english_meaning: To resound through the skies; to ring out loudly and far. Figuratively, to describe a reputation or influence that spreads widely.
explanation_mandarin: 表示聲音非常響亮、能傳得很遠；也可用來形容聲譽或影響力極大、廣為人知。常用於書面或成語式表達。
explanation_english: Indicates an extremely loud sound that carries a great distance; metaphorically, it describes a reputation or influence that is widespread. Often used in literary or idiomatic contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅歌聲響徹雲霄，全場都靜晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 go1 sing1 hoeng2 cit3 wan4 siu1, cyun4 coeng4 dou1 zing6 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的歌声响彻云霄，全场都安静了。
examples.english_sentence: His singing resounded through the venue; the entire audience fell silent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰部電影大賣，導演嘅聲名響徹雲霄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 bou6 din6 jing2 daai6 maai6, dou6 jin2 ge3 sing1 ming4 hoeng2 cit3 wan4 siu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那部电影大卖，导演的声名响彻云霄。
examples.english_sentence: The film was a huge hit, and the director's fame spread far and wide.

mandarin_meaning: 响应该、回应、响应号召或采取行动（xiǎngyìng）
english_meaning: to respond; to echo or answer a call/appeal; to take action in response
explanation_mandarin: 表示對號召、呼籲或請求作出回應或參與相關活動，常用於響應活動或號召。
explanation_english: Indicates responding to a call, appeal, or request—often by participating in or supporting an initiative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 好多市民都響應政府嘅號召，出嚟捐血。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hou2 do1 si5 man4 dou1 hoeng2 jing3 zing3 fu2 ge3 hou6 ziu3, ceot1 lai4 gyun1 hyut3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 很多市民響應政府的號召，出來獻血。
examples.english_sentence: Many citizens responded to the government's call and came forward to donate blood.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司響應員工提出嘅建議，調整咗工作時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 hoeng2 jing3 jyun4 gung1 tai1 ceot1 ge3 gin3 ji5, tiu4 zing2 zo2 gung1 zok3 si4 gaan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司響應員工提出的建議，調整了工作時間。
examples.english_sentence: The company responded to employees' suggestions and adjusted working hours.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我想響應星期日嘅清潔活動，你一齊嚟唔嚟？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 hoeng2 jing3 sing1 kei4 jat6 ge3 cing1 git6 wut6 dung6, nei5 jat1 cai4 lai4 m4 lai4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想響應星期日的清潔活動，你要一起來嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I want to join the Sunday cleanup event. Will you come along?

mandarin_meaning: （口語）发出很大的声响；很吵（罕见、俗语）
english_meaning: (colloq.) to make a loud noise; very noisy (rare/slang)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞/形容詞（口語、罕見用法）
explanation_mandarin: 「響朵」為廣東話口語、較罕見的用法，常用來形容某物或聲音很響、響個不停。此詞在不同地區可能較少見或被其他更常用的詞（如「響」、「嘈」、「響亮」）取代。
explanation_english: "響朵" is a colloquial and relatively rare Cantonese expression used to describe something that makes a loud or persistent noise. It may be regionally uncommon and often replaced by more common words like "響" (make noise) or "noisy".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 條喇叭成日響朵，好嘈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tiu4 laa1 baa1 sing4 jat6 hoeng2 do2, hou2 cou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 喇叭總是很響，很吵。
examples.english_sentence: The speaker keeps making a loud noise; it's very noisy.

mandarin_meaning: 未見於常用粵語詞彙，可能為錯字或圈子內的少數用語
english_meaning: Unattested/unknown in common Cantonese; possibly a typo or niche slang used within a particular group
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 未確定（可能為俗語/俚語）
explanation_mandarin: 逐字來看「響」有發聲、響應之意，「流」與「朵」合在一起無明確語義。這個片語未在主流粵語詞典或常見語料中出現，可能是打字錯誤、口語變體或某個小圈子的內部用語，建議確認上下文或出處。
explanation_english: Literally the characters read as 'sound/echo' (響) + 'flow' (流) + 'flower petal' (朵), which do not form a coherent, attested Cantonese phrase. The term does not appear in mainstream Cantonese dictionaries or corpora and may be a typo, a spoken variant, or niche in-group slang. Check the original context or source for clarification.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺字典搵唔到「響流朵」，估計係打錯字或者係某啲圈子嘅用語。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 zi6 din2 wan2 m4 dou3 "hoeng2 lau4 do2", gu2 gai3 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6 waak6 ze2 hai6 mau5 di1 hyun1 zi2 ge3 jung6 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在字典裡找不到「響流朵」，估計是打錯字或某些圈子的用語。
examples.english_sentence: I can't find '響流朵' in the dictionary; it's probably a typo or slang used within a particular circle.

mandarin_meaning: 響聲的來源 / 聲源
english_meaning: the source of a sound; where a noise comes from
explanation_mandarin: 指發出聲音的地方或聲音來源，口語中常用來問或描述噪音、聲響來自哪裡。
explanation_english: Refers to the place or origin of a sound; commonly used in colloquial speech to ask or describe where a noise is coming from.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我聽到樓下有啲嘈吵，但唔知道響處係邊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 teng1 dou3 lau4 haa6 jau5 di1 cou4 caau2, daan6 m4 zi1 dou6 hoeng2 cyu3 hai6 bin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我听到楼下有些吵闹，但不知道响处在哪里。
examples.english_sentence: I heard some noise downstairs, but I don't know where the sound is coming from.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個響處好大聲，嚇親我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 hoeng2 cyu3 hou2 daai6 sing1, haak3 can1 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那个响处声音很大，把我吓到了。
examples.english_sentence: That source of the noise was very loud; it scared me.

mandarin_meaning: 響螺（海螺、可作號角的螺殼）
english_meaning: conch (a spiral sea shell, often used as a horn/trumpet)
explanation_mandarin: 響螺指帶螺旋殼的海洋貝類，也特指可作吹奏號角的海螺。在傳統儀式、祭祀或宗教場合常用來發聲或號召。
explanation_english: 響螺 refers to a spiral sea shell (conch), particularly one used as a horn. It is commonly used as a loud signaling instrument in traditional ceremonies, rituals, or religious contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺廟裏，師父用響螺吹號，個聲好洪亮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 miu6 leoi5, si1 fu6 jung6 hoeng2 lo4 ceoi1 hou6, go3 seng1 hou2 hung4 loeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在廟裡，師父用響螺吹號，聲音很洪亮。
examples.english_sentence: In the temple, the master blows a conch horn; the sound is very resonant.

mandarin_meaning: 响起；发出声音（声响开始出现）
english_meaning: to sound; to start to ring; a sound begins
explanation_mandarin: 表示某個聲音開始出現或被聽到，常用於鬧鐘、電話、音樂等開始發聲的情況。
explanation_english: Indicates that a sound begins to occur or is heard, commonly used for alarms, phones, music, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 鬧鐘一響起，我就醒咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: naau6 zung1 jat1 hoeng2 hei2, ngo5 zau6 sing2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 闹钟一响起，我就醒了。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as the alarm went off, I woke up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 電話響起，但冇人接聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: din6 waa2 hoeng2 hei2, daan6 mou5 jan4 zip3 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 电话响了，但没人接听。
examples.english_sentence: The phone rang, but no one answered.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 舊歌一響起，我就開始懷念以前嘅日子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gau6 go1 jat1 hoeng2 hei2, ngo5 zau6 hoi1 ci2 waai4 nim6 ji5 cin4 ge3 jat6 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 旧歌一响起，我就开始怀念以前的日子。
examples.english_sentence: When the old song started playing, I began to feel nostalgic for the past.

mandarin_meaning: 回應；回嘴；回答
english_meaning: to respond; to retort; to answer
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語動詞，表示對別人的話作出回應或回嘴。語氣可中性（簡單回覆）或帶有反駁、頂嘴的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to respond or retort to someone's remark. It can be a neutral reply or a sharper comeback/retort depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁講，我都唔想再響道喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 gong2, ngo5 dou1 m4 soeng2 zoi6 hoeng2 dou6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣說，我也不想再回應了。
examples.english_sentence: If you say that, I don't want to respond anymore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日鍾意同人響道，幾煩㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zung1 ji3 tung4 jan4 hoeng2 dou6, gei2 faan4 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常喜歡跟人頂嘴，很煩。
examples.english_sentence: He often likes to retort to people; it's pretty annoying.

mandarin_meaning: 響鈴 / 發出鈴聲（鐘、鬧鐘、風鈴等）
english_meaning: to ring (a bell); to sound (an alarm or chime)
explanation_mandarin: 表示鐘、鬧鐘、風鈴等發出鈴聲的動作，也可用於描述鬧鐘或提示音響起。
explanation_english: Describes the action of a bell, alarm clock, wind chime, etc. producing a ringing sound; can refer to alarms or chimes going off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 朝早六點鬧鐘就響鈴，叫我起身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ziu1 zou2 luk6 dim2 nou6 zung1 zau6 hoeng2 ling4, giu3 ngo5 hei2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 早上六點鬧鐘就響，叫我起床。
examples.english_sentence: The alarm clock rings at 6 AM and wakes me up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 放喺門口嘅風鈴一吹就會響鈴，聲好好聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fong3 hai2 mun4 hau2 ge3 fung1 ling4 jat1 ceoi1 zau6 wui5 hoeng2 ling4, seng1 hou2 hou2 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 放在門口的風鈴一吹就會響，聲音很好聽。
examples.english_sentence: The wind chime at the door rings whenever the wind blows; it sounds very nice.

mandarin_meaning: 響聲；共鳴或迴響的聲音
english_meaning: resonant sound; reverberation or echo; resonant tone
explanation_mandarin: 指具有共鳴、迴響或持續特性的聲音，既可用來描述房間或器物產生的回音或雜音，在技術語境下也可指共振音或特定頻率的響度特性。
explanation_english: Refers to sounds characterized by resonance, reverberation, or echo. It can describe room echoes or unwanted resonant noises, and in technical contexts may denote resonant tones or frequencies.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我聽到間房入面有一啲低沉嘅響音。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 teng1 dou3 gaan1 fong4 jap6 min6 jau5 jat1 di1 dai1 cam4 ge3 hoeng2 jam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我听到房间里面有一些低沉的响声。
examples.english_sentence: I can hear some deep, resonant sounds coming from inside the room.

mandarin_meaning: 页；（书的）页数
english_meaning: page (of a book/document); page as a unit/measure
explanation_mandarin: 表示書本或文件上的一面或一張紙的單位，也可作量詞使用，表示頁數或頁面。
explanation_english: Refers to a page of a book or document (one side or one leaf); can also be used as a measure word for pages or to mean a page/screen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本書有兩百頁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 syu1 jau5 loeng5 baak3 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这本书有两百页。
examples.english_sentence: This book has 200 pages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你翻多一頁畀我睇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 faan1 do1 jat1 jip6 bei2 ngo5 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你翻多一页给我看。
examples.english_sentence: Turn one more page for me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 每一頁嘅插圖都好靚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mui5 jat1 jip6 ge3 caa1 tou4 dou1 hou2 leng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 每一页的插图都很漂亮。
examples.english_sentence: The illustrations on each page are very beautiful.

mandarin_meaning: 页尾（页面的底部或页脚）
english_meaning: end of the page; footer
explanation_mandarin: 指文件或網頁的下方部分，常放置註腳、聯絡資料或版權資訊。
explanation_english: Refers to the bottom part of a document or webpage, often used for footnotes, contact details, or copyright information.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你喺頁尾加多個註腳啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai2 jip6 mei5 gaa1 do1 go3 zyu3 goek3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在页尾多加一个注脚吧。
examples.english_sentence: Add a footnote at the end of the page.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個網頁嘅頁尾寫住聯絡資料。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 mong5 jip6 ge3 jip6 mei5 se2 zyu6 lyun4 lok3 zi1 liu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 网页的页尾写着联系方式。
examples.english_sentence: The webpage's footer contains the contact information.

mandarin_meaning: 页岩油
english_meaning: shale oil (oil produced from oil shale)
explanation_mandarin: 由頁岩（含有機質的岩石）中提取或通過加熱裂解獲得的可燃油類，用作能源來源。
explanation_english: Hydrocarbon liquid derived from oil shale, obtained by extracting or heating (pyrolyzing) organic-rich shale rock; used as an energy resource.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司打算喺本地開採頁岩油。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 daa2 syun3 hai2 bun2 dei6 hoi1 coi2 jip6 ngaam4 jau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司打算在本地開採頁岩油。
examples.english_sentence: The company plans to extract shale oil locally.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頁岩油嘅開採通常需要加熱岩石，可能會造成環境污染。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jip6 ngaam4 jau4 ge3 hoi1 coi2 tung1 soeng4 seoi1 jiu3 gaa1 jit6 ngaam4 sek6, ho2 nang4 wui5 zou6 sing4 waan4 ging2 wu1 jim5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 頁岩油的開採通常需要對岩石加熱，可能會造成環境污染。
examples.english_sentence: Extracting shale oil usually requires heating the rock, which can cause environmental pollution.

mandarin_meaning: 页数 (yèshù)
english_meaning: number of pages; page count
explanation_mandarin: 表示書本、文件等的頁面數量或總頁數。
explanation_english: Refers to the number of pages in a book, document, or similar item (the total page count).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰份報告嘅頁數太多，唔好全部印出嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 fan6 bou3 gou3 ge3 jip6 sou3 taai3 do1, m4 hou2 cyun4 bou6 jan3 ceot1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那份報告的頁數太多，不要全部印出來。
examples.english_sentence: That report has too many pages; don't print them all.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本小說嘅頁數係三百。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 siu2 seot1 ge3 jip6 sou3 hai6 saam1 baak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這本小說的頁數是三百。
examples.english_sentence: This novel has 300 pages.

mandarin_meaning: 页码 (yè mǎ)
english_meaning: page number
explanation_mandarin: 表示書籍或文件中標示每一頁的編號，用於查找或引用特定頁面。
explanation_english: The number assigned to a page in a book or document, used to locate or reference a specific page.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可以喺目錄度睇到每章嘅頁碼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 ji5 hai2 muk6 luk6 dou6 tai2 dou3 mui5 zoeng1 ge3 yip6 maa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以在目录看到每章的页码。
examples.english_sentence: You can see the page numbers for each chapter in the table of contents.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 請將文件嘅頁碼設喺頁腳，方便打印時標示。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cing2 zoeng1 man4 gin6 ge3 yip6 maa5 cit3 hai2 yip6 goek3, fong1 bin6 daa2 jan3 si4 biu1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 請把文件的页码設在页脚，方便打印時標示。
examples.english_sentence: Please place the document's page numbers in the footer so they show when printed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺索引入面搵唔到嗰個主題嘅頁碼，唔知你記唔記得？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 sok3 jan5 jap6 min6 wan2 m4 dou3 go2 go3 zyu2 tai4 ge3 yip6 maa5, m4 zi1 nei5 gei3 m4 gei3 dak1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在索引裡找不到那個主題的頁碼，你還記得嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I can't find the page number for that topic in the index — do you remember it?

mandarin_meaning: 頁面（yèmiàn）
english_meaning: page; (web)page; screen or interface in an app or document
explanation_mandarin: 指網站、應用程式或文件中的單一顯示頁或界面，也可指紙張的一頁，用於描述頁面內容或佈局。
explanation_english: Refers to a single page or screen in a website, application, or document; can mean a physical page or a UI/page layout in digital contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個網站嘅頁面好亂，搵唔到我要嘅資料。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 mong5 zaam6 ge3 jip6 min6 hou2 lyun6, wan2 m4 dou2 ngo5 jiu3 ge3 zi1 liu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個網站的頁面很亂，找不到我要的資料。
examples.english_sentence: The website's page is messy; I can't find the information I need.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 設計師話要優化應用程式嗰個頁面，等用戶更容易使用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sit3 gai3 si1 waa6 jiu3 jau1 faa3 jing3 jung6 cing4 sik1 go2 go3 jip6 min6, dang2 jung6 wu6 gang3 jung6 ji6 si6 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 設計師說要優化應用程式的那個頁面，讓用戶更容易使用。
examples.english_sentence: The designer said to optimize that app page so it's easier for users to use.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可以撳呢個按鈕去下一頁面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 ji5 gam2 ni1 go3 on3 niu5 heoi3 haa6 jat1 jip6 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以按這個按鈕到下一個頁面。
examples.english_sentence: You can press this button to go to the next page.

mandarin_meaning: 页首 (页面的最上方；页眉、页头)
english_meaning: page header; top of the page
explanation_mandarin: 指頁面或文件的最上方區域，通常用來放標題、導航、公司標誌或頁碼等資訊。
explanation_english: Refers to the top area of a page or document, typically used for titles, navigation, logos, or page numbers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可以喺頁首加入公司標誌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 ji5 hai2 jip6 sau2 gaa1 jap6 gung1 si1 biu1 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以在页首加入公司标志。
examples.english_sentence: You can add the company logo to the page header.

mandarin_meaning: 顶；忍受；屋顶；（口语/俚语）硬着头干、抵抗
english_meaning: top/roof; to endure/tolerate; (colloquial) to press on or go all out despite difficulty
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞 / 名詞 / 口語詞
explanation_mandarin: 「頂」在廣東話有多種用法：作動詞時可表示忍受或承受（如「頂唔順」）；作名詞時可表示頂部或屋頂（如「屋頂」）；亦出現在口語或俚語短語中表示硬撐、繼續向前（如「頂硬上」）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '頂' has several uses: as a verb meaning to endure or tolerate (e.g., '頂唔順'); as a noun meaning the top or roof (e.g., '屋頂'); and in colloquial/slang phrases meaning to tough it out or press on despite difficulties (e.g., '頂硬上').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頂唔順佢成日遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ding2 m4 seon6 keoi5 seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我受不了他老是迟到。
examples.english_sentence: I can't stand that he is always late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋頂上有隻鴿仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 ding2 soeng6 jau5 zek3 gap3 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 屋顶上有一只鸽子。
examples.english_sentence: There's a pigeon on the roof.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 遇到困難就頂硬上，唔好輕言放棄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu6 dou3 kwan3 naan4 zau6 ding2 ngaang6 soeng5, m4 hou2 hing1 jin4 fong3 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 遇到困难就硬着头上去，不要轻言放弃。
examples.english_sentence: When you encounter difficulties, push on and don't give up easily.

synonyms: 屋頂 -> 頂部 / 上面

mandarin_meaning: 撐住；忍住；支撐住
english_meaning: hold on; hang on; endure; support
explanation_mandarin: 「頂住」是廣東話口語，常用來叫人暫時撐住或等一下，也可指物理上支撐、頂住某物或忍受某種情況（堅持下去）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb used to tell someone to hold on or wait for a moment; it can also mean to physically prop/support something or to endure/hold out through a situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂住，我快返嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 zyu6, ngo5 faai3 faan1 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 等一下，我馬上回來。
examples.english_sentence: Hold on, I'll be back soon.

mandarin_meaning: （粗俗）表示不滿、不屑或拒絕，也可用來表示受不了、無法忍受某人或某事；相當於「去你的／見鬼去吧／受夠了」
english_meaning: Vulgar Cantonese slang expressing contempt, disbelief or refusal (roughly 'screw that' / 'what the hell'); can also mean to be fed up or unwilling to put up with someone/something.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感嘆詞 / 動詞短語（俗語、粗俗）
explanation_mandarin: 本短語為香港粵語粗俗用語，常作口語化的感嘆或斥責，用來表達不滿、不屑或拒絕，有時也表示無法再忍受某事或某人。使用時屬非正式且可能冒犯他人，應避用於正式場合。
explanation_english: This is a coarse Hong Kong Cantonese slang phrase used as an exclamation of contempt, disbelief, or refusal, and sometimes to indicate being fed up with someone/something. It is informal and potentially offensive, so avoid it in formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂住個雞頭！你以為佢會幫你？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 zyu6 go3 gai1 tau4! nei5 ji5wai6 keoi5 wui5 bong1 nei5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去你的！你以為他會幫你？
examples.english_sentence: Screw that! You think he's going to help you?

mandarin_meaning: （粵語口語/粗話）表示不滿、驚訝或輕蔑，類似「靠」、「他媽的」
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese expletive used to express annoyance, surprise, or contempt; roughly 'damn it' or 'bloody hell'.
explanation_mandarin: 「頂住個鷄頭」在香港粵語中屬於俗語或粗口，常單獨作感嘆詞使用，用以表達不滿、驚訝或輕蔑。字面上為「頂著雞頭」，但一般不是字面意思，多為替代性或誇張的罵人用語，語境多為非正式場合，帶有粗俗色彩。
explanation_english: "頂住個鷄頭" is a Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial expletive. Literally "hold the rooster's head", it is not usually literal and functions as a vulgar interjection to express annoyance, disbelief, or contempt. It is informal and coarse, used in everyday speech rather than in polite contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂住個鷄頭！佢又遲到！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 zyu6 go3 gai1 tau4! keoi5 jau6 ci4 dou3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 靠！他又迟到了！
examples.english_sentence: Dammit! He's late again!

mandarin_meaning: 忍住脾气 / 忍耐
english_meaning: to hold back one's temper; to endure or suppress anger/strong emotions
explanation_mandarin: 表示努力壓抑或控制自己的怒氣或情緒，不當場發作，也可指忍耐痛苦或不滿。
explanation_english: Used to indicate making an effort to suppress or control one's anger or emotions, not losing one's temper; can also mean to endure discomfort or dissatisfaction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好嬲，但係頂住條氣冇發火。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 nau1, daan6 hai6 ding2 zyu6 tiu4 hei3 mou5 faat3 fo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很生气，但忍住脾气没有发火。
examples.english_sentence: He was very angry, but he held back his temper and didn't lose his cool.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頂住條氣等佢講完先，之後先再反駁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ding2 zyu6 tiu4 hei3 dang2 keoi5 gong2 jyun4 sin1, zi1 hau6 sin1 zoi3 faan2 bok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我忍住脾气等他把话说完才反驳。
examples.english_sentence: I held back my temper and waited for him to finish speaking before rebutting.

mandarin_meaning: 頂替（某人的）班次/檔位；暫時代班、撐住崗位
english_meaning: to cover someone's shift/stand/slot temporarily; to hold the fort
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指暫時代替別人守住檔口或班次，繼續工作或撐住崗位，通常用於市場檔口、店舖或輪班工作。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to temporarily take over or cover someone's stall, shift, or position — to hold the post until the person returns or replacement arrives. Commonly used for market stalls, shops, or shift work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我要出街，你可唔可以幫我頂住檔？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 jiu3 ceot1 gaai1, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 zyu6 dong2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我要出門，你可以幫我頂班/頂檔嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I'm going out tonight — can you cover my shift/stall for me?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日人手唔夠，你要幫手頂住檔多陣先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 jan4 sau2 m4 gau3, nei5 jiu3 bong1 sau2 ding2 zyu6 dong2 do1 zan6 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天人手不夠，你要幫忙頂一下檔位一會兒。
examples.english_sentence: We're short-staffed today — you'll need to hold the stall/cover the shift for a while.

mandarin_meaning: 去你的 / 該死（罵人的話）
english_meaning: Damn you; screw you; an expletive expressing anger or frustration
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話粗口用語，用來表達憤怒、不滿或驚訝，通常作感嘆或罵人，屬非正式、粗俗語。
explanation_english: A Cantonese swear phrase used to express anger, annoyance, or surprise. Functions as an interjection/curse directed at a person or situation. Informal and vulgar.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂你個肺，個老闆又唔肯加人工啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 nei5 go3 fai3, go3 lou5 baan2 jau6 m4 hang2 gaa1 jan4 gung1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去你的，老闆又不肯加薪了！
examples.english_sentence: Damn it — the boss still won't give a raise!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂你個肺，你遲到成個鐘，做咩唔早啲出門？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 nei5 go3 fai3, nei5 ci4 dou3 seng4 go3 zung1, zou6 me1 m4 zou2 di1 ceot1 mun4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去你的，你迟到整整一個小時，為什麼不早點出門？
examples.english_sentence: Jesus, you were an hour late — why didn't you leave earlier?

mandarin_meaning: 替人頂罪；替他人承担责任，充当替罪羊或替人掩饰过错
english_meaning: to take the fall for someone; to cover for someone or act as a scapegoat
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指為別人承擔過失或罪責，替別人掩飾錯誤或代人受罰。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang term meaning to accept blame or punishment on behalf of someone else, to cover up someone else's wrongdoing or act as a scapegoat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司發生咗問題，老細叫我去頂包。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 faat3 sang1 zo2 man6 tai4, lou5 sai3 giu3 ngo5 heoi3 ding2 baau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司出了問題，老闆叫我去頂包。
examples.english_sentence: The company had a problem and the boss told me to take the fall.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做咗啲壞事，唔想俾人知，就搵朋友幫手頂包。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 zo2 di1 waai6 si6, m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 zi1, zau6 wan2 pang4 jau5 bong1 sau2 ding2 baau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做了壞事，不想讓人知道，就找朋友幫忙頂包。
examples.english_sentence: He did something bad and didn't want anyone to know, so he asked a friend to cover for him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔會為佢頂包，法律問題要自己負責。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 wui5 wai6 keoi5 ding2 baau1, faat3 leot6 man6 tai4 jiu3 zi6 gei2 fu6 zaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不會替他頂包，法律問題要自己負責。
examples.english_sentence: I won't cover for him; legal issues must be taken care of by oneself.

mandarin_meaning: 顶嘴；回嘴
english_meaning: to talk back; to retort; to answer someone impudently
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，指對長輩、師長或權威人物不服從或不禮貌地反駁、頂撞、回嘴。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb phrase meaning to talk back or retort rudely, especially toward elders or authority figures.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好再頂咀，聽媽媽講就得啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zoi3 ding2 zeoi2, teng1 maa4 maa1 gong2 zau6 dak1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要再顶嘴，听妈妈说就好。
examples.english_sentence: Don't talk back again; just listen to Mom.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢淨係識頂咀，唔識解釋原因。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zing6 hai6 sik1 ding2 zeoi2, m4 sik1 gaai2 sik1 jyun4 jan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他只會頂嘴，不會解釋原因。
examples.english_sentence: He only knows how to talk back; he can't explain the reason.

mandarin_meaning: 受不了 / 撐不下去
english_meaning: can't bear/stand; unable to hold on or cope
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示無法承受某種情況、壓力、痛楚或感覺，類似「受不了」或「撐不住」。可用於生理或心理上的承受力到達極限。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning one cannot bear or withstand something (pressure, pain, discomfort, emotion) anymore — similar to "can't take it" or "can't cope." It can refer to physical or mental limits.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頂唔住呢個壓力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ding2 m4 zyu6 ni1 go3 aat3 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我受不了這個壓力。
examples.english_sentence: I can't stand this pressure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 依家咁凍，我真係頂唔住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 gam3 dung3, ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在這麼冷，我真的受不了了。
examples.english_sentence: It's so cold now, I really can't take it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 加咗好多班，我差啲頂唔住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaa1 zo2 hou2 do1 baan1, ngo5 caa1 di1 ding2 m4 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 加了很多班，我差點兒撐不住。
examples.english_sentence: With so many extra shifts, I almost can't cope.

mandarin_meaning: 頂不住再玩／撐不住應酬（口語）
english_meaning: can't keep partying / can't handle staying out (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俚語，通常用來表示已經撐不住再玩、熬夜或應酬，無法繼續通宵或參與熱鬧活動。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase used to say one can no longer keep up with partying, staying out late, or socializing — i.e., can't handle it anymore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚真係頂唔蒲，唔想出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1maan5 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 pou4, m4 soeng2 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚真的顶不住再去玩了，不想出门。
examples.english_sentence: I really can't party tonight; I don't want to go out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家頂唔蒲喇，唔想再通宵玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 ding2 m4 pou4 laa3, m4 soeng2 zoi3 tung1 siu1 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在頂不住了，不想再通宵玩。
examples.english_sentence: I can't keep going now; I don't want to stay out all night anymore.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上次嗰場Party太癲，我而家頂唔蒲，要瞓返陣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 ci3 go2 coeng4 Party taai3 din1, ngo5 ji4 gaa1 ding2 m4 pou4, jiu3 fan3 faan1 zan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上次那場派對太瘋，我現在頂不住，要睡一會兒。
examples.english_sentence: That last party was too wild — I can't handle it now and need to sleep.

mandarin_meaning: 受不了；忍受不住
english_meaning: can't stand; unable to tolerate; can't take it
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示對某人或某事無法忍受或承受，感到受不了。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning unable to endure or tolerate someone or something; can't stand it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我真係頂唔順佢成日遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 m4 seon6 keoi5 sing4 jat6 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我真的受不了他/她總是遲到。
examples.english_sentence: I really can't stand him/her always being late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個暑假嘅工作太多，我頂唔順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 syu1 gaa3 ge3 gung1 zok3 taai3 do1, ngo5 ding2 m4 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個暑假的工作太多，我受不了。
examples.english_sentence: There is too much work this summer break; I can't take it.

mandarin_meaning: 哎呀／可惡／算了（表示不滿、無奈或放棄）
english_meaning: Damn it / Give me a break / Oh well (expressing annoyance, frustration or resignation)
explanation_mandarin: 「頂啦」是廣東話的口語感嘆詞，用來表示不滿、無奈、厭煩或放棄。語氣可輕可重，視語境可當作抱怨、嘆息或略帶粗口的發洩。
explanation_english: “頂啦” is a Cantonese colloquial interjection used to express annoyance, frustration, resignation or giving up. The tone can be mild or strong depending on context; in stronger uses it can be slightly rude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂啦，我又遲到喇，老闆會嬲死我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 laa1, ngo5 jau6 ci4 dou3 laa3, lou5 baan2 wui5 nau1 sei2 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 糟了，我又迟到了，老板会生我的气。
examples.english_sentence: Damn it, I'm late again, the boss will be mad at me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂啦，唔好再講啦，我真係聽唔落。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 laa1, m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 laa1, ngo5 zan1 hai6 teng1 m4 lok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 哎呀，别再说了，我真的听不下去。
examples.english_sentence: Give it a break, don't talk about it anymore, I really can't listen to it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你成日遲到，頂啦，今次要罰錢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 seng4 jat6 ci4 dou3, ding2 laa1, gam1 ci3 jiu3 fat6 cin2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你老是迟到，真是的，这次要罚款了。
examples.english_sentence: You're always late — damn, this time you'll be fined.

mandarin_meaning: 算了 / 受夠了（表示無奈、不耐煩或放棄）
english_meaning: Enough / forget it / I'm fed up (expresses exasperation, resignation, or giving up)
explanation_mandarin: 「頂喇」是香港口語常用的感嘆詞，用來表示無奈、不耐煩或放棄，語氣可強亦可帶有戲謔成分，視語境而定。
explanation_english: A colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese interjection expressing exasperation, resignation, or giving up. It can mean "enough," "forget it," or "I'm fed up," with tone varying by context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我真係頂喇，等咗成個鐘都仲未到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 laa3, dang2 zo2 seng4 go3 zung1 dou1 zung6 mei6 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我真的受夠了，等了整整一個小時還沒到。
examples.english_sentence: I'm really fed up — I've waited a whole hour and they're still not here.

mandarin_meaning: 表示懊惱、不滿或無奈的感嘆（相當於「哎呀/該死」）
english_meaning: An exclamation expressing annoyance, frustration, or resignation (like "damn it" or "oh no").
explanation_mandarin: 「頂嘞」是廣東話的口語感嘆詞，常用來表達突然的懊惱、不滿或無奈。語氣可從輕微抱怨到強烈不滿，視語境而定。
explanation_english: “頂嘞” is a Cantonese colloquial interjection used to express sudden annoyance, frustration, or resignation. The intensity can range from mild annoyance to strong irritation depending on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂嘞，我又遲到喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 lek1, ngo5 jau6 ci4 dou3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 哎呀，我又遲到了。
examples.english_sentence: Damn, I'm late again.

mandarin_meaning: 顶嘴；顶撞（对长辈或上级回嘴、顶撞）
english_meaning: to talk back; to retort (usually to an elder or authority)
explanation_mandarin: 表示對有權威的人（如父母、長輩、上司）回嘴或頂撞，含有不尊重或反抗的語氣。
explanation_english: Describes talking back or retorting to someone in authority (e.g., parents, elders, or a boss), often implying disrespect or defiance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好頂嘴，媽媽講嘅有道理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ding2 zeoi2, maa4 maa1 gong2 ge3 jau5 dou6 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別頂嘴，媽媽說得有道理。
examples.english_sentence: Don't talk back; Mom has a point.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日對上司頂嘴，點可以升職？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 deoi3 soeng6 si1 ding2 zeoi2, dim2 ho2 ji5 sing1 zik1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是對上司頂嘴，怎麼能升職？
examples.english_sentence: He always talks back to his boss — how can he get promoted?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺長輩面前頂嘴，好唔禮貌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 coeng4 bui3 min6 cin4 ding2 zeoi2, hou2 m4 lai5 maau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要在長輩面前頂嘴，很不禮貌。
examples.english_sentence: Don't talk back in front of elders; it's very rude.

mandarin_meaning: 最多
english_meaning: at most; at the most; tops
explanation_mandarin: 表示最大限度，不會超過某個數量或程度。例如「頂多十個人」表示不會超過十個人，屬於副詞用法。
explanation_english: Indicates the maximum limit—something will not exceed a certain number or degree (e.g. "at most ten people"). Used as an adverb.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日頂多得一個鐘做功課。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 ding2 do1 dak1 jat1 go3 zung1 tau4 zou6 gung1 fo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天最多只有一個小時做功課。
examples.english_sentence: I can only spend at most one hour doing homework today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢頂多只係遲到十分鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ding2 do1 zi2 hai6 ci4 dou3 sap6 fan1 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最多只是遲到十分鐘。
examples.english_sentence: He was at most ten minutes late.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頂多可以幫你半個鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ding2 do1 ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5 bun3 go3 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我最多可以幫你半個小時。
examples.english_sentence: At most I can help you for half an hour.

mandarin_meaning: 顶天立地 (dǐng tiān lì dì) — 形容高大雄偉，或指人正直、氣概不凡
english_meaning: Lofty and imposing; upright, steadfast, and dignified; describes someone or something with great presence or moral integrity
explanation_mandarin: 原本指直抵天際、立於大地之高大形象，現在多用來形容人或事物氣勢雄偉、正直有骨氣或堅定無畏。
explanation_english: Originally describes something that 'reaches the sky and stands on the ground' (i.e., very tall and imposing). Figuratively it describes a person or thing that is heroic, upright, steadfast, and full of presence or moral integrity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係一個頂天立地嘅人，做人好有骨氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 jat1 go3 ding2 tin1 laap6 dei6 ge3 jan4, zou6 jan4 hou2 jau5 gwat1 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是一个顶天立地的人，做事很有骨气。
examples.english_sentence: He is a person of great stature and integrity; he does things with a lot of backbone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢座雕像頂天立地，氣勢磅礴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zo6 diu1 zoeng6 ding2 tin1 laap6 dei6, hei3 sai3 pong4 bok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这座雕像顶天立地，气势磅礴。
examples.english_sentence: This statue is towering and imposing, full of grandeur.

mandarin_meaning: 被夾在中間；進退兩難；（物件）被夾住
english_meaning: to be caught in the middle; to be stuck/sandwiched; (literal) to be pinched or jammed
explanation_mandarin: 「頂夾」可作口語用法，表示人處於兩方或多方夾擊、進退兩難的狀況；也可作字面意思，指物件被夾住或卡住。
explanation_english: In colloquial Cantonese, 頂夾 describes being caught between two sides or under pressure (stuck in the middle). It can also be literal, meaning an object is pinched or jammed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家好頂夾，老闆要快交貨，客人又唔肯付錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hou2 ding2 gaap3, lou5 baan2 jiu3 faai3 gaau1 fo3, haak3 jan4 jau6 m4 hang2 fu6 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在很進退兩難，老闆要快交貨，但客人又不肯付錢。
examples.english_sentence: I'm really stuck right now — the boss wants the delivery fast but the customer won't pay.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 張紙畀櫃門頂夾咗，拆唔開。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng1 zi2 bei2 gwai6 mun4 ding2 gaap3 zo2, caak3 m4 hoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 紙被櫃門夾住了，打不開。
examples.english_sentence: The paper got jammed in the cabinet door and I can't open it.

mandarin_meaning: 顶尖（最优秀、最高水准）
english_meaning: top-notch; top-tier; elite; cutting-edge
explanation_mandarin: 表示在某個領域或範疇中位於最高、最優秀或技術最尖端的程度，常用來形容人、事、物的水準。
explanation_english: Indicates the highest or most excellent level in a field or category; used to describe people, things, or skills that are top-tier or cutting-edge.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係公司入面嘅頂尖員工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 gung1si1 jap6min6 ge3 ding2 zim1 jyun4gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是公司裡的頂尖員工。
examples.english_sentence: He's one of the company's top employees.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅廚師好頂尖，菜好好食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1teng1 ge3 cyu4si1 hou2 ding2 zim1, coi3 hou2 hou2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間餐廳的廚師很頂尖，菜很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: The chef at this restaurant is top-notch; the dishes are delicious.

mandarin_meaning: 顶峰、巅峰 (dǐngfēng, diānfēng)
english_meaning: summit; peak; pinnacle; highest point
explanation_mandarin: 指山峰的最高處，也常用來比喻事業、能力或某事物達到的最高點或最重要的階段。
explanation_english: Refers to the highest point of a mountain; commonly used figuratively to mean the highest point or pinnacle of a career, ability, or other achievement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢座山嘅頂峰成日被雲霧圍住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zo6 saan1 ge3 ding2 fung1 sing4 jat6 bei6 wan4 mou6 wai4 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这座山的顶峰经常被云雾笼罩。
examples.english_sentence: The summit of this mountain is often shrouded in mist.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺事業上終於達到頂峰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 si6 jip6 soeng6 zung1 jyu1 daat6 dou3 ding2 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在事业上终于达到了顶峰。
examples.english_sentence: He finally reached the peak of his career.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 球隊而家正喺頂峰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: kau4 deoi6 ji4 gaa1 zing3 hai2 ding2 fung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 球队现在正处于顶峰。
examples.english_sentence: The team is currently at its peak.

mandarin_meaning: 撑得住 / 顶得住；能忍受、应付得来
english_meaning: able to tolerate/endure; can cope with or withstand (something)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，用來表示能夠承受某種壓力、困難或不舒服的情況，應付得來、撐得住。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to be able to tolerate, endure, or cope with a difficult or uncomfortable situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份工咁多壓力，你頂得順唔？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gung1 gam3 do1 aat3 lik6, nei5 ding2 dak1 seon6 m4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这份工作压力这么大，你顶得住吗？
examples.english_sentence: This job has so much pressure — can you handle it?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 雖然好辛苦，但我頂得順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: seoi1 jin4 hou2 san1 fu2, daan6 ngo5 ding2 dak1 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 虽然很辛苦，但我撑得住。
examples.english_sentence: Although it's very tough, I can cope.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢架車頂得順幾耐？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaa3 ce1 ding2 dak1 seon6 gei2 noi6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这辆车能撑多久？
examples.english_sentence: How long will this car hold up?

mandarin_meaning: 背心；無袖上衣（口語、港式寫法中「杉」常代替「衫」）
english_meaning: tank top; sleeveless vest; undershirt (colloquial Hong Kong usage)
explanation_mandarin: 「頂心杉」是香港口語常見的詞彙，指無袖的上衣或背心。字裡的「杉」在口語書寫中常作「衫」的變體，因此可理解為背心/無袖衫，既可作外穿也可作內衣。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, "頂心杉" colloquially refers to a sleeveless top or tank top (vest/undershirt). The character 杉 here is often used informally in place of 衫 (clothing), so the term denotes a vest-style top that can be worn as outerwear or underwear.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天我成日著頂心杉出街，涼快啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 ngo5 sing4 jat6 zoek3 ding2 sam1 saan1 ceot1 gaai1, loeng4 faai3 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天我常常穿背心出門，涼快一點。
examples.english_sentence: In summer I often wear a tank top when I go out; it's a bit cooler.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇下呢件白色頂心杉，好襯你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 haa5 ni1 gin6 baak6 sik1 ding2 sam1 saan1, hou2 cam3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看看这件白色背心，很襯你。
examples.english_sentence: Look at this white tank top; it suits you well.

mandarin_meaning: 發自內心、刻骨銘心；對人或事非常掛念、非常珍惜，有時也可表示心裡非常痛苦或擔憂
english_meaning: A Cantonese idiom meaning deeply (felt) — from the bottom of one's heart; to cherish someone/something deeply; can also express extreme worry or heartache
explanation_mandarin: 口語化的廣東話慣用語，用來形容情感非常強烈：既可表示對某人或事物極度珍惜、掛念，也可表示極度擔心或心痛。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese idiom used to describe very strong feelings: it can denote deep affection or attachment to someone/something, and can also indicate extreme worry or heartache.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我頂心頂肺嘅家人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 ding2 sam1 ding2 fai3 ge3 gaa1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是我最親愛的家人。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is my dearest family member.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細佬病咗，我頂心頂肺咁擔心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou2 beng6 zo2, ngo5 ding2 sam1 ding2 fai3 gam2 daam1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 弟弟生病了，我非常擔心。
examples.english_sentence: My younger brother is ill; I'm extremely worried.

mandarin_meaning: 頂班；代班；替人頂替（口語）
english_meaning: to cover someone's shift; to fill in for someone (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「頂手」是廣東話口語，通常指臨時替別人上班或代替某人的職務或班次。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to temporarily cover someone's shift or substitute for someone at work or duty.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日我有嘢，唔得閒，你可唔可以幫我頂手？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 ngo5 jau5 je5, m4 dak1 haan4, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 sau2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天我有事，沒空，你能幫我頂班／代我上班嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I have something tomorrow and won't be free — can you cover my shift for me?

mandarin_meaning: 顶撞（顶嘴、回嘴，冒犯或与长辈/上司等发生口角）
english_meaning: to talk back to; to contradict or defy (often rudely), to offend someone by speaking back
explanation_mandarin: “頂撞”指无礼或直接地回嘴、顶嘴、与别人（尤其是长辈、上司）发生口角或冲突，带有冒犯或不尊重的意味。
explanation_english: “頂撞” means to talk back or contradict someone, often rudely; typically used when someone speaks back to or offends an elder, boss, or authority figure.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好頂撞阿媽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ding2 zong6 aa3 maa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 别顶撞妈妈。
examples.english_sentence: Don't talk back to Mom.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日頂撞上司，遲啲可能會有麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 ding2 zong6 soeng6 si1, ci4 di1 ho2 nang4 wui5 jau5 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是顶撞上司，迟早会有麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: He always talks back to his boss; sooner or later it'll cause trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老師唔鐘意學生頂撞佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 si1 m4 zung1 ji3 hok6 saang1 ding2 zong6 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老师不喜欢学生顶撞他/她。
examples.english_sentence: The teacher doesn't like students talking back to him/her.

mandarin_meaning: 替人頂罪／替人償還欠款或代人承擔責任（口語）
english_meaning: To cover for someone — e.g. pay someone's debt, take the blame, or assume responsibility on their behalf (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，通常指替別人承擔責任、幫忙償還欠款或代人擋責備，有時含替人頂罪的意思。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to cover for someone — such as paying their debt, taking the blame, or shouldering responsibility for them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日要我頂數啦，我都唔係成日有錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 jiu3 ngo5 ding2 sou3 laa1, ngo5 dou1 m4 hai6 sing4 jat6 jau5 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要總是讓我替你頂數，我也不是總有錢。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always expect me to cover for you — I'm not always loaded.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗保護朋友，佢幫朋友頂數，最後自己承擔咗後果。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 bou2 wu6 pang4 jau5, keoi5 bong1 pang4 jau5 ding2 sou3, zeoi3 hau6 zi6 gei2 sing4 daam1 zo2 hau6 gwo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了保護朋友，他幫朋友頂罪，最後自己承擔了後果。
examples.english_sentence: To protect his friend, he covered for him and in the end had to bear the consequences himself.

mandarin_meaning: 頂班 / 代班
english_meaning: to cover someone's work shift; to take someone's shift
explanation_mandarin: 「頂更」是廣東話俗語，指替他人頂替工作班次或代人上班，常用於向同事或朋友請求幫忙頂班。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to cover someone else's work shift or take their shift; commonly used to ask a colleague or friend to fill in for you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我有事，唔可以返工，你可唔可以幫我頂更？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 jau5 si6, m4 ho2 ji5 faan1 gung1, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 geng1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我有事，不能上班，你可以幫我頂班嗎？
examples.english_sentence: I have something tonight and can't come to work — can you cover my shift for me?

mandarin_meaning: 顶替 (dǐngtì)：代替、替代或接替某人的位置／職務（有時含暗中取代之意）
english_meaning: to replace; to stand in for; to take someone's place (can sometimes imply usurping)
explanation_mandarin: 表示代替某人或某物的位置、職務或工作，有時強調代為履行或被人取代的情況。
explanation_english: Indicates replacing or taking the place/role of someone or something; can mean standing in for someone or being substituted (occasionally carries a nuance of usurping).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日你可唔可以幫我頂替去開會？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 tai3 heoi3 hoi1 wui6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天你可以幫我頂替去開會嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Can you cover the meeting for me today?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅職位畀人頂替咗，佢而家要搵新工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 zik1 wai6 bei2 jan4 ding2 tai3 zo2, keoi5 ji4 gaa1 jiu3 wan2 san1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她的職位被人頂替了，他/她現在要找新工作。
examples.english_sentence: His/her position was taken by someone else, and now he/she has to look for a new job.

mandarin_meaning: 頂樓 / 屋頂（建築物的最上層）
english_meaning: top floor; rooftop; the highest story of a building
explanation_mandarin: 指建築物的最上層，通常是最高的一層或屋頂，可能用作觀景、放置設備或儲物等用途。
explanation_english: Refers to the topmost floor of a building or the rooftop. Often used for viewing, placing equipment, or storage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋去頂樓睇夜景啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 ding2 lau4 tai2 je6 ging2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們去頂樓看夜景吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the rooftop to watch the night view.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂樓有啲漏水，要快啲修理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 lau4 jau5 di1 lau6 seoi2, jiu3 faai3 di1 sau1 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 頂樓有點漏水，需要快點修理。
examples.english_sentence: The rooftop is leaking; it needs to be repaired soon.

mandarin_meaning: 頂班、代班、臨時替人擔任工作或班次
english_meaning: to cover someone's shift; to stand in or substitute for someone temporarily
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示臨時替別人擔任某個職務或班次（例如工作班次、值班等）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to temporarily take over someone's job or shift (e.g., covering a work shift or duty).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日我唔得閒，唔該你幫我頂檔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 ngo5 m4 dak1 haan4, m4 goi1 nei5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 dong3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天我沒空，拜託你幫我頂班。
examples.english_sentence: I won't be free tomorrow — could you cover my shift?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今晚要去旅行，已經搵人幫佢頂檔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 maan5 jiu3 heoi3 leoi5 hang4, ji5 ging1 wan2 jan4 bong1 keoi5 ding2 dong3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今晚要去旅行，已經找人幫他頂班。
examples.english_sentence: He's going on a trip tonight and has already found someone to stand in for him.

mandarin_meaning: 閣樓；頂樓的小房間（方言用法）
english_meaning: attic; loft; small room under the roof (dialectal)
explanation_mandarin: “頂櫳”是廣東話方言詞，指建築物最上層靠近屋頂的小房間或閣樓，常用於口語表述居住空間位置。
explanation_english: A Cantonese dialectal term referring to a small room or loft at the top of a building under the roof (attic/top-floor room). Commonly used in spoken Cantonese to indicate living space location.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我屋企嘅頂櫳好細，但可以望到條街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 uk1 kei2 ge3 ding2 lung4 hou2 sai3, daan6 ho2 ji5 mong6 dou3 tiu4 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我家裡的閣樓很小，但可以看到街道。
examples.english_sentence: The attic in my house is small, but you can see the street.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）氣得要命／非常惱火／真糟糕
english_meaning: (slang) extremely annoying or infuriating; damn it
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 感嘆詞 / 形容詞（俚語）
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，用來表示對人或事非常生氣、不滿或覺得很糟糕，可作感嘆或形容情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression used to show strong annoyance, frustration, or that something is really awful; used as an exclamation or descriptive phrase.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到佢咁講，我真係頂爛市。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 keoi5 gam2 gong2, ngo5 zan1 hai6 ding2 laan6 si5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听到他那样说，我真是气死了。
examples.english_sentence: Hearing him say that really pissed me off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司又遲交貨，客人投訴，成件事頂爛市。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 jau6 ci4 gaau1 fo3, haak3 jan4 tau4 sou3, sing4 gin6 si6 ding2 laan6 si5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司又迟交货，客户投诉，整件事真糟糕。
examples.english_sentence: The company was late delivering again, customers complained — the whole thing is a mess/damn infuriating.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）老大、頭目；有勢力或地位高的男子，常指黑社會或區內的大哥
english_meaning: slang for a boss or top figure; a powerful or high-status man (often refers to a gang boss or local big shot)
explanation_mandarin: 「頂爺」是香港粵語俚語，用來稱呼或描述地位高、有勢力的男性，語氣可帶敬畏、崇敬或貶義。語境上有時指黑社會頭目或區內「大哥」等人物。
explanation_english: “頂爺” is a Hong Kong Cantonese slang term for a man with high status or power. It can carry tones of respect, fear, or derision and is often used to refer to a gang boss or a local big shot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係呢度嘅頂爺，大家都怕佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 hai6 ni1 dou6 ge3 ding2 je4, daai6gaa1 dou1 paa3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是這裡的大哥，大家都怕他。
examples.english_sentence: He's the big shot around here; everyone is afraid of him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 警方懷疑佢係黑幫嘅頂爺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Ging2 fong1 waai4 ji4 keoi5 hai6 hak1 bong1 ge3 ding2 je4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 警方懷疑他是黑幫的老大。
examples.english_sentence: The police suspect he's a gang boss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生意嗰陣，佢總係好似頂爺咁樣決定晒大方向。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Zo6 saang1 ji3 go2 zan6, keoi5 zung2 hai6 hou2 ci5 ding2 je4 gam2 joeng6 kyut3 ding6 saai3 daai6 fong1 hoeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生意時，他總像個大哥一樣決定大方向。
examples.english_sentence: When doing business, he always acts like the boss who decides the major direction.

mandarin_meaning: 顶班（替别人上班、代班）
english_meaning: to cover a shift; to stand in for someone at work
explanation_mandarin: 指临时替别人上班或代替他人值班，通常用于工作或輪班情況。
explanation_english: To temporarily take someone else's work shift or duty, commonly used in workplace or shift contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日我會遲到，阿珍話會幫我頂班。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 ngo5 wui5 ci4 dou6, aa3 zan1 waa6 wui5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 baan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天我會遲到，阿珍說會幫我頂班。
examples.english_sentence: I'll be late tomorrow; Jane said she'll cover my shift.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆叫我幫同事頂班，等佢去出差。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 giu3 ngo5 bong1 tung4 si6 ding2 baan1, dang2 keoi5 heoi3 ceot1 caai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板叫我替同事顶班，讓他去出差。
examples.english_sentence: The boss asked me to cover a colleague's shift so he could go on a business trip.

mandarin_meaning: 表示驚訝、惱怒或無奈的感嘆詞，相當於「哎呀／真是的／不可思議」
english_meaning: An interjection expressing surprise, annoyance, or exasperation (similar to 'oh man', 'for crying out loud', or 'what the heck').
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語感嘆詞，用來表達驚訝、不滿或無奈，語氣可輕可重，常見於香港口語。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese interjection used to express surprise, annoyance, or exasperation. The tone can be mild or strong, and it's commonly used in Hong Kong speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂瓜瓜，巴士又遲到，我會遲到啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 gwaa1 gwaa1, baa1 si2 jau6 ci4 dou3, ngo5 wui5 ci4 dou3 laa3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 哎呀，公車又遲到了，我要遲到了！
examples.english_sentence: Oh man, the bus is late again — I'm going to be late!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢竟然唔記得我生日，頂瓜瓜！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ging2 jin4 m4 gei3 dak1 ngo5 saang1 jat6, ding2 gwaa1 gwaa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他竟然忘記了我的生日，真是太過分了！
examples.english_sentence: He actually forgot my birthday — unbelievable!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頂瓜瓜，個訂單又錯咗，點算好？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ding2 gwaa1 gwaa1, go3 deng6 daan1 jau6 co3 zo2, dim2 syun3 hou2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 哎呀，訂單又錯了，怎麼辦？
examples.english_sentence: Oh no, the order is wrong again — what should we do?

mandarin_meaning: 替人頂罪／替人承擔責任
english_meaning: to take the blame or punishment for someone else; to act as a scapegoat
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，『頂當』指替別人承擔責任或受罰，相當於『替人頂罪』或『當替罪羊』，多用於口語或俚語情境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to take the blame or punishment on behalf of someone else — to be a scapegoat or cover for another person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢叫我去頂當，話會幫我還債。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 giu3 ngo5 heoi3 ding2 dong1, waa6 wui5 bong1 ngo5 waan4 zai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他叫我去顶当，说会帮我还债。
examples.english_sentence: He asked me to take the blame, saying he'd help me pay off the debt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔會為咗保住自己而幫佢頂當。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 wui5 wai6 zo2 bou2 zyu6 zi6 gei2 ji4 bong1 keoi5 ding2 dong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不会为了保住自己而替他顶罪。
examples.english_sentence: I won't take the blame for him just to protect myself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司唔想曝光，就搵咗人頂當。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 m4 soeng2 baau3 gwong1, zau6 wan2 zo2 jan4 ding2 dong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司不想曝光，就找人顶罪。
examples.english_sentence: The company didn't want it exposed, so they found someone to take the fall.

mandarin_meaning: 解癮、滿足短暫的癮頭
english_meaning: to satisfy/relieve a craving; to get a short-term fix
explanation_mandarin: 「頂癮」為廣東話口語，指暫時滿足自己某種慾望或癮頭（例如吃一點東西、玩一下遊戲或抽一支煙）以解渴或解悶，並不一定意味真正戒除或成癮。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to temporarily satisfy a craving or urge (e.g. eating something, playing a short game, or having a cigarette) — getting a brief fix rather than indicating full addiction.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 食一塊朱古力，頂吓癮先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sik6 jat1 faai3 zyu1 gu2 lik6, ding2 haa5 jan5 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 吃一塊巧克力，先解解癮。
examples.english_sentence: I'll eat a piece of chocolate to take the edge off my craving.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 好耐冇打機，今晚玩返陣，頂吓癮啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hou2 noi6 mou5 daa2 gei1, gam1 maan5 waan2 faan1 zan6, ding2 haa5 jan5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 好久沒打遊戲了，今晚玩一下先解解癮吧。
examples.english_sentence: Haven't gamed in ages — I'll play a bit tonight to satisfy the craving.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想真係上癮，只係想頂吓癮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 zan1 hai6 soeng5 jan5, zi2 hai6 soeng2 ding2 haa5 jan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想真的上癮，只是想稍微解一下癮。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to actually get addicted; I just want to take the edge off my craving.

mandarin_meaning: 太過分；離譜，讓人無法接受
english_meaning: outrageous; excessive; beyond what one can accept
explanation_mandarin: 口語廣東話用語，用來形容某人或某事非常過分、無理或離譜，到了不能接受或令人憤怒的程度。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe someone or something that is extremely unreasonable, excessive, or outrageous — essentially beyond what one can accept.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢遲到仲唔道歉，頂盡！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ci4 dou3 zung6 m4 dou6 hip3, ding2 zeon6!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他遲到還不道歉，太過分了！
examples.english_sentence: He was late and still didn't apologize — that's outrageous!

mandarin_meaning: 顶真（可指粤语口语中“较真/顶嘴”的意思，也可指汉语修辞术语“顶真”，即首尾相接的修辞手法）
english_meaning: “Ding zan” — colloquially in Cantonese: to be pedantic, to nitpick or to argue back; literary: anadiplosis (a rhetorical device where the last word of a clause starts the next)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 动词（口语意义）；名词（修辞术语）
explanation_mandarin: 在粤语口語中，頂眞常用來形容一個人對細節過份計較或愛頂嘴、較真；在語言學/修辭學中，頂真是一種修辭手法（即英文所稱的anadiplosis），以上一語句的末詞作為下一語句的開頭，以增強語氣或連貫性。
explanation_english: In Cantonese colloquial use, 頂眞 refers to being overly pedantic, nitpicky, or arguing back. In linguistics/poetics, 頂真 (anadiplosis) is a rhetorical device where the final word of one clause begins the next, used to strengthen emphasis or continuity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁頂眞啦，冇必要為咁嘅小事計較。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam3 ding2 zan1 laa3, mou5 bit1 jiu3 wai6 gam3 ge3 siu2 si6 gai3 gaau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別那麼較真了，沒必要為這種小事計較。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be so pedantic/picky; there's no need to argue over such a small thing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢段對白用咗頂眞，令語氣更加連貫有力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dyun6 deoi3 baak6 jung6 zo2 ding2 zan1, ling6 jyu5 hei3 gaang1 gaa1 lin4 gwaan3 jau5 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這段對白用了頂真，令語氣更加連貫有力。
examples.english_sentence: This line of dialogue uses anadiplosis (頂真), making the tone more cohesive and forceful.

mandarin_meaning: 顶真（dǐngzhēn），一种修辞手法，把上一句的末词或短语重复到下一句的开头，用于连贯或强调。
english_meaning: Anadiplosis (a rhetorical device): repeating the last word or phrase of one clause at the beginning of the next to create linkage or emphasis.
explanation_mandarin: 顶真是一种常见的修辞方法，把一句话的结尾词或短语直接放到下一句的开头，形成句与句之间的承接与强调，常见于诗歌、相声、对联等。
explanation_english: Dingzhen (anadiplosis) is a rhetorical technique where the final word or phrase of one sentence is repeated at the start of the next, creating continuity and emphasis. It appears in poetry, spoken comedy, couplets, and other forms.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 詩人喺呢首詩入面運用頂真，句與句之間連成一氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si1 jan4 hai2 ni1 sau2 si1 jap6 min6 wan6 jung6 ding2 zan1, geoi3 jyu5 geoi3 zi1 gaan1 lin4 sing4 jat1 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 诗人在这首诗中运用了顶真，使句与句之间连成一气。
examples.english_sentence: The poet uses anadiplosis in this poem, linking the lines seamlessly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 相聲演員成日用頂真嚟串場，觀眾好容易記住笑點。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng1 sing1 jin2 jyun4 sing4 jat6 jung6 ding2 zan1 lai4 cyun3 coeng4, gun1 zung3 hou2 jung4 ji6 gei3 zyu6 siu3 dim2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 相声演员经常用顶真串场，观众很容易记住笑点。
examples.english_sentence: Comedy performers often use anadiplosis to link jokes, making punchlines easier for the audience to remember.

mandarin_meaning: 硬着头皮上/硬拼、硬干
english_meaning: to push on/tough it out; to proceed despite difficulty or resistance; to force one's way
explanation_mandarin: 表示在面对困难或阻力时不退缩，硬着头皮去做或强行推进，常用于口语，带有勉强或硬拼的意思。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to press on or charge ahead despite difficulties or resistance — to tough it out or force one's way through a situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 雖然今次好困難，但冇得退路，我哋唯有頂硬上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: seoi1 jin4 gam1 ci3 hou2 kwan3 naan4, daan6 mou5 dak1 teoi3 lou6, ngo5 dei6 wai4 jau5 ding2 ngaang6 soeng5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 虽然这次很困难，但没有退路，我们只能硬着头皮上。
examples.english_sentence: Although this time is very difficult and there's no way back, we just have to push on.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果客戶即刻提出要求，佢話會頂硬上去解決問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 haak3 wu6 zik1 hak1 tai4 ceot1 jiu1 kau4, keoi5 waa6 wui5 ding2 ngaang6 soeng5 heoi3 gaai2 kyut3 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果客户立刻提出要求，他说会硬着头皮去解决问题。
examples.english_sentence: If the client immediately makes the demand, he said he'll tough it out and go solve the problem.

mandarin_meaning: 硬碰硬；正面對抗；堅決抵抗
english_meaning: to confront head-on; to stand firm and resist; to go toe-to-toe
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，表示以強硬或堅持的態度正面對抗或頂撞對方，不退讓。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to confront someone forcefully or stubbornly, refusing to give ground; to engage in a head-on clash.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到老細要搵數，竟然頂硬檔唔肯退讓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou2 lou5 sai3 jiu3 wan2 sou3, ging2 jin4 ding2 ngaang6 dong2 m4 hang2 teoi3 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到老闆要算帳，竟然硬著頭皮不肯退讓。
examples.english_sentence: When he saw the boss wanted to collect the debt, he actually stood his ground and refused to back down.

mandarin_meaning: 顶替、顶班、代班（粤语口语）
english_meaning: to cover for someone; to fill in (for a shift or duty)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，指臨時替人工作或代替某個職務、班次，幫忙頂替缺席的那一位。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to temporarily replace someone at work or to cover a shift/duty for someone who is absent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日我唔得閒，你可唔可以幫我頂窿？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 ngo5 m4 dak1 haan4, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 lung4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天我没空，你可以帮我顶班吗？
examples.english_sentence: I'm not free tomorrow. Can you cover my shift for me?

mandarin_meaning: 顶端；最上面或最高的位置，也可指等级、地位的最上层
english_meaning: top; apex; summit; the highest point or uppermost part; the highest level in rank or status
explanation_mandarin: 指物體或空間的最上端或最前端位置；引申為組織、等級或地位上的最高層。
explanation_english: Refers to the highest point or uppermost position of something; can also be used figuratively for the highest level in an organization, rank, or status.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢座山嘅頂端好靚，天氣又清爽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zo6 saan1 ge3 ding2 dyun1 hou2 leng3, tin1 hei3 jau6 cing1 song2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这座山的顶端很漂亮，天气也很清爽。
examples.english_sentence: The top of this mountain is beautiful and the weather is refreshing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司嘅頂端係董事會，決策由佢哋嚟做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 ge3 ding2 dyun1 hai6 dung2 si6 wui2, kyut3 caak3 jau4 keoi5 dei6 lai4 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司的顶端是董事会，决策由他们来做。
examples.english_sentence: The top of the company is the board of directors; decisions are made by them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間實驗室專注喺人工智能嘅頂端研究。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 sat6 jim6 sat1 zyun1 zyu3 hai2 jan4 gung1 zi6 nang4 ge3 ding2 dyun1 jin4 gau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间实验室专注于人工智能的顶端研究。
examples.english_sentence: This lab focuses on cutting-edge research in artificial intelligence.

mandarin_meaning: （罕見）粵語俚語，可能表示「生氣／發脾氣」；字面則為「籠子的頂部」
english_meaning: (rare) Cantonese slang possibly meaning "to be angry/get mad"; literally "top of a cage/basket"
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語/俚語（若字面則為名詞）
explanation_mandarin: 「頂籠」並非廣泛記錄的標準詞彙，為地區性或罕見俚語。口語資料顯示它有時被用來形容一個人很容易生氣或發脾氣；從字面看則可解作籠子的頂部。使用時需注意語境與地區差異，部分聽者可能不熟悉該用法。
explanation_english: “Ding lung” is not a widely documented standard term and appears as a regional or rare Cantonese slang. In some spoken contexts it is reportedly used to describe someone who is easily angered or is getting very upset; literally it can mean the top of a cage or basket. Use with caution—meaning and recognition vary by region and context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好頂籠啦，冷靜啲傾下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 ding2 lung4 laa3, laang5 zing6 di1 king1 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別那麼生氣，冷靜一點談談。
examples.english_sentence: Don't get so angry; calm down and talk it over.

mandarin_meaning: 顶级；最高等级的
english_meaning: top-class; top-tier; highest-grade
explanation_mandarin: 表示事物屬於最高等級或品質非常好，常用來形容產品、服務或水平。
explanation_english: Indicates that something is of the highest grade or quality; commonly used to describe products, services, or standards.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間酒店係頂級，服務同設施都好好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 zau2 dim3 hai6 ding2 kap1, fuk6 mou6 tung4 cit3 si1 dou1 hou2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家酒店是顶级的，服务和设施都很好。
examples.english_sentence: This hotel is top-class; the service and facilities are excellent.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅牛扒係頂級嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 ngau4 paa4 hai6 ding2 kap1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家餐厅的牛排是顶级的。
examples.english_sentence: The steaks at this restaurant are top-notch.

mandarin_meaning: 顶罪；替别人承担罪责或惩罚（替罪、顶包）
english_meaning: to take the blame; to take the fall; to be a scapegoat; to accept punishment on behalf of someone else
explanation_mandarin: 指為他人承擔罪責或懲罰，替人頂罪或當替罪羊，常用於口語或法律/社會語境。
explanation_english: To accept blame or punishment on behalf of someone else; to act as a scapegoat. Commonly used in colloquial and legal/social contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔想入獄，所以搵人頂罪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 soeng2 jap6 juk6, so2 ji5 wan2 jan4 ding2 zeoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不想入狱，所以找人顶罪。
examples.english_sentence: He didn't want to go to prison, so he got someone to take the fall.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔會替佢頂罪，呢種嘢我做唔到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 wui5 tai3 keoi5 ding2 zeoi6, ni1 zung2 je5 ngo5 zou6 m4 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不会替他顶罪，这种事我做不到。
examples.english_sentence: I won't take the blame for him; I can't do that kind of thing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢俾人頂罪入咗獄。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 ding2 zeoi6 jap6 zo2 juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人顶罪入狱了。
examples.english_sentence: He was framed and imprisoned (took the fall).

mandarin_meaning: 忍饑 / 忍肚子飢餓（口語）
english_meaning: to endure hunger; to hold off eating (Cantonese colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指忍受饑餓或暫時不吃東西，通常因為忙碌、等候或其他原因而克制進食。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to endure hunger or temporarily refrain from eating, often because one is busy, waiting, or for other reasons.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日冇時間食飯，只好頂肚到下晝先食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 mou5 si4 gaan3 sik6 faan6, zi2 hou2 ding2 tou5 dou3 haa6 zau3 sin1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天沒時間吃飯，只好忍着餓到下午才吃。
examples.english_sentence: I had no time to eat today, so I had to go hungry until the afternoon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頂肚唔到啦，去食嘢先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ding2 tou5 m4 dou2 laa3, heoi3 sik6 je5 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我忍不住了，先去吃東西。
examples.english_sentence: I can't hold my hunger anymore; I'll go eat first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗趕deadline，我頂肚成日冇時間食嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 gon2 deadline, ngo5 ding2 tou5 sing4 jat6 mou5 si4 gaan3 sik6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了趕截止日期，我整天都沒時間吃東西（忍着餓）。
examples.english_sentence: To meet the deadline, I went all day without time to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 暫時止餓、解饞（吃點小食滿足食欲）
english_meaning: to snack to temporarily stave off hunger or satisfy a craving (colloquial Cantonese)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指吃一些小食或零食以暫時止餓或解饞，並非正式的一餐。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to eat a small amount (usually snacks) to temporarily relieve hunger or satisfy a craving, not a full meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家肚餓，買包薯片頂肚癮先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 tou5 ngo6, maai5 baau1 syu4 pin3 ding2 tou5 jan5 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在肚子餓，先買包薯片頂一下肚子。
examples.english_sentence: I'm hungry now — I'll buy a bag of chips to tide me over.

mandarin_meaning: 非常餓；餓得要命
english_meaning: starving; extremely hungry
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，表示餓得非常厲害、難以忍受，類似「餓死了」或「餓到不行」。常在日常對話中使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression indicating extreme hunger or being starving. Used informally in everyday speech, similar to "I'm starving" or "so hungry I could eat a horse."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家頂肚餓，唔想再等，去食嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4gaa1 ding2 tou5 ngo6, m4 soeng2 zoi3 dang2, heoi3 sik6 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在餓到不行，不想再等，去吃東西吧。
examples.english_sentence: I'm starving right now, I don't want to wait any longer — let's go eat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 打完波之後啲人全部都頂肚餓，大家一齊去食嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: daa2 jyun4 bo1 zi1 hau6 di1 jan4 cyun4 bou6 dou1 ding2 tou5 ngo6, daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 heoi3 sik6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 打完球之後大家都餓透了，一起去吃東西吧。
examples.english_sentence: After playing ball everyone was starving, so let's all go get something to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 顶班；替人顶替职务
english_meaning: to cover for someone (take their shift or substitute for their duties)
explanation_mandarin: 口語俚語（香港用法），指臨時替人頂替職務或代人上班（相當於“顶班”“代班”）。
explanation_english: Colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese slang meaning to substitute for someone, especially to cover their work shift or take over a duty temporarily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚身體唔舒服，返唔到工，你可唔可以幫我頂艇？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 san1 tai2 m4 syu1 fuk6, faan1 m4 dou2 gung1, nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 ding2 teng5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚身体不舒服，回不了去上班，你可以帮我顶班吗？
examples.english_sentence: I'm not feeling well tonight and can't get to work — could you cover my shift?

mandarin_meaning: 最高薪酬；合同可獲得的最高工資（常用於體育合同或公司薪資討論）
english_meaning: maximum salary; top pay (the highest salary specified or attainable, often used in sports contracts or company pay discussions)
explanation_mandarin: 指某人所能獲得的最高工資或合約中規定的最高薪酬，常見於體育圈（如頂薪合約）或企業薪酬討論中。
explanation_english: Refers to the highest salary someone can receive or the maximum pay specified in a contract. Commonly used in contexts like sports (e.g., max-salary contracts) or corporate salary discussions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢簽咗一份頂薪合約，成為球隊入面最高人工嘅球員。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 cim1 zo2 jat1 fan6 ding2 san1 hap6 joek3, sing4 wai4 kau4 deoi6 jap6 min6 zeoi3 gou1 jan4 gung1 ge3 kau4 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他簽了一份頂薪合同，成為球隊裡面最高薪的球員。
examples.english_sentence: He signed a max-salary contract and became the highest-paid player on the team.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係球隊嘅頂薪球員，大家都對佢好期待。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 kau4 deoi6 ge3 ding2 san1 kau4 jyun4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 deoi3 keoi5 hou2 kei4 doi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是球隊的頂薪球員，大家都很期待他。
examples.english_sentence: He is the team's top-paid player, and everyone has high expectations of him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我想爭取頂薪，但公司話要再表現先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 zeng1 ceoi2 ding2 san1, daan6 gung1 si1 waa6 jiu3 zoi3 biu2 jin2 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想爭取頂薪，但公司說要再表現才能給。
examples.english_sentence: I want to fight for top pay, but the company says I need to perform more first.

mandarin_meaning: 最高薪點；薪級表上的最高薪資點
english_meaning: top salary point; the maximum pay point on a pay scale
explanation_mandarin: 「頂薪點」指薪級或薪酬表中的最高一級或最高薪資點，通常表示員工已達到可獲得的最高薪酬等級，難以再獲加薪。
explanation_english: “頂薪點” refers to the highest point on a salary/pay scale. It usually means an employee has reached the maximum pay step and is unlikely to receive further salary increases.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家已經去到頂薪點，冇得再加人工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 ji5 ging1 heoi3 dou3 ding2 san1 dim2, mou5 dak1 zoi3 gaa1 jan4 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在已經到達最高薪點，沒辦法再加薪了。
examples.english_sentence: He has already reached the top salary point and can't get any more raises.

mandarin_meaning: 替人提供證詞（常指作假證供）
english_meaning: To give testimony on someone's behalf (often false); to act as a (false) witness or vouch for someone
explanation_mandarin: 「頂證」是粵語俗語，通常指替他人出面作證或提供證詞，常帶有替人作假證供或幫人頂罪的負面含義。也可泛指在口頭上幫人說話作證實。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, "頂證" refers to giving testimony or vouching for someone, often implying providing false testimony or taking the blame for another person. It can also more generally mean testifying or supporting someone's story.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢叫人幫佢頂證，結果畀警方發現。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 giu3 jan4 bong1 keoi5 ding2 zing3, git3 gwo2 bei6 ging2 fong1 faat3 jin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他叫人帮他顶证，結果被警方發現。
examples.english_sentence: He asked someone to vouch for him, and in the end the police discovered it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好幫佢頂證，萬一被捕會有麻煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bong1 keoi5 ding2 zing3, maan6 jat1 bei6 bou6 wui5 jau5 maa4 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要帮他顶证，一旦被捕会有麻烦。
examples.english_sentence: Don't help him by acting as a (false) witness — if you're arrested it'll cause trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 法庭上冇人肯頂證，案件因此無法定罪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 ting4 soeng6 mou5 jan4 hang2 ding2 zing3, on3 gin6 jan1 ci2 mou4 faat3 ding6 zeoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 法庭上没有人肯顶证，案件因此无法定罪。
examples.english_sentence: No one in court was willing to testify on his behalf, so the case couldn't secure a conviction.

mandarin_meaning: 將店鋪或租約等轉讓給他人（尤指店舖頂讓）
english_meaning: to transfer/assign a business or lease (especially a shop tenancy); to hand over business ownership/tenancy
explanation_mandarin: 香港常用詞，指把店舖的經營權、租約、設備等整體轉讓給別人，常見於店舖買賣或租約轉手的情況。
explanation_english: Common in Hong Kong Cantonese; refers to transferring a shop/business including tenancy rights and equipment to another person — often used when selling or handing over a business/lease.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間茶餐廳想頂讓，因為業主退休。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 soeng2 ding2 joeng6, jan1 wai6 jip6 zyu2 teoi1 seoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間茶餐廳想頂讓，因為業主退休。
examples.english_sentence: This cha chaan teng is up for transfer because the owner is retiring.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你有興趣，可以問清楚租約會唔會一齊頂讓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 jau5 hing3 ceoi3, ho2 ji5 man6 cing1 co2 zou1 joek3 wui5 m4 wui5 jat1 cai4 ding2 joeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你有興趣，可以問清楚租約會不會一起頂讓。
