examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 dei6 hok6 haau6 ge3 ling5 zau3 saang1, fu6 zaak3 daai3 ling6 hok6 saang1 wui2 wut6 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是我們學校的學生領袖，負責帶領學生會的活動。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is a student leader at our school, responsible for leading student council activities.

mandarin_meaning: 领军 (lǐngjūn)：带领军队；在某一领域中带头、率领核心力量
english_meaning: to lead troops; to spearhead or head (a group, organization, or effort)
explanation_mandarin: “领军”原指带领军队作战，亦可引申为在某个领域或团队中担当领导、带头或率領核心力量。
explanation_english: Originally refers to commanding or leading troops in battle; figuratively, it means to lead, spearhead, or head a team, organization, or field.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺戰爭期間領軍，指揮作戰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 zin3 zang1 kei4 gaan1 ling5 gwan1, zi2 fai1 zok3 zin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在战争期间领军，指挥作战。
examples.english_sentence: He led the troops during the war, commanding the operations.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間公司由佢領軍，喺市場上表現突出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 gung1 si1 jau4 keoi5 ling5 gwan1, hai2 si5 coeng4 soeng6 biu2 jin6 dat6 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间公司由他领军，在市场上表现突出。
examples.english_sentence: He spearheads the company, which performs outstandingly in the market.

mandarin_meaning: 領取（或取走）宴席菜餚／領走酒席（通常指向酒樓或承辦方取宴席）
english_meaning: to collect/pick up a catered banquet (food) / to take delivery of the banquet dishes
explanation_mandarin: 「領酒席」指到餐廳、酒樓或承辦方處領取宴會的菜餚或確認接收宴席，常見於婚宴或大型聚會的準備流程中。
explanation_english: “領酒席” means going to the restaurant/caterer to collect or take delivery of the banquet dishes for an event (e.g., a wedding). It refers to the act of picking up the catered food or confirming receipt of the banquet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 婚禮前一日要去領酒席。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fan1 lai5 cin4 jat6 jiu3 heoi3 ling5 zau2 zik6。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 婚禮前一天要去取宴席。
examples.english_sentence: We need to go pick up the banquet food one day before the wedding.

mandarin_meaning: 領銜 (lǐng xián)：擔任主要角色或名義上掛頭銜、領導職位
english_meaning: to head or top-bill (a production); to hold a titular position or be named as the lead
explanation_mandarin: 表示在戲劇、電影、活動等中擔任主要或掛名的角色，或在組織中以名義身份擔任某個領導或顧問職務。
explanation_english: Indicates serving as the lead/top-billed performer in a play/film/event, or holding a titular leadership/advisory position (often nominal).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢套劇由佢領銜主演，票房表現好好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tou3 kek6 jau4 keoi5 ling5 haam4 zyu2 jin2, piu3 fong4 biu2 jin6 hou2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這部劇由他領銜主演，票房表現很好。
examples.english_sentence: This drama is headlined by him; its box office performance is very good.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢被邀請做呢個計劃嘅領銜顧問，主要係掛名支持。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei6 jiu1 cing2 zou6 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 ge3 ling5 haam4 gu3 man6, zyu2 jiu3 hai6 gwaa3 ming4 zi1 ci4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被邀請擔任這個計畫的領銜顧問，主要是掛名支持。
examples.english_sentence: He was invited to be the titular advisor of this project, mainly in a nominal/supporting capacity.

mandarin_meaning: 领衔主演
english_meaning: to be top-billed; to star as the lead actor/actress
explanation_mandarin: 指在電影、電視劇或舞台劇等作品中擔任主要角色並被列為主演或領銜出演。
explanation_english: Refers to being credited as the principal actor/actress in a film, TV show, or stage production — to be the headlining or top-billed performer.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次喺部新戲入面領銜主演，表現好好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 hai2 bou6 san1 hei3 jap6 min6 ling5 haam4 zyu2 jin2, biu2 jin6 hou2 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這次在那部新片中領銜主演，表現很好。
examples.english_sentence: He is top-billed in the new movie and gives a great performance.

mandarin_meaning: 领队（团队/旅行团的负责人）
english_meaning: team leader; group leader; tour leader
explanation_mandarin: 指負責帶領、統籌或管理一個隊伍、團體或旅行團的人，可能負責行程安排、安全與協調等工作。
explanation_english: Refers to the person responsible for leading, coordinating, or managing a team, group, or tour — often in charge of itinerary, safety, and group coordination.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋嘅領隊今日唔到，旅程要改動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 ge3 ling5 deoi6 gam1 jat6 m4 dou3, leoi5 cing4 jiu3 goi2 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们的领队今天不到，行程要改动。
examples.english_sentence: Our group leader isn't coming today, so the itinerary needs to be changed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做旅行團嘅領隊已經有十年經驗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 leoi5 hang4 tyun4 ge3 ling5 deoi6 ji5 ging1 jau5 sap6 nin4 ging1 jim6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做旅行团的领队已经有十年经验。
examples.english_sentence: He has ten years of experience as a tour leader.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 領隊要安排集合時間同講解安全事項。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ling5 deoi6 jiu3 ngon1 paai4 zaap6 hap6 si4 gaan3 tung4 gong2 gaai2 on1 cyun4 si6 hong6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 领队要安排集合时间并讲解安全事项。
examples.english_sentence: The leader needs to arrange the meeting time and explain the safety matters.

mandarin_meaning: 领养
english_meaning: to adopt (a child, animal, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 指把沒有血緣關係的兒童或動物等接受到自己家庭撫養或收養。
explanation_english: To take into one's family and raise someone (commonly a child or an animal) who is not biologically related.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋決定領養一隻流浪狗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 kyut3 ding6 ling5 joeng5 jat1 zek3 lau4 long6 gau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们决定领养一只流浪狗。
examples.english_sentence: We decided to adopt a stray dog.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細個嘅時候被人領養，喺新嘅家庭長大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 go3 ge3 si4 hau6 bei6 jan4 ling5 joeng5, hai2 san1 ge3 gaa1 ting4 coeng4 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他小时候被人领养，在新家庭长大。
examples.english_sentence: He was adopted as a child and grew up in a new family.

mandarin_meaning: xié（文言），（多用於複合詞/成語）表示並列、競爭或飛翔；常見於成語「頡頏」，意為勢均力敵
english_meaning: xié (literary); (rarely used alone) conveys notions of competing/soaring; appears in the idiom '頡頏' meaning evenly matched or neck-and-neck
explanation_mandarin: 漢字本義與飛翔、並列、相敵相關，現代漢語中較少單獨使用，常見於成語「頡頏」，用以形容雙方勢均力敵或競相飛翔的景象（文言用法）。
explanation_english: A classical/literary character related to flying or competing. Rarely used alone in modern Chinese; commonly appears in the idiom '頡頏', which describes two parties being evenly matched or competing closely.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字『頡』好少單獨使用，一般出現喺成語『頡頏』入面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 'kit3' hou2 siu2 daan1 duk6 si6 jung6, jat1 baan1 ceot1 jin6 hai2 sing4 jyu5 'kit3 hong4' jap6 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字“頡”很少单独使用，通常出现在成语“頡頏”里。
examples.english_sentence: The character '頡' is rarely used on its own; it usually appears in the idiom '頡頏'.

mandarin_meaning: 颐；下巴；養護、頤養（如「頤養天年」）
english_meaning: chin; to nourish; as in 'to live out one's days in comfort' (e.g. 頤養天年)
explanation_mandarin: 「頤」本義指下巴、下顎，亦有養護、調養的意思，常見於詞語如「頤養」、「頤養天年」，或地名「頤和園」。
explanation_english: The character refers to the chin or lower jaw and can also mean to nourish or care for oneself. It appears in compounds like 頤養 (to nourish) and names such as 頤和園 (Summer Palace).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近去咗頤和園旅遊，覺得好寫意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 heoi3 zo2 ji4 wo4 jyun4 leoi5 jau4, gok3 dak1 hou2 se2 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近去了颐和园旅游，觉得很惬意。
examples.english_sentence: He recently visited the Summer Palace and felt very relaxed.

mandarin_meaning: 摆出高高在上的样子，专横地指挥或命令别人（颐指气使，yí zhǐ qì shǐ）。
english_meaning: to act arrogantly and boss others around; to give orders in an imperious, haughty manner.
explanation_mandarin: 形容一个人态度傲慢、盛气凌人，喜欢发号施令、指挥别人，带有居高临下的感觉。
explanation_english: Describes someone who behaves arrogantly and imperiously, ordering or directing others with a haughty, overbearing attitude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日對員工頤指氣使，好多人都唔鍾意佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 deoi3 jyun4 gung1 ji4 zi2 hei3 si2, hou2 do1 jan4 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常对员工颐指气使，很多人都不喜欢他。
examples.english_sentence: He often bosses the employees around; many people don't like him.

mandarin_meaning: 颐养天年
english_meaning: to enjoy one's remaining years in peace; to live out one's old age in comfort
explanation_mandarin: 意指安享晚年、保養身體，平靜舒適地度過餘生。
explanation_english: Refers to enjoying one's old age in comfort and good health; to spend the remainder of one's life peacefully.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢想頤養天年，唔想再辛苦做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 ji4 joeng5 tin1 nin4, m4 soeng2 zoi3 san1 fu2 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他想颐养天年，不想再辛苦工作。
examples.english_sentence: He wants to enjoy his remaining years in peace and no longer work hard.

mandarin_meaning: 头（身体部位）；首、开始、上端；领导
english_meaning: head (body part); top/beginning; leader
explanation_mandarin: 表示身体的头部；也可以指事物的上端、开始或领导者。在粤语中常见於合成词如“頭先”（刚才）或用作称呼职务的“頭”。
explanation_english: Refers to the physical head; can also mean the top/beginning of something or a leader. In Cantonese it appears in compounds like “頭先” (just now) and as a term for a unit head or boss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頭好痛，要休息下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tau4 hou2 tung3, jiu3 jau1 sik1 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的头很痛，要休息一下。
examples.english_sentence: My head hurts a lot; I need to rest a bit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我哋部門嘅頭，負責統籌工作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 dei6 bou6 mun4 ge3 tau4, fu6 zak1 tung2 cau4 gung1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是我们部门的头，负责统筹工作。
examples.english_sentence: He is the head of our department and is responsible for coordinating the work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頭先落咗好大雨，依家太陽出咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tau4 sin1 lok6 zo2 hou2 daai6 jyu5, ji4 gaa1 taai3 joeng4 ceot1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 刚才下了很大雨，现在太阳出来了。
examples.english_sentence: It rained heavily just now; now the sun has come out.

mandarin_meaning: 頭腦發熱；衝動、急躁
english_meaning: hot-headed; impulsive; short-tempered
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，用來形容一個人容易衝動、情緒激動或做事欠考慮，像是「頭腦發熱」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who is hot-headed or impulsive — prone to acting emotionally or without thinking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢頭㷫，見到啲細事就發火。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tau4 jit6, gin3 dou3 di1 sai3 si6 zau6 faat3 fo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他脾氣急躁，看到小事就發火。
examples.english_sentence: He's hot-headed; he gets angry over small things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好頭㷫，冷靜啲諗下再決定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 tau4 jit6, laang5 zing6 di1 nam2 haa5 zoi3 kyut3 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別衝動，冷靜想一想再決定。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be impulsive; calm down and think before deciding.

mandarin_meaning: 头七
english_meaning: the seventh day after a person's death (traditional memorial ritual)
explanation_mandarin: 在華人傳統習俗中，死者過世後第七天稱為「頭七」，相信亡靈會在這天回來或須接受家人的祭祀，家屬通常會舉行拜祭、燒紙等儀式。
explanation_english: In traditional Chinese custom, the seventh day after a person's death is called 'touqi' (頭七). It is believed the deceased's spirit may return on this day, and families commonly hold memorial rites such as offerings and burning joss paper.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽頭七嗰日，我哋要返屋企拜祭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 tau4 cat1 go2 jat6, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 faan1 uk1 kei2 baai3 zai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈头七那天，我们要回家祭拜。
examples.english_sentence: On my mother's seventh day after death, we have to go home to pay our respects.

mandarin_meaning: 头也不回
english_meaning: without turning back; not even looking back; to leave resolutely
explanation_mandarin: 表示離開或面對某事時毫不回頭，形容態度堅決、果斷或冷漠。
explanation_english: Indicates leaving or facing something without looking back; describes a resolute, decisive, or indifferent attitude.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀人鬧完就頭也不回走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 naau6 jyun4 zau6 tau4 jaa5 bat1 wui4 zau2 zo2
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被骂完就头也不回地走了。
examples.english_sentence: He left without even looking back after being scolded.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢決定搬去外國，頭也不回就開始咗新生活。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kyut3 ding6 bun1 heoi3 ngoi6 gwok3 tau4 jaa5 bat1 wui4 zau6 hoi1 ci2 zo2 san1 sang1 wut6
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他决定搬去国外，头也不回地开始了新生活。
examples.english_sentence: He decided to move abroad and started a new life without looking back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 面對困難，佢頭也不回就衝上前去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: min6 deoi3 kwan3 naan4 keoi5 tau4 jaa5 bat1 wui4 zau6 cung1 soeng5 cin4 heoi3
examples.mandarin_sentence: 面对困难，他头也不回地冲上前去。
examples.english_sentence: Facing the difficulty, he rushed forward without looking back.

mandarin_meaning: 头像 (指用于社交媒体、论坛等的个人图像或照片)
english_meaning: avatar; profile picture; portrait used to represent a person online
explanation_mandarin: 指用作個人辨識或代表的頭部照片或圖像，常見於社交媒體、聊天室、論壇等平台上，也可指畫像或頭部半身像。
explanation_english: Refers to the image or photo used to represent a person (often a headshot or portrait), commonly used as a profile picture on social media, forums, chat apps, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啲社交媒體頭像要換一個。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 di1 se5 gaau1 mui4 tai2 tau4 zoeng6 jiu3 wun6 jat1 go3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的社交媒体头像要换一个。
examples.english_sentence: I need to change my social media profile picture.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅頭像睇落好專業。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 tau4 zoeng6 tai2 lok6 hou2 zyun1 jip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他／她的头像看起来很专业。
examples.english_sentence: Their avatar looks very professional.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上載一張清晰嘅頭像會好啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng5 zoi6 jat1 zoeng1 cing1 sik1 ge3 tau4 zoeng6 wui5 hou2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上传一张清晰的头像会好一些。
examples.english_sentence: Uploading a clear profile picture would be better.

mandarin_meaning: 剛才 / 方才
english_meaning: just now; a moment ago
explanation_mandarin: 表示剛剛發生的動作或情況，指離現在不遠的過去。屬於口語常用詞。
explanation_english: Indicates an action or situation that happened a short time ago (recent past). Commonly used in colloquial Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頭先你有冇見到佢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: tau4 sin1 nei5 jau5 mou5 gin3 dou3 keoi5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剛才你有看到他嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Did you see him just now?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你頭先食咗嘢未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tau4 sin1 sik6 zo2 je5 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你剛才吃東西了嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Did you eat just now?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我頭先已經放咗喺枱上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tau4 sin1 ji5 ging1 fong3 zo2 hai2 toi2 soeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我剛才已經放在桌上了。
examples.english_sentence: I already put it on the table just now.

mandarin_meaning: 從頭到尾；完全、徹底
english_meaning: completely; from start to finish; utterly
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語/俗語，用作副詞，表示從頭到尾或完全、徹底，常用於強調某事物完全發生或完全失敗。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang adverb meaning from start to finish or completely/utterly. Used in informal speech to emphasize totality or completeness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個計劃頭冚都唔掂，要重做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 gai3 waak6 tau4 ham2 dou1 m4 dim6, jiu3 cung4 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個計畫從頭到尾都不行，要重做。
examples.english_sentence: The project is completely not working; it needs to be redone.

mandarin_meaning: 吃第一口湯；首當其衝／當第一個嘗試或承受損失（常指吃虧或承擔風險）
english_meaning: Literally 'the first mouthful of soup'. Figuratively, to be the first to try something or to take the initial hit/lose out; to be the guinea pig or bear the brunt.
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「第一口湯」，引申為當第一個嘗試某事或首當其衝，往往含有會吃虧或承擔風險的意思。常用於不想承擔風險時說「唔想做頭啖湯」。
explanation_english: The phrase literally means 'the first mouthful of soup'. It is used figuratively to describe being the first to try something or to take the initial hit—often implying suffering a loss or bearing risk. Commonly used when someone doesn't want to be the guinea pig.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次嘅新系統有好多問題，冇人想做頭啖湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 ge3 san1 hai6 tung2 jau5 hou2 do1 man6 tai4, mou5 jan4 soeng2 zou6 tau4 daam2 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次的新系統有很多問題，沒有人想當第一個試用（承擔風險）。
examples.english_sentence: The new system has many problems; nobody wants to be the first to try it / be the guinea pig.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做第一個接手呢個項目，結果食咗頭啖湯，賠咗好多錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 wai2 tung4 si6 zou6 dai6 jat1 go3 zip3 sau2 ni1 go3 hoeng6 muk6, git3 gwo2 sik6 zo2 tau4 daam2 tong1, pui4 zo2 hou2 do1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是第一個接手這個項目，結果吃了頭啖湯，賠了很多錢。
examples.english_sentence: He was the first to take on the project and ended up taking the hit, losing a lot of money.

mandarin_meaning: 頭有點暈、頭腦迷糊（口語）
english_meaning: feeling lightheaded, dizzy, or a bit groggy (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語說法，表示頭腦有些暈、迷糊或不清醒，常用於描述疲倦、睡眠不足或酒醉後的狀態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing a state of lightheadedness, dizziness, or grogginess — often used after poor sleep, fatigue, or drinking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝起身頭嗒嗒，可能訓得唔好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 hei2 san1, tau4 daap6 daap6, ho2 nang4 fan3 dak1 m4 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上起來，頭有點暈，可能睡得不好。
examples.english_sentence: I woke up this morning feeling a bit lightheaded — maybe I didn't sleep well.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢飲多咗酒，講嘢都有啲頭嗒嗒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jam2 do1 zo2 zau2, gong2 je5 dou1 jau5 di1 tau4 daap6 daap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他喝多了酒，說話都有點頭暈不清。
examples.english_sentence: He drank too much and is talking a bit groggily/dizzily.

mandarin_meaning: 首場；第一場；開場（演出、比賽或活動的第一個場次）
english_meaning: the opening show / first session / first round (the first slot in a series of events, performances, or matches)
explanation_mandarin: 用於指一系列活動、演出或比賽中的第一場次或開場的場次，常用於演唱會、戲劇、比賽等場合，表明是首個場次或開場時間。
explanation_english: Used to refer to the first session or opening slot in a series of events, performances, or competitions (e.g., concerts, plays, matches). It denotes the initial/first show or round.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋買咗頭場飛，七點半入場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 maai5 zo2 tau4 coeng4 fei1, cat1 dim2 bun3 jap6 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們買了首場的票，七點半入場。
examples.english_sentence: We bought tickets for the opening show; entry at 7:30.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個歌手有兩場演出，頭場係今晚八點開始，尾場係聽日七點半。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 go1 sau2 jau5 loeng5 coeng4 jin2 ceot1, tau4 coeng4 hai6 gam1 maan5 baat3 dim2 hoi1 ci2, mei5 coeng4 hai6 ting1 jat6 cat1 dim2 bun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個歌手有兩場演出，首場是今晚八點開始，尾場是明天七點半。
examples.english_sentence: That singer has two shows; the opening one starts tonight at 8pm, and the closing one is tomorrow at 7:30pm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺比賽嘅頭場就被淘汰咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 bei2 coi3 ge3 tau4 coeng4 zau6 bei6 tou4 taai3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在比賽的首場就被淘汰了。
examples.english_sentence: He was eliminated in the first round of the competition.

mandarin_meaning: 头疼；感到烦恼、压力大、难以应付
english_meaning: to have a headache; to feel stressed/overwhelmed or bothered by something; something is troublesome/complicated
explanation_mandarin: 口语用法，表示生理上的头痛或心理上的烦恼、压力大、被某事弄得不知所措，也可形容事情复杂麻烦。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning either a physical headache or a feeling of being troubled, stressed, or overwhelmed by something; can also describe a complicated or troublesome matter.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我呢排成日頭大，工作太多做唔切。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ni1 paai4 sing4 jat6 tau4 daai6, gung1 zok3 taai3 do1 zou6 m4 cit3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我最近老是覺得頭大，工作太多做不完。
examples.english_sentence: I've been feeling overwhelmed lately; there's too much work to finish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個問題好複雜，真係令我頭大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 man6 tai4 hou2 fuk1 zaap6, zan1 hai6 ling6 ngo5 tau4 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個問題很複雜，真的讓我頭大。
examples.english_sentence: This problem is so complicated; it really makes my head spin.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我成日頭大，可能係因為瞓唔夠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing4 jat6 tau4 daai6, ho2 nang4 hai6 jan1 wai6 fan3 m4 gau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我經常覺得頭大，可能是因為睡眠不足。
examples.english_sentence: I often have headaches/feel overwhelmed; it might be because I'm not getting enough sleep.

mandarin_meaning: 沒腦子／笨、沒主意（口語）
english_meaning: brainless; stupid; clueless (slang, literally 'big head no brain')
explanation_mandarin: 「頭大冇腦」是廣東話的俗語，用來形容一個人愚蠢、沒腦筋或做事糊塗、不考慮後果。字面意思是「頭大但沒有腦」，帶有貶義，常用於口語或非正式場合。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase used to describe someone as brainless, stupid, or thoughtless. Literally 'big head no brain.' It is colloquial and typically derogatory, used in informal contexts to criticize someone's lack of sense or poor decisions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係頭大冇腦，成日忘記重要嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 tau4 daai6 mou5 nou5, sing4 jat6 mong4 gei3 zung6 jiu3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她真的沒腦子，總是忘記重要的事情。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is really brainless, always forgetting important things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試前你仲玩遊戲，真係頭大冇腦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si5 cin4 nei5 zung6 waan2 jau4 hei3, zan1 hai6 tau4 daai6 mou5 nou5!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考試前你還玩遊戲？真是沒腦子！
examples.english_sentence: You're playing games before the exam? That's really brainless!

mandarin_meaning: 髮夾；用來固定頭髮的小夾子（口語）
english_meaning: hair clip; a small clip used to hold hair in place (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，多指固定頭髮的夾子。正式或書面上常用「髮夾」。在香港粵語日常會話中可見。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for a hair clip — a small accessory used to secure hair. The standard term is 髮夾 (faat3 gaap3). Commonly heard in Hong Kong Cantonese speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔小心弄壞咗個頭夾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 nung6 waai6 zo2 go3 tau4 gaap3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不小心弄壞了一個髮夾。
examples.english_sentence: I accidentally broke a hair clip.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝風好大，我差啲冇帶頭夾，頭髮全部飛晒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 fung1 hou2 daai6, ngo5 caa1 di1 mou5 daai3 tau4 gaap3, tau4 faat3 cyun4 bou6 fei1 saai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上風很大，我差點沒帶髮夾，頭髮全都被吹亂了。
examples.english_sentence: This morning the wind was strong; I almost forgot my hair clip and my hair was all blown messy.

mandarin_meaning: 头奖；最高奖（“奬”為“獎”的異體字）
english_meaning: first prize; jackpot; the top prize
explanation_mandarin: 指比賽或抽獎中的最高獎項，即獲得最高獎賞或頭等獎。書寫時“奬”為“獎”的異體字，口語常用於彩票、比賽、抽獎等情境。
explanation_english: Refers to the highest prize in a competition or lottery — the top award or jackpot. The character 奬 is a variant of 獎; commonly used in spoken contexts for lotteries, contests, and raffles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果今次中咗頭奬，就可以買間樓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 gam1 ci3 zung1 zo2 tau4 zoeng2, zau6 ho2 ji5 maai5 gaan1 lau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果这次中了头奖，就可以买房子。
examples.english_sentence: If I win the jackpot this time, I can buy a house.

mandarin_meaning: 擺架子；裝腔作勢；擺威風
english_meaning: to put on airs; act high-and-mighty; show off authority
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，形容一個人擺出高人一等或顯示權勢、裝腔作勢的態度，通常帶貶義。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who puts on airs, acts arrogantly, or displays their authority/power. Usually has a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日頭威頭勢，大家都唔鐘意同佢一齊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 tau4 wai1 tau4 sai3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3 tung4 keoi5 jat1 cai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天擺架子，大家都不喜歡跟他在一起。
examples.english_sentence: He's always putting on airs; nobody likes being around him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度頭威頭勢，大家平等傾偈就得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 tau4 wai1 tau4 sai3, daai6 gaa1 ping4 dang2 king1 gai2 zau6 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別在這兒擺架子，大家平等地聊就行。
examples.english_sentence: Don't act all high-and-mighty here—just talk with everyone as equals.

mandarin_meaning: 笨蛋；傻瓜（俚語）
english_meaning: a fool; an idiot (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，用來罵人笨或做傻事，語氣帶貶義。屬口語、非正式用法，來源不明或方言色彩濃厚。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese slang term used to call someone a fool or describe foolish behavior. Informal and derogatory; likely of regional/dialect origin.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係頭婄，成日做啲蠢嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 tau4 mau4, sing4 jat6 zou6 di1 ceon2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是個笨蛋，總是做些愚蠢的事。
examples.english_sentence: He's really an idiot; he always does stupid things.

mandarin_meaning: 頭尾；始末，從頭到尾
english_meaning: the beginning and the end; the whole story or whole sequence; from start to finish
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用法，指事情的前因後果或整個過程（從頭到尾）。也可用來問該如何處理結果或總結。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression referring to the beginning and end of something or the whole sequence (from start to finish). It can also be used when asking about the outcome or how to handle the situation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講吓頭尾畀我聽，點解會咁呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 haa5 tau4 mei5 bei2 ngo5 teng1, dim2 gaai2 wui5 gam2 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 把事情的頭尾告訴我，為什麼會這樣？
examples.english_sentence: Tell me the whole story — why did this happen?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頭尾都係佢嘅錯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tau4 mei5 dou1 hai6 keoi5 ge3 co3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 始終都是他的錯。
examples.english_sentence: It was his fault from start to finish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頭尾點算？你講吓先。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tau4 mei5 dim2 syun3? nei5 gong2 haa5 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 到底怎麼辦？你先說說。
examples.english_sentence: So what should we do? You say it first.

mandarin_meaning: 頭痛欲裂
english_meaning: splitting headache; head feels like it's going to split
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容頭痛得非常厲害，好像頭要裂開一樣，相當於普通話「頭痛欲裂」。
explanation_english: Used to describe an extremely severe headache, as if the head is splitting; equivalent to the Mandarin idiom '頭痛欲裂' and the English expression 'splitting headache'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日頭崩額裂，痛到要即刻食止痛藥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tau4-baang1-ngok6-lit3, tung3 dou3 jiu3 zik1-haak1 sik6 zi2-tung3 joek6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天頭痛欲裂，痛得要立刻吃止痛藥。
examples.english_sentence: My head is splitting today; it's so painful I need to take painkillers immediately.

mandarin_meaning: 头巾
english_meaning: headscarf; headkerchief; bandana; head wrap
explanation_mandarin: 包在頭部或用來遮蓋頭髮或保暖的布料或配件，常見於日常防寒、運動或作為服飾裝飾。
explanation_english: A piece of cloth worn on or around the head to cover the hair or keep the head warm; used for warmth, sport, or as a fashion accessory.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢戴住條頭巾去跑步。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daai3 zyu6 tiu4 tau4 gan1 heoi3 paau2 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她戴着头巾去跑步。
examples.english_sentence: He/she wore a headscarf to go running.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 冬天用頭巾包住耳仔會暖啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dung1 tin1 jung6 tau4 gan1 baau1 zyu6 ji5 zai2 wui5 nyun5 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 冬天用头巾包住耳朵会暖一些。
examples.english_sentence: Wrapping your ears with a headscarf in winter keeps them warmer.

mandarin_meaning: 前廳；正廳（住宅的入門或主要接待空間）
english_meaning: front hall; main reception hall (the principal hall near the entrance of a house)
explanation_mandarin: 指傳統華人住宅入門處的廳堂，通常用來接待客人、擺放供桌或作日常活動的主要空間。
explanation_english: Refers to the front or main hall of a traditional Chinese house, typically used to receive guests, place an ancestral/offerings table, or serve as a primary living/reception space.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老屋嘅頭廳通常係用嚟接待客人同擺供桌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 uk1 ge3 tau4 teng1 tung1 soeng4 hai6 jung6 lai4 zip3 doi6 haak3 jan4 tung4 baai2 gung1 zoek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老房子的頭廳通常用來接待客人和擺放供桌。
examples.english_sentence: The front hall of an old house is usually used to receive guests and place an ancestral/offerings table.

mandarin_meaning: 頭腦發蒙 / 呆住 / 發愣
english_meaning: dazed; stunned; spaced out; light-headed
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，用來形容頭腦昏沉、發愣或被嚇到一時呆住的狀態。帶有擬聲和口語色彩，常用於日常會話。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing a dazed, stunned, or spaced-out state of mind. It is onomatopoeic and commonly used in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到個消息之後，成個人頭愕愕，唔知點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 dou3 go3 siu1 sik1 zi1 hau6, seng4 go3 jan4 tau4 ngok6 ngok6, m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他聽到這個消息後，整個人發愣了，不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: After he heard the news, he was completely dazed and didn't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 正室；大房（在多妻或大家庭中位居首位的妻子或家族分支）
english_meaning: principal wife; main/first wife (the primary spouse or main household branch in a polygamous or extended family)
explanation_mandarin: 「頭房」在粵語語境中多用以指家中位居首位的妻子或主要的家族分支，尤其見於傳統或過去存在多妻情況的家庭。也可泛指大家庭中佔重要地位的分支。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, 頭房 refers to the principal or first wife, or the main household branch in an extended/polygamous family. It is often used in historical/traditional contexts to denote the spouse or branch with senior status.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺舊時嘅大家庭，頭房通常有優先繼承權。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gau6 si4 ge3 daai6 gaa1 ting4, tau4 fong2 tung1 soeng4 jau5 jau1 sin1 gai3 sing4 kyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在旧时的大家庭，头房通常有优先继承权。
examples.english_sentence: In old extended families, the principal wife usually had priority in inheritance rights.

mandarin_meaning: 頭道/初榨（油或醬油），即第一次榨取出的油或第一批豉油，通常風味較濃、品質較佳。
english_meaning: first-press (oil or soy sauce); the initial extraction (often considered premium and more aromatic).
explanation_mandarin: 「頭抽」在粵語常用於描述食用油（如麻油）或豉油的「頭道榨取」，意指第一遍擠壓或提取出來的油/醬油，風味和香氣較佳，屬於較高級的產品標示。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "頭抽" refers to the first extraction/pressing of an oil (e.g., sesame oil) or soy sauce. It denotes the initial batch, which is typically more aromatic and considered higher quality.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢支麻油係頭抽，炒菜落少少就已經夠香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zek3 maa4 jau4 hai6 tau4cau1, caau2 coi3 lok6 siu2 siu2 zau6 ji5 ging1 gau3 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這瓶麻油是頭抽，炒菜只要放一點就很香。
examples.english_sentence: This bottle of sesame oil is first-pressed; you only need a little when stir-frying for a strong aroma.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做生魚片嘅醬油我哋會用頭抽，味道清鮮啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 saang1 jyu4 pin2 ge3 zoeng3 jau4 ngo5 dei6 wui5 jung6 tau4cau1, mei6 dou6 cing1 sin1 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做生魚片的醬油我們會用頭抽，味道比較清鮮。
examples.english_sentence: For sashimi, we use first-pressed soy sauce; the flavor is fresher.

mandarin_meaning: 很厲害；非常出色
english_meaning: very good; excellent; outstanding
explanation_mandarin: 「頭掂」是香港廣東話的口語/俚語，用來稱讚某人或某事很厲害、表現出色或很能幹。
explanation_english: “頭掂” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang used to praise someone or something as very capable, excellent, or outstanding.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做得頭掂喎，老闆一定會讚你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 dak1 tau4 dim6 wo3, lou5 baan2 jat1 ding6 wui5 zaan3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你做得很棒，老闆一定會讚你。
examples.english_sentence: You did a great job; the boss will definitely praise you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次比賽佢表現得最頭掂，攞咗第一名。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 bei2 coi3 keoi5 biu2 jin6 dak1 zeoi3 tau4 dim6, lo2 zo2 dai6 jat1 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次比賽他表現得最出色，拿了第一名。
examples.english_sentence: He performed the best in this competition and won first place.

mandarin_meaning: 捶頭；捶打頭部；（口語）形容因後悔、懊惱或沮喪而懊悔自責
english_meaning: to pound/beat one's head; to bang one's head (physically); figuratively, to feel extreme regret or frustration and beat oneself up
explanation_mandarin: 「頭搥」可指用手或拳頭拍打或捶打自己的頭部；引申為因後悔、懊惱或氣惱而自責、懊悔的表現或動作。屬口語用法。
explanation_english: Literally, to hit or pound one's own head. Figuratively used to describe strong feelings of regret, frustration, or self-reproach. This is colloquial usage.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做錯嘢之後成日頭搥，覺得好後悔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 co3 je5 zi1 hau6 sing4 jat6 tau4 ceoi1, gok3 dak1 hou2 hau6 fui3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做錯事之後一直在捶頭，覺得很後悔。
examples.english_sentence: After he made the mistake, he kept pounding his head, feeling very regretful.

mandarin_meaning: 有點頭暈、頭腦不太清醒（口語）
english_meaning: a bit dizzy/woozy; feeling lightheaded (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「頭擰擰」為廣東話口語說法，多用來形容頭有點暈或腦袋不太清楚。書寫上有時會用「頭暈暈」，但口語裡也會出現「擰」作為發音替代或方言寫法。
explanation_english: “頭擰擰” is a colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe feeling a little dizzy or lightheaded. In writing people often use 「頭暈暈」, but 「擰」 can appear in spoken forms or dialectal spellings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家頭擰擰，可能係冇瞓夠覺。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 tau4 ning2 ning2, ho2 nang4 hai6 mou5 fan3 gau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在有點頭暈，可能是沒睡夠覺。
examples.english_sentence: I'm feeling a bit dizzy right now; maybe I didn't get enough sleep.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺車上坐太耐會令你頭擰擰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 ce1 soeng5 co5 taai3 noi6 wui5 ling6 nei5 tau4 ning2 ning2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在車上坐太久會讓你有點頭暈。
examples.english_sentence: Sitting in the car too long can make you feel a bit dizzy.

mandarin_meaning: 头昏脑胀（头晕、头脑昏沉）
english_meaning: dizzy and foggy-headed; light-headed with a heavy or muddled feeling in the head
explanation_mandarin: 表示頭腦昏沉、頭暈或感到腦袋不清楚，常因疲勞、熬夜、壓力或生病而引起。
explanation_english: Describes a state of dizziness or a foggy, muddled head. Often caused by tiredness, lack of sleep, stress, or illness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我昨晚捱夜寫報告，今日成日頭昏腦脹，做唔到嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zok6 maan5 aai4 je6 se2 bou3 gou3, gam1 jat6 seng4 jat6 tau4 fan1 nou5 zoeng3, zou6 m4 dou2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我昨晚熬夜写报告，今天整天头昏脑胀，做不了事。
examples.english_sentence: I stayed up late last night writing a report; today I'm dizzy and foggy-headed and can't get anything done.

mandarin_meaning: 头晕
english_meaning: dizzy; lightheaded
explanation_mandarin: 感觉头部晕眩、眼前发黑或失去平衡，常见于疲劳、低血糖、血压波动或中暑等情况。
explanation_english: A sensation of dizziness or lightheadedness—feeling faint, unsteady, or as if the surroundings are spinning; often caused by fatigue, low blood sugar, blood pressure changes, or heatstroke.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家覺得好頭暈，要坐低休息一下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 gok3 dak1 hou2 tau4 wan4, jiu3 co5 dai1 jau1 sik1 jat1 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我现在觉得很头晕，要坐下休息一下。
examples.english_sentence: I feel very dizzy right now; I need to sit down and rest a bit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 天氣太熱，我有啲頭暈，可能係中暑嘅徵狀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tin1 hei3 taai3 jit6, ngo5 jau5 di1 tau4 wan4, ho2 nang4 hai6 zung1 syu2 ge3 zing1 zong6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 天气太热，我有点头晕，可能是中暑的征兆。
examples.english_sentence: The weather is too hot; I'm a bit dizzy—maybe it's a sign of heatstroke.

mandarin_meaning: 頭暈／頭昏（感到頭腦不清醒、暈眩）
english_meaning: feeling dizzy; light-headed; woozy
explanation_mandarin: 口語化的粵語表達，用來形容感到頭腦不清醒、暈眩或有點想要暈倒的感覺，通常為暫時性的不適。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression used to describe feeling dizzy, light-headed, or woozy—typically a temporary sensation of unsteadiness or faintness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家頭暈暈，想坐低休息一下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 tau4 wan1 wan1, soeng2 co5 dai1 jau1 sik1 jat1 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在頭暈暈，想坐下休息一下。
examples.english_sentence: I'm feeling a bit dizzy right now; I want to sit down and rest for a bit.

mandarin_meaning: 头晕眼花
english_meaning: dizzy and having blurred vision; lightheaded; feeling overwhelmed or disoriented
explanation_mandarin: 表示頭腦暈眩、視力模糊或感覺不穩，有時也用來形容因疲勞、驚訝或事物繁多而感到混亂、無所適從。
explanation_english: Describes a state of dizziness and blurred vision or lightheadedness; can also be used figuratively to mean feeling overwhelmed, confused, or dazzled by too many things or sudden shock.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我起身太快，頭暈眼花，要坐低休息下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hei2 san1 taai3 faai3, tau4 wan4 ngaan5 faa1, jiu3 co5 dai1 jau1 sik1 haa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我起身太快，头晕眼花，要坐下休息一下。
examples.english_sentence: I stood up too quickly and felt dizzy and lightheaded; I need to sit down and rest for a bit.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 坐完雲霄飛車我頭暈眼花。
examples.jyutping_sentence: co5 jyun4 wan4 siu1 fei1 ce1 ngo5 tau4 wan4 ngaan5 faa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 坐完过山车我头晕眼花。
examples.english_sentence: After the roller coaster I felt dizzy and lightheaded.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司突然而來咁多變動，老細講到我頭暈眼花，唔知點做最好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 dat6 jin4 ji4 loi4 gam2 do1 bin3 dung6, lou5 sai3 gong2 dou3 ngo5 tau4 wan4 ngaan5 faa1, m4 zi1 dim2 zou6 zeoi3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司突然來了這麼多變動，老闆說得我頭暈眼花，不知道該怎麼做。
examples.english_sentence: So many sudden changes at work left me dazed and confused by what the boss said; I don't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 頭暈、全身乏力（感到虛弱或想昏厥）
english_meaning: feeling dizzy and physically weak (lightheaded, faint, or generally unwell)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，形容人感到頭昏、頭暈，同時全身無力、可能出汗或想暈厥的不適狀態，常用來描述暫時性的身體不適。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression describing a state of dizziness and general physical weakness—often with sweating, faintness, or lightheadedness. Commonly used to describe a temporary feeling of being unwell.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日行咗成日，宜家覺得頭暈身㷫，要休息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 haang4 zo2 sing4 jat6, ji4 gaa1 gok3 dak1 tau4 wan1 san1 zaap6, jiu3 jau1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天走了一整天，現在覺得頭暈、全身乏力，要休息。
examples.english_sentence: I walked around all day today; now I feel dizzy and weak all over and need to rest.

mandarin_meaning: 擺架子；（指人）有架子、擺出高人一等的樣子
english_meaning: putting on airs; having an arrogant or pretentious attitude
explanation_mandarin: 「頭架」是廣東話口語，指一個人擺出傲慢或自以為高人一等的態度，也可說某人有「頭架」。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, '頭架' refers to an air of arrogance or a pretentious attitude—i.e., someone 'putting on airs'. It is commonly used as a noun describing that manner.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近有啲頭架，唔肯同人傾偈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 jau5 di1 tau4 gaa3, m4 hang2 tung4 jan4 king1 gai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近有點擺架子，不肯和別人聊天。
examples.english_sentence: He's been putting on airs lately and won't chat with others.

mandarin_meaning: 头条 (tóutiáo) — 新闻中的主要标题或头版新闻
english_meaning: headline; front-page news; top story
explanation_mandarin: 指報紙、媒體或網絡上最重要或最顯著的新聞標題（頭版）。口語中也可用於短語「上頭條」，表示成為頭條新聞或被媒體大力報導。
explanation_english: Refers to the most prominent news headline or front-page story in newspapers, media, or online. In colloquial use, the phrase "make the headlines" (e.g. 上頭條) means to become headline news.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單醜聞即刻上咗頭條。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 cau2 man4 zik1 hak1 soeng5 zo2 tau4 tiu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這宗醜聞立刻成了頭條。
examples.english_sentence: This scandal immediately made the headlines.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日報紙嘅頭條都係講緊經濟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 bou3 zi2 ge3 tau4 tiu4 dou1 hai6 gong2 gan2 ging1 zai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天報紙的頭條都是在談論經濟。
examples.english_sentence: The newspaper's front-page headlines are all about the economy today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢想靠緋聞上頭條。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng2 kaau3 fei1 man4 soeng5 tau4 tiu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他想靠緋聞上頭條。
examples.english_sentence: He/She wants to use a scandal to make the headlines.

mandarin_meaning: 頭槌；用頭猛撞（作為攻擊的動作）
english_meaning: headbutt (the act of striking someone or something with one's head)
explanation_mandarin: 表示用頭部猛撞某人或某物的行為，通常指作為攻擊或犯規的動作；亦可作為名詞指該次動作（頭槌）。
explanation_english: Refers to the action of striking someone or something with one's head, usually as an attack or foul; can be used as a noun (a headbutt) or a verb (to headbutt).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺比賽入面用頭槌撞向對手，結果被罰出場。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 bei2 coi3 jap6 min6 jung6 tau4 ceoi4 zong6 hoeng3 deoi3 sau2, git3 gwo2 bei6 fat6 ceot1 coeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在比賽中用頭槌撞向對手，結果被罰出場。
examples.english_sentence: He headbutted his opponent during the match and was sent off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友唔好用頭槌去玩，會好危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 m4 hou2 jung6 tau4 ceoi4 heoi3 waan2, wui5 hou2 ngai4 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友不要用頭槌玩，會很危險。
examples.english_sentence: Kids shouldn't play by headbutting; it's dangerous.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）頭、腦袋；頭腦、智力
english_meaning: head; skull; (colloquial) mind or brain/intelligence
explanation_mandarin: 「頭殼」是廣東話的口語用詞，可指人的頭或頭顱（物理上），也常用來指頭腦、腦力或智慧（比喻用法）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for the head or skull (literal) and often used figuratively to mean the mind, brain, or mental ability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個頭殼好使，成日諗到新主意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 tau4 hok3 hou2 si2, sing4 jat6 lam2 dou3 san1 zyu2 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的頭腦很靈活，經常想出新主意。
examples.english_sentence: He has a clever mind and often comes up with new ideas.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日頭殼好痛，唔想做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 tau4 hok3 hou2 tung3, m4 soeng2 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天頭很痛，不想做事。
examples.english_sentence: My head hurts today; I don't feel like working.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你頭殼有問題咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tau4 hok3 jau5 man6 tai4 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你的腦子有問題嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Is there something wrong with your head?

mandarin_meaning: （口語）形容人固執、倔強、頑固
english_meaning: stubborn; pig-headed; obstinate (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「頭殼頂」在廣東話中多用來形容一個人很固執、死腦筋、不肯變通。常與「硬」連用成「頭殼頂硬」以加強語氣。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "頭殼頂" is used colloquially to describe someone who is stubborn or pig-headed and unwilling to change. It is often intensified as "頭殼頂硬."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好頭殼頂，乜嘢人講都唔聽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 tau4 hok3 ding2, mat1 je5 jan4 gong2 dou1 m4 teng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的很固執，別人怎麼說都不聽。
examples.english_sentence: He's really stubborn; he doesn't listen to what anyone says.

mandarin_meaning: 头发；头上的毛
english_meaning: hair (on the head); head hair
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指人頭上的毛，與「頭髮」同義，常見於粵語日常會話中。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese term referring to the hair on a person's head, synonymous with '頭髮' (toufa) in Mandarin; commonly used in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你洗咗頭未？你啲頭毛仲濕住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sai2 zo2 tau4 mei6? nei5 di1 tau4 mou4 zung6 sap1 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你洗头了吗？你的头发還是濕的。
examples.english_sentence: Did you wash your hair yet? Your hair is still wet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲頭毛開始變白，係唔係老咗？
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 tau4 mou4 hoi1 ci2 bin3 baak6, hai6 m4 hai6 lou5 zo2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的头发開始變白，是不是老了？
examples.english_sentence: His hair is starting to turn white—has he gotten older?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日剪頭毛啦，我啲頭毛太長唔方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ting1 jat6 zin2 tau4 mou4 laa1, ngo5 di1 tau4 mou4 taai3 coeng4 m4 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天剪頭髮吧，我的頭髮太長不方便。
examples.english_sentence: I'll get a haircut tomorrow—my hair is too long and inconvenient.

mandarin_meaning: 笨蛋；傻瓜（粗俗俚語）
english_meaning: idiot; fool (slang, derogatory)
explanation_mandarin: 「頭泥」是廣東話的俚語，帶有貶義，用來形容或罵人笨、頭腦遲鈍，也可作形容詞或名詞使用，語氣較粗俗。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang insult meaning someone is stupid or slow-witted. It can be used as a noun or adjective and is colloquial/pejorative.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你做咩咁頭泥㗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zou6 me1 gam2 tau4 nai4 gaa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你為什麼這麼笨？
examples.english_sentence: Why are you being such an idiot?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢考到咁低分，真係頭泥喎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haau2 dou3 gam2 dai1 fan1, zan1 hai6 tau4 nai4 wo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他考了這麼低的分，真是個笨蛋。
examples.english_sentence: He got such a low score — he's really an idiot.

mandarin_meaning: 头注；首次下注、首笔赌注
english_meaning: initial bet; opening wager; first stake
explanation_mandarin: 指在赌博、投注或博彩活动中下的第一笔赌注或开局下注。
explanation_english: Refers to the first bet placed in a gambling or betting context—the opening wager or initial stake.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你落咗頭注未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 lok6 zo2 tau4 zyu3 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你下了头注了吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you placed the initial bet yet?

mandarin_meaning: 头一炷香；开始的阶段；比喻持续时间很短
english_meaning: the first stick of incense; the beginning phase; figuratively a very short-lived period
explanation_mandarin: 原指祭祀或拜神時焚燒的第一炷香；在口語中常用來比喻開始的時期或形容某事持續時間很短（例如：只持續一會兒、很快結束）。
explanation_english: Literally the first stick of incense burned during worship or a ceremony; colloquially used metaphorically to mean the initial stage or something that lasts only a short time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份工我連頭炷香都唔夠就畀炒咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gung1 ngo5 lin4 tau4 zyu3 hoeng1 dou1 m4 gau3 zau6 bei2 caau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份工作我連頭一炷香都不夠就被炒了。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't even last a short while at that job before I got fired.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲承諾可能只係頭炷香，之後根本冇跟進。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 sing4 nok6 ho2 nang4 zi2 hai6 tau4 zyu3 hoeng1, zi1 hau6 gan1 bun2 mou5 gan1 zeon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些承諾可能只是頭一炷香，之後根本沒有跟進。
examples.english_sentence: Those promises might be just for show at the start and there was no follow-up afterwards.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 拜神嗰陣，廟裏會先焚頭炷香。
examples.jyutping_sentence: baai3 san4 go2 zan6, miu6 leoi5 wui5 sin1 fan4 tau4 zyu3 hoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 拜神的時候，廟裡會先焚燒頭炷香。
examples.english_sentence: When worshipping, the temple will first burn the initial stick of incense.

mandarin_meaning: 头灯；车头灯；头戴式手电筒
english_meaning: headlight; headlamp (vehicle headlight or wearable headlamp)
explanation_mandarin: 指安裝在車頭的照明燈（車頭燈），或可戴在頭上用作照明的頭燈/頭戴式手電筒。
explanation_english: Refers to the light mounted on the front of a vehicle (headlight), or a wearable lamp worn on the head for hands-free illumination (headlamp).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夜晚開車記得開頭燈。
examples.jyutping_sentence: je6 maan5 hoi1 ce1 gei3 dak1 hoi1 tau4 dang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 晚上开车记得打开车头灯。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to turn on the headlights when driving at night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 行山嗰陣我帶咗個頭燈，好方便，唔使拎手電筒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haang4 saan1 go2 zan6 ngo5 daai3 zo2 go3 tau4 dang1, hou2 fong1 bin6, m4 sai2 ling1 sau2 din6 tung2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 爬山的时候我带了一个头灯，很方便，不用拿手电筒。
examples.english_sentence: I brought a headlamp when hiking; it's convenient so I don't have to carry a flashlight.

mandarin_meaning: 头版：报纸或新闻媒体的首页，通常刊载最重要或最引人注目的新闻。
english_meaning: front page; the first page of a newspaper or media outlet, usually featuring the most important or eye-catching news.
explanation_mandarin: 指報紙、雜誌或新聞網站的第一版面，通常放置最重要或最受關注的新聞或頭條。
explanation_english: Refers to the first page or main page of a newspaper, magazine, or news site, typically displaying the most significant or attention-grabbing stories.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢條新聞上咗頭版。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 tiu4 san1 man4 soeng5 zo2 tau4 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这条新闻上了头版。
examples.english_sentence: This news story made the front page.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日嗰張報紙頭版係一宗大醜聞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 go2 zoeng1 bou3 zi2 tau4 baan2 hai6 jat1 zung1 daai6 cau2 man4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天那张报纸的头版是一宗大丑闻。
examples.english_sentence: The front page of today's paper is about a major scandal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 記者話如果冇重大消息就唔會上頭版。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gei3 ze2 waa6 jyu4 gwo2 mou5 zung6 daai6 siu1 sik1 zau6 m4 wui5 soeng5 tau4 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 记者说如果没有重大消息就不会上头版。
examples.english_sentence: Reporters say that without major news, it won't make the front page.

mandarin_meaning: 開業首日；（習俗上）開市或年初營業的第一天，常有慶祝或請客的習慣
english_meaning: the first business day / opening day (especially at the start of the year); often celebrated with treats or a meal
explanation_mandarin: 「頭牙」是廣東話俗語，常指商戶或公司在新年或開張時的第一個營業日，僱主或店主常會在這日請員工或客人吃飯、慶祝，象徵開市興旺。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '頭牙' refers to the first business/opening day (often at the start of a new year). Employers or shop owners commonly treat staff or customers to a meal or small celebration on this day as a sign of prosperity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日係鋪頭嘅頭牙，老闆請大家食飯慶祝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 hai6 pou3 tau4 ge3 tau4 ngaa4, lou5 baan2 cing2 daai6 gaa1 sik6 faan6 hing3 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天是店裡的頭牙，老闆請大家吃飯慶祝。
examples.english_sentence: Today is the shop's 'tou4 ngaa4' (first business day), and the boss is treating everyone to a meal to celebrate.

mandarin_meaning: 首個犧牲者；替罪羊
english_meaning: first casualty; scapegoat
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，指在事件中第一個被責備、懲罰或犧牲的人，類似「替罪羊」或「首當其衝」的意思。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for the person who becomes the first to be blamed, punished, or sacrificed in an incident; similar to 'scapegoat' or 'first casualty.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次計劃失敗，佢做咗頭牲畀大家鬧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 gai3 waak6 sat1 baai6, keoi5 zou6 zo2 tau4 saang1 bei2 daai6 gaa1 naau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這次計劃失敗，他成了第一個被大家責備的人。
examples.english_sentence: The project failed this time; he became the first person to be blamed by everyone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做頭牲，遇到問題要即刻講清楚責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 tau4 saang1, jyu6 dou3 man6 tai4 jiu3 zik1 hak1 gong2 cing1 co2 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別當替罪羊，遇到問題要立即把責任講清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be the scapegoat; when problems arise, state the responsibilities clearly right away.

mandarin_meaning: 頭獎 (tóu jiǎng)
english_meaning: jackpot; first prize; top prize
explanation_mandarin: 指比賽、抽獎或彩票中最高的獎項或最高獎金，例如彩票的最高獎。
explanation_english: The top prize in a competition, raffle, or lottery; the highest award or payout (jackpot).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗張彩票，中咗頭獎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 zoeng1 coi2-piu3, zung2 zo2 tau4-zoeng2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他買了一張彩票，中了頭獎。
examples.english_sentence: He bought a lottery ticket and won the jackpot.

mandarin_meaning: 首班；第一班（班次或輪班）
english_meaning: the first shift or the first scheduled run (e.g., first bus/train)
explanation_mandarin: 指一天中最早的一班工作班次或交通工具的首班車次，例如早上的第一班巴士或火車。
explanation_english: Refers to the earliest shift of the day or the first scheduled service of a vehicle (e.g., the first bus or train of the day).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我聽日早上要返頭班。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ting1 jat6 zou2 soeng6 jiu3 faan1 tau4 baan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我明天早上要上早班。
examples.english_sentence: I have to work the morning (first) shift tomorrow.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頭班車幾點開？
examples.jyutping_sentence: tau4 baan1 ce1 gei2 dim2 hoi1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 首班车/头班车几点开？
examples.english_sentence: What time does the first bus/train leave?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔鐘意做頭班，因為要好早起身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 zung1 ji3 zou6 tau4 baan1, jan1 wai6 jiu3 hou2 zou2 hei2 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不喜欢上早班，因为要很早起床。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't like working the early shift because he has to get up very early.

mandarin_meaning: 令人頭疼／棘手、讓人困惑
english_meaning: puzzling; troublesome; a head-scratcher
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，字面上是「頭癢/頭要抓」，引申為某事讓人覺得麻煩、難以處理或令人困惑。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning 'head-itch' or 'head-scratching'. It describes something that is troublesome, awkward to deal with, or puzzling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事真係幾頭痕， 我唔知點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 zan1 hai6 gei2 tau4 han4, ngo5 m4 zi1 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事真有點令人頭疼，我不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: This matter is really a bit puzzling/troublesome; I don't know what to do.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日提出好多野但又互相矛盾，好頭痕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 tai4 ceot1 hou2 do1 je5 daan6 jau6 wu6 soeng1 maau4 deon6, hou2 tau4 han4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是提出很多要求但又互相矛盾，真讓人頭疼。
examples.english_sentence: He always brings up many requests that contradict each other — it's really a headache.

mandarin_meaning: 头痛
english_meaning: headache; a troublesome problem or nuisance
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名词（亦可比喻用作形容词或动词）
partOfSpeech_english: noun (can be used figuratively to mean a nuisance/problem)
explanation_mandarin: 指頭部的疼痛，也可比喻為令人煩惱、麻煩或難以處理的問題。
explanation_english: Refers to pain in the head (a headache). Figuratively, it describes a troublesome issue or nuisance that causes difficulty or worry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家頭痛，要唔要休息一下？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 tau4 tung3, jiu3 m4 jiu3 jau1 sik1 jat1 haa5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我现在头痛，要不要休息一下？
examples.english_sentence: I have a headache right now — should I rest for a bit?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個客戶真係頭痛，成日改要求。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 haak3 wu6 zan1 hai6 tau4 tung3, seng4 jat6 goi2 jiu1 kau4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个客户真是让人头痛，总是改要求。
examples.english_sentence: This client is really a headache — always changing the requirements.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日頭痛，可能係壓力太大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 tau4 tung3, ho2 nang4 hai6 aat3 lik6 taai3 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常头痛，可能是压力太大。
examples.english_sentence: He often gets headaches; it might be due to too much stress.

jyutping: tau4 tung3 ji1 tau4, goek3 tung3 ji1 goek3
mandarin_meaning: 遇到什麼問題就局部處理、各自解決，而不從根本上或整體上解決問題。
english_meaning: To deal with problems on a case-by-case or ad hoc basis; treating symptoms only and not addressing the root causes; patchwork solutions.
explanation_mandarin: 形容只針對個別問題作臨時或局部處理，缺乏整體或長遠的解決辦法，往往治標不治本。
explanation_english: Describes handling issues individually and superficially rather than addressing underlying or systemic causes — an ad hoc, piecemeal approach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司只係頭痛醫頭，腳痛醫腳，唔會做長遠嘅計劃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 zi2 hai6 tau4 tung3 ji1 tau4, goek3 tung3 ji1 goek3, m4 wui5 zou6 coeng4 jyun5 ge3 gai3 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司只是头痛医头、脚痛医脚，不会做长远的计划。
examples.english_sentence: The company only treats problems ad hoc and doesn't make any long-term plans.

mandarin_meaning: 頭皮（頭部的皮膚）；口語上也可指感到毛骨悚然或發麻的感覺
english_meaning: scalp (the skin on the head); colloquially used to describe a tingling/creepy feeling (e.g. 'scalp tingling')
explanation_mandarin: 「頭皮」字面上指頭部的皮膚，即頭皮。在口語中常出現像「頭皮發麻」的用法，用來形容因害怕、緊張、毛骨悚然或不舒服而產生的刺麻感。
explanation_english: Literally refers to the skin of the head (scalp). In colloquial Cantonese it is often used in expressions like '頭皮發麻' to describe a tingling or creepy feeling caused by fear, nervousness, or disgust.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢頭皮好痕，所以要去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tau4 pei4 hou2 han4, so2 ji5 jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她頭皮很癢，所以要去看醫生。
examples.english_sentence: His/her scalp is very itchy, so (they) need to see a doctor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到佢咁講，我條頭皮都發麻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 keoi5 gam2 gong2, ngo5 tiu4 tau4 pei4 dou1 faat3 maa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到他那樣說，我的頭皮都發麻了。
examples.english_sentence: Hearing him say that made my scalp tingle.

mandarin_meaning: 头盔 (tóukuī)
english_meaning: helmet
explanation_mandarin: 指戴在頭部以保護頭顱的防護裝備，常見於騎車、摩托車、施工等情況，用來減少頭部受傷的風險。
explanation_english: A protective head covering worn to protect the head, commonly used when cycling, riding motorcycles, on construction sites, etc., to reduce the risk of head injury.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 踩單車記得戴頭盔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caai2 daan1 ce1 gei3 dak1 daai3 tau4 kwai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 骑自行车记得戴头盔。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to wear a helmet when cycling.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 摩托車司機應該戴頭盔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mo1 tok3 ce1 si1 gei1 jing1 goi1 daai3 tau4 kwai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 摩托车司机应该戴头盔。
examples.english_sentence: Motorcycle riders should wear helmets.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 工地上嘅工人要戴安全頭盔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 dei6 soeng5 ge3 gung1 jan4 jiu3 daai3 on1 cyun4 tau4 kwai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 工地上的工人要戴安全头盔。
examples.english_sentence: Workers on the construction site must wear safety helmets.

mandarin_meaning: 头目；首领（有时指帮派或团伙的首领）
english_meaning: leader; chief; boss; ringleader (often of a group or gang)
explanation_mandarin: 指某个团体或组织的领导者、首领，口语中常用来称呼帮派或团伙的头子。
explanation_english: Refers to the leader or head of a group or organization; in colloquial usage it often denotes the ringleader of a gang or clique.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係呢班人嘅頭目，大家都聽佢嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ni1 baan1 jan4 ge3 tau4-muk6, daai6 gaa1 dou1 teng1 keoi5 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是这群人的头目，大家都听他的。
examples.english_sentence: He is the ringleader of that group; everyone listens to him.

mandarin_meaning: 头破血流（tóu pò xuè liú）：原指头部受伤流血，现多作成语，形容被打得很惨或遭受重大损失。
english_meaning: Bloodied and battered; literally 'head broken and blood flowing' — used to say someone was severely injured or suffered heavy losses/defeat.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語／形容詞或動詞短語
explanation_mandarin: 原指頭部受重創流血，現常用作比喻，表示受到了嚴重的身體傷害或遭遇慘重的失敗或損失。
explanation_english: Originally refers to the head being seriously injured and bleeding. Now commonly used figuratively to describe being badly beaten or suffering a crushing defeat or severe losses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街市同人打交，打到頭破血流，要送院。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gaai1 si5 tung4 jan4 daa2 gaau1, daa2 dou3 tau4 po3 hyut3 lau4, jiu3 sung3 jyun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在街市和人打架，被打得頭破血流，要送院。
examples.english_sentence: He got into a fight at the market and was beaten bloody; he had to be taken to the hospital.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 經濟危機令好多公司頭破血流，裁員不停。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ging1 zai3 ngai4 gei1 ling6 hou2 do1 gung1 si1 tau4 po3 hyut3 lau4, coi4 jyun4 bat1 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 經濟危機使很多公司慘遭重創，裁員不斷。
examples.english_sentence: The economic crisis left many companies badly hit, with layoffs continuing.

mandarin_meaning: 首祭；對祖先或神靈的首次或重要祭祀（古語、民俗用語）
english_meaning: the first or primary offering/ritual in ancestral or religious sacrifice (archaic/folk term)
explanation_mandarin: 「頭禡」為較少見的文言或民俗術語，字面為「首要的祭祀」，通常指為祖先或神靈所做的第一場或重要祭祀儀式。現代廣東話中甚少使用，主要出現在古文或描述傳統習俗的語境中。
explanation_english: A rare/archaic Cantonese term literally meaning the 'first/primary sacrificial offering'. It usually refers to the initial or principal ritual offering made to ancestors or deities. Seldom used in modern spoken Cantonese and mainly appears in literary or folk-custom contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個係古時做頭禡嘅儀式。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 hai6 gu2 si4 zou6 tau4 maa6 ge3 ji4 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這是古時舉行頭禡的儀式。
examples.english_sentence: This is the ceremony for performing the 'toumaa' in ancient times.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企啲長輩仲保留頭禡嘅習俗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei5 di1 zoeng2 bui3 zung6 bou2 lau4 tau4 maa6 ge3 zaap6 zuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡的長輩還保留頭禡的習俗。
examples.english_sentence: The elders in the family still retain the custom of the 'toumaa'.

mandarin_meaning: 首站、起點站
english_meaning: first stop; starting station
explanation_mandarin: 指路線或行程中的第一個停靠站或起點站，常用於交通或旅遊行程描述。
explanation_english: Refers to the first stop or starting station of a route or itinerary, commonly used in transportation and travel contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次行程嘅頭站係尖沙咀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 hang4 cing4 ge3 tau4 zaam6 hai6 zim1 saa1 zeoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次行程的首站是尖沙咀。
examples.english_sentence: The first stop of this trip is Tsim Sha Tsui.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 地鐵嘅頭站通常會有轉車設施。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dei6 tit3 ge3 tau4 zaam6 tung1 soeng4 wui5 jau5 zyun2 ce1 cit3 si1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 地铁的首站通常会有换乘设施。
examples.english_sentence: The metro's first station usually has transfer facilities.

mandarin_meaning: 斗笠 / 帽子
english_meaning: conical hat; hat (often a rain hat or traditional straw hat)
explanation_mandarin: 指戴在頭上的帽子，常指農人或漁民使用的斗笠或用來遮雨、遮陽的帽子。
explanation_english: Refers to a hat worn on the head, often a conical straw hat (douli) used by farmers or fishers, or a hat used to shelter from rain or sun.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出門記得戴頭笠，外面落緊大雨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 mun4 gei3 dak1 daai3 tau4 lap1, ngoi6 min6 lok6 gan2 daai6 jyu5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出門記得戴斗笠（或帽子），外面正在下大雨。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to wear a hat (douli) when you go out — it's raining heavily outside.

mandarin_meaning: 头等（最高等级、第一等）
english_meaning: first-class; top-ranking; of the highest priority
explanation_mandarin: 表示等級最高或最重要，常用來修飾名詞，如「頭等艙」「頭等大事」，也可表示首要或優先。
explanation_english: Indicates the highest rank or top priority; commonly used to modify nouns (e.g., 'first-class cabin', 'matter of top importance').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今次旅行我哋坐頭等艙，好舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ci3 leoi5 hang4 ngo5 dei6 co5 tau4 dang2 cong1, hou2 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这次旅行我们坐头等舱，很舒服。
examples.english_sentence: We flew first class on this trip; it was very comfortable.

mandarin_meaning: 头等大事 (tóuděng dàshì) — 极其重要的事情，最应优先处理的事
english_meaning: a top priority; a matter of utmost importance
explanation_mandarin: 表示某件事情非常重要，位於首要位置，需要優先處理或特別重視。
explanation_english: Indicates that something is extremely important and should be treated as the highest priority.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試對佢嚟講係頭等大事，所以每日都溫書。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 deoi3 keoi5 lai4 gong2 hai6 tau4 dang2 daai6 si6, so2 ji5 mui5 jat6 dou1 wan1 syu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 对他来说，考试是头等大事，所以每天都在复习。
examples.english_sentence: For him, exams are a top priority, so he studies every day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 保護環境係頭等大事，唔可以掉以輕心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bou2 wu6 waan4 ging2 hai6 tau4 dang2 daai6 si6, m4 ho2 ji5 diu6 ji5 hing1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 保护环境是头等大事，不能掉以轻心。
examples.english_sentence: Protecting the environment is of utmost importance; we cannot be careless.

mandarin_meaning: 髮箍 / 頭帶
english_meaning: headband; hairband
explanation_mandarin: 用來固定或裝飾頭髮的帶子，可以是布、彈性材料或吸汗材質，常見於日常造型或運動時使用。
explanation_english: A band worn around the head to hold hair in place or as an accessory; can be made of cloth, elastic, or sweat-absorbing material and is used for fashion or during sports.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢戴咗個靚頭箍，好襯佢個髮型。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 daai3 zo2 go3 leng3 tau4 gu1, hou2 can1 keoi5 go3 faat3 jing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她戴了一个漂亮的发箍，很配她的发型。
examples.english_sentence: She put on a pretty headband; it suits her hairstyle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 跑步時戴返個吸汗嘅頭箍會舒服啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: paau2 bou6 si4 daai3 faan1 go3 kap1 hon4 ge3 tau4 gu1 wui5 syu1 fuk6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 跑步时戴个吸汗的头箍会舒服一点。
examples.english_sentence: Wearing an absorbent headband while running makes you more comfortable.

mandarin_meaning: 头簪（用来固定或装饰头发的簪子）
english_meaning: hairpin (an ornamental pin used to secure or decorate the hair)
explanation_mandarin: 頭簪是插在頭髮上用來固定髮型或作為裝飾的簪飾，既有實用功能也常具有裝飾性，常見於傳統與古典造型中。
explanation_english: A hairpin worn in the hair to secure a hairstyle or serve as an ornament. It is both functional and decorative and is common in traditional or classical hairstyles.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢插咗支頭簪喺頭髮入面，好有古典氣質。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 caap3 zo2 zi1 tau4 zaam1 hai2 tau4 faat3 jap6 min6, hou2 jau5 gu2 din2 hei3 zat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她插了一支头簪在头发里，看起来很有古典气质。
examples.english_sentence: She had a hairpin tucked into her hair and looked very classically elegant.

mandarin_meaning: 头绪；线索、头绪（表示是否有线索或头绪可以着手）
english_meaning: clue; lead; thread (an idea or lead to begin solving or understanding something)
explanation_mandarin: 表示有沒有線索或可供著手的頭緒，常用於「沒有頭緒」「有了一點頭緒」等表達，屬於名詞。
explanation_english: Refers to a clue, lead, or thread — an idea or piece of information that gives a starting point for solving or understanding something. Commonly used in phrases like "have no clue" or "get a lead."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我對呢件事完全冇頭緒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 deoi3 ni1 gin6 si6 jyun4 cyun4 mou5 tau4 seoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我对这件事完全没有头绪。
examples.english_sentence: I have no clue about this matter.

mandarin_meaning: 头绪；线索（对事情的头绪或线索，表示能否着手或推进）
english_meaning: clue; lead; thread; an indication or hint that allows one to proceed or make progress on a matter
explanation_mandarin: 表示對一件事能否開始著手或是否已有線索、頭緒；常見用法有「有頭緒」或「冇/沒頭緒」。
explanation_english: Refers to a clue, lead, or thread that lets someone begin or make progress on a problem or situation. Commonly used in phrases like 'have a clue' or 'have no clue.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事我暫時冇頭緒，唔知點樣處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 ngo5 zam6 si4 mou5 tau4 seoi3, m4 zi1 dim2 joeng6 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事我暂时没有头绪，不知道该怎样处理。
examples.english_sentence: I don't have any clue about this matter right now; I don't know how to handle it.

mandarin_meaning: 垂頭喪氣；鬱悶、沒精打采
english_meaning: to hang one's head; downcast; dejected; listless
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人垂頭、沒有精神或情緒低落，常見於口語表達。
explanation_english: Describes someone with their head hanging, lacking energy and feeling downcast; commonly used in colloquial Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考咗兩次試都唔及格，阿明成日頭耷耷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 zo2 loeng5 ci3 si3 dou1 m4 kap6 gaak3, aa3 ming4 sing4 jat6 tau4 daat6 daat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考了兩次試都不及格，阿明整天垂頭喪氣。
examples.english_sentence: He failed the exam twice, and Ah Ming was downcast all day.

jyutping: tau4 dap6 dap6, ngaan5 sap1 sap1
mandarin_meaning: 垂頭喪氣、眼睛含淚（像要哭的樣子）
english_meaning: head hung low and eyes teary; looking dejected and on the verge of crying
explanation_mandarin: 形容一個人垂著頭、情緒低落，眼睛濕潤或含淚的樣子，通常表示難過、失望或沮喪。
explanation_english: Describes someone with their head drooped and eyes wet or teary—appearing sad, disappointed, or dejected.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到壞消息，佢就頭耷耷，眼溼溼咁坐喺度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 waai6 siu1 sik1, keoi5 zau6 tau4 dap6 dap6, ngaan5 sap1 sap1 gam2 co5 hai2 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到壞消息，他就垂著頭，眼含淚地坐在那裡。
examples.english_sentence: When he heard the bad news, he sat there with his head hung low and teary eyes.

jyutping: tau4 dap6 dap6, ngaan5 sap1 sap1
mandarin_meaning: 垂頭喪氣，眼眶濕潤（快要流淚）
english_meaning: downcast and teary; dejected with watery/teary eyes
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容一個人情緒低落或難過，通常表現為低著頭和眼睛濕潤，像快要流淚的樣子。
explanation_english: Describes someone who is feeling dejected or sad, typically shown by hanging their head and having watery or teary eyes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考試唔及格之後，阿明成日頭耷耷，眼濕濕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 si3 m4 gap1 gaak3 zi1 hau6, aa3 ming4 sing4 jat6 tau4 dap6 dap6, ngaan5 sap1 sap1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考試不及格後，小明整天垂頭喪氣，眼睛濕潤。
examples.english_sentence: After failing the exam, Ah Ming was downcast all the time, with teary eyes.

mandarin_meaning: 头脑（指大脑或思维、智力）
english_meaning: brain; mind; one's thinking ability; intelligence
explanation_mandarin: 指人的大腦，也泛指思考能力、智力或處理問題的能力。
explanation_english: Refers to the physical brain and, by extension, a person's mind, thinking ability, or intelligence.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好有頭腦，諗嘢好快。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 jau5 tau4nou5, nam2 je5 hou2 faai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很有頭腦，思考問題很快。
examples.english_sentence: He is very smart; he thinks through problems quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 頭腫眼腫（形容被打或受傷後臉部腫脹、狼狽的樣子）
english_meaning: head and eyes swollen (describes a battered, puffy, or dishevelled appearance, often after being hurt)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，字面為「頭腫、眼膇」，用來形容人被打或受刺激後，頭臉腫脹、樣子很慘或很狼狽，也可泛指看起來非常不好或失態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression literally meaning 'head swollen, eyes puffy'. It describes someone who looks battered, swollen, or very dishevelled—often after being hurt—or more generally someone who looks in a sorry or embarrassed state.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你睇佢個樣，成個頭腫眼膇，肯定比人打過。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 tai2 keoi5 go3 joeng6, sing4 go3 tau4 zung2 ngaan5 coet3, hang2 ding6 bei2 jan4 daa2 gwo3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你看他/她的樣子，整個頭腫眼腫，肯定被人打過。
examples.english_sentence: Look at him/her — head and eyes all swollen; they must have been beaten.

mandarin_meaning: 頭落／被斬首；（引申）受到嚴重處罰或被開除、失去重要地位
english_meaning: Literally 'the head falls' (beheaded); figuratively, to be severely punished, sacked, or suffer severe consequences
explanation_mandarin: 「頭落」原義可指斬首（頭顱掉落），在口語中常作比喻，表示受到嚴厲懲罰、被解僱或失去權位。語氣偏口語或粗俗，使用時多為威脅或形容後果嚴重。
explanation_english: Originally referring to beheading (the head falling), in colloquial Cantonese it's used metaphorically to mean suffering severe punishment, being fired, or losing an important position. It's informal and can be coarse, often used to warn or emphasize serious consequences.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 古代嗰啲戰犯會畀人斬頭，頭落嗰一刻好恐怖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 doi6 go2 di1 zin3 faan6 wui5 bei2 jan4 zaan2 tau4, tau4 lok6 go2 jat1 hak1 hou2 hung2 bou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 古代那些戰犯會被斬首，頭落的那一刻很可怕。
examples.english_sentence: In ancient times those war criminals would be beheaded; the moment the head fell was terrifying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你再搞事，小心，真係會頭落。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zoi3 gaau2 si6, siu2 sam1, zan1 hai6 wui5 tau4 lok6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你再惹事，小心真的會受到嚴厲處罰（或被解雇）。
examples.english_sentence: If you cause trouble again, be careful — you might really 'lose your head' (face severe punishment).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司裁員，佢驚頭落，已經開始搵工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 coi4 jyun4, keoi5 geng1 tau4 lok6, ji5 ging1 hoi1 ci2 wan2 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司裁員，他擔心會被解僱，已經開始找工作。
examples.english_sentence: With company layoffs, he's afraid he'll be sacked and has already begun looking for a job.

mandarin_meaning: 头号；第一；最重要
english_meaning: number one; top; top-ranked; most important
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容词 / 名词修饰语
explanation_mandarin: 表示某人或某事物在同類中排名最高或最重要，常用作名詞的修飾語，例如「頭號敵人」「頭號粉絲」。
explanation_english: Indicates someone or something ranked highest among peers or the most important; commonly used as a modifier before a noun (e.g. "number-one enemy", "top fan").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係公司嘅頭號銷售員。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 gung1si1 ge3 tau4 hou6 siu1sau6 jyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是公司的头号销售员。
examples.english_sentence: He is the company's top salesperson.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個罪犯係警方嘅頭號通緝犯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zeoi6 faan6 hai6 ging2fong1 ge3 tau4 hou6 tung1 kap1 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个罪犯是警方的头号通缉犯。
examples.english_sentence: This criminal is the police's number-one most wanted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係明星嘅頭號粉絲，乜嘢演唱會都會去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ming4sing1 ge3 tau4 hou6 fan2si1, mat1 je5 jin2coeng3wui2 dou1 wui5 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是明星的头号粉丝，什么演唱会都会去。
examples.english_sentence: He's the celebrity's number-one fan and goes to every concert.

mandarin_meaning: 字面：頭上的蠟；在粵語中並無廣泛公認的成語或俗語意義，可能是地方用語、誤寫或罕見詞彙。可理解為與蠟或蠟燭相關的字面意義。
english_meaning: Literal: wax on the head; not a widely recognized Cantonese idiom or slang. Possibly a regional term, a mistaken form, or a literal compound related to wax/candle.
partOfSpeech_english: noun (literal) / rare slang or regional term
explanation_mandarin: 「頭蠟」由「頭」（head）和「蠟」（wax）組成，字面意思可指頭上的蠟或與蠟有關的東西。但在主流粵語資源中並無廣泛收錄為固定成語或常用俗語。若見到此詞，應注意可能為方言用法、口語變體或書寫錯誤（如誤寫「蠟燭」等）。
explanation_english: Composed of the characters for 'head' and 'wax,' the literal reading would refer to wax on the head or something to do with wax. However, this term is not widely recorded as a standard Cantonese idiom or common slang. If encountered, it may be a regional/local usage, a colloquial innovation, or a mistaken/written form (for example, confusion with '蠟燭' — candle).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔識「頭蠟」呢個講法，係唔係某啲地區嘅俗語？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 sik1 "tau4 laap6" ni1 go3 gong2 faat3, hai6 m4 hai6 mau5 di1 dei6 keoi1 ge3 zuk6 jyu5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不認識「頭蠟」這個說法，是不是某些地區的俗語？
examples.english_sentence: I don't recognize the term '頭蠟' — is it a regional colloquialism?

mandarin_meaning: 厚顏無恥；不知羞恥
english_meaning: brazen; shameless; thick-skinned
explanation_mandarin: 口語用詞，形容人臉皮厚、無恥、做事不覺得丟臉或害羞，帶貶義。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term describing someone who is brazen or shameless—thick-skinned and unashamed; carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好頭赤，欠人錢仲唔還，仲呃人講大話。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 tau4 cek3, him3 jan4 cin2 zung6 m4 waan4, zung6 aak1 jan4 gong2 daai6 waa6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真是厚顏無恥，欠了別人的錢還不還，還欺騙別人說謊。
examples.english_sentence: He's really shameless — he still won't pay back the money he owes and even lies to people.

mandarin_meaning: 頭部發紅／赤裸頭部（口語）
english_meaning: head is red (sunburned, embarrassed, or angry) / bareheaded (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「頭赤赤」是廣東話口語，字面指頭部呈現紅色。常用來形容因日晒、尷尬、害羞或生氣而頭部（或臉部）發紅；有時也可指裸露頭部、沒戴帽子。語氣隨語境可屬描述或略帶俚語色彩。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression literally meaning 'head red'. It commonly describes the head (or face) turning red from sunburn, embarrassment/shyness, or anger. It can also be used to indicate someone is bareheaded (not wearing a hat). Tone and nuance depend on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔戴帽出街，頭赤赤㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 daai3 mou6 ceot1 gaai1, tau4 cek3 cek3 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不戴帽子出門，頭被曬得紅紅的。
examples.english_sentence: He went out without a hat; his head got red from the sun.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講錯嘢，好尷尬，頭赤赤㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 co3 je5, hou2 gon1ngaak3, tau4 cek3 cek3 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說錯話，很尷尬，頭（或臉）都紅了。
examples.english_sentence: He said the wrong thing and felt embarrassed—his head went red.

mandarin_meaning: 工作；職位
english_meaning: job; employment; position
explanation_mandarin: 粵語（香港常用）口語，指工作、職位或謀生的職業。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial term meaning a job, position, or means of earning a living.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家有冇頭路？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 jau5 mou5 tau4 lou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你現在有沒有工作？
examples.english_sentence: Do you have a job right now?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我搵到份新頭路，下星期開始上班。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 wan2 dou3 fan6 san1 tau4 lou6, haa6 sing1 kei4 hoi1 ci2 soeng5 baan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我找到一份新工作，下星期開始上班。
examples.english_sentence: I got a new job and start work next week.

mandarin_meaning: 領頭車；最前面的車輛；（引申）帶頭者
english_meaning: lead vehicle; the front car in a convoy or train; (figurative) the one who takes the lead
explanation_mandarin: 本詞字面上指車隊或列車中最前面的車輛或車廂。在口語中也可引申為帶頭、率先行動的人或事物。
explanation_english: Literally refers to the front vehicle in a convoy or the front carriage of a train. Colloquially it can also mean a person or thing that takes the lead or acts first.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我坐喺頭車嘅車廂，可以望到前面嘅風景。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 co5 hai2 tau4 ce1 ge3 ce1 soeng1, ho2 ji5 mong6 dou3 cin4 min6 ge3 fung1 ging2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我坐在列車的頭車車廂，可以看到前方的風景。
examples.english_sentence: I'm sitting in the front carriage of the train and can see the scenery ahead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日車隊出發，佢開頭車帶隊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 ce1 deoi6 ceot1 faat3, keoi5 hoi1 tau4 ce1 daai3 deoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天車隊出發，他開領頭車帶隊。
examples.english_sentence: The convoy set off today; he drove the lead car to lead the team.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺公司成日想做頭車，率先帶領大家嘗試新計劃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 gung1 si1 sing4 jat6 soeng2 zou6 tau4 ce1, leot6 sin1 daai3 ling5 daai6 gaa1 soeng4 si3 san1 gai3 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在公司經常想做帶頭的人，率先帶領大家嘗試新計劃。
examples.english_sentence: He often wants to be the leader at the company, taking the initiative to lead everyone in trying new projects.

mandarin_meaning: 头部；人的头或者物体的上端部分
english_meaning: head; the head region or the top part of something
explanation_mandarin: 指人的頭部或物體的最上端部位，常用於描述解剖位置或受傷部位。
explanation_english: Refers to the head of a person or the top part of an object; commonly used to describe anatomical location or injury site.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個頭部受傷，要去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 tau4 bou6 sau6 soeng1, jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的头部受伤，要去看医生。
examples.english_sentence: His head is injured; he needs to see a doctor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 頭部位於身體嘅最上面。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tau4 bou6 wai6 jyu1 san1 tai2 ge3 zeoi3 soeng6 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 头部位于身体的最上方。
examples.english_sentence: The head is located at the top of the body.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）頭都大了 / 感到非常困惑、煩惱或不堪負荷
english_meaning: I'm totally overwhelmed / I'm at my wit's end (literally 'my head's become big')
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語用語，表示因為事情複雜、麻煩或壓力大而感到頭痛、困惑或無從下手，常用於抱怨或表達無奈。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to say one is overwhelmed, baffled, or exasperated by complicated/troublesome matters. Often used to complain or express helplessness.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 成日加班又要趕最後期限，搞到我頭都大埋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 jat6 gaa1 baan1 jau6 jiu3 gon2 zeoi3 hau6 kei4 haan6, gaau2 dou3 ngo5 tau4 dou1 daai6 maai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 經常加班又要趕最後期限，搞得我頭都大了。
examples.english_sentence: I'm always working overtime and rushing to meet deadlines — it's making my head spin.

mandarin_meaning: 头重脚轻（形容上重下轻，不稳固或不平衡）
english_meaning: Top-heavy; unbalanced or unstable (literally heavier at the top than the bottom; figuratively lacking a solid foundation)
explanation_mandarin: 原指物体上重下轻，容易倾倒；比喻组织、机构或事物不稳固，上层负担或权力过重而基层薄弱。
explanation_english: Originally describes an object that is heavier at the top than the bottom and thus prone to tipping over; figuratively used for organizations, systems, or situations that are unstable or unbalanced, with excessive weight or power at the top and a weak foundation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢把椅子設計唔好，頭重腳輕，好易倒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 baa2 ji2 zi2 cit3 gai3 m4 hou2, tau4 zung6 goek3 heng1, hou2 ji6 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这把椅子设计不好，头重脚轻，很容易倒。
examples.english_sentence: This chair is poorly designed — top-heavy and unstable, it tips over easily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司管理頭重腳輕，基層員工冇發言權，運作好唔穩定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gun2 lei5 tau4 zung6 goek3 heng1, gei1 cang4 jyun4 gung1 mou5 faat3 jin4 kyun4, wan6 zok3 hou2 m4 wan6 deng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司管理头重脚轻，基层员工没有发言权，运作很不稳定。
examples.english_sentence: The company's management is top-heavy; lower-level staff have no say and operations are very unstable.

mandarin_meaning: 头部感觉沉重
english_meaning: heavy-headed; feeling a heaviness in the head (often with dizziness or fatigue)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容頭部感覺沉重，常伴隨頭暈或疲倦，可能由睡眠不足、疲勞、感冒或宿醉等引起。
explanation_english: Describes a sensation of heaviness in the head, often accompanied by dizziness or tiredness; commonly caused by lack of sleep, fatigue, cold, or hangover.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家頭重重，可能係訓得唔夠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 tau4 cung4 cung4, ho2 nang4 hai6 fan3 dak1 m4 gau3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在頭很沉，可能是睡眠不足。
examples.english_sentence: My head feels heavy right now; maybe I didn't get enough sleep.

mandarin_meaning: 頭銜（表示職位、稱號或榮譽的名稱）
english_meaning: title; designation; rank; honorific
explanation_mandarin: 頭銜是用來表示某人所擔任的職位、獲得的稱號或所享有的榮譽稱呼，常見於職場或正式場合。
explanation_english: A title or designation used to indicate a person's position, rank, or honorific; commonly used in workplaces or formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司畀咗佢個新頭銜，係項目經理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 bei2 zo2 keoi5 go3 san1 tau4 haam4, hai6 hoeng6 muk6 ging1 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司給了他新的頭銜，是項目經理。
examples.english_sentence: The company gave him a new title — project manager.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個頭銜聽落幾響亮，但唔一定代表佢工作能力好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 tau4 haam4 ting1 lok6 gei2 hoeng2 loeng6, daan6 m4 jat1 ding6 doi6 biu2 keoi5 gung1 zok3 nang4 lik6 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的頭銜聽起來很響亮，但不一定代表他的工作能力好。
examples.english_sentence: His title sounds impressive, but it doesn't necessarily reflect his job ability.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔在乎頭銜，主要係想做啱我嘅工作。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zoi6 fu1 tau4 haam4, zyu2 jiu3 hai6 soeng2 zou6 ngaam1 ngo5 ge3 gung1 zok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不在乎頭銜，主要是想做適合我的工作。
