explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression literally meaning "took the wrong medicine." It is used to describe someone behaving irrationally, crazily, or unreasonably — often as a scolding or expression of disbelief.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你係咪食錯藥呀？點解要咁做？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hai6 mai6 sik6 co3 joek6 aa3? dim2 gaai2 jiu3 gam2 zou6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你是不是吃錯藥了？為什麼要這樣做？
examples.english_sentence: Are you out of your mind? Why would you do this?

mandarin_meaning: 按鐘點計酬；按小時計酬
english_meaning: to be paid by the hour; to work on an hourly basis
explanation_mandarin: 「食鐘」是粵語俗語，指按鐘點或按小時計算薪酬，常用於鐘點工或臨時工的情況。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to be paid by the hour; commonly used for hourly or casual work where pay is calculated per hour.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺酒樓做侍應，係食鐘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 zau2 lau4 zou6 si6 jing3, hai6 sik6 zung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在酒楼当服务员，按小时计酬。
examples.english_sentence: He works as a waiter at a restaurant and is paid by the hour.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份工係食鐘，冇年假同醫療福利。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gung1 hai6 sik6 zung1, mou5 nin4 gaa3 tung4 ji1 liu4 fuk1 lei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这份工作按小时计薪，没有年假和医疗福利。
examples.english_sentence: This job pays by the hour and has no annual leave or medical benefits.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做鐘點工通常都係食鐘，工時彈性。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 zung1 dim2 gung1 tung1 soeng4 dou1 hai6 sik6 zung1, gung1 si4 daan6 sing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做钟点工通常按小时计酬，工时有弹性。
examples.english_sentence: Hourly workers are usually paid by the hour and have flexible working hours.

mandarin_meaning: 領取長期薪水；長期依賴他人或機構供養
english_meaning: to be on the long-term payroll; to receive regular long-term pay or financial support; to be dependent on someone/ an institution for support
explanation_mandarin: 「食長糧」是廣東話俗語，字面是「吃長期的糧食」。引申為長期領取薪水或由某人/某機構長期供養，常用來表示有穩定的飯碗或依賴性。有時帶有負面含義（過度依賴）。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '食長糧' (literally 'eat long rations') is a colloquial expression meaning to receive long-term pay or be financially supported by someone/a company. It often denotes having a steady job or being on the payroll, and can imply dependency.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家喺間公司做咗十年，已經食長糧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 gaan1 gung1si1 zou6 zo2 sap6 nin4, ji5 ging1 sik6 coeng4 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在在那間公司做了十年，已經領長期薪水。
examples.english_sentence: He's been at that company for ten years and is already on the long-term payroll.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果你唔想一輩子靠屋企食長糧，就要學識搵錢自立。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 m4 soeng2 jat1 bui3 zi2 kaau3 uk1 kei5 sik6 coeng4 loeng4, zau6 jiu3 hok6 sik1 wan2 cin2 zi6 lap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果你不想一輩子靠家裡吃長期供養，就要學會賺錢自立。
examples.english_sentence: If you don't want to rely on your family for support your whole life, you should learn to earn money and be independent.

mandarin_meaning: 吃闭门羹（被拒绝、被冷落）
english_meaning: To be turned away or refused entry; to be rebuffed or snubbed
explanation_mandarin: 「吃闭门羹」比喻遭到拒绝、被挡在门外或受到冷落，常用于表示请求、访问或参加活动时未被接受。
explanation_english: Literally 'eat a closed-door soup'; figuratively means to be refused, turned away, or given the cold shoulder—often used when someone is denied entry, service, or acceptance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我去佢屋企搵佢，點知俾人食閉門羹，佢連門都唔開。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 heoi3 keoi5 uk1 kei2 wan2 keoi5, dim2 zi1 bei2 jan4 sik6 bai3 mun4 gang1, keoi5 lin4 mun4 dou1 m4 hoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我去他家找他，结果被拒之门外，他连门都不打开。
examples.english_sentence: I went to his house to see him, but I was turned away—he didn't even open the door.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢去面試，結果食咗閉門羹，冇畀入去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 heoi3 min6 si5, git3 gwo2 sik6 zo2 bai3 mun4 gang1, mou5 bei2 jap6 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他去面试，结果被拒之门外，没有被允许进去。
examples.english_sentence: He went to the interview but was refused entry; he wasn't allowed in.

mandarin_meaning: 遭遇慘敗／非常丟臉、吃虧
english_meaning: to suffer a crushing defeat; to fail miserably; to be humiliated/take a big hit
explanation_mandarin: 俚語，主要在香港廣東話中使用。用來形容在比賽、競爭或事情上遭受慘敗、吃大虧或非常丟臉。常帶有誇張、口語化的語氣。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese slang (used mainly in Hong Kong). It describes suffering a crushing defeat, failing miserably, taking a big loss, or being humiliated. It is informal and often emphatic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺決賽輸到食陀地，對手實在太強。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 kyut3 coi3 syu1 dou3 sik6 to4 dei6, deoi3 sau2 sat6 zoi6 taai3 koeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在決賽輸得很慘，對手實在太強。
examples.english_sentence: We lost the final badly — the opponent was just too strong.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰個項目做唔成，最後公司要食陀地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 go3 hong6 muk6 zou6 m4 sing4, zeoi6 hau6 gung1 si1 jiu3 sik6 to4 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個項目做不成，最後公司要吃大虧／慘敗。
examples.english_sentence: That project failed, and the company ended up taking a big hit.

mandarin_meaning: （网络/俚语）玩《绝地求生》或类似的大逃杀游戏；在此类游戏中获得胜利（即“吃鸡”）
english_meaning: (slang) to play battle-royale games like PUBG; to win such a game — to get the 'chicken dinner' victory
explanation_mandarin: “食雞”源自英语“winner winner chicken dinner”的网络流行语，常用来表示玩大逃杀类游戏或在游戏中获胜。
explanation_english: "食雞" (sik6 gai1) comes from the phrase "winner winner chicken dinner" and is used online to refer to playing battle-royale games or achieving victory in them.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去唔去玩《PUBG》，一齊食雞呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 m4 heoi3 waan2 PUBG, jat1 cai4 sik6 gai1 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去不去玩《绝地求生》，一起吃鸡吗？
examples.english_sentence: Are you going to play PUBG tonight? Shall we get a chicken dinner together?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋終於食雞啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 zung1 jyu1 sik6 gai1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们终于吃鸡了！
examples.english_sentence: We finally got the chicken dinner!

mandarin_meaning: 吃雞胸肉（常指為了減肥或健身而只吃清淡的雞胸肉）
english_meaning: to eat chicken breast (often used to mean eating plain chicken breast as part of dieting or fitness regimen)
explanation_mandarin: 俚語/口語用法，字面是吃雞胸肉，常用來表示為了減肥或健身而採取的清淡飲食或節食行為。
explanation_english: Slang/colloquial expression: literally 'eat chicken breast.' Commonly used to describe following a bland, restrictive diet (often for weight loss or fitness), especially eating chicken breast frequently.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近佢開始做gym，每餐都食雞胸想減肥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 keoi5 hoi1 ci2 zou6 gym1, mui5 caan1 dou1 sik6 gai1 hung1 soeng2 gam2 fei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近他開始去健身房，每餐都吃雞胸肉想減肥。
examples.english_sentence: He recently started going to the gym and eats chicken breast for every meal to lose weight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想淨係食雞胸，想食啲有味道嘅嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 zing6 hai6 sik6 gai1 hung1, soeng2 sik6 di1 jau5 mei6 dou6 ge3 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想只吃雞胸肉，想吃些有味道的東西。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to only eat chicken breast; I want to eat something flavorful.

mandarin_meaning: 吃雪條（吃冰棒）
english_meaning: to eat an ice pop / to eat a popsicle
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是吃雪條（即冰棒、雪糕棒）。在廣東話日常用語中主要用作字面義，指吃冷凍甜品。有時口語化地用於描述在夏天或炎熱時吃雪條的行為或感受，但並非一個常見的特殊成語或俚語用法。
explanation_english: Literally means to eat an ice pop (popsicle). In Cantonese it is mainly used in the literal sense to refer to eating a frozen treat. Occasionally used colloquially to describe enjoying a popsicle in hot weather, but it is not a widely recognized idiom or slang with a separate figurative meaning.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天行街好熱，不如去買支雪條食下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 haang4 gaai1 hou2 jit6, bat1 jyu4 heoi3 maai5 zi1 syut3 tiu4 sik6 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天逛街很熱，不如去買支雪條吃一下。
examples.english_sentence: It's hot walking around in summer; why not buy a popsicle to eat?

mandarin_meaning: 吃雪糕 / 吃冰淇淋
english_meaning: to eat ice cream
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是吃雪糕，常用於日常對話，表示享用雪糕或去買雪糕的動作。
explanation_english: Literally 'eat ice cream'. Common everyday phrase used to indicate eating or going to get ice cream.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 夏天好熱，我想食雪糕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haa6 tin1 hou2 jit6, ngo5 soeng2 sik6 syut3 gou1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 夏天很熱，我想吃雪糕。
examples.english_sentence: It's so hot in summer; I want to eat ice cream.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 行街見到雪糕舖，一齊入去食雪糕啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haang4 gaai1 gin3 dou3 syut3 gou1 pou3, jat1 cai4 jap6 heoi3 sik6 syut3 gou1 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 逛街時看到雪糕店，一起進去吃雪糕吧。
examples.english_sentence: We saw an ice cream shop while walking around; let's go in and have ice cream together.

mandarin_meaning: 触电；（俚）被某人吸引或心动
english_meaning: to get an electric shock; (slang) to be strongly attracted to someone / feel a spark
explanation_mandarin: 原指被电击（触电），日常口语亦用作俚语，表示被某人吸引、心动或被對方的外表/氣質“電到”。
explanation_english: Literally, to receive an electric shock. Colloquially used as slang to mean being strongly attracted to someone or feeling a spark.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔小心摸到露線，俾電食咗，隻手好痛。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 siu2 sam1 mo2 dou3 lou6 sin3, bei2 din6 sik6 zo2, zek3 sau2 hou2 tung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不小心摸到露出的电线，被电到了，手很痛。
examples.english_sentence: He accidentally touched an exposed wire, got an electric shock, and his hand hurts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到佢第一眼我就食電，心都跳快咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou3 keoi5 dai6 jat1 ngaan5 ngo5 zau6 sik6 din6, sam1 dou1 tiu3 faai3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 第一眼看到他我就被电到了，心跳都加快了。
examples.english_sentence: I felt a spark the first time I saw him; my heart started racing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日靠甜言蜜語想食電女仔，大家要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 kaau3 tim4 jin4 mat6 jyu5 soeng2 sik6 din6 neoi5 zai2, daai6 gaa1 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是靠甜言蜜语想吸引女生，大家要小心。
examples.english_sentence: He always tries to charm girls with sweet talk; everyone should be careful.

mandarin_meaning: 吃霸王餐（逃單）
english_meaning: to dine and dash; to eat without paying
explanation_mandarin: 「食霸王雞」是粵語口語/俚語，源自「霸王餐」，意思是吃完飯或用餐後不付錢就離開，即「逃單」。多用於非正式語境，尤其在香港口語中可聽到。
explanation_english: “食霸王雞” is Cantonese slang derived from “霸王餐” and means to eat (a meal) and leave without paying — i.e., to dine and dash. It is informal and commonly used in conversational Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今次又食霸王雞，食完就走，冇畀錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ci3 jau6 sik6 baa3 wong4 gai1, sik6 jyun4 zau6 zau2, mou5 bei2 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這次又吃霸王餐，吃完就走，沒付錢。
examples.english_sentence: He did the 'eat-and-run' again — after eating he left without paying.

mandarin_meaning: 吃霸王餐（逃单／不付钱就离开）
english_meaning: to dine and dash; to get a free meal by not paying
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，指在餐廳或食肆吃完東西後不付錢就離開，或被用來形容占便宜、白吃白喝的人。
explanation_english: A colloquial phrase meaning to eat at a restaurant and leave without paying (dine-and-dash); can also refer more generally to freeloading or taking advantage to get free food.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺餐廳食霸王飯，食完就走，俾人報警捉咗佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 caan1 teng1 sik6 baak3 wong4 faan6, sik6 jyun4 zau6 zau2, bei2 jan4 bou3 ging2 zuk1 zo2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在餐厅吃霸王餐，吃完就溜走，最后被人报警抓住了。
examples.english_sentence: He dined and dashed at the restaurant—after finishing the meal he ran off and was eventually reported and caught.

mandarin_meaning: 吃霸王餐；不付钱就吃完饭，赖账或占便宜
english_meaning: to dine and dash; to eat without paying; to freeload a meal
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指在餐廳或飯局中吃完東西卻拒絕付款或找藉口不付錢，亦可泛指占便宜不付代價。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang meaning to eat a meal without paying (dine and dash) or to freeload; can also refer more broadly to taking advantage without paying the cost.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢上次喺餐廳食霸王餐，依家俾店員報警。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng6 ci3 hai2 caan1 teng1 sik6 baa3 wong4 caan1, ji4 gaa1 bei2 dim3 jyun4 bou3 ging2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他上次在餐厅吃霸王餐，现在被店员报警了。
examples.english_sentence: He dined and dashed at the restaurant last time and has now been reported to the police by the staff.

mandarin_meaning: 吃霸王餐（不付餐錢／白吃）
english_meaning: to dine and dash; to eat without paying; to freeload a meal
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，指在餐館或小吃店吃了東西卻不付錢，或習慣性佔便宜、白吃白拿。有時也用來形容佔別人便宜不付出代價的行為。
explanation_english: Colloquial expression meaning to eat at a restaurant or stall and refuse to pay (dine and dash), or more generally to freeload or take advantage without paying the cost.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日去嗰間茶餐廳食霸王鷄，從來唔俾錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 heoi3 go2 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 sik6 baa3 wong4 gai1, cung4 loi4 m4 bei2 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常去那間茶餐廳吃霸王餐，從來不付錢。
examples.english_sentence: He often goes to that cha chaan teng and dines and dashes; he never pays.

mandarin_meaning: （原為麻將術語）在第一輪就胡牌；（口語）被人欺騙或吃虧
english_meaning: (originally a mahjong term) to win/lose on the first hand; (colloquial) to be fooled, taken advantage of, or suffer a loss
explanation_mandarin: 「食頭糊」字面源自麻將，指在開局或第一輪就胡牌（或被人胡）；在廣東話口語中常用來表示被人欺騙、吃虧或遭受不利的結果。
explanation_english: Literally from mahjong, referring to winning/losing on the first hand. Colloquially in Cantonese it means to be duped, taken advantage of, or to suffer a loss/unfavourable outcome.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔想畀人食頭糊，做乜嘢都要小心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 sik6 tau4 wu4, zou6 mat1 je5 dou1 jiu3 siu2 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不想被人欺騙，做什麼都要小心。
examples.english_sentence: I don't want to be taken advantage of, so I have to be careful about everything.

mandarin_meaning: 吃回扣；私下抽取款項（俚語）
english_meaning: to take a cut/commission; to skim off money (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，指在交易或工程等情況下私自收取回扣或抽取一部分款項，常帶貶義，暗示不正當得利。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang verb meaning to take a cut or commission (often illicitly) from a transaction or project; carries a negative connotation of skimming money or taking kickbacks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺呢個工程度食額，好似每單都抽成。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 ni1 go3 gung1 cing4 dou6 sik6 ngok6, hou2 ci5 mui5 daan1 dou1 caau1 sing4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在這個工程中吃回扣，似乎每一單都抽成。
examples.english_sentence: He takes a cut on this project — it seems he gets a commission from every job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好畀人食額，簽約前要查清楚條款同價錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 sik6 ngok6, cim1 joek3 cin4 jiu3 caa4 cing1 co2 tiu4 fun2 tung4 gaa3 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要讓人吃回扣，簽約前要把條款和價格查清楚。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let people take a cut — check the terms and prices carefully before signing.

mandarin_meaning: 出去透透氣／散步
english_meaning: to go out for fresh air; to take a walk or step outside to relax
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語詞，字面為「吃風」，用來表示出去透透氣、散步或短暫到戶外放鬆或冷靜一下，常用於日常會話中。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase literally meaning 'eat wind'. It refers to going out for fresh air, taking a short walk, or stepping outside briefly to relax or calm down. Common in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 天氣咁好，我出去食風吓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tin1 hei3 gam2 hou2, ngo5 ceot1 heoi3 sik6 fung1 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 天气这么好，我出去透透气。
examples.english_sentence: The weather's so nice; I'm going out to get some fresh air.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱同女朋友大鑊，出去食風冷靜下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ngaam1 ngaam1 tung4 neoi5 pang4 jau5 daai6 wok6, ceot1 heoi3 sik6 fung1 ling4 zing6 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他刚和女朋友吵架，出去透透气冷静一下。
examples.english_sentence: He just had a fight with his girlfriend and went out to get some fresh air to calm down.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做完通宵我好攰，要出街食風一陣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 jyun4 tung1 siu1 ngo5 hou2 gui6, jiu3 ceot1 gaai1 sik6 fung1 jat1 zan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 熬夜做完我很累，要出去透透气一下。
examples.english_sentence: After pulling an all-nighter I'm exhausted; I need to go out and get some fresh air for a bit.

mandarin_meaning: 吃饭
english_meaning: to eat (a meal); to have a meal
explanation_mandarin: 指吃一顿饭，也可用作邀请别人一起吃或询问对方是否已用餐。
explanation_english: Refers to eating a meal; can also be used to invite someone to eat or to ask whether someone has eaten.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你食咗飯未呀？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你吃饭了吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you eaten yet?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚去食飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 sik6 faan6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚去吃饭吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go have dinner tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細路通常喺學校食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 lou6 tung1 soeng4 hai2 hok6 haau6 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子通常在学校吃饭。
examples.english_sentence: Children usually eat at school.

jyutping: sik6 faan6 m4 zi1 mai5 gwai3
mandarin_meaning: 吃饭不知米贵
english_meaning: to be oblivious to the cost/value of one's food or livelihood; to be ungrateful or wasteful
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「吃飯卻不知道米的珍貴」，引申指不懂得珍惜、不知感恩或揮霍浪費，對生計或他人付出缺乏體諒。
explanation_english: Literally 'eating without knowing rice is expensive.' Figuratively, it describes someone who doesn't appreciate the value of what they have—wasteful, ungrateful, or taking others' efforts and livelihood for granted.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日亂花錢，真係食飯唔知米貴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 lyun6 faa1 cin2, zan1 hai6 sik6 faan6 m4 zi1 mai5 gwai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是乱花钱，真是吃饭不知米贵。
examples.english_sentence: He always spends money recklessly; he really doesn't appreciate the value of what he has.

mandarin_meaning: 餐桌 / 飯桌
english_meaning: dining table
explanation_mandarin: 指用來吃飯的桌子，通常放置餐具和菜餚，是家庭或餐廳用餐的場所。
explanation_english: Refers to a table used for eating, where dishes and utensils are placed; the place for family or restaurant meals.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 將碗擺喺食飯枱上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng1 wun2 baai2 hai2 sik6 faan6 toi4 soeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 把碗放在餐桌上。
examples.english_sentence: Put the bowl on the dining table.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋成個家庭喺食飯枱一齊食晚飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 seng4 go3 gaa1 ting4 hai2 sik6 faan6 toi4 jat1 cai4 sik6 maan5 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們全家在餐桌一起吃晚飯。
examples.english_sentence: Our whole family eats dinner together at the dining table.

mandarin_meaning: 吃饱
english_meaning: to be full (after eating); to have eaten enough
explanation_mandarin: 表示已经吃得足够，不再感到饥饿，口语常用。
explanation_english: Indicates having eaten enough and no longer feeling hungry; a common colloquial expression.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我食飽喇，唔使再買嘢食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik6 baau2 laa3, m4 sai2 zoi3 maai5 je5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我吃饱了，不用再买东西吃。
examples.english_sentence: I'm full; I don't need to buy anything else to eat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你食飽未？我哋去飲茶唔？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 baau2 mei6? ngo5 dei6 heoi3 jam2 caa4 m4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你吃饱了吗？我们去喝茶吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you eaten? Shall we go for dim sum/tea?

mandarin_meaning: 吃飽沒煩惱；衣食無憂（口語）
english_meaning: Well-fed and carefree; having no worries about basic needs (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 表示生活有基本溫飽，無需為食或生計擔憂，帶有口語或俚語色彩。
explanation_english: Expresses that one has enough to eat and is free from concerns about basic livelihood; a colloquial/slang way to say one is secure and carefree.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家有份穩定工作，食飽無憂米啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 jau5 fan6 wan2 ding6 gung1 zok3, sik6 baau2 mou4 jau1 mai5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在有一份穩定的工作，吃飽沒煩惱了。
examples.english_sentence: Now that I have a steady job, I'm well-fed and have no worries.

cantonese: 食飽睡一睡，好過做元帥
jyutping: sik6 baau2 seoi6 jat1 seoi6, hou2 gwo3 zou6 jyun4 seoi3
mandarin_meaning: 吃饱睡一觉，胜过当元帅（宁愿安逸地享受生活，也不愿承担权力和责任）
english_meaning: Better to eat and take a nap than to be a marshal (preferring comfort/idleness over power and responsibility).
explanation_mandarin: 這句俗語用來形容寧可享受安逸、無所事事，也不願意承擔領導地位或重大責任，常帶有幽默或自嘲意味。
explanation_english: This colloquial saying expresses a preference for comfort and idleness over holding power or taking on major responsibilities; often used jokingly or self-deprecatingly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做領導要負責任，我寧願食飽睡一睡，好過做元帥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 ling5 dou6 jiu3 fu6 zaak3 jam6, ngo5 ning4 jyun6 sik6 baau2 seoi6 jat1 seoi6, hou2 gwo3 zou6 jyun4 seoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做领导要负责任，我宁愿吃饱睡一觉，也比当元帅好。
examples.english_sentence: Being a leader means having responsibilities; I'd rather eat and take a nap than be a marshal.

jyutping: sik6 baau2 faan6 mou5 si2 o1
mandarin_meaning: 沒事找事 / 閒得發慌
english_meaning: having nothing better to do; looking for trouble; bored and meddlesome
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 口語／俚語（短語，用於責備或形容）
partOfSpeech_english: colloquial phrase / slang (phrase used to scold or describe someone idle/meddlesome)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某人沒事做、閒得發慌或愛管閒事、找麻煩，帶有責備或嘲諷意味。字面意思是「吃飽了卻沒屎可以拉」，比喻閒得無聊。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who has nothing to do and therefore meddles or looks for trouble; a reproachful or mocking expression. Literally 'ate one's fill but have no poop to pass', metaphorically meaning idle/bored.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日對人指指點點，真係食飽飯冇屎屙。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 deoi3 jan4 zi2 zi2 dim2 dim2, zan1 hai6 sik6 baau2 faan6 mou5 si2 o1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天對人指指點點，真是沒事找事。
examples.english_sentence: He constantly criticizes others — he's really just looking for something to do.

jyutping: sik6 baau2 faan6 mou5 si2 o1
mandarin_meaning: 沒事做／閒得發慌（口語、帶粗俗意味）
english_meaning: to have nothing to do; to be idle or bored (colloquial, vulgar); often used to criticize someone for meddling or wasting time
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俚語，字面為「吃飽了卻拉不出屎」，用來形容沒事做、閒得無聊，或責怪別人多管閒事。語氣粗俗或帶貶義，通常用於口語。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese vulgar slang phrase literally meaning "ate until full but can't shit." It describes having nothing to do or being bored, and can be used to scold someone for meddling or wasting time. Colloquial and somewhat offensive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你食飽飯冇屎痾，成日多管閒事做乜？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 baau2 faan6 mou5 si2 o1, sing4 jat6 do1 gun2 haan4 si6 zou6 mat1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你沒事做嗎？整天多管閒事做什麼？
examples.english_sentence: Have you nothing better to do? Why are you always meddling in other people's business?

mandarin_meaning: 字面：吃香肠；俚语：（粗俗）指接受口交（被动一方）
english_meaning: Literal: to eat sausage; Slang (vulgar): to receive oral sex (passive partner)
explanation_mandarin: “食香腸”字面意思是吃香腸（食物）。在香港粵語口語中，這個短語也有粗俗的俚語用法，用來暗指某人（通常指男性）是接受口交的一方。這種用法非正式且可能冒犯他人，應酌情使用。
explanation_english: Literally it means 'to eat sausage' (the food). In Hong Kong Cantonese, the phrase is also used as a vulgar slang to imply that someone (often a man) is the passive recipient of oral sex. This usage is informal and potentially offensive, so use caution.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我食咗香腸炒飯，幾好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 sik6 zo2 hoeng1 coeng4 caau2 faan6, gei2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我吃了香肠炒饭，很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: I ate sausage fried rice tonight; it was tasty.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂講人話佢食香腸，咁講好容易得罪人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 gong2 jan4 waa6 keoi5 sik6 hoeng1 coeng4, gam2 gong2 hou2 jung6 ji6 dak1 zeoi6 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要随便说人家“吃香肠”，这样说很容易冒犯别人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't casually say someone 'ate sausage' — saying that can easily offend people.

synonyms: 吃香腸（普通話對應的字面說法，用於描述相同粗俗含義時可見）

mandarin_meaning: 尝到好处后便贪得无厌，越尝越想要
english_meaning: Once someone gets a taste of something good or powerful, they want more; to get a taste for it
explanation_mandarin: 比喻嘗到甜頭或好處後，貪心增加，越來越想得到更多。
explanation_english: A metaphor meaning that after tasting the benefits or pleasures of something, a person becomes greedy and increasingly wants more.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿強第一次開公司賺到錢，食髓知味，之後不停開分公司搵更多錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 koeng4 dai6 jat6 ci3 hoi1 gung1 si1 zaan6 dou3 cin2, sik6 seoi2 zi1 mei6, zi1 hau6 bat1 ting4 hoi1 fan1 gung1 si1 wan2 gang1 do1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿强第一次开公司赚钱，尝到甜头，之后食髓知味，不断开分公司赚更多钱。
examples.english_sentence: When Ah Keung made money the first time he started a company, he got a taste for it and kept opening branches to earn even more.

mandarin_meaning: 去你的；該死（粗俗說法）
english_meaning: Screw you; go to hell (vulgar expletive)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語/粗口，用作表示憤怒、不滿或罵人，相當於普通話的「去你的」或「去死」。語氣粗魯，不宜在正式場合使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expletive used to express anger, annoyance, or contempt. Equivalent to "screw you" or "go to hell." Vulgar — not appropriate in formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 食鬼啦，你以為我會信你？
examples.jyutping_sentence: sik6 gwaai2 laa1, nei5 ji5wai6 ngo5 wui5 seon3 nei5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去你的，你以為我會相信你嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Screw you — do you think I'd believe you?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你食鬼啦，咪再煩我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 gwaai2 laa1, mai5 zoi3 faan4 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去你的，別再煩我。
examples.english_sentence: Go to hell; stop bothering me.

mandarin_meaning: 嫖妓；买春（付费与妓女发生性关系）
english_meaning: to solicit a prostitute; to pay for sex (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俚语，指付费与妓女发生性关系或招妓。用法粗俗，含贬义或不雅的语气。
explanation_english: A Cantonese vulgar slang verb meaning to pay for sex or solicit a prostitute. Considered coarse and derogatory; used in informal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢上星期去尖沙咀食鷄，俾警察捉咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 soeng6 sing1 kei4 heoi3 zim1 saa1 zeoi2 sik6 gai1, bei2 ging2 caat3 zuk1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他上星期在尖沙咀嫖妓，被警察抓了。
examples.english_sentence: He went to Tsim Sha Tsui to solicit a prostitute last week and got caught by the police.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好公開講佢食鷄，咁講唔禮貌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gung1 hoi1 gong2 keoi5 sik6 gai1, gam2 gong2 m4 lai5 maau6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要公开说他嫖妓，那样很不礼貌。
examples.english_sentence: Don't publicly say he paid for sex; that's impolite.

mandarin_meaning: 吃鸡胸肉（指节食或健身时吃清淡的鸡胸）
english_meaning: to eat chicken breast; (slang) to stick to a bland chicken-breast diet for dieting or fitness
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是吃雞胸肉；在口語中常用於形容為了減肥或練肌肉而吃清淡、低脂的雞胸，帶有節食或健身飲食的含義。
explanation_english: Literally 'eat chicken breast'. Colloquially used to describe eating plain, low-fat chicken breast as part of dieting or fitness — implies following a strict, bland diet to lose weight or build muscle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家日日都食鷄胸，為咗減肥同練肌肉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4gaa1 jat6 jat6 dou1 sik6 gai1 hung1, wai6 zo2 gaam2fei4 tung4 lin6 gei1juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他现在每天都吃鸡胸，为了减肥和练肌肉。
examples.english_sentence: He's eating chicken breast every day now to lose weight and build muscle.

mandarin_meaning: 1) 吃鹽（字面意思）；2) （口語、俚語）比喻有經驗、資歷較深或見得多
english_meaning: 1) to eat salt (literal); 2) (slang) to have more experience / to have been around longer
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 動詞（字面）；口語俚語用法可作述語/比喻用法
explanation_mandarin: 「食鹽」字面上指吃鹽，日常用於飲食。口語上可用作比喻，表示比別人經驗豐富或資歷較深（如「我食鹽多過你」）。
explanation_english: Literally 'to eat salt'. In everyday speech it can mean consuming salt. Colloquially it can be used idiomatically to say someone has more experience or seniority (e.g. 'I have eaten more salt than you').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生話我血壓高，要少食鹽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 waa6 ngo5 hyut3 aat3 gou1, jiu3 siu2 sik6 jim4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 医生说我血压高，要少吃盐。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor said my blood pressure is high; I should eat less salt.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好教我做，我食鹽多過你。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gaau3 ngo5 zou6, ngo5 sik6 jim4 do1 gwo3 nei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別教我做，我比你經驗多。
examples.english_sentence: Don't tell me what to do; I have more experience than you.

jyutping: sik6 jim4 do1 gwo3 nei5 sik6 mai5
mandarin_meaning: 我比你更有經驗；我比你年長
english_meaning: I've lived/experienced more than you; I'm older/more experienced than you
explanation_mandarin: 這句粵語俚語用來表明說話者比對方年長或經驗更多，常用來反駁、顯示權威或貶低對方的意見語氣，有時帶挑釁性。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang/idiom literally meaning "I've eaten more salt than you've eaten rice." It asserts that the speaker is older or has more life experience than the other person, often used to dismiss or rebuke someone and can sound rude or confrontational.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再教訓我，我食鹽多過你食米。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gaau3 fan3 ngo5, ngo5 sik6 jim4 do1 gwo3 nei5 sik6 mai5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再教訓我，我比你有更多經驗。
examples.english_sentence: Don't lecture me again — I've got more experience than you.

cantonese: 食鹽多過你食米，行橋多過你行路
jyutping: sik6 jim4 do1 gwo3 nei5 sik6 mai5, haang4 kiu4 do1 gwo3 nei5 haang4 lou6
mandarin_meaning: 比你經驗豐富、資歷更深（俗語）
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese proverb meaning someone has far more experience or has been through more than someone else.
explanation_mandarin: 一句廣東話俗語，字面為「吃的鹽比你吃的米多、過的橋比你走的路多」，用來表示某人經歷豐富、資歷深，常帶自豪或輕視意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese proverb literally saying 'I've eaten more salt than you've eaten rice, crossed more bridges than you've walked roads.' It expresses that someone has much more experience or seniority, often said boastfully or dismissively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿明唔好小看師傅，佢食鹽多過你食米，行橋多過你行路，經驗真係好豐富。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 ming4 m4 hou2 siu2 hon3 si1 fu6, keoi5 sik6 jim4 do1 gwo3 nei5 sik6 mai5, haang4 kiu4 do1 gwo3 nei5 haang4 lou6, ging1 jim6 zan1 hai6 hou2 fung1 fu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿明不要小看師傅，他吃的鹽比你吃的米多，過的橋比你走的路多，經驗真的很豐富。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Ming, don't underestimate the master; he's far more experienced than you—he has a lot of experience.

mandarin_meaning: 吃斋 / 吃素
english_meaning: to eat vegetarian food; to observe a vegetarian diet
explanation_mandarin: 指以素食為主的飲食習慣或暫時戒除葷食，常因宗教、文化或健康原因而為之。
explanation_english: To eat vegetarian food or follow a vegetarian diet. Often done for religious, cultural, or health reasons; can also mean temporarily abstaining from meat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日食齋，唔食肉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 sik6 zaai1, m4 sik6 juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天吃素，不吃肉。
examples.english_sentence: I'm eating vegetarian today; not eating meat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 去廟入面食齋係宗教儀式嘅一部分。
examples.jyutping_sentence: heoi3 miu6 jap6 min6 sik6 zaai1 hai6 zung1 gaau3 ji4 sik1 ge3 jat1 bou6 fan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在寺庙里吃斋是宗教仪式的一部分。
examples.english_sentence: Eating vegetarian food in a temple is part of religious rituals.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢暫時食齋保養身體。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zam6 si4 sik6 zaai1 bou2 joeng5 san1 tai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他暂时吃斋以保养身体。
examples.english_sentence: He is temporarily eating vegetarian to improve his health.

jyutping: sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6
mandarin_meaning: 即使吃到龍肉也覺得沒味道 / 毫無趣味
english_meaning: Not enjoyable or interesting at all (it's tasteless/boring even if it were the best thing)
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容某事物非常無聊或毫無吸引力，就算遇到再稀罕或美好的東西也覺得沒意思。
explanation_english: Used to describe something extremely boring or unappealing — even if it were the most extraordinary or delicious thing (metaphorically 'dragon meat'), it would still be tasteless/uninteresting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢部電影好悶，食龍肉都冇味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bou6 din6 jing2 hou2 mun6, sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這部電影很無聊，就算吃到龍肉也覺得沒味道。
examples.english_sentence: This movie is so boring that it wouldn't be enjoyable even if you were eating dragon meat.

jyutping: sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6
mandarin_meaning: 即使吃龍肉也覺得無味；形容對再好的事物也感到索然無味或麻木，不再有興趣或滿足感。
english_meaning: Literally 'even eating dragon meat tastes bland' — used to say that even the greatest pleasures bring no enjoyment; to be jaded, numb, or unimpressed.
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容人在心情或興趣上麻木、厭倦，連極佳的享受也覺得沒有滋味、提不起勁。
explanation_english: Used to describe someone who is emotionally numb or jaded — even intensely pleasurable things fail to give any enjoyment or interest.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 分手之後，佢連好嘅嘢都覺得冇意思，食龍肉都無味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fan1 sau2 zi1 hau6, keoi5 lin4 hou2 ge3 je5 dou1 gok3 dak1 mou5 ji3 si1, sik6 lung4 juk6 dou1 mou5 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 分手之後，他連好的東西都覺得沒意思，吃龍肉都無味。
examples.english_sentence: After the breakup, he finds even good things meaningless — even eating dragon meat tastes bland.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見詞語，無法確認通用或確切含義；字面上為「吃𩜠𩜠」，其中「𩜠」為罕用字，資料不足以提供標準解釋或對等詞
english_meaning: Rare/attested slang phrase with unclear or unconfirmed meaning; literally "eat 𩜠𩜠" where 𩜠 is a rare character and the phrase's usage/meaning cannot be confidently determined
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語/口語（疑似動詞或動賓結構，未能確定）
explanation_mandarin: 此詞包含罕用字「𩜠」，在常用粵語詞典及公開語料庫中缺乏可參考的例證。因資料不足，無法提供精確讀音與確定含義。若需準確解釋，建議提供更多語境或出處（例如對話、社交媒體原文、報章節錄）。
explanation_english: The phrase contains the rare character 𩜠 and lacks attested examples in common Cantonese dictionaries and corpora. Because information is insufficient, both pronunciation and meaning cannot be confirmed. To determine an accurate meaning, please supply more context or the original source (e.g., a quote from social media, conversation, or publication).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我冇聽過「食𩜠𩜠」，你講緊啲咩？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mou5 teng1 gwo3 "sik6 𩜠 𩜠", nei5 gong2 gan2 di1 me1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我沒聽過「食𩜠𩜠」，你在說什麼？
examples.english_sentence: I've never heard '食𩜠𩜠'—what are you talking about?

mandarin_meaning: （與「食」同義）吃、食物，為「食」的古字或異體字
english_meaning: An archaic/variant form of the character '食' — to eat; food
explanation_mandarin: 飠為漢字「食」的古字或異體字，常見於古籍或字形中，表示吃、食物等概念。現代漢語多用「食」或「吃」。
explanation_english: 飠 is an archaic/variant form of the character 食, used historically to denote eating or food. In modern usage, 食 or 吃 are typically used instead.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字係飠，係「食」嘅古字。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 hai6 sik6, hai6 'sik6' ge3 gu2 zi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字是飠，是“食”的古字。
examples.english_sentence: This character is '飠', an archaic form of '食' (to eat).

mandarin_meaning: 饑、饑餓
english_meaning: hunger; hungry (denoting lack of food)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞/形容詞 (表示饑餓狀態)
explanation_mandarin: 表示缺乏食物或感到饑餓，常與其他字合用形成詞語（如飢餓、飢荒），在書面語或成語中較常見。
explanation_english: Denotes lack of food or the condition of being hungry. Often combined with other characters (e.g., 飢餓, 飢荒). More common in written/formal contexts and idioms.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 長期飢餓會影響健康。
examples.jyutping_sentence: coeng4 kei4 gei1 ngo6 wui5 jing2 hoeng2 gin6 hong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 長期飢餓會影響健康。
examples.english_sentence: Prolonged hunger can affect health.

mandarin_meaning: 饥不择食
english_meaning: When starving or desperate, one cannot be picky; will accept anything available (often used as 'beggars can't be choosers').
explanation_mandarin: 形容人在飢餓或窮困、急需時不能挑剔，只能接受任何食物或機會。
explanation_english: Describes being so hungry or desperate that one cannot afford to be selective and must accept whatever food or opportunity is available.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰陣佢失業咗好耐，急需搵食，結果飢不擇食，乜都肯做。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 zan6 keoi5 sat1 jip6 zo2 hou2 noi6, gap1 seoi1 wan2 sik6, git3 gwo2 gei1 bat1 zaak6 sik6, mat1 dou1 hang2 zou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那時他失業很久，急需謀生，所以飢不擇食，什麼工作都肯做。
examples.english_sentence: At that time he had been unemployed for a long time and urgently needed to earn a living, so he would accept any job.

mandarin_meaning: 饑寒交迫（形容極度貧困，飢餓受凍）
english_meaning: suffering from hunger and cold; in dire poverty; in desperate need
explanation_mandarin: 形容生活極度貧困，缺乏衣食，飢餓受寒，處於非常困境之中。
explanation_english: Describes a state of extreme want — lacking food and shelter, suffering from hunger and cold; used to indicate dire poverty or desperate need.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 疫情咁嚴重，啲失業人士好快就會飢寒交迫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jik6 cing4 gam2 jim4 zung6, di1 sat1 jip6 jan4 si6 hou2 faai3 zau6 wui5 ji1 hon4 gaau1 bik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 疫情這麼嚴重，失業的人很快就會饑寒交迫。
examples.english_sentence: With the epidemic so severe, unemployed people will soon be in dire need, suffering from hunger and cold.

mandarin_meaning: 饥民（因饥荒或缺粮而受困的人民）
english_meaning: starving people; famine victims; the hungry populace
explanation_mandarin: 指因饥荒、粮食短缺或其他原因而挨饿的民众，常用于书面语或报道中。
explanation_english: Refers to people suffering from hunger or famine — those who are starving. The term is often used in written reports or formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 連年旱災，村入面出現咗好多飢民，需要外界援助。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lin4 nin4 hon6 zoi1, cyun1 jap6 min6 ceot1 jin2 zo2 hou2 do1 gei1 man4, seoi1 jiu3 ngoi6 gaai3 jyun4 zo6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 连年旱灾，村里出现了许多饥民，需要外界援助。
examples.english_sentence: Years of drought caused many people in the village to starve; they need external assistance.

mandarin_meaning: 饥渴（字面：又饿又渴；引申：渴望、急切，常用来形容性或关注上的“急切/饥渴”）
english_meaning: hungry and thirsty (literal); eager/desperate, often used figuratively to mean sexually or attention-wise desperate
explanation_mandarin: 「飢渴」可以指字面上的又餓又渴，也常用作比喻，表示對某事物（例如關注、性或認可）非常渴求、急切或看起來很「求關注/求愛」的狀態。
explanation_english: Literally means hungry and thirsty. Figuratively it describes a strong craving or eagerness (e.g., for attention or sex), implying someone appears desperate.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家好飢渴，想即刻搵嘢食同飲嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hou2 gei1 hot3, soeng2 zik1 hak1 wan2 je5 sik6 tung4 jam2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在又餓又渴，想馬上找東西吃和喝。
examples.english_sentence: I'm really hungry and thirsty right now; I want to find something to eat and drink immediately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢晒咗啲好挑逗嘅相，人哋話睇落好飢渴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 saai3 zo2 di1 hou2 tiu1 dau3 ge3 soeng2, jan4 dei6 waa6 tai2 lok6 hou2 gei1 hot3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他發了些很挑逗的照片，被人說看起來很饑渴。
examples.english_sentence: He posted some very provocative photos and people said he looked desperate.

mandarin_meaning: 饑荒 (jīhuāng)；糧食短缺導致的大規模飢餓現象
english_meaning: famine; widespread food shortage leading to mass hunger
explanation_mandarin: 指由於糧食減產、供應中斷或其他原因，導致大量人口缺乏食物、出現飢餓與營養不良的現象。
explanation_english: A situation in which large numbers of people lack sufficient food—often caused by crop failure, disrupted supplies, or other factors—resulting in widespread hunger and malnutrition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰年發生咗嚴重嘅飢荒，好多村民都冇嘢食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 nin4 faat3 sang1 zo2 jim4 zung6 ge3 gei1 fong1, hou2 do1 cyun1 man4 dou1 mou5 je5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那一年發生了嚴重的饑荒，很多村民都沒有東西吃。
examples.english_sentence: That year a severe famine occurred and many villagers had nothing to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 饥时吃荔枝，饱时吃黄皮；比喻人见利忘义、见好就来、没好处就走，或形容态度和口味随情况改变，善变或机会主义。
english_meaning: Literally 'eat lychees when hungry, eat yellow peel when full' — an idiom describing opportunistic, fickle or self‑serving behavior: people who flock to you for benefits but abandon you when there's nothing in it for them.
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語用水果的比喻表達人隨境遇改變態度或只圖利害、見好就來、見壞就走的機會主義或善變行為。
explanation_english: This Cantonese proverb uses fruit imagery to describe someone who changes their attitude with circumstances or acts opportunistically — coming around when there's something to gain and disappearing when there isn't.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啲朋友有利就湊埋嚟，無利又走，真係飢食荔枝，飽食黃皮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 di1 pang4 jau5 lei6 zau6 cau3 maai4 lai4, mou4 lei6 jau6 zau2, zan1 hai6 gei1-sik6-lai6-zi1, baau2-sik6-wong4-pei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他那些朋友有利可圖時就湊上來，沒利益時又走，真是飢時吃荔枝，飽時吃黃皮。
examples.english_sentence: His friends flock to him when there's profit but leave when there's none — truly 'eat lychees when hungry, eat yellow peel when full' (i.e., opportunistic).

mandarin_meaning: 饥饿；缺乏食物或感到饿
english_meaning: hunger; starving; the state of lacking food or feeling hungry
explanation_mandarin: 表示缺乏食物或感到肚子餓的狀態，可作名詞（飢餓）或形容詞（感到飢餓）。在書面或正式語境中較常見。
explanation_english: Refers to the state of lacking food or feeling hungry. Can function as a noun (hunger) or an adjective (hungry). More common in formal or written contexts compared with colloquial terms like "hungry."

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋因為失業，長期處於飢餓狀態，連一餐都食唔飽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 jan1 wai6 sat1 jip6, coeng4 kei4 cyu5 jyu1 gei1 ngo6 zong6 taai3, lin4 jat1 caan1 dou1 sik6 m4 baau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们因为失业，长期处于饥饿状态，连一顿饭都吃不饱。
examples.english_sentence: They have been in a state of hunger for a long time due to unemployment, not even able to eat a full meal.

mandarin_meaning: 饑荒；嚴重缺乏糧食
english_meaning: famine; severe shortage of food
explanation_mandarin: 指因天災、戰亂或其他原因導致糧食大量短缺，造成廣泛飢餓和死亡的災害。
explanation_english: A severe shortage of food, often caused by drought, war, or other disasters, leading to widespread hunger and sometimes death.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個地區多年旱災，最後爆發咗嚴重嘅飢饉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 dei6 keoi1 do1 nin4 hon6 zoi1, zeoi3 hau6 baau3faat3 zo2 jim4 zung6 ge3 gei1 gan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個地區多年乾旱，最後爆發了嚴重的饑荒。
examples.english_sentence: This region suffered years of drought and eventually a severe famine broke out.

mandarin_meaning: 飯；餐食（多用於書面或古語，常指晚飯或正餐）
english_meaning: meal; (literary) dinner or main meal
explanation_mandarin: 「飧」為書面或古漢語用字，指一餐或正餐，常用於組合詞如「晚飧」「晏飧」等，表示吃飯、用膳。
explanation_english: A literary or classical term for a meal, often referring to dinner or a main meal. Appears in compounds like '晚飧' (dinner).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋食飧去邊？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 sik6 seon1 heoi3 bin1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我们去哪里吃饭？
examples.english_sentence: Where are we going to eat dinner tonight?

mandarin_meaning: 餛飩／雲吞（小型麵皮包餡的中式餃類）
english_meaning: wonton (a small Chinese dumpling with filling)
explanation_mandarin: 指一種以薄麵皮包住肉或其他餡料的中式小吃，常見於餛飩或雲吞，通常可做成雲吞湯或雲吞麵。廣東話中常作為雲吞或餛飩的字，讀作 tan2。
explanation_english: Refers to a wonton — a small Chinese dumpling made with a thin dough wrapper and savory filling. Commonly served in wonton soup or with noodles. In Cantonese the character is pronounced tan2 and appears in words like 雲吞.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我肚餓，想食碗熱騰騰嘅雲吞湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tou5 ngo6, soeng2 sik6 wun2 jit6 tang4 tang4 ge3 wan4 tan2 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我肚子餓，想吃一碗熱騰騰的雲吞湯。
examples.english_sentence: I'm hungry; I want a bowl of hot wonton soup.

mandarin_meaning: 烹饪（rèn），指烹調食物
english_meaning: to cook; cooking; culinary arts
explanation_mandarin: 表示烹調食物的行為或技藝，常見於詞語「烹飪」。
explanation_english: Refers to the act or skill of preparing and cooking food; commonly used in the compound "烹飪" (cooking).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我鍾意烹飪，成日喺屋企試新嘅食譜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung1 ji3 paang1 jam6, seng4 jat6 hai2 uk1 kei5 si3 san1 ge3 sik6 pou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我喜欢烹饪，经常在家尝试新的菜谱。
examples.english_sentence: I like cooking; I often try new recipes at home.

mandarin_meaning: 饭；一餐（煮熟的米饭或泛指一顿饭）
english_meaning: rice; a meal
explanation_mandarin: 指煮熟的米饭，也常用来泛指一餐（例如「食飯」表示吃飯）。在粵語中可與其他詞組合，如飯盒、飯局等。
explanation_english: Refers to cooked rice and commonly to a meal (e.g., 食飯 = to eat a meal). In Cantonese it combines with other words like 飯盒 (lunchbox) or 飯局 (dinner gathering).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你食咗飯未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你吃饭了吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you eaten yet?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚我哋一齊去食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚我们一起去吃饭。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go have dinner together tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗個飯盒返工食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 go3 faan6 hap6 faan1 gung1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他买了饭盒带到公司吃。
examples.english_sentence: He bought a lunchbox to eat at work.

mandarin_meaning: 罕見字組合，第二字「㼞」為罕用漢字，現代普通話中無固定意義或讀音；在粵語資料中亦甚少見，常需視上下文判斷或認為為誤寫／古文用字。
english_meaning: An obscure/rare written form: the second character '㼞' is an extremely uncommon Chinese character with no established modern Cantonese or Mandarin pronunciation or meaning. Typically seen only in historical texts, rare names, or as a possible typo/variant.
explanation_mandarin: 「飯㼞」包含普通字「飯」，但「㼞」為罕見漢字，現代粵語與普通話中無固定讀音與釋義。遇到此組合時，常需參考原文上下文、校勘或專家注釋；在日常口語中幾乎不用。
explanation_english: The compound '飯㼞' pairs the common character '飯' with a highly obscure character '㼞'. The latter has no established modern pronunciation or meaning in Cantonese or Mandarin. When encountered, interpretation depends on context or textual emendation; it is virtually absent from everyday spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 『飯㼞』呢個寫法好罕見，日常粵語好少見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: 「faan6 (㼞 zi6 duk6 jam1 bat1 coeng4)」 ni1 go3 se2faat3 hou2 hon2gin3, jat6soeng4 jyut6jyu5 hou2 siu2 gin3 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「飯㼞」這種寫法很罕見，日常粵語中很少見到。
examples.english_sentence: '飯㼞' is a very rare written form and is seldom seen in everyday Cantonese.

mandarin_meaning: 便當盒；飯盒；用來裝飯或食物的容器
english_meaning: lunchbox; food container (used to carry meals)
explanation_mandarin: 指用來裝飯或其他食物、方便外出或上學、上班時帶飯的容器，類似便當盒或飯盒的意思。
explanation_english: A container used to hold rice or other food for taking meals away from home—essentially a lunchbox or tiffin.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我成日都帶個飯兜返工，咁就唔洗喺公司買午餐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sing4 jat6 dou1 daai3 go3 faan6 dau1 faan1 gung1, gam2 zau6 m4 sai2 hai2 gung1 si1 maai5 ng5 caan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我经常带着饭兜去上班，这样就不用在公司买午餐。
examples.english_sentence: I often bring a lunchbox to work, so I don't have to buy lunch at the office.

mandarin_meaning: 靠別人吃飯；寄生、當免費食客
english_meaning: freeloader; someone who lives off others
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俚語，指不自力更生、依靠他人供養或常常吃別人免費的飯，類似“靠人吃飯”或“寄生”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang term for a person who freeloads — someone who depends on others for food or support and does not fend for themselves.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日唔做嘢，淨係識做飯公。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 m4 zou6 je5, zing6 hai6 sik1 zou6 faan6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他整天不工作，只會靠別人吃飯。
examples.english_sentence: He never works and just freeloads off other people.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好做飯公，快啲搵工啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zou6 faan6 gung1, faai3 di1 wan2 gung1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別當飯公，快點找工作吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be a freeloader — find a job quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 餐飲商家；以售賣食物或經營餐館為業的人或商家
english_meaning: a food vendor / restaurateur; a business or person engaged in selling food or running a restaurant
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指以售賣食物、經營食肆或餐館為職業或營業對象的個人或商家，常見於香港粵語語境。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term referring to a person or business whose trade is selling food or operating eateries/restaurants; commonly used in Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺街市做飯商，專門賣熟食俾街坊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 gaai1 si5 zou6 faan6 soeng1, zyun1 mun4 maai6 suk6 sik6 bei2 gaai1 fong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在街市做飯商，專門賣熟食給街坊。
examples.english_sentence: He works as a food vendor in the market, specializing in selling cooked food to the neighbors.

mandarin_meaning: 饭团（用白饭捏成的球状或三角形食物，有时包海苔或夹馅）
english_meaning: rice ball (a ball- or triangle-shaped food made of cooked rice, sometimes wrapped with seaweed or filled)
explanation_mandarin: 飯團是用煮熟的白飯捏成的食物，可以是圓形或三角形，常見於日本（如御飯糰）或亞洲其他地區，有時會包上海苔或包入餡料。
explanation_english: A food item made from cooked rice formed into a ball or triangle. Commonly seen in Japan (onigiri) and other Asian cuisines; often wrapped with seaweed or filled with savory ingredients.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我朝早買咗個飯團當早餐食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 maai5 zo2 go3 faan6 tyun4 dong3 zou2 caan1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我早上买了一个饭团当早餐吃。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a rice ball this morning to eat for breakfast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 日本嘅飯團通常用海苔包住。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat6 bun2 ge3 faan6 tyun4 tung1 soeng4 jung6 hoi2 toi4 baau1 zyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 日本的饭团通常用海苔包着。
examples.english_sentence: Japanese rice balls are usually wrapped in seaweed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 細個我最鍾意媽媽整嘅飯團。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sai3 go3 ngo5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 maa4 maa1 zing2 ge3 faan6 tyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小时候我最喜欢妈妈做的饭团。
examples.english_sentence: When I was little I liked my mom's rice balls the most.

mandarin_meaning: 饭堂 / 餐厅（供集體用餐的場所）
english_meaning: canteen; cafeteria; dining hall
explanation_mandarin: 指學校、公司或其他機構內供師生或員工集體就餐的場所，也泛指提供簡餐的食堂或自助餐區。
explanation_english: Refers to a place where people in schools, companies, or institutions eat together; a canteen/cafeteria or dining hall that provides meals, often inexpensive and for a group.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學校嘅飯堂今日有新嘅午餐選擇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 haau6 ge3 faan6 tong4 gam1 jat6 jau5 san1 ge3 ng5 caan1 syun2 zaak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 学校的饭堂今天有新的午餐选择。
examples.english_sentence: The school's cafeteria has new lunch options today.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲職員都喺飯堂食緊午餐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 zik1 jyun4 dou1 hai2 faan6 tong4 sik6 gan2 ng5 caan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 员工都在饭堂吃午餐。
examples.english_sentence: The staff are all eating lunch in the canteen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 飯堂嘅價錢比外面平好多。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faan6 tong4 ge3 gaa3 cin4 bei2 ngoi6 min6 peng4 hou2 do1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 饭堂的价格比外面便宜很多。
examples.english_sentence: The cafeteria's prices are much cheaper than outside.

mandarin_meaning: 饭局 (聚餐、宴請，常指社交或公事性的應酬吃飯)
english_meaning: dinner engagement; meal gathering; banquet (often a social or business dinner)
explanation_mandarin: 指為了社交、應酬或處理公事而聚在一起吃飯的場合，可包含朋友聚餐、應酬客戶或宴會。
explanation_english: Refers to a meal gathering or banquet held for socializing, entertaining, or business purposes; can be a friendly meal, a client entertainment, or a banquet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚有個飯局，我要去應酬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jau5 go3 faan6 guk6, ngo5 jiu3 heoi3 jing3 cau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚有个饭局，我得去应酬。
examples.english_sentence: There's a dinner engagement tonight; I have to attend for social/business reasons.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個飯局係同客戶傾生意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 faan6 guk6 hai6 tung4 haak3 wu6 king1 saang1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个饭局是和客户谈生意。
examples.english_sentence: This dinner is to discuss business with the client.

mandarin_meaning: 饭店（可指餐馆或旅馆/酒店，视语境而定）
english_meaning: fàndiàn / a restaurant or hotel (meaning depends on context)
explanation_mandarin: 「飯店」在不同語境下可指提供用餐的場所（尤其是中式餐館）或指旅館、酒店；具體含義需看上下文。
explanation_english: The term can mean a restaurant (often a Chinese-style eatery) or a hotel; the exact sense depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺飯店訂咗位，八點見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 faan6 dim3 deng6 zo2 wai6, baat3 dim2 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们在饭店订了位，八点见。
examples.english_sentence: We booked a table at the restaurant. See you at 8.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話佢住喺嗰間飯店，幾方便。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 keoi5 zyu6 hai2 go2 gaan1 faan6 dim3, gei2 fong1 bin6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他说他住在那家饭店，很方便。
examples.english_sentence: He said he stays at that hotel; it's very convenient.

mandarin_meaning: 饭厅 / 餐厅（家居內用來吃飯的房間）
english_meaning: dining room
explanation_mandarin: 指住宅內用來吃飯的房間，通常放有餐桌和椅子，供家庭用餐或招待客人用餐。
explanation_english: A room in a home used for having meals, typically furnished with a dining table and chairs for family meals or entertaining guests.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚喺飯廳食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 hai2 faan6 teng1 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚在饭厅吃饭。
examples.english_sentence: We're eating dinner in the dining room tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 飯後鬧鐘 / 飯後提醒（通常用來提醒在飯後做某事，例如吃藥、散步或運動）
english_meaning: post-meal alarm / reminder (an alarm set for after a meal, often to remind someone to take medicine, walk, or exercise)
explanation_mandarin: 指設定在飯後響起的鬧鐘或提醒，用途通常是提醒人在飯後服藥、散步、運動或做其他需要在飯後進行的事。
explanation_english: Refers to an alarm or reminder set to go off after a meal. Common uses include reminding someone to take medication, go for a walk, or perform other post-meal tasks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我設咗個飯後鐘俾爸媽，等佢哋唔會唔記得食藥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 cit3 zo2 go3 faan6 hau6 zung1 bei2 baa4 maa1 deng2 keoi5 dei6 m4 wui5 m4 gei3 dak1 sik6 joek6
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我給爸媽設置了飯後提醒，讓他們不會忘記吃藥。
examples.english_sentence: I set a post-meal alarm for my parents so they won't forget to take their medicine.

mandarin_meaning: 飯桌、餐桌
english_meaning: dining table
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指用來吃飯的桌子，等同普通話的「飯桌/餐桌」。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term for the table used for meals (dining table).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺飯枱食晚飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 faan6 toi2 sik6 maan5 faan6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在飯桌上吃晚飯吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's eat dinner at the dining table.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友唔可以喺飯枱度玩手機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 m4 ho2 ji5 hai2 faan6 toi2 dou6 waan2 sau2 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友不可以在飯桌上玩手機。
examples.english_sentence: Children should not play with phones at the dining table.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗張新飯枱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 zoeng1 san1 faan6 toi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她買了一張新飯桌。
examples.english_sentence: He/She bought a new dining table.

mandarin_meaning: 飯桌（餐桌，用於吃飯的桌子）
english_meaning: dining table; meal table
explanation_mandarin: 指一家人或多人吃飯時所用的桌子；也可引申為飯桌上的聚會或談話場合（例如『在飯桌上聊天』）。
explanation_english: Refers to the table used for meals; can also be extended to mean gatherings or conversations that happen at the dining table (e.g., 'at the dinner table').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺飯桌上傾偈，唔好講公事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 faan6 zoek3 soeng6 king1 gai2, m4 hou2 gong2 gung1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在飯桌上聊天，不要談公事。
examples.english_sentence: We're chatting at the dining table; don't talk about work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 飯桌唔係討論生意嘅地方。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faan6 zoek3 m4 hai6 tou2 leon6 saang1 ji3 ge3 dei6 fong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 飯桌不是討論生意的地方。
examples.english_sentence: The dining table is not a place to discuss business.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽買咗張新飯桌，屋企而家大啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 maai5 zo2 zoeng1 san1 faan6 zoek3, uk1 kei5 ji4 gaa1 daai6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽買了張新的飯桌，家裡現在寬敞多了。
examples.english_sentence: Mom bought a new dining table; the home feels bigger now.

mandarin_meaning: 饭桶 (fàntǒng)：比喻无能、没用或懒惰的人；字面意思是盛饭的容器。
english_meaning: A useless person; good-for-nothing (literally 'rice bucket').
explanation_mandarin: 在粤语中，“飯桶”常作贬义，指不做事、没用或懒惰的人；也有字面意义指盛饭的容器。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '飯桶' is a derogatory slang term for someone useless, lazy, or good-for-nothing. Literally it means a container for rice.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日都唔做嘢，真係個飯桶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 dou1 m4 zou6 je5, zan1 hai6 go3 faan6 tung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是不做事，真是个饭桶。
examples.english_sentence: He never does any work — he's really a good-for-nothing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老細唔鍾意懶人，唔會要一個飯桶入職。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 sai3 m4 zung1 ji3 laan5 jan4, m4 wui5 jiu3 jat1 go3 faan6 tung4 jap6 zik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板不喜欢懒人，不会聘用饭桶。
examples.english_sentence: The boss doesn't like lazy people; he won't hire a deadbeat.

mandarin_meaning: 飯桌；（口語）指請客吃飯、應酬的場合或飯局
english_meaning: dining table; (colloquial) a meal/banquet or occasion for social or business entertaining (a business meal to entertain clients)
explanation_mandarin: 字面上指擺放飯菜的桌子（飯桌）。口語中常用來指吃飯應酬、招待客戶或洽談生意的飯局場合。
explanation_english: Literally the dining table. Colloquially used to refer to a meal or banquet used for social or business entertaining — e.g., taking clients out for a meal to socialize or do business.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢張飯檯好大，夠晒我哋一家人食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 zoeng1 faan6 toi4 hou2 daai6, gau3 saai3 ngo5 dei6 jat1 gaa1 jan4 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這張飯桌很大，夠我們一家人吃飯。
examples.english_sentence: This dining table is big enough for our whole family to eat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日要去飯檯應酬客戶，攰到冇時間休息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 jiu3 heoi3 faan6 toi4 jing3 cau3 haak3 wu6, gui6 dou3 mou5 si4 gaan3 jau1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常要去飯局應酬客戶，累得沒時間休息。
examples.english_sentence: He often has to attend business meals to entertain clients and is so tired he has no time to rest.

mandarin_meaning: （1）米壳、稻壳；（2）口語、貶義：靠他人（尤其靠父母）養活的人，類似“啃老族”或“寄生蟲”。
english_meaning: (1) rice husk / rice hull; (2) colloquial (derogatory): a person who lives off others (especially parents) — a freeloader/parasite.
explanation_mandarin: 「飯殼」在廣東話有兩種常見用法：一是字面義，指米加工後剩下的外殼（米糠／稻殼）；二是口語貶義，用來形容不工作、靠父母或他人養活的成年人，相當於“啃老者”或“寄生蟲”。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "飯殼" has two common uses: (1) literal — the husk/hull left after processing rice; (2) colloquial (pejorative) — someone who doesn't work and lives off others (especially parents), i.e., a freeloader or parasite.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲米碾完之後成堆嘅飯殼可以做堆肥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 mai5 lin6 jyun4 zi1 hau6 sing4 deoi1 ge3 faan6 hok3 ho2 ji5 zou6 deoi1 fei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些米加工后剩下的米壳可以做堆肥。
examples.english_sentence: The rice husks left after milling can be used as compost.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日唔肯搵工，淨係做個飯殼，靠父母養。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 m4 hang2 wan2 gung1, zing6 hai6 zou6 go3 faan6 hok3, kaau3 fu6 mou5 joeng5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他成天不肯找工作，只靠父母养活，简直就是个啃老族。
examples.english_sentence: He never looks for a job and just lives off his parents; he's basically a freeloader.

mandarin_meaning: 飯後犯困；因消化或血流分配導致的胸悶、頭暈或強烈想睡
english_meaning: post-meal drowsiness/discomfort (postprandial somnolence); feeling sleepy, dizzy, or chest discomfort after eating
explanation_mandarin: 飯氣攻心是粵語俗語，指吃完飯後由於消化或血液由腦部轉向消化器官等原因，出現胸悶、頭暈、腹脹或強烈想睡的現象，也常用來泛指餐後犯困。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial idiom describing the drowsiness or discomfort after eating. Caused by digestion-related factors and blood-flow redistribution, it can produce chest tightness, dizziness, bloating, or a strong desire to sleep. Often used to mean 'post-meal sleepiness.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我食完飯之後好易就飯氣攻心，成個人好想訓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sik6 jyun4 faan6 zi1 hau6 hou2 ji6 zau6 faan6 hei3 gung1 sam1, sing4 go3 jan4 hou2 soeng2 fan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我吃完饭后很容易犯困，整个人很想睡觉。
examples.english_sentence: After I eat I easily get post-meal drowsiness and feel like sleeping.

mandarin_meaning: 饭汤 / 米汤（煮饭或煮稀饭时产生的淀粉水或稀薄的汤汁）
english_meaning: rice water / rice soup (the starchy broth produced when cooking rice or thin broth from porridge)
explanation_mandarin: 指煮饭时产生的淀粉水或煮稀饭（粥）时的稀薄汤汁，可作为汤底、给婴幼儿食用或作为家常养生食材。
explanation_english: Refers to the starchy liquid produced when cooking rice or the thin broth from porridge. It can be used as a soup base, given to infants, or used in home cooking for its mild flavor and nutrition.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日話飲飯湯對腸胃好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 waa6 jam2 faan6 tong1 deoi3 coeng4 wai6 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 妈妈常说喝饭汤对肠胃好。
examples.english_sentence: Mom often says drinking rice water is good for the stomach.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋用飯湯整湯底，令味道更鮮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jung6 faan6 tong1 zing2 tong1 dai2, ling6 mei6 dou6 gang3 sin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们用饭汤做汤底，令味道更鲜。
examples.english_sentence: We use rice water as a soup base to make the flavor fresher.

examples.cantonese_sentence: BB唔肯食飯，只肯飲飯湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: BB m4 hang2 sik6 faan6, zi2 hang2 jam2 faan6 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 宝宝不肯吃饭，只肯喝饭汤。
examples.english_sentence: The baby won't eat rice, only drinks the rice water.

mandarin_meaning: 鍋巴；飯煲底煮焦或煎脆的飯
english_meaning: scorched rice; the crispy crust of rice stuck to the bottom of a pot
explanation_mandarin: 指在煮飯或焗飯時，鍋底形成焦脆的一層飯，常被當作小食或調味的配料。
explanation_english: Refers to the layer of rice that becomes scorched and crispy at the bottom of the pot when cooking; often eaten as a snack or prized for its texture and flavor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲飯焦好香，我鍾意食脆脆嗰啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 faan6 ziu1 hou2 hoeng1, ngo5 zung1 ji3 sik6 ceoi3 ceoi3 go2 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那些鍋巴很香，我喜歡吃脆脆的部分。
examples.english_sentence: The scorched rice is fragrant; I like eating the crispy parts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 媽媽煮飯時唔小心整焦咗，底部有層飯焦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maa4 maa1 zyu2 faan6 si4 m4 siu2 sam1 zeng2 ziu1 zo2, dai2 bou6 jau5 cang4 faan6 ziu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽煮飯時不小心把飯煮焦了，底部有一層鍋巴。
examples.english_sentence: Mom accidentally burned the rice while cooking; there's a layer of scorched rice at the bottom.

mandarin_meaning: 电饭煲；饭锅
english_meaning: rice cooker; rice pot (especially electric rice cooker)
explanation_mandarin: 指用來煮飯的容器，尤指電飯煲或飯鍋。在香港口語中常簡稱電飯煲為「飯煲」。
explanation_english: A container used to cook rice, especially an electric rice cooker; a common household appliance. In Hong Kong colloquial speech it is often shortened to "faan bou" to mean an electric rice cooker.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我買咗個新飯煲，今晚可以煮多啲飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 maai5 zo2 go3 san1 faan6 bou1, gam1 maan5 ho2 ji5 zyu2 do1 di1 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我买了一个新的电饭煲，今晚可以煮多些饭。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a new rice cooker, we can cook more rice tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 饭盒 (fànhé)
english_meaning: lunchbox; food container; tiffin box
explanation_mandarin: 用來盛載午餐或便當的容器，常見於上班、上學或外出時攜帶食物。
explanation_english: A container used to hold lunch or packed meals, commonly brought to work, school, or outings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝帶咗個飯盒返工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 daai3 zo2 go3 faan6 hap6 faan1 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天早上带了一个饭盒去上班。
examples.english_sentence: This morning I brought a lunchbox to work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢個飯盒好重，裡面有好多餸。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 go3 faan6 hap6 hou2 zung6, leoi5 min6 jau5 hou2 do1 sung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她的饭盒很重，里面有很多菜。
examples.english_sentence: His/her lunchbox is heavy; it has a lot of dishes inside.

mandarin_meaning: 飯碗（字面：盛飯的碗；引申：工作、職位或維持生計的來源）
english_meaning: Rice bowl (literal: a bowl for rice; figurative: a job, position, or means of livelihood)
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是盛飯的碗；在口語中常用作比喻，指一個人維持生計的工作或職位，例如「保住飯碗」表示保住工作。
explanation_english: Literally a bowl for rice. Colloquially used metaphorically to mean a person's job, position, or source of livelihood (e.g. "to keep one's rice bowl" = to keep one's job).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗養家，我要保住條飯碗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 joeng5 gaa1, ngo5 jiu3 bou2 zyu6 tiu4 faan6 wun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了養家，我要保住這份工作。
examples.english_sentence: To support my family, I need to keep my job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 飯碗打破咗，要買個新嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faan6 wun2 daa2 po3 zo2, jiu3 maai5 go3 san1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 飯碗打破了，要買一個新的。
examples.english_sentence: The rice bowl broke; I need to buy a new one.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府想保住本地人嘅飯碗，推出咗新政策。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 soeng2 bou2 zyu6 bun2 dei6 jan4 ge3 faan6 wun2, teoi1 ceot1 zo2 san1 zing3 caak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府為了保住本地人的工作，推出了新政策。
examples.english_sentence: The government introduced new policies to protect local people's jobs.

mandarin_meaning: 饭票；比喻提供经济支持的人（如包养者）或保证生计的来源/稳定收入
english_meaning: literally 'meal ticket'; colloquially a person who provides financial support (e.g. a 'sugar daddy/mama') or a guaranteed source of income/livelihood
explanation_mandarin: 「飯票」原意為可換飯錢的票券，在粵語口語中常用作比喻：指為某人提供經濟支持的人（如包養者），或指穩定的收入來源、賴以謀生的對象。
explanation_english: Originally 'meal ticket', in Cantonese slang it's used metaphorically to mean a person who provides financial support (e.g. a sugar daddy/mama) or a stable source of income/a livelihood.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我嘅飯票。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 ge3 faan6 piu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他／她是我的饭票。
examples.english_sentence: He/She is my meal ticket (provides for me financially).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好淨係當人係你嘅飯票。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 dong3 jan4 hai6 nei5 ge3 faan6 piu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要只是把人当成你的饭票。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just treat someone as your meal ticket.

mandarin_meaning: 飯團 (fàntuán)
english_meaning: rice ball
explanation_mandarin: 指用煮熟的米（常為糯米或白米）捏成的球或卷，通常包有餡料，是常見的小吃或早餐。
explanation_english: A ball or roll made from cooked rice (often glutinous or plain rice), typically filled with ingredients; a common snack or breakfast item.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我朝早喺街市買咗個熱辣辣嘅飯糰做早餐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 hai2 gaai1 si5 maai5 zo2 go3 jit6 laat6 laat6 ge3 faan6 tyun4 zou6 zou2 caan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我早上在菜市場買了一個熱騰騰的飯團當早餐。
examples.english_sentence: I bought a hot rice ball at the market this morning for breakfast.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢好鍾意食飯糰，尤其係有肉鬆嗰款。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6 faan6 tyun4, jau4 kei4 hai6 jau5 juk6 sung1 go2 fun2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他很喜歡吃飯團，尤其是有肉鬆的那種。
examples.english_sentence: He really likes eating rice balls, especially the ones with pork floss.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）開始或習慣吃素、成為素食者
english_meaning: Colloquial: to start or habitually eat a vegetarian diet; to go vegetarian
explanation_mandarin: 飯素是廣東話的口語說法，表示開始或習慣吃素、成為素食者，與普通話的「吃素／食素」相當。此用法較口語化，部分地區或場合中較少見，通常可以和「食素」互換。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to start or habitually follow a vegetarian diet (to go vegetarian). It is roughly equivalent to Mandarin "吃素" or Cantonese "食素" and is mainly used in informal speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近開始飯素，已經一個月冇食過肉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 hoi1 ci2 faan6 sou3, ji5 ging1 jat1 go3 jyut6 mou5 sik6 gwo3 juk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近開始吃素，已經一個月沒吃過肉。
examples.english_sentence: He recently started eating vegetarian; he hasn't eaten meat for a month.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好逼人飯素，尊重別人嘅選擇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bik1 jan4 faan6 sou3, zyun1 zung6 bit6 jan4 ge3 syun2 zaak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要逼人吃素，尊重別人的選擇。
examples.english_sentence: Don't force people to be vegetarian; respect others' choices.

mandarin_meaning: 聚餐；吃飯聚會
english_meaning: a meal gathering; to meet up for a meal
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞／動詞（可作名詞或動詞）
partOfSpeech_english: noun / verb (can be used as either)
explanation_mandarin: 「飯聚」是粵語口語，指朋友、同事等為了吃飯而聚在一起的活動，相當於普通話的“聚餐”。
explanation_english: “飯聚” is a Cantonese colloquial term referring to people gathering to eat together (e.g., friends or colleagues). It corresponds to Mandarin '聚餐' and means a meal get-together.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚有個飯聚，你會唔會去？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 jau5 go3 faan6 zeoi6, nei5 wui5 m4 wui5 heoi3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚有一個聚餐，你會不會去？
examples.english_sentence: There's a dinner gathering tonight — are you going?

mandarin_meaning: 提供經濟支持或經常請客的人；靠他/她吃飯的人（口語、俚語）
english_meaning: a person who provides regular financial support or who frequently treats someone to meals; a provider/sponsor (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「飯腳」是廣東話口語，指經常為另一人付出生活開支或經常請客的人；有時帶有依賴或靠他人生活的含義。
explanation_english: In Cantonese slang, '飯腳' refers to someone who regularly provides financial support or treats another person to meals. It can imply a dependent–provider relationship (e.g., a sponsor or 'sugar daddy'), or more generally an income/provider source.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日請我食飯，佢係我個飯腳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 cing2 ngo5 sik6 faan6, keoi5 hai6 ngo5 go3 faan6 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他經常請我吃飯，他是我的飯腳（提供經濟支持的人）。
examples.english_sentence: He often treats me to meals; he's my provider/sponsor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司裁員之後，我冇飯腳，唔知道點算好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 coi4 jyun4 zi1 hau6, ngo5 mou5 faan6 goek3, m4 zi1 dou3 dim2 syun3 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司裁員之後，我沒有飯腳，也不知道該怎麼辦。
examples.english_sentence: After the company's layoffs, I have no provider/income source and don't know what to do.

mandarin_meaning: 饭盖（饭锅或饭煲等容器的盖子）
english_meaning: lid/cover of a rice pot or rice cooker (rice container lid)
explanation_mandarin: 指盛饭的容器（例如饭锅、饭煲、饭盒等）所使用的盖子，日常口语中直接称为“饭盖”。
explanation_english: Refers to the lid or cover of a rice container (e.g., rice pot, rice cooker, lunchbox). A common everyday noun for that household item.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廚房個飯蓋唔見咗，你見過未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyu4 fong4 go3 faan6 goi3 m4 gin3 zo2, nei5 gin3 gwo3 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 厨房的饭盖不见了，你有看见吗？
examples.english_sentence: The rice pot lid in the kitchen is missing — have you seen it?

mandarin_meaning: 饭渣；剩下的米粒
english_meaning: rice residue; leftover grains of rice (small bits stuck in a bowl or at the mouth)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语词，指碗里、碟上或嘴边剩下的小米粒、饭粒，常用于日常生活描述残留的饭粒。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term referring to small grains or bits of rice left behind in a bowl, on a plate, or stuck at the mouth/teeth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 碗底仲有啲飯蕊，記得掃乾淨。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wun2 dai2 zung6 jau5 di1 faan6 jeoi2, gei3 dak1 sou3 gon1 zeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 碗底还有些饭渣，记得扫干净。
examples.english_sentence: There are still some rice grains at the bottom of the bowl; remember to clean them out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你口邊有飯蕊，要唔要我幫你抹下？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 hau2 bin1 jau5 faan6 jeoi2, jiu3 m4 jiu3 ngo5 bong1 nei5 mut3 haa5?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你嘴边有饭粒，要不要我帮你擦一下？
examples.english_sentence: You have rice stuck at the side of your mouth; do you want me to wipe it for you?

mandarin_meaning: 進餐時穿的保護衣物（如嬰兒圍兜或簡單圍裙）
english_meaning: a garment worn while eating (e.g., a baby's bib or a simple dining apron)
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，通常指小孩或嬰兒吃飯時穿的圍兜或保護衣，用來防止弄髒衣服。有時亦可泛指在飯時穿的簡單圍裙。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese term for a protective garment worn during meals, typically a baby's bib or a simple apron to keep clothes clean while eating.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿仔食飯個陣要著返件飯衣，免得整污糟衫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 zai2 sik6 faan6 go3 zan6 jiu3 zoek3 faan1 gin6 faan6 ji1, min5 dak1 zing2 wu1 zou1 saam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 孩子吃飯的時候要穿上飯衣，以免把衣服弄髒。
examples.english_sentence: Put a bib on the child when eating so their clothes don't get dirty.

mandarin_meaning: 饭钱 (fàn qián)
english_meaning: meal money; money for food or meals; meal allowance
explanation_mandarin: 指用來買飯或支付餐費的錢，口語中常用於粵語（香港）表示吃飯所需的錢或膳食津貼。
explanation_english: Refers to money used to buy meals or pay for food. Commonly used in Cantonese (Hong Kong) to mean meal money or a meal allowance.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我冇帶飯錢，唔該借我二十蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 mou5 daai3 faan6 cin2, m4 goi1 ze3 ngo5 ji6 sap6 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我沒帶飯錢，請借我二十塊。
examples.english_sentence: I didn't bring any meal money; please lend me HK$20.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司會俾加班嘅員工飯錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 wui5 bei2 gaa1 baan1 ge3 jyun4 gung1 faan6 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司會給加班的員工飯錢。
examples.english_sentence: The company gives meal money to employees who work overtime.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿媽成日問我去學校有冇帶飯錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 maa1 sing4 jat6 man6 ngo5 heoi3 hok6 haau6 jau5 mou5 daai3 faan6 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 媽媽常常問我去學校有沒有帶飯錢。
examples.english_sentence: My mom often asks whether I brought meal money to school.

mandarin_meaning: 饭铲（用來盛飯或鏟飯的廚具）
english_meaning: rice spatula / rice scoop (kitchen utensil for serving or scooping rice)
explanation_mandarin: 指廚房中用來盛、鏟或翻動飯的鏟子，通常為塑膠、木或金屬製。
explanation_english: A kitchen utensil used for scooping, serving, or turning rice; commonly made of plastic, wood, or metal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 可唔可以畀我個飯鏟？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bei2 ngo5 go3 faan6 caan2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 可以把飯鏟給我嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Could you give me the rice spatula?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 廚房入面嗰個飯鏟唔見咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cyu4 fong4 jap6 min6 go2 go3 faan6 caan2 m4 gin3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 廚房裡面的那把飯鏟不見了。
examples.english_sentence: The rice spatula in the kitchen is missing.

mandarin_meaning: 负责做饭的人；厨子（俗称）
english_meaning: the person who cooks / the cook (colloquial, joking)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语俗称，通常指家中或单位里负责煮食、做饭的人，常带玩笑或自嘲意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial term referring to the person who prepares/cooks meals at home or in a workplace. Often used jokingly or in self-deprecation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚唔使你煮，我做飯鏟頭啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 m4 sai2 nei5 zyu2, ngo5 zou6 faan6 caan2 tau4 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚不用你做饭，我来当厨子。
examples.english_sentence: You don't have to cook tonight — I'll be the cook.

mandarin_meaning: 饭馆 / 餐馆（提供饮食的场所）
english_meaning: restaurant; eatery
explanation_mandarin: 指提供飲食服務的場所或商店，即餐館、飯店等。
explanation_english: A place where meals are prepared and served to customers; a restaurant or eatery.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去飯館食飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 faan6 gun2 sik6 faan6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去饭馆吃饭吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the restaurant to eat tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 喝
english_meaning: to drink; to take (medicine); to consume alcohol
explanation_mandarin: 表示吞嚥或攝入液體，也可用於吃藥或飲酒等情況。
explanation_english: Means to swallow or consume liquids; also used for taking medicine or drinking alcohol.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我想飲水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 jam2 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想喝水。
examples.english_sentence: I want to drink some water.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今晚想去飲嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 heoi3 jam2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今晚想去喝一杯。
examples.english_sentence: He wants to go out for drinks tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 飲藥要跟醫生指示。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jam2 joek6 jiu3 gan1 ji1 sang1 zi2 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 吃藥要遵照醫生指示。
examples.english_sentence: Take the medicine according to the doctor's instructions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好飲太多酒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jam2 taai3 do1 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別喝太多酒。
examples.english_sentence: Don't drink too much alcohol.

mandarin_meaning: 干杯 / 乾杯
english_meaning: cheers; bottoms up; a toast said when drinking
explanation_mandarin: 「飲勝」是廣東話在飲酒或聚會時用來敬酒、催促大家一起喝的一句口語用語，等同於普通話的「乾杯」或「干杯」。
explanation_english: A Cantonese exclamation used when toasting or urging people to drink together. It functions like 'cheers' or 'bottoms up.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 大家一齊飲勝！
examples.jyutping_sentence: daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 jam2 sing3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 大家一起干杯！
examples.english_sentence: Everyone, cheers!

mandarin_meaning: 白吃白喝；占人便宜；享受別人的好處而不回報或不知感恩
english_meaning: to freeload; to take advantage of someone's hospitality or kindness without gratitude or reciprocation
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容接受別人的食物、照顧或好處，卻不回報或不知感恩，有占便宜、白吃白喝的意思。
explanation_english: Used to describe accepting someone's food, care, or benefits without reciprocating or showing gratitude; to take advantage of someone's generosity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日嚟我屋企飲和食德，從來冇幫手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 lai4 ngo5 uk1 kei2 jam2 wo4 sik6 dak1, cung4 loi4 mou5 bong1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是來我家白吃白喝，從來不幫忙。
examples.english_sentence: He always freeloads at my place and never helps out.

mandarin_meaning: 喝咖啡
english_meaning: to drink coffee; to have coffee (often implying meeting someone to chat or as a casual date)
explanation_mandarin: 字面意思是「喝咖啡」。在香港粵語中常用作日常用語，除了字面喝咖啡外，也常指與人約出來聊天、見面談事或有時當作約會。
explanation_english: Literally 'to drink coffee.' In Hong Kong Cantonese it's commonly used both literally and idiomatically to mean meeting someone for a chat, a casual meeting, or sometimes a date.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去飲咖啡傾下計啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 jam2 gaa3 fe1 king1 haa5 gai3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去喝咖啡聊聊吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go have coffee and chat tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢約我出嚟飲咖啡，可能係約會。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 joek3 ngo5 ceot1 lai4 jam2 gaa3 fe1, ho2 nang4 hai6 joek3 wui6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他約我出來喝咖啡，可能是約會。
examples.english_sentence: They asked me out for coffee; it might be a date.

mandarin_meaning: 被帶去派出所/被當局帶走問話
english_meaning: to be taken in by authorities (e.g., to the police station) for questioning
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，指被警方或有權力的人士帶走到差館或有關部門接受盤問或訊問。帶有口語或俚語色彩，常用於非正式語境。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to be taken by authorities (for example, to the police station) for questioning. It carries informal/colloquial connotations and is used in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀人帶去差館，之後聽講佢飲咗門官茶。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 jan4 daai3 heoi3 caa1 gun2, zi1 hau6 teng1 gong2 keoi5 jam2 zo2 mun4 gwaan1 caa4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被人帶到派出所，之後聽說他被帶去問話（飲咗門官茶）。
examples.english_sentence: He was taken to the police station; afterwards I heard he was taken in for questioning (飲咗門官茶).

mandarin_meaning: 饮品
english_meaning: beverage; drink
explanation_mandarin: 泛指供人飲用的各種液體或飲料類產品，如茶、咖啡、果汁、汽水等，常用於商店或餐飲業的分類。
explanation_english: A general term for beverages intended for drinking, such as tea, coffee, juice, soda, etc.; commonly used to categorize drinks in shops and the foodservice industry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間咖啡店有好多唔同嘅飲品。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 gaa3 fe1 dim3 jau5 hou2 do1 m4 tung4 ge3 jam2 ban2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家咖啡店有很多不同的饮品。
examples.english_sentence: This café has many different beverages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個新飲品好易賣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 san1 jam2 ban2 hou2 ji6 maai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个新饮品很受欢迎。
examples.english_sentence: This new beverage is very popular.

mandarin_meaning: 喝（飲料/酒），去喝一杯（口語）
english_meaning: to drink (a beverage); to go for a drink / have a drink (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 「飲嘢」是廣東話的口語表達，字面意思是“喝東西”，可以指喝飲料，也常用於指外出喝一杯、喝酒或聚會喝東西。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "飲嘢" literally means "to drink things". It's a colloquial expression used for drinking beverages and commonly for going out to have a drink (often alcoholic) or social drinking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去飲嘢啦？
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 jam2 je5 laa1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去喝一杯嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Shall we go for a drink tonight?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日去飲嘢，同朋友去酒吧玩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 heoi3 jam2 je5, tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3 zau2 baa1 waan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是出去喝酒，和朋友去酒吧玩。
examples.english_sentence: He always goes out for drinks, hanging out with friends at pubs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺茶餐廳飲嘢好平，咖啡同奶茶都唔貴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 caa4 caan1 teng1 jam2 je5 hou2 peng4, gaa3 fe1 tung4 naai5 caa4 dou1 m4 gwai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在茶餐廳喝飲料很便宜，咖啡和奶茶都不貴。
examples.english_sentence: Drinks are cheap at the cha chaan teng; coffee and milk tea aren't expensive.

mandarin_meaning: 吃大虧／上當受騙
english_meaning: to get scammed / to suffer a big loss
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，通常指被人欺騙或遭受重大損失（多指金錢上的損失）。
explanation_english: Cantonese colloquial slang meaning to be cheated/scammed or to suffer a substantial loss (often financial).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今朝俾人呃，飲大咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 ziu1 bei2 jan4 ngaau6, jam2 daai6 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天被人騙了，吃了大虧。
examples.english_sentence: I got cheated this morning and suffered a big loss.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小心啲，唔好亂投資，免得飲大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 sam1 di1, m4 hou2 lyun6 tau4 zi1, min5 dak1 jam2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小心點，不要亂投資，免得吃虧。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful; don't invest recklessly or you'll get ripped off.
