english_meaning: can't warm to (someone/something); unable to develop affection or interest
explanation_mandarin: 口語（廣東話俚語），用來表示對某人或某事無法培養出感情或興趣，提不起熱情，通常指對人際關係或工作等無法投入感情或喜好。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb phrase meaning one cannot warm to someone or something — unable to develop feelings or interest. Often used about people, jobs, or activities when you just don't feel a connection or enthusiasm.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我同佢相處咗幾次，但就養唔熱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 tung4 keoi5 soeng1 cyu5 zo2 gei2 ci3, daan6 zau6 joeng5 m4 jit6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我和他相處了幾次，但就是提不起好感。
examples.english_sentence: I've hung out with him a few times, but I just can't warm to him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份工我試做咗一排，始終養唔熱，可能唔啱我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gung1 ngo5 si3 zou6 zo2 jat1 paai4, ci2 zung1 joeng5 m4 jit6, ho2 nang4 m4 aap3 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這份工作我試做了一陣子，但總是提不起興趣，可能不適合我。
examples.english_sentence: I tried this job for a while, but I couldn't get into it — maybe it's not right for me.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對我好好，但我養唔熱佢，唔想拖佢落水。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 ngo5 hou2 hou2, daan6 ngo5 joeng5 m4 jit6 keoi5, m4 soeng2 to1 keoi5 lok6 seoi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對我很好，但我就是提不起感情，不想拖累他。
examples.english_sentence: He's really nice to me, but I just can't warm up to him, and I don't want to string him along.

mandarin_meaning: 把（孩子、動物、事業等）養育長大；培養、扶持使成長
english_meaning: to raise (to adulthood); to bring up; to rear; to grow (e.g., a business)
explanation_mandarin: 指將孩子、動物或事物飼養、照顧、培育直到長大或成熟。可用於具體的養育（如養大小孩、動物），亦可引申為把事業或團隊培養壯大。
explanation_english: Refers to feeding, caring for, and nurturing someone or something until grown or mature. Used for raising children or animals and can be used metaphorically for growing a business or project.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋將隻小狗養大咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 zoeng1 zek3 siu2 gau2 joeng5 daai6 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們把小狗養大了。
examples.english_sentence: They raised the puppy to adulthood.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我細個係屋企人養大㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 hai6 uk1 kei5 jan4 joeng5 daai6 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小時候是家人養大的。
examples.english_sentence: I was raised by my family when I was young.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢花咗好多年先將公司養大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faa1 zo2 hou2 do1 nin4 sin1 zoeng1 gung1 si1 joeng5 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他花了很多年才把公司養大。
examples.english_sentence: He spent many years growing the company.

mandarin_meaning: 養女 / 养女（被收養的女兒）
english_meaning: adopted daughter
explanation_mandarin: 指被非親生父母收養的女孩，法律或家庭上視為子女的一種身分。
explanation_english: Refers to a girl who has been adopted (not biologically the child of her parents); considered a daughter in legal and familial terms.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢其實係養女，唔係親生嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kei4 sat6 hai6 joeng5 neoi5, m4 hai6 can1 saang1 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她其實是養女，不是親生的。
examples.english_sentence: She is actually an adopted daughter, not a biological child.

mandarin_meaning: 養活妻兒；供養妻子和子女
english_meaning: to provide for/support one's wife and children; to support a family
explanation_mandarin: 指負責供養妻子和子女、承擔家庭經濟責任。常用以描述一個人為家庭謀生、維持生計。
explanation_english: Refers to providing for one's wife and children and taking on the family's financial responsibilities. Commonly used to describe someone earning a living to support their household.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢每日朝早做兩份工，係為咗養妻活兒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 mui5 jat6 ziu1 zou6 loeng5 fan6 gung1, hai6 wai6 zo2 joeng5 cai1 wut6 ji4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他每天早上做兩份工，是為了養活妻兒。
examples.english_sentence: He works two jobs every day to support his wife and children.

mandarin_meaning: 奶娘；負責餵養或照顧嬰兒的婦女（可指乳母或養母）
english_meaning: wet nurse / foster mother; a woman who feeds or cares for a baby
explanation_mandarin: 「養娘」在粵語中常指被請來餵養或照顧嬰兒的女性，類似普通話的「奶娘」或「乳母」。在某些語境下也可指養育孩子的養母。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "養娘" commonly refers to a woman hired to breastfeed or care for an infant (similar to Mandarin 奶娘/乳母). In some contexts it can also mean a foster/adoptive mother.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋請咗個養娘去餵細路仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 ceng2 zo2 go3 joeng5 noeng4 heoi3 wai3 sai3 lou6 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們請了個養娘去餵小孩。
examples.english_sentence: They hired a wet nurse to feed the baby.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我嘅養娘，但佢唔係親生母親。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 ge3 joeng5 noeng4, daan6 keoi5 m4 hai6 can1 saang1 mou5 can1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她是我的養娘，但她不是親生母親。
examples.english_sentence: She is my foster mother, but she is not my biological mother.

mandarin_meaning: 包養情婦；養情人
english_meaning: to keep a mistress; to financially support a woman as a mistress
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，指由男性供養某個女性作為情婦或情人（包養的意思），帶有負面或非正式語氣。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese term meaning a man financially supports a woman as his mistress (to keep a mistress). It is informal and often carries a negative connotation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢老豆喺外面養孃，成日畀錢畀嗰個女人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 lou5 dau6 hai2 ngoi6 min6 joeng5 noeng4, seng4 jat6 bei2 cin2 bei2 go2 go3 neoi5 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他爸爸在外面養情婦，經常給那個女人錢。
examples.english_sentence: His father keeps a mistress; he often gives money to that woman.

mandarin_meaning: 養子（被收養成為家庭成員的兒子／子女）
english_meaning: adopted son; adopted child
explanation_mandarin: 指被他人或家庭收養、成為家庭成員的子弟（通常指男孩，但也可泛指被收養的子女）。
explanation_english: Refers to a child who has been legally or informally adopted into a family (often used for a son, but can mean adopted child generally).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我哋嘅養子，已經同我哋一齊住咗十年。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 dei6 ge3 joeng5 zi2, ji5 ging1 tung4 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 zyu6 zo2 sap6 nin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是我們的養子，已經和我們一起住了十年。
examples.english_sentence: He is our adopted son; he has lived with us for ten years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋決定收養一個小朋友，成為佢哋嘅養子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 kyut3 ding6 sau1 joeng5 jat1 go3 siu2 pang4 jau5, sing4 wai4 keoi5 dei6 ge3 joeng5 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們決定收養一個小朋友，成為他們的養子。
examples.english_sentence: They decided to adopt a child and make him their adopted son.

mandarin_meaning: 养家
english_meaning: to support/provide for one's family
explanation_mandarin: 為家庭提供經濟上的支持或養活家人，通常指以工作收入支撐家計。
explanation_english: To provide financial support for one's family or dependents, usually by working to cover household expenses.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家想搵穩定嘅工，可以養家。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 soeng2 wan2 wan2 ding6 ge3 gung1, ho2 ji5 joeng5 gaa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在想找穩定的工作，可以養家。
examples.english_sentence: I want to find a stable job now so I can support my family.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做兩份工，係因為要養家。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 loeng5 fan6 gung1, hai6 jan1 wai6 jiu3 joeng5 gaa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做兩份工作，是因為要養家。
examples.english_sentence: He works two jobs because he has to support his family.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做父母要養家嘅時候，壓力好大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 fu6 mou5 jiu3 joeng5 gaa1 ge3 si4 hau6, aat3 lik6 hou2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 當父母需要養家時，壓力很大。
examples.english_sentence: When parents need to provide for the family, the pressure is high.

mandarin_meaning: 養尊處優（過著受寵或安逸、優裕的生活）
english_meaning: to live in comfort and ease; to be pampered and enjoy a life of luxury with little hardship
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 成語 / 形容詞性短語
explanation_mandarin: 形容生活安逸、受到優待，不用操勞或受艱苦磨練。
explanation_english: Describes someone living a life of ease and comfort, often pampered or spared from hardship and responsibility.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢細個畀人寵壞，長大之後一直養尊處優，冇試過自己搵食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sai3 go3 bei2 jan4 cung2 waai6, zoeng2 daai6 zi1 hau6 jat1 zik6 joeng5 zyun1 cyu2 jau1, mou5 si3 gwo3 zi6 gei2 wan2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他小時候被寵壞，長大之後一直養尊處優，沒試過自己謀生。
examples.english_sentence: He was spoiled as a child and continued to live in comfort when he grew up; he never tried to earn a living himself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好養尊處優，應該學識承擔責任。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 joeng5 zyun1 cyu2 jau1, jing1 goi1 hok6 sik1 sing4 daam1 zaak3 jam6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要養尊處優，應該學會承擔責任。
examples.english_sentence: Don't live a life of ease; you should learn to take on responsibilities.

mandarin_meaning: 养成；培养，形成（习惯、性格等）
english_meaning: to cultivate; to develop (a habit, skill, or trait); to raise
explanation_mandarin: 表示通过长期的训练或影响，使某种习惯、性格或能力逐步形成或养育（如养成习惯、养成某种行为）。
explanation_english: Indicates the process of developing or cultivating a habit, trait, skill, or raising someone/something so that a particular behavior or characteristic is formed over time.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 養成習慣好重要。
examples.jyutping_sentence: joeng5 sing4 zaap6 gwaan3 hou2 zung6 jiu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 养成习惯很重要。
examples.english_sentence: Developing habits is very important.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你要養成每日做運動嘅習慣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jiu3 joeng5 sing4 mui5 jat6 zou6 wan6 dung6 ge3 zaap6 gwaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你要养成每天做运动的习惯。
examples.english_sentence: You need to develop the habit of exercising every day.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 學校會幫學生養成良好嘅學習態度。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hok6 haau6 wui5 bong1 hok6 saang1 joeng5 sing4 loeng4 hou2 ge3 hok6 zaap6 taai3 dou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 学校会帮助学生养成良好的学习态度。
examples.english_sentence: Schools help students develop good study attitudes.

mandarin_meaning: 被供养者；被包养的人；（也用于评价是否值得供养）
english_meaning: A kept person (someone financially supported/maintained by another); slang for a person who is 'kept' or not worth keeping
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，指被他人供養或包養的人（如情人、被養對象）；亦可用來評論某人是否值得被供養（如「唔係養料」）。
explanation_english: Cantonese slang for a person who is financially supported or kept by someone else (e.g., a kept lover/sugar baby). It can also be used evaluatively to say someone is or isn't worth keeping.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日同一個有錢男人出去，大家都話佢係養料。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 tung4 jat1 go3 jau5 cin2 naam4 jan4 ceot1 heoi3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 waa6 keoi5 hai6 joeng5 liu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她经常和一个有钱男人出去，大家都说她是养料。
examples.english_sentence: She often goes out with a rich man; everyone says she's a kept woman.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係唔養料，你唔好浪費錢喺佢身上。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 m4 joeng5 liu6, nei5 m4 hou2 long6 fai3 cin2 hai2 keoi5 san1 soeng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她真的不值得供养，你不要在她身上浪费钱。
examples.english_sentence: She's really not worth supporting—don't waste your money on her.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢唔想畀人養料，寧願自己搵食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 m4 soeng2 bei2 jan4 joeng5 liu6, ning4 jyun6 zi6 gei2 wan2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他不想被人养着，宁愿自己赚钱。
examples.english_sentence: He doesn't want to be kept by anyone; he'd rather earn his own living.

mandarin_meaning: 養殖（以人工方式飼養或培育動植物，尤指水產或家畜）
english_meaning: to breed; to farm; to cultivate (animals or aquatic products)
explanation_mandarin: 指以人工或管理的方式飼養、培育動植物，常用於水產、畜牧業或溫室栽培等情況。
explanation_english: Refers to raising or cultivating animals or plants under controlled or managed conditions, commonly used for aquaculture, livestock farming, or controlled cultivation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢度有好多魚場，主要係養殖海產。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 dou6 jau5 hou2 do1 jyu4 coeng4, zyu2 ji3 hai6 joeng5 zik6 hoi2 caan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這裡有很多魚場，主要是養殖海產。
examples.english_sentence: There are many fish farms here, mainly for cultivating seafood.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋個農場專門養殖對蝦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 go3 nung4 coeng4 zyun1 mun4 joeng5 zik6 deoi3 haa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們的農場專門養殖對蝦。
examples.english_sentence: Their farm specializes in farming tiger prawns.

mandarin_meaning: 养母（yǎng mǔ）：收养或抚养孩子的母亲，非亲生母亲。
english_meaning: Foster mother; adoptive mother — a woman who raises or legally adopts a child, not the biological mother.
explanation_mandarin: 指被收养或抚养孩子的那位母亲，通常指法律上或事实上的养育者，而非亲生母亲。
explanation_english: Refers to a mother who has raised or legally adopted a child. She is the caregiver or legal mother, not the biological mother.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅養母係一個好溫柔嘅人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 joeng5 mou5 hai6 jat1 go3 hou2 wan1 jau4 ge3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的养母是一个很温柔的人。
examples.english_sentence: His foster mother is a very gentle person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我細個係由養母撫養長大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 sai3 go3 hai6 jau4 joeng5 mou5 fu2 joeng5 coeng4 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我小时候是由养母抚养长大的。
examples.english_sentence: I was raised by my foster mother when I was a child.

mandarin_meaning: 养活；供养；维持生活
english_meaning: to support (financially); to provide for; to keep alive
explanation_mandarin: 指提供足夠的生活費用或物資，使個人或家庭能夠生活下去。
explanation_english: To provide enough financial resources or necessities for a person or family to live; to support or sustain.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢份工好難養活我成個家庭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 fan6 gung1 hou2 naan4 joeng5 wut6 ngo5 sing4 go3 gaa1 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这份工作很难养活我整个家庭。
examples.english_sentence: This job can't support my whole family.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢靠打零工養活自己。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kaau3 daa2 ling4 gung1 joeng5 wut6 zi6 gei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他靠打零工养活自己。
examples.english_sentence: He supports himself by doing odd jobs.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿爸話靠佢一個人好難養活兩個細路。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 baa4 waa6 kaau3 keoi5 jat1 go3 jan4 hou2 naan4 joeng5 wut6 loeng5 go3 sai3 lou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 爸爸说靠他一个人很难养活两个孩子。
examples.english_sentence: Dad said it's hard for him alone to support two children.

mandarin_meaning: 養父
english_meaning: adoptive father; foster father
explanation_mandarin: 指非親生、被依法或依感情收養並擔任父親角色的人（即養父）。
explanation_english: A man who has legally or informally taken a child as his son or daughter; an adoptive or foster father.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我嘅養父喺去年過身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ge3 joeng5 fu6 hai2 heoi3 nin4 gwo3 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的養父在去年去世。
examples.english_sentence: My adoptive father passed away last year.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢係我嘅養父，不過我哋冇血緣關係。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 ge3 joeng5 fu6, bat1 gwo3 ngo5 dei6 mou5 hyut3 jyun4 gwaan1 hai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他是我的養父，但我們沒有血緣關係。
examples.english_sentence: He is my adoptive father, but we have no blood relation.

mandarin_meaning: 恩將仇報／忘恩負義（形容被幫助的人反而加害於幫助者）
english_meaning: To repay kindness with harm; to bite the hand that feeds you — to be ungrateful or betray one's benefactor
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容受惠者不但不感恩，反而傷害或背叛施惠者，好像養了狗最後咬自己的袋（下體）一樣。
explanation_english: An idiom describing someone who, after receiving help or support, turns against or harms their benefactor — literally 'raise a dog that bites the scrotum', used metaphorically for ingratitude or betrayal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司當初畀咗機會佢，點知佢養狗咬春袋，最後爆出公司內幕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 dong1 co1 bei2 zo2 gei1 wui6 keoi5, dim2 zi1 keoi5 joeng5 gau2 ngaau5 ceon1 doi6, zeoi3 hau6 baau3 ceot1 gung1 si1 noi6 muk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司當初給了他機會，沒想到他恩將仇報，最後爆出公司的內幕。
examples.english_sentence: The company initially gave him a chance, but he bit the hand that fed him and ended up exposing the company's inside information.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小心唔好畀人養狗咬春袋，做事之前要睇清楚人品。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 sam1 m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 joeng5 gau2 ngaau5 ceon1 doi6, zou6 si6 zi1 cin4 jiu3 tai2 cing1 co2 jan4 ban2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小心不要讓人恩將仇報，做事之前要看清楚人品。
examples.english_sentence: Be careful not to be betrayed by someone you help; check people's character before you act.

jyutping: joeng5 long4 gau2, ngaau5 sam1 hau2
mandarin_meaning: 养了狼狗，最后反咬自己；比喻恩将仇报或养虎为患
english_meaning: Literally 'raise a wolf‑dog, it bites the chest' — to nurture or help someone who later betrays or harms you; similar to 'bite the hand that feeds you' or 'raise a tiger and be harmed by it'.
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俗語比喻你幫助或養育了某人，結果對方反過來傷害或背叛你，含有被恩將仇報或自招禍患之意。
explanation_english: A Cantonese saying used to describe the situation where someone you helped or raised turns on you and harms or betrays you; conveys betrayal by someone you trusted or enabled.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好再幫佢，免得養狼狗，咬心口。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 bong1 keoi5, min5 dak1 joeng5 long4 gau2, ngaau5 sam1 hau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別再幫他，免得養了狼狗，最後反咬你一口。
examples.english_sentence: Don't help him again; you might be raising a wolf‑dog that will bite you — he'll betray you in the end.

mandarin_meaning: 养生
english_meaning: to maintain health; health preservation; wellness
explanation_mandarin: 指通过饮食、作息、运动、养护等方法保持和促进身体健康的行为或理念，也可指与此相关的生活方式。
explanation_english: Refers to practices or a lifestyle aimed at maintaining and promoting physical health through diet, rest, exercise, and other care; can be used as an action or a concept.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你而家咁忙，都應該抽啲時間養生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ji4 gaa1 gam2 mong4, dou1 jing1 goi1 cau1 di1 si4 gaan3 joeng5 saang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你现在这么忙，也应该抽出时间养生。
examples.english_sentence: You're so busy right now; you should take some time to look after your health.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老人家好注重養生，成日飲芝麻糊同做運動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jan4 gaa1 hou2 zyu3 zung6 joeng5 saang1, sing4 jat6 jam2 zi1 maa4 wu4 tung4 zou6 wan6 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老人家很注重养生，经常喝芝麻糊和做运动。
examples.english_sentence: Elderly people pay a lot of attention to health maintenance; they often drink sesame paste and exercise.

mandarin_meaning: 養病（休養、靜養）
english_meaning: to recuperate; to rest and recover from illness; to convalesce
explanation_mandarin: 指為了恢復健康而休息或接受治療，暫時減少外出或工作以促進康復。
explanation_english: To rest and receive treatment in order to recover health; to convalesce, often implying staying home or reducing activities until one gets better.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家喺屋企養病，唔可以出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 uk1 kei2 joeng5 beng6, m4 ho2 ji5 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在在家養病，不能出門。
examples.english_sentence: He is recuperating at home and cannot go out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 醫生話你要返屋企養病，多啲休息。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 sang1 waa6 nei5 jiu3 faan1 uk1 kei2 joeng5 beng6, do1 di1 jau1 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 醫生說你要回家養病，多休息。
examples.english_sentence: The doctor said you should go home to recuperate and get more rest.

mandarin_meaning: 养眼 (yǎng yǎn) — 令人赏心悦目；好看、好看得让人觉得舒服
english_meaning: pleasing to the eye; easy on the eyes; visually attractive
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容人或物外表吸引、好看或讓人覺得賞心悅目的感覺，口語中常用來稱讚長相、服飾或設計。
explanation_english: Used to describe a person or thing that is visually attractive or pleasant to look at. Commonly used colloquially to compliment appearance, clothing, or design.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個女仔真係好養眼。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 neoi5 zai2 zan1 hai6 hou2 joeng5 ngaan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个女孩真养眼。
examples.english_sentence: This girl is really easy on the eyes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 張海報設計得好養眼，可以吸引到好多觀眾。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng1 hoi2 bou3 sik1 gai3 dak1 hou2 joeng5 ngaan5, ho2 ji5 kap1 jan5 dou3 hou2 do1 gun1 zung3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这幅海报设计得很养眼，可以吸引很多观众。
examples.english_sentence: This poster is very eye-catching; it can attract a lot of viewers.

mandarin_meaning: 養精蓄銳（yǎng jīng xù ruì）：休養並積蓄力量，為將來的工作或戰鬥做準備。
english_meaning: To recuperate and conserve one's strength/energy; to rest and build up energy in preparation for future effort or challenges.
explanation_mandarin: 指通過休息、調養或減少消耗，恢復體力並積蓄力量，以便在未來重要時刻發揮。
explanation_english: Refers to resting, recuperating, or reducing exertion in order to restore and accumulate strength so one can perform well in an upcoming important task or challenge.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 教練話今個星期少操，等球員養精蓄銳，為決賽做準備。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaau3 lin6 waa6 gam1 go3 sing1 kei4 siu2 cou1, dang2 kau4 jyun4 joeng5 zing1 cuk1 jeoi6, wai6 kyut3 coi3 zou6 zeon2 bei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 教练说这星期少训练，让球员养精蓄锐，为决赛做准备。
examples.english_sentence: The coach said to cut back training this week so the players can recuperate and save their strength for the finals.

mandarin_meaning: 養精蓄銳（休養、積蓄精力以待時機）
english_meaning: To recuperate and store up strength; to conserve energy and prepare for future action
explanation_mandarin: 指休養生息，積蓄精力以便將來再發揮或應付挑戰。
explanation_english: Refers to resting and gathering one's energy so as to be ready for future efforts or challenges.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考完試之後，我會養精蓄鋭，準備下一個挑戰。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 jyun4 si3 zi1 hau6, ngo5 wui5 joeng5 zing1 cuk1 jeoi6, zeon2 bei6 haa6 jat1 go3 tiu1 zin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考完試之後，我會養精蓄銳，準備下一個挑戰。
examples.english_sentence: After the exams, I'll recuperate and build up my strength to prepare for the next challenge.

mandarin_meaning: 养老；赡养（年老的人）；退休后的生活或老人照护
english_meaning: to support or provide for the elderly; elderly care; retirement
explanation_mandarin: 指供養或照顧年老的人，也可指退休後的生活安排或社會上的養老制度。
explanation_english: Refers to supporting or caring for elderly people; can also mean retirement or arrangements/systems for elderly care.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 香港好多家庭要面對父母嘅養老問題。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 hou2 do1 gaa1 ting4 jiu3 min6 deoi3 fu6 mou5 ge3 joeng5 lou5 man6 tai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 香港很多家庭要面对父母的养老问题。
examples.english_sentence: Many families in Hong Kong have to face the issue of caring for their parents in old age.

mandarin_meaning: 养声
english_meaning: to rest, protect, or train one's voice (vocal care/vocal training)
explanation_mandarin: 指為了保護或訓練嗓音而休息、做發聲練習或注意使用方法，常用於歌手、老師等需要頻繁用嗓的人。
explanation_english: Refers to resting, protecting, or training the voice (vocal cords) — e.g., taking vocal rest or doing vocal exercises. Commonly used for singers, teachers, or others who use their voice a lot.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋演唱會前要養聲幾日。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jin2 coeng3 wui6 cin4 jiu3 joeng5 seng1 gei2 jat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在演唱會前要養聲幾天。
examples.english_sentence: We need to rest our voices for a few days before the concert.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唱歌要練聲同養聲，先可以唱到高音。
examples.jyutping_sentence: coeng3 go1 jiu3 lin6 seng1 tung4 joeng5 seng1, sin1 ho2 ji5 coeng3 dou3 gou1 jam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 唱歌要練聲和養聲，才能唱到高音。
examples.english_sentence: To sing well you need vocal practice and to take care of your voice so you can hit high notes.

mandarin_meaning: 养育、抚养、培养
english_meaning: to raise; to bring up; to nurture (children or young)
explanation_mandarin: 指父母或其他监护人对孩子进行抚养、教育和照顾，使其成长和发展。
explanation_english: To care for, nurture, and bring up children (or young), including provision, education, and guidance for their growth and development.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 父母有責任養育子女。
examples.jyutping_sentence: fu6 mou5 jau5 zaak3 jam6 joeng5 juk6 zi2 neoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 父母有责任养育子女。
examples.english_sentence: Parents have the responsibility to raise their children.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢由親戚幫手養育到長大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jau4 can1 cik1 bong1 sau2 joeng5 juk6 dou3 zoeng2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他由亲戚帮忙养育到长大。
examples.english_sentence: He was raised by relatives until he grew up.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 社會應該提供更多資源去養育兒童。
examples.jyutping_sentence: se5 wui6 jing1 goi1 tai4 gung1 gang1 do1 zi1 jyun4 heoi3 joeng5 juk6 ji4 tung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 社会应该提供更多资源去养育儿童。
examples.english_sentence: Society should provide more resources to nurture and raise children.

mandarin_meaning: 养虎遗患（yǎng hǔ yí huàn）：縱容或培養會帶來災禍的人或事，遲早會引致禍患。
english_meaning: To nurture a tiger and leave a hidden danger — to foster or tolerate something/someone dangerous that will cause trouble later.
explanation_mandarin: 比喻放任或培養會帶來禍害的人或事，最終會招致災禍。
explanation_english: An idiom meaning to allow or nurture someone/something dangerous, thereby creating trouble that will surface in the future.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢放任有問題嘅員工繼續做，就係養虎遺患。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 fong3 jam6 jau5 man6 tai4 ge3 jyun4 gung1 gai3 zuk6 zou6, zau6 hai6 joeng5 fu2 wai4 waan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他放任有問題的員工繼續做，就是養虎遺患。
examples.english_sentence: By allowing problematic employees to keep working, he's inviting future trouble.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府對犯罪分子網開一面，可能係養虎遺患。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 deoi3 faan6 zeoi6 fan6 zi2 mong5 hoi1 jat1 min6, ho2 nang4 hai6 joeng5 fu2 wai4 waan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府對犯罪分子網開一面，可能是養虎遺患。
examples.english_sentence: If the government is lenient with criminals, it may be creating future problems.

mandarin_meaning: 养蜂
english_meaning: beekeeping; to raise bees
explanation_mandarin: 指飼養蜜蜂以獲取蜂蜜、蜂蠟或提供授粉服務的行為或行業，既可作為愛好也可作為商業經營。
explanation_english: The practice of keeping and breeding bees to collect honey and beeswax or to provide pollination services; can be a hobby or a commercial/agricultural activity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺鄉下養蜂，賣蜂蜜做生意。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 hoeng1 haa6 joeng5 fung1, maai6 fung1 mat6 zou6 saang1 ji3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在乡下养蜂，卖蜂蜜做生意。
examples.english_sentence: He raises bees in the countryside and sells honey as a business.

mandarin_meaning: 养车
english_meaning: to keep/maintain a car (cover the costs of ownership and upkeep)
explanation_mandarin: 指擁有並維持一輛車，承擔保養、維修、保險、燃油、泊車等相關費用；在香港口語中常用來談論養車的開支。
explanation_english: Refers to owning and maintaining a car, taking on expenses like upkeep, repairs, insurance, fuel, and parking; commonly used colloquially in Hong Kong to talk about the costs of keeping a car.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家養車真係好貴，保險、油費同泊車位成個月都要幾千蚊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 joeng5 ce1 zan1 hai6 hou2 gwai3, bou2 him2, jau4 fai3 tung4 paak3 ce1 wai2 sing4 go3 jyut6 dou1 jiu3 gei2 cin1 man1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在養車真的很貴，保險、油費和停車位一個月就要幾千塊。
examples.english_sentence: Keeping a car nowadays is really expensive—insurance, fuel, and parking can cost several thousand HKD a month.

mandarin_meaning: 养颜
english_meaning: to beautify the complexion; to maintain or improve facial skin appearance
explanation_mandarin: 指通過護膚、飲食或中藥等方法使面容更好、皮膚保持光澤健康。
explanation_english: Refers to improving or maintaining the appearance of the face/skin through skincare, diet, herbs, or treatments to keep the complexion healthy and glowing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 飲多啲紅棗水有助養顏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jam2 do1 di1 hung4 zou2 seoi2 jau5 zo6 joeng5 ngaan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 多喝紅棗水有助於養顏。
examples.english_sentence: Drinking more red jujube (date) water helps beautify the complexion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢款面膜可以養顏兼保濕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 kwan2 min6 mok6 ho2 ji5 joeng5 ngaan4 gim1 bou2 sap1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這款面膜可以養顏兼保濕。
examples.english_sentence: This sheet mask can beautify the skin and also provide moisture.

mandarin_meaning: （1）养小鬼：指进行招魂、供奉或操控亡灵的民间巫术；（2）养小三：俗称供养外遇对象（包养情妇/小三）
english_meaning: (1) to 'raise' or keep a ghost in folk occult practice (raise a spirit to serve/protect someone); (2) slang: to keep/support a mistress or secret lover financially
explanation_mandarin: 「養鬼仔」在廣東話中有兩種常見用法：一是字面/迷信意義，指按照某些民間做法「養」小鬼或供奉亡靈以求保佑或達成目的；二是俚語用法，指某人以金錢或物質供養外遇對象（即「養小三」）。在使用時要注意語境，以免誤會。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '養鬼仔' has two common senses: literally/occult—raising or keeping a spirit/ghost according to folk practices for protection or benefit; slang—keeping or financially supporting a mistress/secret lover (similar to 'keeping a sidepiece'). Context determines which meaning is intended.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂信嗰啲人話可以幫你養鬼仔，啲嘢好危險。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 leon6 seon3 go2 di1 jan4 waa6 ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5 joeng5 gwai2 zai2, di1 je5 hou2 ngai4 him2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要随便相信那些说可以帮你养小鬼的人，那种事情很危险。
examples.english_sentence: Don't casually trust people who say they can help you 'raise a ghost'—that kind of thing is dangerous.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽講阿成喺外面養鬼仔，仲供樓畀佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 gong2 aa3 sing4 hai2 ngoi6 min6 joeng5 gwai2 zai2, zung6 gung1 lau4 bei2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 听说明成在外面养小三，还替她供房子。
examples.english_sentence: I heard Ah Sing is keeping a mistress on the side and even paying her mortgage.

mandarin_meaning: 饵（用来钓鱼或诱捕动物的食物或诱饵；引申为诱惑、诱饵）
english_meaning: bait; lure (something used to entice or lure, literally for fishing/trapping or metaphorically)
explanation_mandarin: 餌（或寫作饵）指用於釣魚或誘捕動物的食物或誘餌，也可引申為用來引誘或誘惑他人的事物或手段。
explanation_english: “餌” means bait used for fishing or trapping; figuratively it refers to something used to entice or lure someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 漁夫用魚餌釣魚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 fu1 jung6 jyu4 ji5 diu3 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 漁夫用魚餌釣魚。
examples.english_sentence: The fisherman uses bait to catch fish.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋用低價做餌，吸引顧客入嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 jung6 dai1 gaa3 zou6 ji5, kap1 jan5 gu3 haak3 jap6 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他們用低價作誘餌，吸引顧客進來。
examples.english_sentence: They use low prices as bait to attract customers to come in.

mandarin_meaning: 餐；饭（如午餐、晚餐）
english_meaning: meal; (in compounds) lunch/dinner; (colloquial) to eat a meal
explanation_mandarin: 「餐」主要表示一餐或饭食，常与其他字组合（如午餐、晚餐、餐廳）。在粤语口语中也常作动词使用，如「食餐」表示吃饭。
explanation_english: “餐” primarily means a meal and appears in compounds (e.g. lunch, dinner, restaurant). In Cantonese colloquial use it can also function as a verb meaning to have a meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋一齊食餐飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 sik6 caan1 faan6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们一起吃顿饭吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's have a meal together.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日食咗三餐未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 sik6 zo2 saam1 caan1 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天吃了三餐了吗？
examples.english_sentence: Have you eaten your meals today?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅午餐好抵食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 ng5 caan1 hou2 dai2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家餐厅的午餐很划算。
examples.english_sentence: The lunch at this restaurant is very good value.

mandarin_meaning: 餐具 — 在用餐時使用的器具，例如碗、筷子、叉子、湯匙等。
english_meaning: Tableware; utensils used for eating or serving food (e.g., bowls, chopsticks, forks, spoons, plates).
explanation_mandarin: 指用來盛放、夾取或入口食物的器具，包含碗、盤、筷子、刀叉、湯匙等。
explanation_english: Refers to implements used to hold, serve, or eat food, including bowls, plates, chopsticks, forks, knives, and spoons.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你洗緊啲餐具未？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 sai2 gan2 di1 caan1 geoi6 mei6?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你在洗餐具嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Are you washing the dishes/tableware?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老人嘅餐具要特別小心處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 jan4 ge3 caan1 geoi6 jiu3 dak6 bit6 siu2 sam1 cyu3 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老人的餐具要特別小心處理。
examples.english_sentence: The elderly person's tableware should be handled with extra care.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅一次性餐具唔環保。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 jat1 ci3 sing3 caan1 geoi6 m4 waan4 bou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間餐廳的一次性餐具不環保。
examples.english_sentence: This restaurant's disposable tableware is not environmentally friendly.

mandarin_meaning: 餐刀（用于进餐时切割食物的刀具）
english_meaning: dining knife; table knife (a knife used to cut food at the table)
explanation_mandarin: 指用于进餐时切割食物的刀具，即餐具中的刀。主要为实物名称，而非常见俚语或成语。
explanation_english: A knife used at the table for cutting food — part of the cutlery. It is a literal noun referring to the utensil, not a common slang or idiom.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢把餐刀唔鋒利，要換一把。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 baa2 caan1 dou1 m4 fung1 lei6, jiu3 wun6 jat1 baa2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这把餐刀不锋利，要换一把。
examples.english_sentence: This dining knife isn't sharp; we need to replace it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳每位客人都有餐刀同叉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 mui5 wai2 haak3 jan4 dou1 jau5 caan1 dou1 tung4 caa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这间餐厅每位客人都有餐刀和叉。
examples.english_sentence: This restaurant provides each diner with a knife and fork.

mandarin_meaning: 饭券（用于兑换餐食的凭证）
english_meaning: meal voucher; meal ticket
explanation_mandarin: 用于兑换餐食的票券或凭证，常由公司、超市或餐厅发放，作为补助、礼物或促销手段。
explanation_english: A voucher or ticket used to redeem meals, often issued by companies, supermarkets, or restaurants as subsidies, gifts, or promotional offers.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司發放餐券畀員工，用嚟喺員工餐廳換餐。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 faat3 fong3 caan1 hyun3 bei2 jyun4 gung1, jung6 lai4 hai6 jyun4 gung1 caan1 teng1 wun6 caan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司发放餐券给员工，用来在员工餐厅兑换餐食。
examples.english_sentence: The company issued meal vouchers to employees to redeem meals at the staff canteen.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋收到一張餐券，可以喺附近嘅食肆度用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 sau1 dou6 jat1 zoeng1 caan1 hyun3, ho2 ji5 hai6 fu6 gan6 ge3 sik6 si2 dou6 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们收到一张餐券，可以在附近的食肆使用。
examples.english_sentence: They received a meal voucher that can be used at nearby eateries.

mandarin_meaning: 餐包；小圓麵包，類似晚餐小麵包或餐廳常見的麵包
english_meaning: bread roll; dinner roll (a small round bread commonly eaten with meals)
explanation_mandarin: 指一種小型的麵包，通常在早餐或與正餐一起食用，常見於茶餐廳或麵包店，可塗抹牛油、果醬等。
explanation_english: Refers to a small bread bun or roll, commonly eaten at breakfast or with meals; often sold at cafés or bakeries and eaten with butter or jam.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我朝早喺茶餐廳買咗個餐包，抹咗牛油同果醬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 hai2 caa4 caan1 teng1 maai5 zo2 go3 caan1 baau1, mut6 zo2 ngau4 jau4 tung4 gwo2 zoeng3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我早上在茶餐廳買了一個餐包，抹了牛油和果醬。
examples.english_sentence: This morning I bought a bread roll at a cha chaan teng and spread butter and jam on it.

mandarin_meaning: 餐叉；叉子（餐具）
english_meaning: fork (eating utensil)
explanation_mandarin: 指用來夾取或刺取食物的餐具，通常有多齒，用於西式或混合式用餐場合。
explanation_english: An eating utensil with prongs used to pick up or spear food, commonly used in Western or mixed dining settings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔識用餐叉，得閒教我啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 sik1 jung6 caan1 caa1, dak1 haan4 gaau3 ngo5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不会用餐叉，有空教我吧。
examples.english_sentence: I don't know how to use a fork; teach me when you have time.

mandarin_meaning: 菜单
english_meaning: menu (list of dishes offered by a restaurant or eatery)
explanation_mandarin: 指餐厅或食肆列出可供选择的菜式及价格的单子，也可指推荐或当天特别菜式的列表。
explanation_english: Refers to the list of dishes and prices offered by a restaurant or food outlet; can also refer to recommended or daily special listings.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔該，畀我睇下餐單。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 goi1, bei2 ngo5 tai2 haa5 caan1 daan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不好意思，请把菜单给我看一下。
examples.english_sentence: Excuse me, may I see the menu, please?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅餐單有好多地道小食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 caan1 daan1 jau5 hou2 do1 dei6 dou6 siu2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这家餐厅的菜单有很多地道小吃。
examples.english_sentence: This restaurant's menu has many local snacks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐單上寫住今日推介係燒鵝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 daan1 soeng6 se2 zyu6 gam1 jat6 teoi1 gaai3 hai6 siu1 ngo4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 菜单上写着今日推荐是烧鹅。
examples.english_sentence: The menu lists today's recommendation as roast goose.

mandarin_meaning: （非標準詞）可能是打錯字，應為「餐廳」「餐室」或「餐時」等
english_meaning: Not a standard Cantonese word; likely a typo or miswriting (possibly intended as 'restaurant', 'dining room' or 'meal time')
explanation_mandarin: 「餐士」並非廣泛認可的廣東話詞彙，常見於打字錯誤或口誤。根據上下文，可能原意是「餐廳」「餐室」或把「時」（餐時）誤寫為「士」。
explanation_english: “餐士” is not a recognized Cantonese lexical item; it commonly appears as a typo or slip of the tongue. Depending on context, the intended word may be '餐廳' (restaurant), '餐室' (dining room) or '餐時' (meal time) where the character '時' was mistaken for '士'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 「餐士」唔係一個正規嘅廣東話詞，通常係打錯字或者口誤。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 si6 m4 hai6 jat1 go3 zing3 gwai1 ge3 gwong2 dung1 waa2 ci4, tung1 soeng4 hai6 daa2 co3 zi6 waak6 ze2 hau2 ng6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 「餐士」不是一個正規的廣東話詞，通常是打錯字或口誤。
examples.english_sentence: '餐士' is not a standard Cantonese word; it is usually a typo or a slip of the tongue.

mandarin_meaning: 餐厅；饭厅
english_meaning: dining room; restaurant; canteen
explanation_mandarin: 「餐室」指供人用餐的場所，可指家中的飯廳、公司或學校的餐廳，或一般小型餐館。在香港口語中也常用來稱呼某些食肆。
explanation_english: “餐室” denotes a place for eating meals — it can mean a home's dining room, a company's or school's canteen, or a small restaurant. In Hong Kong usage it commonly refers to eateries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚去間新開嘅餐室食飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 gaan1 san1 hoi1 ge3 caan1 sat1 sik6 faan6 laa1。
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚去那家新开的餐厅吃饭吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to that newly opened restaurant to eat tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 吃屎（比喻遭受屈辱、受氣、或被騙、受損失；亦用作罵人）
english_meaning: Literally 'eat shit' — slang meaning to be humiliated, badly treated, screwed over, or used as an insult ('go eat shit')
explanation_mandarin: 「餐屎」是廣東話粗口俚語，字面為「吃屎」。常用來表示遭遇不幸、被人欺負或受屈，也可用作侮辱性的斥罵語句（例如叫人「餐屎」）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese coarse slang phrase literally meaning 'eat shit'. It is used to indicate being humiliated, mistreated, or badly unlucky/screwed over. It can also be used as an insulting interjection (e.g. 'go eat shit').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上次嗰單生意搞到我哋餐屎晒，賠咗好多錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 ci3 go2 daan1 sang1 ji3 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 dei6 caan1 si2 saai3, pui4 zo2 hou2 do1 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上次那筆生意把我們弄得很慘，賠了很多錢。
examples.english_sentence: That last deal screwed us over — we lost a lot of money.

mandarin_meaning: 餐巾（cān jīn）
english_meaning: napkin; serviette (a piece of cloth or paper used to wipe mouth or hands at a meal)
explanation_mandarin: 指用於餐桌上擦拭嘴巴或手的布或紙製品，既有一次性紙製餐巾，也有可重複使用的布餐巾。
explanation_english: A cloth or paper item used at the dining table to wipe the mouth or hands. Can be disposable (paper napkin) or reusable (cloth napkin).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我可唔可以借張餐巾？我啲手濕咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 ze3 zoeng1 caan1 gan1? ngo5 di1 sau2 sap1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我可以借一張餐巾嗎？我的手濕了。
examples.english_sentence: Can I borrow a napkin? My hands are wet.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐廳有無紙餐巾？
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 teng1 jau5 mou5 zi2 caan1 gan1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餐廳有沒有紙餐巾？
examples.english_sentence: Does the restaurant have paper napkins?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲係一次性餐巾，食完可以即刻拋掉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 hai6 jat1 ci3 sing3 caan1 gan1, sik6 jyun4 ho2 ji5 zik1 hak1 paau1 diu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這些是一次性餐巾，吃完可以馬上丟掉。
examples.english_sentence: These are disposable napkins; you can throw them away after eating.

mandarin_meaning: 餐廳 (cāntīng)
english_meaning: restaurant; dining room
explanation_mandarin: 指供人用餐的場所，可以指商業性的餐館或建築內的飯堂。
explanation_english: A place where people eat meals; can refer to a commercial restaurant or an indoor dining hall.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去餐廳食飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 caan1 teng1 sik6 faan6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去餐廳吃飯吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the restaurant to eat tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間餐廳嘅菜好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 coi3 hou2 hou2 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這家餐廳的菜很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: The food at this restaurant is very tasty.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 要唔要訂位呀？呢間餐廳好多人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jiu3 m4 jiu3 deng6 wai2 aa3? ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 hou2 do1 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 要不要訂位？這間餐廳很多人。
examples.english_sentence: Do you need to reserve a table? This restaurant is very crowded.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）愣住、茫然、不知所措
english_meaning: to be stunned, dazed, or momentarily at a loss; to be bewildered
explanation_mandarin: 「餐懵」是廣東話口語，形容因突發事情或意外而一時間愣住、反應不及或迷糊。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to be momentarily stunned or bewildered—usually as a sudden reaction to unexpected news or events.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到嗰件事即刻餐懵咗，唔知點回應。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Keoi5 teng1 dou3 go2 gin6 si6 zik1 hak1 caan1 mung4 zo2, m4 zi1 dim2 wui4 jing3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他聽到那件事立刻愣住了，不知道怎麼回應。
examples.english_sentence: He was immediately stunned when he heard that and didn't know how to respond.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 第一次見到咁多錢，我真係餐懵。
examples.jyutping_sentence: Dai6 jat1 ci3 gin3 dou3 gam2 do1 cin2, ngo5 zan1 hai6 caan1 mung4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 第一次看到這麼多錢，我真的愣住了。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing so much money for the first time, I was really stunned.

mandarin_meaning: 謀生；賺取生活費
english_meaning: to make a living; to earn a livelihood
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，用來表示為了維持生計而工作或賺錢。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to work or earn money to support oneself — to make a living.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一個人喺外國打工，成日都係為咗餐揾餐食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 go3 jan4 hai2 ngoi6 gwok3 daa2 gung1, sing4 jat6 dou1 hai6 wai6 zo2 caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一個人在外國打工，經常都是為了謀生。
examples.english_sentence: He works abroad; he's often doing it to make a living.

jyutping: caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6 caan1 caan1 cing1
mandarin_meaning: 日常為謀生奔波，過著吃一餐、賺一餐、拮据度日（入不敷出、勉強維持生計）
english_meaning: living hand-to-mouth; scraping by day to day — working only to earn the next meal and having little or no savings
explanation_mandarin: 這句廣東話俚語用重複「餐」字強調每日只為溫飽而忙碌，暗示生活捉襟見肘、沒有積蓄，勉強維持生計。
explanation_english: This Cantonese slang phrase repeats the character for 'meal' to emphasize living day-to-day: earning just enough to eat, with little or no savings — i.e., living hand-to-mouth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢搬到城入之後冇穩定工，依家真係餐揾餐食餐餐清。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bong1 dou3 sing4 jap6 zi1 hau6 mou5 wan2 ding6 gung1, ji1 gaa1 zan1 hai6 caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6 caan1 caan1 cing1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他搬到城裡後沒有穩定工作，現在真的是每天為了溫飽而奔波，入不敷出。
examples.english_sentence: After moving to the city he didn't find steady work; now he's really living hand-to-mouth.

mandarin_meaning: 谋生；为温饱而工作
english_meaning: to earn a living; to work to put food on the table
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语，意思是为了温饱而工作、赚钱，用来表示谋生。常见变体为“搵餐搵食”。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase meaning to earn a living or work to put food on the table. Often used to describe having to work to support oneself or one's family. Common variant: '搵餐搵食'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢為咗養家，日日都要餐搵餐食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 wai6 zo2 joeng5 gaa1, jat6 jat6 dou1 jiu3 caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他为了养家，每天都要工作赚钱谋生。
examples.english_sentence: He works every day to support his family — he has to earn a living.

jyutping: caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6 -- caan1 caan1 cing1
mandarin_meaning: 靠做工或打零工維持生計，日子清苦，勉強糊口。
english_meaning: Working merely to make a living; living hand-to-mouth with meager meals; barely scraping by.
explanation_mandarin: 常用於形容為了生計而不停工作，收入微薄，生活清苦，飯餐都唔多好過。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing someone who works just to get by, with meager meals and a hard, hand-to-mouth existence.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢而家做零工，真係餐搵餐食——餐餐清，啲日子過得好辛苦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zou6 ling4 gung1, zan1 hai6 caan1 wan2 caan1 sik6 -- caan1 caan1 cing1, di1 jat6 zi2 gwo3 dak1 hou2 san1 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他現在做零工，真的是為了維持生計而忙，日子過得很清苦。
examples.english_sentence: He's doing odd jobs now, really just scraping by — his meals are meager and life is very hard.

jyutping: wan2 caan1 wan2 sik6, caan1 caan1 cing1 gwong1（推測讀音，常見說法為「搵餐搵食，餐餐清光」）
mandarin_meaning: 為了糊口而辛苦工作，但錢常常一用就光，形容勉強度日、經常入不敷出。
english_meaning: Working just to earn daily meals but ending up broke every time; to barely make ends meet and live day-to-day.
explanation_mandarin: 此句多用來形容人為了糊口辛苦工作，但收入微薄或支出大，以致經常沒有積蓄、剛夠度日。通常屬口語或俚語表達。
explanation_english: This colloquial phrase describes working merely to earn daily food yet repeatedly ending up with no money; it conveys living hand-to-mouth and barely scraping by.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家人工咁低，真係搵餐搵食，餐餐清光。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 jan4 gung1 gam2 dai1, zan1 hai6 wan2 caan1 wan2 sik6, caan1 caan1 cing1 gwong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 現在工資這麼低，真的是為了糊口而忙碌，飯錢總是一下子就花光了。
examples.english_sentence: With wages so low, I'm really just earning a living and end up broke every time.

mandarin_meaning: 餐会；宴会；聚餐（正式或半正式的用餐聚會）
english_meaning: banquet; luncheon; dinner party; a meal gathering (formal or semi-formal reception)
explanation_mandarin: 指以用餐為主要內容的聚會或宴會，常用於公司、學校或社團舉辦的正式或半正式活動，如年終餐會、歡迎餐會等。
explanation_english: Refers to a gathering centered on a meal, often a formal or semi-formal event such as a company banquet, farewell luncheon, or reception.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司年終餐會下星期五舉行，記得準時出席。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 nin4 zung1 caan1 wui6 haa6 sing1 kei4 ng5 geoi2 hang4, gei3 dak1 zeon2 si4 ceot1 zik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司年终餐会在下星期五举行，记得准时出席。
examples.english_sentence: The company's year-end banquet will be held next Friday; remember to attend on time.

mandarin_meaning: 餐桌 / 飯桌
english_meaning: dining table
explanation_mandarin: 指用來吃飯的桌子，通常放在飯廳或廚房，供人用餐時坐/放碗筷。
explanation_english: A table used for dining, typically placed in a dining room or kitchen for people to sit and eat or place dishes and utensils.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺餐枱食飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 caan1 toi4 sik6 faan6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在餐桌吃飯吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's eat at the dining table.

mandarin_meaning: 餐桌；饭桌
english_meaning: dining table; table where meals are eaten
explanation_mandarin: 用來擺放食物和供人用餐的桌子，常見於家中或餐廳。
explanation_english: A table used for placing food and for people to eat at; commonly found at home or in restaurants.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐桌上已經擺好咗，大家可以開始食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 zoek3 soeng6 ji5 ging1 baai2 hou2 zo2, daai6 gaa1 ho2 ji5 hoi1 ci2 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餐桌已经摆好，大家可以开始吃饭。
examples.english_sentence: The dining table is already set; everyone can start eating.

mandarin_meaning: 餐桌
english_meaning: dining table
explanation_mandarin: 家中或餐廳用來擺放食物、讓人用膳的桌子。
explanation_english: A table used for eating meals, commonly found in homes or restaurants.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋喺餐檯度食飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 hai2 caan1 toi4 dou6 sik6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們在餐桌上吃飯。
examples.english_sentence: We are eating at the dining table.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 張餐檯太細，放唔晒啲碗碟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zoeng1 caan1 toi4 taai3 sai3, fong3 m4 saai3 di1 wun2 dip6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這張餐桌太小，放不下這些碗碟。
examples.english_sentence: This dining table is too small to hold all the plates and bowls.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺餐檯上唔好擺手機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 caan1 toi4 soeng6 m4 hou2 baai2 sau2 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在餐桌上不要放手機。
examples.english_sentence: Don't put your phone on the dining table.

mandarin_meaning: 隨餐附送或作為配菜的湯（常見於套餐或茶餐廳）
english_meaning: Soup served with a meal; soup included as part of a set meal
explanation_mandarin: 指隨餐提供的湯品，通常是套餐或港式茶餐廳附送的例湯或配湯。
explanation_english: Refers to the soup provided with a meal, typically the soup included in a set meal or served at Hong Kong-style eateries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 嗰間茶餐廳嘅餐湯幾好飲，我會再嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go2 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 ge3 caan1 tong1 gei2 hou2 jam2, ngo5 wui5 zoi3 lei4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那間茶餐廳的餐湯挺好喝，我會再來。
examples.english_sentence: The cha chaan teng's meal soup is pretty good; I'll come again.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你買嘅套餐包唔包餐湯？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 maai5 ge3 tou3 caan1 baau1 m4 baau1 caan1 tong1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你買的套餐有沒有包含餐湯？
examples.english_sentence: Does the set meal you bought include soup?

mandarin_meaning: 菜单 / 餐单
english_meaning: menu (in a restaurant)
explanation_mandarin: 指餐厅或食肆提供給顧客選擇菜式與價格的紙本或電子清單。
explanation_english: A restaurant's list (paper or electronic) showing dishes and prices for customers to choose from.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 可以畀我張餐牌睇下嗎？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ho2 ji5 bei2 ngo5 zoeng1 caan1 paai4 tai2 haa5 maa3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 可以给我一张菜单看看吗？
examples.english_sentence: Could you give me a menu to look at?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 而家好多餐廳改用電子餐牌，掃條碼就可以落單。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji4 gaa1 hou2 do1 caan1 teng1 goi2 jung6 din6 zi2 caan1 paai4, sou3 tiu4 maa5 zau6 ho2 ji5 lok6 daan1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 现在很多餐厅改用电子菜单，扫二维码就可以下单。
examples.english_sentence: Nowadays many restaurants use electronic menus — scan the QR code and you can place an order.

mandarin_meaning: （廣東話）吃茶/喝茶，通常指與用餐或社交有關的喝茶（可作名詞或動詞）
english_meaning: In Hong Kong Cantonese: having tea (often with food) — a tea-time meal or tea as a social/meal occasion; can also mean to invite someone for a meal/tea
explanation_mandarin: 在香港粵語裡，「餐茶」通常指以喝茶為主、同時包含小吃或簡餐的用餐/社交活動。有時也用作動詞，表示請人吃飯或喝茶（例如「請你餐茶」）。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese, "餐茶" usually refers to having tea (often accompanied by light food) as part of a meal or social occasion. It can also be used as a verb meaning to invite someone to a meal/tea (e.g., to treat someone).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽日有冇空？我哋去餐茶傾下計。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 jat6 jau5 mou5 hung1? ngo5 dei6 heoi3 caan1 caa4 king1 haa5 gai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 明天有空嗎？我們去喝茶吃點東西聊聊天吧。
examples.english_sentence: Are you free tomorrow? Let's go have tea and chat.

mandarin_meaning: 港式茶餐廳常見的簡餐，通常用即食麵或公仔麵，配上一片午餐肉（或火腿）和煎蛋。
english_meaning: A Hong Kong-style simple dish of noodles topped with a slice of luncheon meat (Spam) and a fried egg.
explanation_mandarin: 「餐蛋麪」常見於香港茶餐廳與快餐店，做法簡單、份量適中，屬於平民化的快餐選擇。麵可以是即食麵或公仔麵，配料通常為午餐肉和煎蛋，也可加蔥或湯底。
explanation_english: Common in Hong Kong cha chaan tengs and casual eateries, this inexpensive, quick meal usually uses instant noodles topped with a slice of luncheon meat and a fried egg. Variations may include scallions or a light broth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想去茶餐廳食餐蛋麪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 heoi3 caa4 caan1 teng1 sik6 caan1 daan6 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚想去茶餐廳吃餐蛋面。
examples.english_sentence: I want to go to a cha chaan teng tonight to eat noodles with luncheon meat and an egg.

mandarin_meaning: 配有午餐肉和煎蛋的面（香港茶餐廳常見的菜式）
english_meaning: noodles topped with luncheon meat (Spam) and a fried egg — a common Hong Kong café (cha chaan teng) dish
explanation_mandarin: 餐蛋麵是香港茶餐廳常見的一種面食，通常在面上配以煎蛋和切片午餐肉（例如罐頭午餐肉），有時使用即食麵作基底，口味簡單且普及。
explanation_english: A popular dish in Hong Kong cha chaan tengs consisting of noodles served with a fried egg and slices of luncheon meat (e.g., canned Spam). It can be made with fresh or instant noodles and is a common, affordable comfort food.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去茶餐廳食餐蛋麵啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 caa4 caan1 teng1 sik6 caan1 daan6 min6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去茶餐厅吃餐蛋面吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the cha chaan teng for some spam-and-egg noodles tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 餐肉蛋面（常指餐厅/茶餐厅用餐肉和鸡蛋搭配的面）
english_meaning: noodles with luncheon meat and egg (a common Hong Kong cha chaan teng/comfort dish)
explanation_mandarin: 「餐蛋麵」是香港茶餐廳常見的一道簡便餐點，通常以即食麵或香港蛋麵，配上切片餐肉（如罐頭午餐肉）及煎蛋或溏心蛋，既便宜又具本地風味，常作早餐或快餐。
explanation_english: “Can daan min” is a common Hong Kong café (cha chaan teng) comfort dish, typically noodles (instant or egg noodles) served with slices of luncheon meat and an egg (fried or soft-boiled). It's inexpensive and a popular breakfast or quick meal.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我朝早食咗一碗餐蛋麵，真係幾滿足。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ziu1zou2 sik6 zo2 jat1 wun2 can1 daan6 min6, zan1 hai6 gei2 mun5 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我早上吃了一碗餐蛋面，真的很满足。
examples.english_sentence: I had a bowl of can daan min this morning — it was really satisfying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 茶餐廳嘅餐蛋麵好平，學生好鍾意食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caa4 caan1 teng1 ge3 can1 daan6 min6 hou2 peng4, hok6 saang1 hou2 zung1 ji3 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 茶餐厅的餐蛋面很便宜，学生很喜欢吃。
examples.english_sentence: The can daan min at cha chaan tengs is cheap; students really like it.

mandarin_meaning: 餐風飲露 / 餐風露宿：在風雨露天中生活，形容生活艱苦、漂泊或露宿受苦。
english_meaning: To live exposed to the elements; to endure hardship outdoors; to lead a rough, itinerant life.
explanation_mandarin: 「餐風飲露」原指在風露下飲食，後用來形容生活在外、露宿風餐或歷經艱苦與漂泊。
explanation_english: Literally 'eat the wind and drink the dew' — an idiom describing living exposed to the elements, enduring hardship, or living a rough, itinerant life.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢啱啱出嚟打拼嗰陣，成日要餐風飲露，實在好辛苦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 aam1 aam1 ceot1 lai4 daa2 ping3 go2 zan6, seng4 jat6 jiu3 caan1 fung1 jam2 lou6, sat6 zoi6 hou2 san1 fu2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛出來打拼的時候，經常餐風飲露，實在很辛苦。
examples.english_sentence: When he first went out to make a living, he was often exposed to the elements and really struggled.

mandarin_meaning: 餐饮 (cānyǐn) — 食物和饮料；亦指餐饮业或用餐相关的服务
english_meaning: food and drink; catering; the food and beverage industry
explanation_mandarin: 指有關飲食的事物或行業，例如餐館、飲料和相關服務；可用於泛指飲食本身或餐飲業。
explanation_english: Refers to matters or industries related to eating and drinking, such as restaurants, beverages, and related services; can denote food and drink themselves or the catering/food & beverage industry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 香港嘅餐飲業好發達。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 ge3 caan1 jam2 jip6 hou2 faat3 daat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 香港的餐饮业很发达。
examples.english_sentence: Hong Kong's food and beverage industry is very developed.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出街餐飲要注意衞生同食物安全。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 gaai1 caan1 jam2 jiu3 zyu3 ji3 wai6 sang1 tung4 sik6 mat6 ngon1 cyun4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 外出用餐要注意卫生和食品安全。
examples.english_sentence: When eating out, pay attention to hygiene and food safety.

mandarin_meaning: 餐馆 (cānguǎn)
english_meaning: restaurant
explanation_mandarin: 指提供餐饮服务的场所，如中式或西式餐馆，用来就餐的地方。
explanation_english: A place where meals are prepared and served to customers; a restaurant.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚去餐館食飯啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 caan1 gun2 sik6 faan6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚去餐馆吃饭吧。
examples.english_sentence: Let's go to the restaurant to eat tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 挨餓、饑餓（現代漢語中較少用）
english_meaning: to starve; famished; to be hungry (archaic/rare in Mandarin; sometimes used in Cantonese writing as a variant of 'hungry')
explanation_mandarin: 表示飢餓、挨餓。此字在現代普通話中較罕見，多見於古文或書面語；在廣東話書寫中偶爾用作「餓」的變體，表達肚餓的狀態。
explanation_english: Denotes hunger or starvation. The character is relatively rare in modern Mandarin and appears more in classical or literary contexts. In Cantonese written usage it can act as a variant of '餓' to indicate being hungry or famished.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我而家好餒，要搵嘢食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hou2 noi5, jiu3 wan2 je5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我現在很餓，要找東西吃。
examples.english_sentence: I'm really hungry right now; I need to find something to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 饿 (è)
english_meaning: hungry
explanation_mandarin: 表示肚子空、需要進食。常用來描述感到需要食物的狀態。
explanation_english: Indicates the physical state of needing food; describes feeling hungry.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我好餓，想食嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hou2 ngo6, soeng2 sik6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我很饿，想吃东西。
examples.english_sentence: I'm very hungry and want to eat something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你餓唔餓？我哋去食晚飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ngo6 m4 ngo6? ngo5 dei6 heoi3 sik6 maan5 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你饿不饿？我们去吃晚饭。
examples.english_sentence: Are you hungry? Let's go have dinner.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個小朋友成日話肚餓。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 siu2 pang4 jau5 sing4 jat6 waa6 tou5 ngo6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个小朋友总是说肚子饿。
examples.english_sentence: This child is always saying he's hungry.

jyutping: ngo6 m4 can1 baau2 m4 sei2
mandarin_meaning: 餓也不會死，飽也不會死（別把小事看得太嚴重）
english_meaning: You won't starve and you won't die from being full (used to say it's not a big deal)
explanation_mandarin: 香港粵語俗語，用來表示某事不是生死攸關，忍一忍或不理也沒大礙，常用來勸人別太擔心或過於在意小事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial saying meaning the situation is not life-threatening — you can endure a bit; it’s not worth making a fuss. Often used to tell someone not to worry or overreact about something minor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好咁放大件事，餓唔親飽唔死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 gam2 fong3 daai6 gin6 si6, ngo6 m4 can1 baau2 m4 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別把這件小事看得太嚴重，餓也不會死，飽也不會死。
examples.english_sentence: Don't blow this out of proportion — you won't starve and you won't die from being full.

jyutping: ngo6 sei2 lou5 po4 fan1 cau3 nguk1
mandarin_meaning: （粵語俗語）形容人非常吝嗇／小氣，寧可讓妻子受苦（餓著），也不願多花錢或做事；是誇張又帶有幽默或貶義的說法。
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang phrase—hyperbolic and often humorous/pejorative—used to describe someone extremely stingy; they'd rather let their wife go hungry than spend money or make any effort.
explanation_mandarin: 此短語以誇張手法表達「極度小氣」的意思，多用於日常會話中批評吝嗇的人，帶有幽默與貶義色彩。
explanation_english: This phrase uses hyperbole to express extreme stinginess. Commonly used in conversational Cantonese to criticize someone as miserly; it carries humorous and derogatory overtones.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做嘢咁小氣，成日慳到戥，真係餓死老婆熏臭屋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 je5 gam3 siu2 hei3, seng4 jat6 haan1 dou3 dang3, zan1 hai6 ngo6 sei2 lou5 po4 fan1 cau3 nguk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做事這麼小氣，整天摳門，真是餓死老婆熏臭屋。
examples.english_sentence: He's so stingy and always saving every penny—truly the type who'd 'let his wife starve and stink up the house' (i.e., extremely miserly).

jyutping: ngo6 sei2 lou5 po4 man1 cau3 uk1
mandarin_meaning: 一種廣東話的粗俗詛咒語，字面是«讓老婆餓死、房子瘟臭»，實際用來表達強烈憤怒或輕蔑，類似「去死」或英語的『fuck you』/『drop dead』。
english_meaning: A vulgar Cantonese curse phrase. Literally reads 'let (your) wife starve to death, (your) house be plagued and stink', but it's used as a coarse expression of extreme anger or contempt — roughly equivalent to 'go to hell', 'drop dead', or 'fuck you'.
explanation_mandarin: 此短語為粗俗罵人用語，帶有詛咒和強烈情緒色彩，多用於生氣或侮辱對象。通常不按字面理解，而是作為粗口表達厭惡或憤怒。
explanation_english: This phrase is a vulgar insult used to curse someone, conveying strong emotion. It is not usually meant literally but functions as a coarse expression of contempt or anger.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢真係好煩，我忍唔住鬧佢：餓死老婆瘟臭屋！
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4, ngo5 jan2 m4 zyu6 naau6 keoi5: ngo6 sei2 lou5 po4 man1 cau3 uk1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他真的很煩，我忍不住罵他：餓死老婆瘟臭屋！
examples.english_sentence: He's really annoying; I couldn't help but yell at him: '餓死老婆瘟臭屋!'

jyutping: ngo6 sei2 lou5 po4 fan1 cau3 uk1
mandarin_meaning: 吝嗇到極點，犧牲家庭成員的生活品質，讓妻子挨餓、屋子變得難聞（用以譏諷極度小氣的人）
english_meaning: An ironic/slang expression for extreme stinginess — so miserly one would let their wife go hungry and the house reek (used to mock someone extremely cheap).
explanation_mandarin: 此俗語用來形容某人小氣到離譜，為省錢不顧家人基本生活，帶有譏諷或批評意味，常見於粵語口語中。
explanation_english: This Cantonese slang/idiom describes a person so miserly they harm their family's basic living standards—used sarcastically or critically in spoken Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢咁慳錢，簡直係餓死老婆薰臭屋，連買菜都捨不得。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam2 kan1 cin2, gaan2 zik6 hai6 ngo6 sei2 lou5 po4 fan1 cau3 uk1, lin4 maai5 coi3 dou1 se2 bat1 dak1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他這麼吝嗇，簡直是「餓死老婆薰臭屋」，連買菜都捨不得。
examples.english_sentence: He's so stingy—he's the type to 'starve his wife and stink up the house'; he won't even buy groceries.

mandarin_meaning: 突然的一陣飢餓感
english_meaning: a sudden wave of hunger; hunger pang
explanation_mandarin: 指短時間內突然湧上的強烈飢餓感，屬口語或俚語用法，常用來形容忽然想吃東西的感覺。
explanation_english: Refers to a sudden, strong feeling of hunger (hunger pang). It is a colloquial/slang term used to describe a brief but intense urge to eat.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱行完街，突然有個餓波，快啲去食嘢啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ngaam1 ngaam1 hang4 jyun4 gaai1, dak6 syun4 jau5 go3 ngo6 bo1, faai3 di1 heoi3 sik6 je5 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我剛剛逛完街，突然有一陣餓意，快點去吃東西吧。
examples.english_sentence: I just finished walking around and suddenly got a wave of hunger—let's hurry to get something to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 形容為了微不足道或無價值的東西而爭得很激烈、狼狽
english_meaning: Describes people desperately and messily scrambling for trivial, worthless, or shameful gains (lit. 'starving dogs fighting over feces').
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語（比喻性短語/形容用法）
explanation_mandarin: 用來比喻人們為了一點小利、廉價贈品或卑微的東西而爭搶、表現狼狽或下作的情況。
explanation_english: A vulgar Cantonese slang phrase used to liken people who scramble desperately and shamefully for trivial or worthless things to starving dogs fighting over excrement.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 為咗啲免費禮物，大家排隊，搞到好似餓狗搶屎咁。
examples.jyutping_sentence: wai6 zo2 di1 min5 fai3 lai5 mat6, daai6 gaa1 paai4 deoi6, gaau2 dou3 hou2 ci5 ngo6 gau2 coeng2 si2 gam2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 為了那些免費禮物，大家排隊，場面搞得像餓狗搶屎一樣。
examples.english_sentence: For the free giveaways, everyone lined up, making a scene like starving dogs fighting over shit.

mandarin_meaning: 曾經挨餓；經歷過饑餓（可引申為歷經艱苦）
english_meaning: to have experienced hunger; to have gone hungry (can be extended to mean having endured hardship)
explanation_mandarin: 表示曾經缺乏食物、挨餓。口語中也常用來泛指經歷過艱苦、困難的日子。
explanation_english: Indicates having experienced lack of food or having gone hungry. In colloquial use it can also refer more generally to having endured hard or difficult times.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢以前餓過飢，依家做嘢特別勤力。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ji5 cin4 ngo6 gwo3 gei1, ji4 gaa1 zou6 je5 dak6 bit6 kan4 lik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他以前挨過餓，現在做事特別勤奮。
examples.english_sentence: He used to go hungry; now he works especially hard.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好笑佢，佢餓過飢，唔似你咁揮霍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 siu3 keoi5, keoi5 ngo6 gwo3 gei1, m4 ci5 nei5 gam2 fai1 hok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別嘲笑他，他曾挨餓，不像你那樣揮霍。
examples.english_sentence: Don't make fun of him; he's been hungry before and doesn't splurge like you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 講起以前餓過飢嘅日子，佢眼濕濕。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gong2 hei2 ji5 cin4 ngo6 gwo3 gei1 ge3 jat6 zi2, keoi5 ngaan5 sap1 sap1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一談起以前挨餓的日子，他眼眶就濕了。
examples.english_sentence: When he talks about the days he went hungry, his eyes get teary.

mandarin_meaning: 吃（文言用字）
english_meaning: to eat (classical/literary)
explanation_mandarin: 「餔」為文言字，意指吃、進食。現代漢語中較少單獨使用，常見於古文或書面語境。
explanation_english: A classical/literary character meaning to eat or take a meal. Rarely used in modern spoken language and primarily appears in classical texts or written contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺古文入面，「餔」解作食嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 gu2 man4 jap6 min6, 'buk6' gaai2 zok3 sik6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在古文中，「餔」意思是吃東西。
examples.english_sentence: In classical texts, '餔' means to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 剩餘；多餘；（古）我
english_meaning: remainder, leftover, surplus; (classical) I
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 名詞/形容詞（古代亦作代詞）
partOfSpeech_english: noun / adjective (in classical Chinese also pronoun)
explanation_mandarin: 表示剩下或多餘的部分，在文言文中有時用作第一人稱「我」。
explanation_english: Indicates what remains or is in excess; in classical Chinese it can serve as the first-person pronoun "I".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餘下嘅錢點算？
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 haa6 ge3 cin2 dim2 syun3?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剩下的钱怎么办？
examples.english_sentence: What should we do with the remaining money?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺呢個情況下，呢個步驟就多餘。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai6 ni1 go3 cing4 fong3 haa6, ni1 go3 bou6 zou6 zau6 do1 jyu4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在這種情況下，這個步驟就是多餘的。
examples.english_sentence: In this situation, this step is redundant.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 古文裏面，『餘』有時用嚟表示『我』。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gu2 man4 leoi5 min6, 'jyu4' jau5 si4 jung6 lai4 biu2 si6 'ngo5'.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 古文里面，“餘”有時用來表示“我”。
examples.english_sentence: In classical texts, '餘' is sometimes used to mean 'I'.

mandarin_meaning: （和）剩下 / 余下 (shèng xià / yú xià)
english_meaning: remaining; left over; what is left
explanation_mandarin: 表示還留下來的部分或數量，可作形容詞或動詞使用，表示某物或某量剩餘。
explanation_english: Indicates what remains or is left over; can function as an adjective or a verb to describe the remaining amount or items.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餘下嘅時間唔多，我哋要快啲決定。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 haa6 ge3 si4 gaan3 m4 do1, ngo5 dei6 jiu3 faai3 di1 kyut3 ding6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 剩下的時間不多，我們要快點決定。
examples.english_sentence: There isn't much time left; we need to decide quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餐廳餘下嘅菜可以打包帶走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: caan1 teng1 jyu4 haa6 ge3 coi3 ho2 ji5 daa2 baau1 daai3 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 餐廳剩下的菜可以打包帶走。
examples.english_sentence: The food left at the restaurant can be packed to take away.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你仲餘下幾多錢？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zung6 jyu4 haa6 gei2 do1 cin2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你還剩多少錢？
examples.english_sentence: How much money do you have left?

mandarin_meaning: 余力（剩余的力量或精力）
english_meaning: spare strength; remaining energy; residual capacity
explanation_mandarin: 指剩下的力量或精力，能夠繼續完成某些事情的餘下能力。常用來表示還有多餘的體力或時間去做某事。
explanation_english: Refers to the remaining strength or spare energy left to continue doing something. Commonly used to indicate leftover physical energy, time, or capacity to do additional tasks.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我仲有少少餘力，可以幫你搬嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung6 jau5 siu2 siu2 jyu4 lik6 , ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5 bun1 je5 .
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我还有一些余力，可以帮你搬东西。
examples.english_sentence: I still have some spare strength and can help you move things.

mandarin_meaning: 余地；回旋的空間或餘裕
english_meaning: room to maneuver; leeway; margin for adjustment or negotiation
explanation_mandarin: 表示還有調整、協商或緩衝的空間或可能性，常用來指在處理事情時可以變通或保留的餘地。
explanation_english: Indicates remaining space or flexibility for adjustment, negotiation, or buffering; the possibility or margin to maneuver when handling matters.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個方案冇乜餘地可以修改。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 fong1 on3 mou5 mat1 jyu4 dei6 ho2 ji5 sau1 goi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這個方案沒有多少餘地可以修改。
examples.english_sentence: This plan doesn't leave much room to make changes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你講嘅條件仲有冇餘地商量？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gong2 ge3 tiu4 gin6 zung6 jau5 mou5 jyu4 dei6 soeng1 loeng4?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你說的條件還有沒有餘地商量？
examples.english_sentence: Is there any room to negotiate the terms you're proposing?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做嘢成日要留啲餘地，唔好咁死板。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 je5 sing4 jat6 jiu3 lau4 di1 jyu4 dei6, m4 hou2 gam2 sei2 baan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做事要留一些餘地，不要這麼死板。
examples.english_sentence: When working, leave some leeway; don't be so rigid.

mandarin_meaning: 余弦（餘弦函數）
english_meaning: cosine (trigonometric function)
explanation_mandarin: 餘弦（cos）是三角函數之一，在直角三角形中定義為鄰邊與斜邊的比值；在單位圓上對應於角的 x 坐標。
explanation_english: The cosine (cos) is a trigonometric function. In a right triangle it is the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse; on the unit circle it corresponds to the x-coordinate of a point at a given angle.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 喺直角三角形入面，餘弦係鄰邊除以斜邊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai2 zik6 gok3 saam1 gok3 jing4 jap6 min6, jyu4 jin4 hai6 leon4 bin1 ceoi4 ji5 ce4 bin1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 在直角三角形中，余弦是邻边除以斜边。
examples.english_sentence: In a right triangle, the cosine is the adjacent side divided by the hypotenuse.

mandarin_meaning: 余数 (yúshù)
english_meaning: remainder (in division)
explanation_mandarin: 在數學裡，除法運算中被除數除以除數後剩下不能被整除的部分稱為餘數。
explanation_english: In mathematics, the remainder is the part left over after dividing one integer by another when the division is not exact.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 七除三，餘數係一。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cat1 ceoi4 saam1, jyu4 sou3 hai6 jat1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 七除以三，余数是1。
examples.english_sentence: 7 divided by 3 has a remainder of 1.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你計錯餘數，答案唔啱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gai3 co3 jyu4 sou3, daap3 on3 m4 ngaam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你算錯了余数，答案不對。
examples.english_sentence: You calculated the remainder incorrectly; the answer is wrong.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老師教我哋點樣計餘數。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 si1 gaau3 ngo5 dei6 dim2 joeng6 gai3 jyu4 sou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老師教我們怎麼計算餘數。
examples.english_sentence: The teacher taught us how to calculate remainders.

mandarin_meaning: 闲暇；空闲时间（古书或书面用语，普通话读作 yúxiá）
english_meaning: leisure; spare time
explanation_mandarin: 表示闲暇、空闲时间，多用于书面或正式语境。
explanation_english: Refers to leisure or spare time; commonly used in written or formal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果有餘暇，佢會去做義工幫助社區。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 jau5 jyu4 haa6, keoi5 wui5 heoi3 zou6 ji6 gung1 bong1 zo6 se5 keoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果有闲暇，他会去做义工帮助社区。
examples.english_sentence: If he has spare time, he volunteers to help the community.

mandarin_meaning: 余波（yúbō）：指事情結束後遺留的影響或後續反應
english_meaning: aftermath; residual effects; repercussions
explanation_mandarin: 「餘波」用來形容事件、衝突或變故結束後仍然持續產生的影響或反應，常見於新聞或描述社會、政治、經濟等方面的後續效應。
explanation_english: ‘餘波’ refers to the after-effects or lingering repercussions that continue after an event, conflict, or incident has ended. It is often used to describe ongoing impacts in social, political, economic, or personal contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢場醜聞雖然過咗，但餘波仲喺度，影響緊公司聲譽。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 coeng4 cau2man4 seoi1jin4 gwo3 zo2, daan6 jyu4 bo1 zung6 hai2 dou6, jing2 hoeng2 gan2 gung1si1 sing1 jyu6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这场丑闻虽然过去了，但余波还在，正在影响公司的声誉。
examples.english_sentence: Although the scandal has passed, the after-effects remain and are affecting the company's reputation.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢單官司雖然判咗，但仲有好多餘波未平。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 daan1 gun1si1 seoi1jin4 pun3 zo2, daan6 zung6 jau5 hou2 do1 jyu4 bo1 mei6 ping4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这起官司虽然判了，但还有很多余波未平。
examples.english_sentence: Although this lawsuit has been decided, many after-effects are still ongoing.

mandarin_meaning: 余生 (yú shēng) — 剩下的生命或未來的日子
english_meaning: the rest of one's life; remaining years
explanation_mandarin: 指個體從現在起剩下的生命或未來的日子，常用於表達對未來的期望、承諾或感慨（例如「共度餘生」）。
explanation_english: Refers to the remaining portion of a person's life or the years ahead; often used to express hopes, commitments, or reflections about the future (e.g. "spend the rest of my life").

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我想同你共度餘生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 soeng2 tung4 nei5 gung6 dou6 jyu4 saang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我想和你共度余生。
examples.english_sentence: I want to spend the rest of my life with you.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 餘生唔長，要珍惜眼前人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 saang1 m4 coeng4, jiu3 zan1 sik1 ngaan5 cin4 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 余生不長，要珍惜眼前人。
examples.english_sentence: Life is not long; cherish the people around you.

mandarin_meaning: 余粮（yúliáng）—— 储备的粮食或多余的口粮
english_meaning: surplus provisions; reserve food or rations
explanation_mandarin: 指多餘或儲備的糧食，常用於家庭、社區或應急情況下作為備用食物。
explanation_english: Refers to extra or stored food supplies kept as reserves, often used by households, communities, or for emergencies.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企有足夠嘅餘糧，唔使擔心短期內會缺糧。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 jau5 zuk1 gau3 ge3 jyu4 loeng4, m4 sai2 daam1 sam1 dyun2 kei4 noi6 wui5 kyut3 loeng4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家里有足够的余粮，不用担心短期内会缺粮。
examples.english_sentence: We have enough reserves at home, so we don't need to worry about short-term shortages.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府建議市民儲備三日嘅餘糧以應付緊急情況。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 gin3 ji5 si5 man4 cyu5 bei6 saam1 jat6 ge3 jyu4 loeng4 ji5 jing3 fu6 gan2 gap1 cing4 fong3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府建议市民储备三天的余粮以应对紧急情况。
examples.english_sentence: The government recommends that citizens stock up on three days' worth of provisions to cope with emergencies.

mandarin_meaning: 余兴；演出結束後額外的表演或節目
english_meaning: encore; after-show entertainment; additional performance after the main event
explanation_mandarin: 指演出或節目結束後，為回應觀眾或延長活動而安排的額外表演或環節。
explanation_english: Refers to an additional performance or segment arranged after the main show, often in response to audience applause or to extend the event.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚嘅演唱會有餘興節目，仲有一位嘉賓會上台唱多首歌。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 ge3 jin2 coeng3 wui2 jau5 jyu4 hing3 zit3 muk6, zung6 jau5 jat1 wai2 gaa1 ban1 wui5 soeng5 toi4 coeng3 do1 sau2 go1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚的演唱會有餘興節目，還有一位嘉賓會上台再唱幾首歌。
examples.english_sentence: Tonight's concert has an encore segment; a guest will come on stage to sing a few more songs.

mandarin_meaning: 余震 (yúzhèn)
english_meaning: aftershock
explanation_mandarin: 主震發生後隨之出現的較小地震震動，通常稱為餘震。
explanation_english: A smaller earthquake that follows the mainshock; secondary tremors occurring after the primary earthquake.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 地震之後仲有幾次餘震，大家都好驚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: dei6 zan3 zi1 hau6 zung6 jau5 gei2 ci3 jyu4 zan3, daai6 gaa1 dou1 hou2 geng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 地震之後還有幾次余震，大家都很害怕。
examples.english_sentence: There were several aftershocks after the earthquake, and everyone was very scared.

mandarin_meaning: 余韵：事物、音乐、话语或经历留下的余味、回响或余音
english_meaning: lingering resonance; aftertaste; the lingering impression or echo left by music, speech, an experience, etc.
explanation_mandarin: 指在某種經驗或表演之後仍然留在心裡或感覺上的餘味或回響，常用於音樂、文學或情感層面。
explanation_english: Refers to the lingering taste, echo, or impression that remains after an experience or performance; often used for music, literature, or emotional aftereffects.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢首歌唱完之後，仲留有一種悠長嘅餘韻。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 sau2 go1 coeng3 jyun4 zi1 hau6, zung6 lau4 jau5 jat1 zung2 jau1 coeng4 ge3 jyu4 wan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这首歌唱完之后，仍然留有一种悠长的余韵。
examples.english_sentence: After this song finishes, a lingering resonance remains.

mandarin_meaning: 余额 (yú'é)
english_meaning: balance; remaining balance (e.g., account balance)
explanation_mandarin: 指帳戶或賬目中剩下的金額，可用來表示銀行戶口、電話卡或其他帳戶的可用餘款。
explanation_english: The amount of money remaining in an account or ledger; the available balance in a bank account, prepaid card, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你銀行戶口嘅餘額仲有幾多？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ngan4 hong4 wu6 hau2 ge3 jyu4 ngok6 zung6 jau5 gei2 do1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你銀行戶口的餘額還有多少？
examples.english_sentence: How much balance do you have left in your bank account?

mandarin_meaning: （名）佳肴；美味的菜餚
english_meaning: delicacy; fine dish; cooked dish
explanation_mandarin: 較書面或文言的詞，指美味的菜餚或佳肴，常見於詞語如「佳餚」「菜餚」。
explanation_english: A literary/formal term referring to delicious dishes or delicacies; commonly appears in compounds like "佳餚" (fine dishes).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚屋企煮咗好多佳餚，大家一齊嚟食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 uk1 kei5 zyu2 zo2 hou2 do1 gaai1 ngaau4, daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 lai4 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚家裡做了很多佳肴，大家一起來吃吧。
examples.english_sentence: They cooked many fine dishes at home tonight; let's all eat together.

mandarin_meaning: （常見於「餛飩」）餛：與餛飩相關的字，指餛飩（雲吞）
english_meaning: The character used in 'wonton' (餛飩); refers to wonton (a type of dumpling)
explanation_mandarin: 單字本身較少單獨使用，主要出現在詞語「餛飩」中，表示一種餃類小吃（即雲吞／wonton）。也屬於漢字的構件或古字用法。
explanation_english: The character is rarely used alone and mainly appears in the compound '餛飩' (wonton). It denotes the wonton dumpling and is otherwise an uncommon/archaic character used in compounds.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字「餛」通常喺「餛飩」裏面見到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 "wan4" tung1 soeng4 hai2 "wan4 tan1" leoi5 min6 gin3 dou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字“餛”通常出现在“餛飩”这个词里。
examples.english_sentence: The character '餛' usually appears in the word '餛飩' (wonton).

mandarin_meaning: 餛飩（húntún）— 一種包有餡的中式麵食，常在湯中食用或油炸作小吃
english_meaning: wonton — a Chinese dumpling made of a thin dough wrapper filled with meat, seafood, or vegetables, often served in soup or deep-fried
explanation_mandarin: 餛飩是用薄麵皮包住肉類或蝦等餡料的食品，可放入湯中作餛飩湯，亦可油炸或伴麵食用。
explanation_english: A wonton is a dumpling made by wrapping seasoned fillings (commonly pork or shrimp) in a thin dough wrapper. Wontons are typically served in soup, added to noodles, or deep-fried as a snack.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想食餛飩湯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 sik6 wan4 tan1 tong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚想吃餛飩湯。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat wonton soup tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友鍾意食炸餛飩做小食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 zung1 ji3 sik6 zaa3 wan4 tan1 zou6 siu2 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小朋友喜歡吃炸餛飩當小吃。
examples.english_sentence: Kids like eating fried wontons as a snack.

mandarin_meaning: 餛飩麵（粵式）
english_meaning: wonton noodles
explanation_mandarin: 一道粵式麵食，通常以清湯或雞湯為湯底，配以蛋麵和包有餡料的餛飩（小雲吞）。
explanation_english: A Cantonese noodle dish of thin egg noodles served in a clear broth (often chicken broth) topped with wontons (small filled dumplings).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今晚想食餛飩麪。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 maan5 soeng2 sik6 wun6 tan1 min6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今晚想吃餛飩麵。
examples.english_sentence: I want to eat wonton noodles tonight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間舖嘅餛飩麪好出名。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 pou3 ge3 wun6 tan1 min6 hou2 ceot1 ming4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間店的餛飩麵很有名。
examples.english_sentence: This shop's wonton noodles are very famous.

mandarin_meaning: 餛飩麵 / 馄饨面（湯麵配餛飩）
english_meaning: wonton noodles (noodles in broth served with wontons)
explanation_mandarin: 一種廣東/香港常見的小吃或主食，由湯麵和餛飩（包有肉或蝦的餡料）組成，常見於茶餐廳和麵店。
explanation_english: A popular Cantonese/Hong Kong dish consisting of noodles served in broth with wontons (dumplings typically filled with pork and/or shrimp). Commonly found in cha chaan tengs and noodle shops.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我今日食咗碗餛飩麵，好好味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 gam1 jat6 sik6 zo2 wan4-tan1-min6, hou2-hou2-mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我今天吃了一碗餛飩麵，很好吃。
examples.english_sentence: I had a bowl of wonton noodles today; it was delicious.

mandarin_meaning: （动/名）为别人举办送别宴、送行；也指送别宴（餞別、送行）
english_meaning: to see off; to hold a farewell banquet; (noun) a farewell banquet or send-off
explanation_mandarin: 「餞」常用於為將要離開的人設宴或敬酒以表示送行，也可指那個宴會本身或所送的酒食。
explanation_english: Used when hosting a meal or offering food/drink to send someone off; can also refer to the farewell party itself or the food/drink given at the send-off.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚幫阿明開個餞，記得嚟呀。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 bong1 aa3 ming4 hoi1 go3 zin3, gei3 dak1 lai4 aa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们今晚为阿明办个送别会，记得来哦。
examples.english_sentence: We're having a send-off for Ah Ming tonight; remember to come.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢出國之前，公司請咗個餞送佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ceot1 gwok3 zi1 cin4, gung1 si1 ceng2 zo2 go3 zin3 sung3 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他出国之前，公司请了个送别会为他送行。
examples.english_sentence: Before he left the country, the company held a farewell party to see him off.

mandarin_meaning: 送別（餞行、為離別舉行的歡送）
english_meaning: farewell; to see someone off; farewell party
explanation_mandarin: 指為將要離開的人舉行歡送、送行或餞行的活動或行為，也可指這類歡送會本身。
explanation_english: Refers to holding a farewell/seeing-off event for someone who is leaving; can mean the act of bidding farewell or the farewell party itself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋今晚為佢搞個餞別飯。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 wai6 keoi5 gaau2 go3 zin3 bit6 faan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我們今晚為他辦個送別宴。
examples.english_sentence: We're having a farewell dinner for him tonight.
